entities.okrs: NA

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Contract Lifecycle Management is delivering a single enterprise CLM platform (Icertis) across Commercial and Procurement to standardize contract terms, digitize end to end workflows, and provide a scalable global contract repository that reduces financial and compliance risk. The program is key to addressing contractual non compliance, improving negotiation readiness, and replacing fragmented, manual contract processes with controlled, auditable workflows.

To date, the R1 Commercial pilot went live on 13 Apr 2026 with all planned scope enabled, production contracts processed end to end, and zero Sev1 or Sev2 incidents, while R1a Procurement and R2 Commercial are both in progress against their 31 Jul 2026 planned completion dates. R1a has improved from Red to Amber following positive alignment on the Contract Express integration, but R2 configuration, UAT scheduling, and data migration dependencies continue to compress the June UAT and July rollout window.

Overall status is AMBER, driven primarily by R2 Commercial timeline compression that risks on time completion of configuration, QA, and extended UAT ahead of the planned July rollout.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing R2 design and configuration gaps and locking the full UAT and rollout plan by 29 May 2026, while in parallel resolving data access and migration readiness dependencies by 12 Jun 2026 so that July data migration does not delay the R2 rollout. In addition, we will complete Contract Express SOW approval by 22 May 2026 and finalize clause library decisions by 12 Jun 2026 to stabilize the R1a Procurement timeline and remove remaining integration related uncertainty.

## Milestones

- Complete R2 design and configuration gaps across templates and Order Capture data flow by 29 May 2026 to enable QA/SIT readiness.  
- Finalize the full UAT timeline and rollout options for R2 by 29 May 2026.  
- Deliver R2 Commercial Tech and Business Go Live, with hypercare concluded, by 31 Jul 2026.  
- Deliver the R1a Procurement rollout, including Contract Express–Icertis integration, by 29 Aug 2026.  
- Complete overall CLM program implementation and transition to steady state by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: R2 Commercial timeline compression may delay June UAT and July rollout
risks.description: Configuration and QA testing for R2 Commercial (covering NDA, MSA, GPV, and Term Letter) may not complete on time because design for MSA, Special Offers, and Modifications is not yet finalized. This compresses the schedule and could jeopardize the planned sequence of configuration, QA by end-May, extended UAT in June, and business rollout in July.
risks.impact_description: If R2 configuration and QA are delayed, extended UAT in June will be shortened or pushed out, reducing testing coverage and quality. This could force a delay of the July business rollout, or result in a lower-quality deployment with unresolved defects, impacting Commercial contract processes and stakeholder confidence.
risks.mitigation: Maintain focus on finalizing designs for MSA, Special Offers, and Modifications as quickly as possible, and continue driving core build activities across NDA, MSA, GPV, and Term Letter so configuration and QA can complete by end-May. Monitor progress closely and apply timeline mitigation actions to protect June UAT and July rollout.
risks.source_file_name: CLM Program - Weekly status update - 12th May 2026.msg

risks.title: Procurement R1a go-live at risk due to unresolved Contract Express integration and clause library strategy
risks.description: The R1a Procurement workstream remains Amber because the approach for integrating Contract Express and the strategy for clause library storage in Icertis have not yet been fully finalized. These decisions are required for the Procurement solution to go live, although positive business alignment on the Contract Express integration has improved the status from Red to Amber and enabled a revised go-live date of 29 Aug 2026.
risks.impact_description: If the Contract Express integration scope and clause library storage strategy are not confirmed and implemented in time, the Procurement R1a go-live on 29 Aug 2026 will be delayed. This will postpone Procurement’s adoption of the CLM platform, extend manual processes, and may create misalignment between Procurement and Commercial contract workflows. It could also require rework of integration and change management activities if the SOW is not approved as expected.
risks.mitigation: Continue and conclude discussions on the Contract Express integration approach and clause library strategy in Icertis, and make the necessary design and scope decisions so that Procurement R1a can proceed to build and deployment. Secure positive business alignment for the Contract Express integration, complete the integration walkthrough with Accenture, and drive SOW approval targeted for 22 May 2026 to enable formal progression towards the revised 29 Aug 2026 go-live.
risks.source_file_name: CLM Program - Weekly status update - 12th May 2026.msg

risks.title: Data migration start may slip due to data access and template deployment dependencies
risks.description: The Data workstream is Amber/At Risk because of dependencies on data access, migration readiness, and closure of open design items related to special offers and contract implementation. The start of data migration may shift to July due to dependency on template deployment and US Government data handling requirements. Data discovery is in progress and an analyst has been onboarded to support the D&A team, but the dependencies remain.
risks.impact_description: If data access issues, open design items for special offers and contract implementation, template deployment delays, and US Gov data handling requirements push the data migration start beyond July, downstream testing and deployment activities that rely on migrated data will be delayed. This could jeopardize alignment with R2 timelines and affect the availability and quality of the global contract repository at rollout, increasing the risk of rework and late discovery of data quality issues.
risks.mitigation: Progress data discovery activities and leverage the newly onboarded analyst to support the D&A team, while working with relevant stakeholders to resolve data access issues and ensure template deployment completes in time to start migration by July. Closely manage finish-to-start interdependencies between contract implementation and data migration, assess and address potential rework case-by-case, and ensure US Gov data handling requirements are understood and incorporated into the migration plan.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The S3NS Cloud Provider Build and Support project remains in green status, with pre-prod stable and testing set to begin on 27 May following a short operational delay. Key technical issues have either been mitigated or are currently unblocked, including database connectivity and Sentinel One/GKE versioning, while the absence of Cloud Armor WAF is not expected to impact June go-live. The team continues to monitor a few open dependencies, including production build confirmation, Truccr bandwidth resolution, and downstream coordination for Splunk, Wiz, and ESSO activities.

Overall status is Green, driven by strong progress on ISRM tooling migration (80% complete) and closure of core security control actions ahead of the 01 Sep 2026 mandate date.

## Path to Green

All risks have been mitigated around customer onboarding tooling by validating the Memority eSSO solution and confirming ISRM workarounds are sufficient to support S3NS testing and early onboarding.

## Milestones

-   Complete SentinelOne installation across in-scope endpoints and finalize Memority eSSO configuration and exceptions by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Meet French e-invoicing and e-reporting security readiness requirements for Pagero customers and suppliers in France by 01 Sep 2026.
    
-   Implement Truccr integration for core data loads and enable Splunk / PLE centralized logging ingestion for S3NS by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Activate Wiz cloud security monitoring for the S3NS environment and complete 100% of ISRM tooling migration for Pagero by 2026-12-31.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Pagero Cloud Migration (Public) and Office Networking is delivering TR-standard public cloud foundations, CI/CD tooling, and integrated office networks (routers, switches, WAPs, ISP connectivity, and cabling) across six European offices as part of the Pagero acquisition integration. This work enables consistent operations, smoother application migrations, and a clean handover to TechM support for ongoing stability.

To date, 40% of network integration activities across the six offices are complete against the 100% target by 30 Sep 2026, with site-level progress ranging from 50% to 75% and the aggregate end date still aligned to plan. CI/CD tooling migration is delayed due to Pagero resource focus on S3NS client onboarding, though the restart window is already planned for Aug 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by office integration being 40% complete and tracking to the 30 Sep 2026 target while delays from ISPs are being contained through active risk management.

## Path to Green

The top risk mitigation focuses on ISP-related connectivity delays, with close tracking of landlords and cabling vendors and proactive stakeholder communication to keep the 30 Sep 2026 office integration target intact.

## Milestones

- Complete office integration for Ostersund by 29 May 2026, increasing site completion from the current 75% toward full handover to TechM support.
- Complete office integration for Skovde by 29 May 2026, moving from the current 60% toward full network and ISP commissioning.
- Complete office integration for Stockholm by 17 Jun 2026, resolving the outstanding cross-connect dependency and finalizing network services.
- Complete office integration across all six European offices by 30 Sep 2026, up from 40% of activities completed today to 100% of the target scope.
- Complete migration to TR-standard CI tooling and supporting infrastructure by 30 Dec 2026, followed by overall program closure by 17 Dec 2027.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Product Engineering and Platform Readiness is delivering S3NS-based pre-production and production environments, replicating the existing Pagero platform and enabling France e‑invoicing and e‑reporting with French PA and audit compliance. This matters because France customers and suppliers will rely on the platform as a regulated digital channel, and audit‑ready operations are a prerequisite for go‑live.

Pre‑production build in S3NS is now complete as of 25 May 2026, 10 days later than the 15 May 2026 plan, and platform microservices replication and production environment build are in progress with the current latest‑estimate completion on 12 Jun 2026, slipping 12 days beyond the 31 May 2026 target. Internal functional testing in pre‑prod is at 50% completion toward a 31 May 2026 sign‑off, while 80% of Linux developer laptops are Intune‑compliant against a 100% compliance objective before mid‑year audits.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by the remaining 20% of Linux laptops not yet Intune‑managed, which creates a significant audit and security compliance risk if unresolved before the upcoming mid‑year audit window.

## Path to Green

- Complete internal functional testing in pre‑production and achieve sign‑off by 31 May 2026.

- Finalize service management process approvals and adoption by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Bring all Linux developer laptops back into Intune compliance, increasing from the current 80% to 100%, by 31 Jul 2026.

risks.description: A large number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers dropped out of Intune because users did not log into the Intune app at least monthly. While day‑to‑day end‑user work is not currently impacted, this creates a compliance gap and a risk that non‑managed or even private Linux devices could be used to access customer data.

Lack of device control increases the risk that private, non‑company Linux devices are used to access customer data, potentially breaching internal security standards and regulatory obligations. risks.title: Lack of Wiz support in SANS may delay required cloud security coverage for S3NS
risks.description: The Wiz security solution is currently not supported by SANS in the targeted environment. Recent discussions with Google (around 22 April) did not yield a clear delivery timeline for support. If support is significantly delayed, the project may lack the desired level of cloud security visibility and control, and compensating controls may be required.
risks.impact_description: If Wiz remains unsupported in SANS for an extended period, the S3NS platform will not have the intended Wiz-based visibility and protections. This may leave gaps in cloud security monitoring and vulnerability management, and could lead to deviations from TR security policy, which expects this to be in place by 2026. If auditors or internal security governance identify this gap, additional scrutiny or corrective actions may be imposed. Implementing compensating controls later under time pressure could consume significant time and resources and potentially delay other security and platform readiness activities.
risks.mitigation: Bill will obtain a more definitive timeline from SANS/Google regarding when Wiz will be supported and use that to decide on the strategy. If support can be delivered within 2026 (for example by Q4), the project may accept the delay with careful monitoring. If the timeline extends significantly (e.g., into 2027), Bill and the security team will design and implement compensating controls that provide a similar level of visibility and protection, balancing the effort and resources required against the expected duration until Wiz support becomes available.

## Executive Summary

Pagero – Legal Entity migrations will transition Belgium, Italy, and Poland from IFS legal entities to new TR legal entities, aligning with the broader Legal Entity Migration Strategy through Commercial Policy. This enables compliant billing, contracting, and renewals under the correct TR entities while minimizing operational disruption.

To date, 7 of 11 defined milestones are complete, including all foundational configuration items (legal entity naming, GSI updates, WRP Sales Org creation, and IFS/Pagero data collection). All completed milestones met their planned dates with zero schedule variance, and remaining work focuses on Pagero Temails changes, Conga order form enhancements, UAT sign-off, and country go-lives by 30 Jun 2026 and 01 Jul 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by all completed milestones tracking to plan and the Belgium, Italy, and Poland launch dates holding to 30 Jun 2026 and 01 Jul 2026.

## Path to Green

The key mitigation focus is on managing the one-day offset between Belgium/Italy and Poland go-live dates by confirming that contract language, renewals, and notifications operate correctly across both 30 Jun 2026 and 01 Jul 2026. The team will continue to validate assumptions and downstream impacts ahead of the Poland launch to ensure no service or compliance gaps.

- Obtain formal UAT sign-off by 22 May 2026.  
- Complete Pagero Temails requirements, testing, and code release by 23 May 2026.  
- Finalize Conga / Order Capture order form enhancements for the new legal entities by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Execute business launch for Belgium and Italy on 30 Jun 2026 and for Poland on 01 Jul 2026.  
- Close out the Pagero – Legal Entity migrations project and transition to steady-state operations by 10 Jul 2026.

## Executive Summary

Plat Eng AI Reimagine is deploying AI and automation across infrastructure services, platform operations, and software development to shift teams from manual execution to exception management. The program aims to deliver measurable productivity and efficiency gains across the platform engineering landscape over the two-year horizon.

Overall status is Green, driven by alignment of all three major workstreams to a clarified value model and closure of earlier risks around pipeline scalability, financial gap identification, and coding efficiency measurability.

## Path to Green

The primary focus is on sustaining Green status by continuing to refine how AI-driven productivity gains are measured and captured, including using capacity redeployment and avoided cost metrics for coding agents by 30 Jun 2026.

## Milestones

-   Complete Agentic Infrastructure Services POVs and MVPs that automate code modernization, CI/CD migration, database patching, network operations, and incident response by 31 Dec 2026.

-   Implement PLE Service Management Agents to automate platform operational tasks using AISM agents and reusable patterns by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete the Plat Eng AI Reimagine program and transition to steady-state operations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: [PE14] Agentic CD Pipeline Generation Automation: AI Model context window limitation impacts Cumulus Agent scalability
risks.description: The current AI model used for the AI‑assisted Cumulus pipeline creation tool has a 1,000‑file context window limitation, which may restrict its ability to accurately process and validate large or complex repositories. This constraint presents a risk to the reliability, scalability, and completeness of pipeline generation and validation as the solution evolves beyond the current POC scope.
risks.impact_description: If the context window limitation is not addressed, the AI‑assisted pipeline creation tool may fail to fully analyze larger codebases or complex repository structures, produce incomplete or inaccurate pipeline definitions, require increased manual intervention (reducing expected productivity gains), and limit the solution’s ability to scale for broader enterprise adoption. This would delay progression beyond POC and weaken the business value case for MVP and Scale phases.
risks.mitigation: Engage the Tiger Team to assess architectural or design patterns that mitigate context size constraints (e.g., repository chunking, staged analysis, or selective context loading).

risks.title: Discover additional opportunities to close financial gap
risks.description: The current set of identified PLE Point Solutions (e.g., ADO Assist) may be insufficient to close the remaining gap to PLE financial targets, with limited additional use cases identified to date.
risks.impact_description: If additional opportunities are not discovered in a timely manner, PLE may fall short of committed financial targets, requiring re‑baselining or reliance on higher‑risk assumptions.
risks.mitigation: Initiate a structured discovery effort across PLE teams to identify incremental, high‑impact point solutions; prioritize use cases with short time‑to‑value and clear benefit attribution.

risks.title: Market‑Benchmarked Coding Efficiency Limits
risks.description: Coding efficiency improvements are market‑benchmarked at approximately 8–10%, making benefits planning and realization complex. Gains are incremental, distributed across multiple teams and tools, and not concentrated in a single measurable outcome, which complicates planning and value realization for the AI coding agents efficiency initiative.
risks.impact_description: Difficulty in quantifying, attributing, and realizing savings from coding efficiency improvements. Benefits may remain theoretical or be absorbed as additional delivery capacity rather than converted to measurable financial value. This will increase the challenge of demonstrating clear ROI to leadership and could erode confidence in coding efficiency as a defensible value lever for the PLE AI Reimagine program.
risks.mitigation: Shift success metrics from pure efficiency percentage improvements to capacity redeployment or avoided cost. Define clear benefit capture mechanisms (for example, reduced backlog growth and reduced contractor usage). Bundle incremental gains into aggregated benefit stories instead of reporting per use case. Apply risk‑adjusted benefit forecasting for coding efficiency use cases.

issues.title: Infrastructure Coding Efficiency Benefits Gap vs Target
issues.description: There is a gap to the target of $0.35M in infrastructure coding efficiency benefits, with no clear additional use case currently identified to close the shortfall. issues.impact_assessment: There is a risk of missing the committed $0.35M efficiency target, which would impact overall PLE AI Reimagination value delivery. It reduces confidence in coding efficiency as a primary value lever and may require re-baselining benefits expectations or reallocating value targets to other pillars.
issues.resolution: Refocus benefits planning on fewer, higher-impact coding workflows rather than broad incremental gains; accelerate benefits validation for in-flight coding agents to confirm realizable savings early; and explore cross-pillar contributions (such as CI/CD, repository migration, and infrastructure-as-code initiatives) that can partially offset coding efficiency targets.

## Executive Summary

Service Mgmt AI Reimagine is delivering AI-driven L0/L1 support, SRE recovery agents, standardized deployment pipelines, and automated ITIL workflows so that service teams can move from manual execution to exception-based assurance and higher-value product delivery. This matters because current service operations rely on human triage and fragmented pipelines, which make scaling service quality economically unsustainable.

By design, the SRE workstream plans 23 production agents by 31 Dec 2026, with an initial 4-agent AWS proof of concept followed by three tranches of 4, 6, and 5 agents. However, the proof of concept scheduled to complete by 15 May 2026 is still in progress as of 22 May 2026 and Diamond Lane has 4 of 11 core milestones still open against a 30 Jun 2026 readiness target, indicating schedule pressure on the 2026 benefit case.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by Diamond Lane readiness criteria and pipeline automation not yet reaching the maturity needed to safely scale application onboarding by 30 Jun 2026.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on completing the delayed AWS 4-agent proof of concept with clear pass and fail criteria while enforcing a gate that prevents wider SRE agent rollout until accuracy and recovery benefits are evidenced. In parallel, the team will prioritize closure of the remaining Diamond Lane criteria, contracts, scorecard, and pipeline automation milestones by 30 Jun 2026, gating new product onboarding until those controls are in place.

## Milestones

- Complete AWS SRE agent proof of concept for Compute Build, Storage Build, Network Build, and Legal Tracker SRE by 15 May 2026.
- Stabilize Diamond Lane continuous integration criteria, product contracts, scorecard version 1, and pipeline driven change automation by 30 Jun 2026.
- Deliver Tranche 1 SRE agents (Compute Build, Storage Build, Network Build, Legal Tracker SRE) fully operational in production by 14 Aug 2026.
- Deliver Tranche 2 and Tranche 3 SRE agents fully operational in production by 30 Nov 2026.
- Complete Service Mgmt AI Reimagine program outcomes and transition to steady state operations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unproven technology dependency
risks.description: The workstream places a strategic "big-bet" on AI agent technology that has not yet been validated in production SRE environments. The core automated remediation and runbook execution capabilities depend on cloud-native AI services (AWS) whose reliability, accuracy, and performance at scale remain unproven within the organization.
risks.impact_description: Failure to prove out the technology delays or eliminates SRE productivity gains, exposing the portfolio to material concentration risk. Teams continue operating at current capacity, preventing each SRE from supporting additional Product Engineering teams and eroding the business case for the investment.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate validation through a time-boxed proof-of-concept using AWS infrastructure with the embedded AI Squad on a long-term basis. Define clear technical pass/fail criteria up front. Run parallel runbook execution (manual and automated) during the trial to measure accuracy and reduction in mean time to recovery (MTTR) before full commitment.

risks.title: SRE Agent: Unclear path to scaled benefits beyond initial scope
risks.description: The aggregate business value of the SRE Agent workstream is predicated on scaling beyond the initial product suite (LPP). There is currently no confirmed product roadmap or suitability assessment that provides a clear, sequenced line-of-sight into which additional products will benefit from automation, or when.
risks.impact_description: Without a defined scaling path, benefits remain constrained to a narrow initial scope, significantly reducing ROI and undermining stakeholder confidence. The workstream may be deprioritized before reaching the scale at which SRE-to-team coverage ratios improve materially across the portfolio.
risks.mitigation: Pillar LT to confirm the short-list of candidate products for the initial roadmap (noted as complete). Develop a detailed scaling plan that documents: (1) prioritization criteria for product suitability, (2) the sequencing logic that maximizes early benefit realization, and (3) a governance checkpoint at the end of each phase to validate the next tranche of candidates before expanding scope.

risks.title: DevOps: Diamond Lane Scale Readiness Risk – Incomplete Automation and Criteria Frameworks
risks.description: With 4 of 11 core milestones still in progress and ServiceNow policy integration intentionally deferred, there is a risk that Diamond Lane's CI criteria, product contracts, scorecard v1, and pipeline-driven change automation will not reach sufficient maturity by the 30 Jun 2026 target. This could prevent the program from enforcing eligibility and routing decisions in an auditable, repeatable way before broader application onboarding begins.
risks.impact_description: If the pipeline automation, rollback patterns, and scorecard frameworks are not stabilized before expansion, Diamond Lane risks scaling ahead of proven templates and controls. This could result in ungoverned production changes, audit exposure, and potential rollback failures for onboarded applications — undermining the program's core value proposition of faster, compliant delivery.
risks.mitigation: Gate all new application onboarding behind defined readiness criteria tied to scorecard v1 and crawl-stage rollback completion. Prioritize the 30 Jun 2026 milestone for CI criteria, contracts, and pipeline automation. Maintain the deferral of ServiceNow policy integration to avoid scope creep. Conduct bi-weekly checkpoint reviews against the path-to-green plan to surface blockers early and allow resource reallocation if needed.

risks.title: DevOps Diamond Lane – Limited '26 Product Coverage and VC Benefit Realization
risks.impact_description: Without a product in the 2026 plan that delivers meaningful VC benefits, the Diamond Lane program risks being perceived as a capability buildout rather than a value driver. This could affect stakeholder confidence, funding continuity, and prioritization decisions heading into 2027 planning cycles — particularly if leadership expects demonstrable ROI from the DevOps Acceleration investment within the year.
risks.mitigation: Identify and evaluate whether any current or near-term candidate products could be onboarded to Diamond Lane in a way that surfaces measurable VC benefits without compromising pilot integrity. In parallel, develop a clear narrative that frames the 2026 crawl-stage work as the prerequisite to VC realization in 2027, with defined benefit milestones tied to the expansion and enablement phase. Establish leading indicators (e.g., deployment frequency, change failure rate, manual effort reduction) that can serve as proxy VC metrics while the full model matures.

## Executive Summary

Comm Eng AI Reimagine is scaling AI-assisted development, testing, and service management across Commercial Engineering to deliver $3.3m in efficiency savings and improve engineering productivity and service reliability. The program focuses on CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency and CE Service Management Agents, with benefits tracked through finance-backed plans and AI adoption metrics.

Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption is currently around 60% against a 70% target, with adoption metric calculation refined and AI capabilities implemented on selected user stories to demonstrate value. SAP developers have 95–98% GitHub Copilot coverage, but dashboards for consistent usage and efficiency tracking are still being finalised and the current use case-level plan remains short of the committed $3.3m benefits target.

Overall status is Amber, driven by the current use case-level benefits plan falling short of the finance-backed $3.3m efficiency target.

## Path to Green

To return to Green we will close the $3.3m benefits gap by 30 Jun 2026 through discovery and onboarding of additional AI use cases, while raising Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption from ~60% to at least 70% via targeted training, engagement, and value-focused POCs. In parallel, we will complete AI adoption dashboards and strengthen GitHub Copilot governance for SAP and testing tools so that productivity gains are reliably measured and attributed to the finance-backed savings plan.

## Milestones

- Close the gap to the $3.3m committed benefits target by discovering and onboarding additional AI use cases by 30 Jun 2026.
- Ensure each team updates AI-related user stories in Azure DevOps on a two-week sprint cadence, moving reporting off spreadsheets, by 15 May 2026.
- Complete implementation and tracking of the finance-backed quarterly savings plan for SAP GitHub Copilot adoption by 31 Jul 2026.
- Increase Salesforce Coding Assistant adoption from ~60% toward the 70% target and close the associated risk by 30 Sep 2026.
- Deliver CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency and CE Service Management Agents outcomes and close the Comm Eng AI Reimagine program by 31 Dec 2027.

This could result in missed Q1 adoption and usage targets, reduced benefits realisation, and potential gaps against the finance-backed quarterly savings plan for the CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency project.
risks.mitigation: Adopt GitHub Copilot for SAP development with strong governance for both vendor and FTE teams to drive deeper usage. Implement an enablement plan to provide access to the majority of target users (aiming for 95–98% coverage) and configure an AI usage dashboard for tracking usage percentages and benefits. Revise Q1 targets as needed while agreeing critical actions with the VP to improve the baseline adoption and ensure alignment with the finance-backed quarterly savings plan.

## Executive Summary

CIO Co-Counsel Next Rollout is defining and applying a concise operational readiness framework and guardrails for the CoCounsel Next AI ESE rollout, so that GA and continuous changes are controlled without slowing the catalyst model. This framework will protect production for a high-visibility AI product and become the baseline for future catalyst launches.

The project has expanded from a Service Management focus to cover all of CIO in order to provide a holistic view of readiness and central monitoring of risks, issues and dependencies. Discovery work is in progress to identify the full scope of CIO requirements. The first iteration of the Service Management operational readiness framework is in review this week with the CoCo Next Prod Eng team.

Overall status is Green, driven by the progress being made with forming the CIO scope and agreeing a working method (ADO) with Product Engineering for tracking work and dependencies.

## Path to Green

None required.

## Milestones

-   Finalize CIO-wide deliverables and requirements for the CoCounsel Next rollout by 05 Jun 2026.

risks.title: Unsecured HTTP connections between internal systems not remediated by GA
risks.description: Some internal systems in the CoCounsel Next architecture are communicating over HTTP instead of HTTPS. ISRM accepted this configuration for beta but explicitly stated it is not acceptable for GA. There is a risk that the required security changes may not be completed before GA.
risks.impact_description: If HTTP communication between internal components remains in place at GA, CoCounsel Next may be non-compliant with ISRM security requirements. This could delay or block GA approval, create security vulnerabilities, increase audit findings, and require emergency remediation work close to or after launch.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Product engineering team for CoCounsel Next (e.g., delivery manager Chetan Singh and architect Josh Schmidt)

risks.mitigation: Track the HTTP-to-HTTPS remediation as a required GA guardrail item and ensure it is included in the operational readiness tracker. Coordinate with product engineering (delivery manager Chetan Singh and architect Josh Schmidt) to plan and implement secure HTTPS communication between all relevant internal systems before GA. Confirm with ISRM that the final configuration meets GA security expectations. As of 13 May 2026, ISRM has indicated that a solution exists, but service management has verified that the production load balancer is still accepting port 80/8080 traffic and routing to port 80 targets. Service management will re-check lower environments and production configuration after the target closure date to confirm that HTTPS has been fully deployed end-to-end.

milestones.name: First iteration of operational readiness framework ready for alignment with Product Engineering leadership

risks.title: Potential impact of CoCounsel Next on shared infrastructure capacity
risks.description: CoCounsel Next (an AI ESE project) may place significant additional load on shared infrastructure. Service management has identified a continuing risk that the traffic generated during multi-wave beta and upcoming GA could negatively impact shared systems, leading to degraded performance or instability for CoCounsel Next and other services sharing the same infrastructure.
risks.impact_description: If CoCounsel Next's usage exceeds the capacity of shared infrastructure, it could cause performance degradation, timeouts, or outages for CoCounsel Next and other shared services. This may jeopardize the GA launch, harm customer experience, and require emergency remediation effort across SRE, GCC, and product engineering teams.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with the product engineering team and the service management scale program to ensure infrastructure scale testing adequately covers CoCounsel Next's expected and peak loads before GA. Review scale and load test results regularly, and ensure tests are run in pre-prod at higher levels than expected in production. Track this as a formal guardrail requirement for GA and ensure it is included in the operational readiness checklist. As of 13 May 2026, the team has improved visibility into scale testing and is confident in the current trajectory, but recognizes that scale and capacity validation must remain an ongoing activity throughout beta and post-GA rather than a one-time exercise.
risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Lack of defined operational guardrails for AI ESE launches
risks.description: Service management does not yet have an agreed list of minimum operational readiness requirements (“guardrails”) for AI ESE projects like CoCounsel Next. ESE projects are intentionally doing things differently to enable speed, which changes the typical division of accountability and processes (e.g., change management, incident management, scale testing). Without defined guardrails, CoCounsel Next could proceed to GA without essential operational controls in place.
risks.impact_description: If the minimum operational requirements for ESE launches are not defined and agreed with product engineering before CoCounsel Next GA, the product may launch with inconsistent or insufficient processes for change, incident, and scale management. This could lead to operational instability, unclear responsibilities, and reduced ability for service management to protect production, potentially impacting customer experience and setting a problematic precedent for future ESE launches.
risks.mitigation:
Service management (including Kathy Holtzleiter and Justin Jenkins) will compile a list of critical guardrails and requirements needed for operational readiness in the ESE model, including scale testing expectations, use of ServiceNow (or alternative tools) for changes and incidents, and pre‑prod testing thresholds. Present this list to Wil LeBlanc for review and refinement, then align with ESE program leadership (e.g., via Wil’s discussions with Viola Matisse and Jason) to agree on a minimum set of requirements that must be met before GA.

 Once confirmed these requirements will form the scope of the project from a Service Management perspective.  Requirements will be used to create ADO work items and be tracked to completion.  This risk will be closed at that time.

milestones.name: First iteration of operational readiness framework ready for alignment with Product Engineering leadership

risks.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

risks.title: Unclear production support ownership model for CoCounsel Next post-GA
risks.description: There is no agreed model on who will own and provide production support for CoCounsel Next after GA. For non-ESE products, service management typically owns production support. However, ESE messaging emphasizes that product engineering builds it, deploys it, supports it. Individual engineers, however, have expressed assumptions that service management might take over after beta. This misalignment means operational responsibilities are not defined.
risks.impact_description: If production support responsibilities remain unclear at GA, there may be gaps or overlaps in incident response, on-call coverage, and problem management. This can lead to delayed incident handling, finger-pointing, and poor customer experience, as well as burnout of teams unintentionally bearing unsupported workloads. In addition, misalignment with the EASY objective of keeping product engineering close to the impact of their deployments could cause friction with leadership expectations.
risks.mitigation:
Drive a discussion between service management leadership (Wil LeBlanc), CoCounsel product engineering leadership (e.g., Viola Matisse), and relevant stakeholders to explicitly define the production support model for CoCounsel Next (who owns support during beta, GA, and beyond). Document the agreed model, including escalation paths and hand-offs, and incorporate it into the operational readiness criteria for GA. 

As of 13 May 2026, the team has confirmed that the production support model is not part of the current guardrails list and must be managed as a separate deliverable (the support flow), with potentially significant staffing and training implications depending on the model chosen.

risks.description: In the ESE model, there is active discussion of using alternatives to ServiceNow for incident and change management. Some stakeholders view traditional tools as inconvenient or not “easy.” Service management relies on consistent tools like ServiceNow to operate effectively and ensure consistent processes for GCC staff and SRE teams. issues.title: Limited visibility and confidence in CoCounsel Next scale testing and readiness
issues.description: Service management has limited visibility into CoCounsel Next scale testing, which is currently owned and run by product engineering. Scale tests are being referred to as 'load tests' and typically run for about two hours, which may not be sufficient to represent real production behaviour. There are concerns that scale tests are not staying ahead of increasing beta usage and that problems appear when simulating higher loads (e.g., double wave one for anticipated wave two). The service management scale program is not being used, and the service management team lacks confidence that CoCounsel Next is prepared for GA or even higher beta usage.
issues.impact_assessment: Because scale testing is controlled by product engineering with limited transparency, service management cannot properly assess operational readiness or ensure sufficient capacity and stability prior to General Availability. The current short-duration load tests may fail to reveal issues that would surface under sustained production load. Evidence of problems when attempting to simulate higher waves of beta usage suggests that performance and reliability risks may materialize if GA is pursued without robust, long-running scale tests. This threatens GA timelines and risks customer-facing instability.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependent on product engineering scale tests and potential engagement of the Service Management Scale Team; affects CoCounsel Next GA readiness and AI EASY operational guardrails.
issues.resolution: Engagement with the AIESE team to discuss scale testing concerns and agree a plan to address. As of 11 May 2026, Jenkins, Justin P. (TR Technology) confirms he has access to scale testing meetings and results, but the adequacy of the testing approach and alignment with service management expectations are still being actively worked.
issues.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

issues.title: Service management lacks adequate communication and planning visibility for CoCounsel Next
issues.description: Service management has limited visibility into CoCounsel Next planning and day-to-day decisions. Many discussions occur in Slack with restricted membership (e.g., only specific individuals such as Dante De Luca and Jenkins, Justin P. have access), and there are few or no ongoing project planning meetings involving service management. The AI EASY approach intentionally uses different communication tools and restricted channels, which reduces transparency for the broader service management team.
issues.impact_assessment: The lack of structured communication and visibility impairs service management's ability to identify risks, track progress toward GA, and ensure operational readiness. Without consistent updates on scale testing, milestones, and decisions, service management cannot reliably define or verify minimum guardrails, increasing the risk of misalignment and last-minute surprises before GA.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Depends on CoCounsel Next product and engineering teams sharing information via meetings or communication channels (e.g., Slack). Affects service management readiness, guardrails definition, and coordination with AI EASY leadership.
issues.resolution: Identify a contact from the AI ESE program who can provide the engagement that we require to adequately plan Service Management tasks to support the GA launch.
issues.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

issues.title: Traditional go/no-go sign-off model unclear under AI ESE approach
issues.description: Under the AI ESE model, it is unclear whether there will be formal go/no-go or sign-off meetings involving service management, product engineering, and other stakeholders prior to CoCounsel Next GA. Service management expects some form of multi-team sign-off but does not currently know if or how this will occur for CoCounsel Next.
issues.impact_assessment: Without a clear go/no-go decision process, CoCounsel Next could be promoted to GA without service management's confirmation that operational guardrails and requirements are met. This undermines governance, increases the risk of unapproved changes reaching production, and may result in post-release incidents that could have been mitigated through formal readiness checks.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependent on AI ESE program leadership, service management leadership (e.g., LeBlanc, Wil), and CoCounsel Next product leadership defining and agreeing a GA sign-off process.
issues.resolution: This issue will be resolved when the list of requirements/guardrails is finalized.
issues.source_file_name: Operational Readiness — CoCounsel Next Product Launch - Scope & requirements.docx

dependencies.title: Enterprise security governance (ISRM and BISO) engagement for CoCounsel Next GA
dependencies.description: CoCounsel Next GA readiness depends on enterprise security governance teams, including ISRM and the assigned Business Information Security Officer (BISO), performing required security scanning, validating remediation of findings such as HTTP-to-HTTPS changes, and formally confirming that security non-negotiables are met before GA.

dependencies.mitigation: Include the presence of an assigned BISO and completed ISRM security scanning as explicit items in the non-negotiable operational readiness checklist. If these conditions are not met, GA readiness will be flagged Red in executive reporting and product engineering will be required to resolve the gap before proceeding.

decisions.title: Use shared Azure DevOps (ADO) project and RAG-scored epics as central tracker for CoCounsel Next operational readiness
decisions.description: The project will use a shared Azure DevOps (ADO) project and board as the central tracker for CoCounsel Next operational readiness. Epics will be organized under high-level categories such as change/release and incident management (based on the service management guardrails document). Features and tasks will be nested under these epics. Each epic will carry a RAG status to represent GA readiness along that dimension, and stakeholders will review and update these statuses in a weekly call, with the intention that all epics are Green by the end of August.
decisions.rationale: A single ADO project with structured epics, features, and tasks provides a shared, transparent view for ISRM, service management, product engineering, and platform engineering to coordinate CoCounsel Next operational readiness work and track progress toward GA. RAG statuses on epics allow quick assessment of readiness across multiple dimensions and align with executive reporting expectations.
decisions.options_considered: Continue tracking readiness items in static documents and separate backlogs per team (service management ways-of-working backlog, product engineering backlog in Linear), versus using a shared ADO project as the central connective backlog; defer structuring until after GA.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Service management visibility into CoCounsel Next communications and scale results; Consolidate CIO requirements and deliverables for CoCounsel Next operational readiness; Review service management guardrails list with CoCounsel Next product engineering leadership.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

IA Remediations will deliver a consolidated view and governance framework for CIO-owned Internal Audit remediation items so that commitments are tracked consistently, ownership is clear, and risks are surfaced before they require enterprise-level escalation. This matters because unmanaged or overdue audit findings directly increase operational, compliance, and reputational risk for the CIO organization.

So far, 2 of 19 Protecht issues (11%) are marked completed, 1 of 19 is in progress, and the remaining 16 (84%) have not started. Against plan, 5 of 19 issues (26%) have planned end dates in the past and remain open, indicating early schedule slippage and a need for structured recovery. Investigation into a few of the past due items show the work appears to be complete, but it has not been marked complete in Protecht. Further review in progress with objective to reach out to owners to step them through official Protecht sign off.

Overall status is Red, driven by multiple Internal Audit findings with past-due planned completion dates and no active remediation underway.

## Path to Green

To move toward Green, the project will prioritize a recovery plan for all past-due issues, including confirming owners, validating realistic new completion dates, requesting extensions where appropriate and monitoring progress weekly until closure. In parallel, a monthly status update will be established to share with CIO leadership on internal audit remediation findings owned by the CIO organization.

## Milestones

-   Complete closure activities and evidence for Protecht Issue ID 1016865 (Business Continuity Plan and Disaster Recovery) against its original planned end date of 06 Mar 2026.
    
-   Finalize remediation for Protecht Issue ID 1016549 (Lack of Formalized Support and Governance Structure) against its original planned end date of 31 Dec 2025.
    
-   Complete remediation for Protecht Issue ID 1016545 (Inadequate Remediation Process for License Compliance) by 31 May 2026.
    
-   Complete remediation for Protecht Issue IDs 1016488 (Governance of BU Managed Accounts) and 1028549 (Unused GCP Accounts) by 30 Jun 2026, and for Protecht Issue IDs 1011986 and 1011988 (Access Management findings) by 30 Nov 2026.
    
-   Deliver remaining OSS and EOL-related remediations for Protecht Issue IDs 1016555, 1016557, and 1016565, and transition the IA Remediations project to steady-state governance by 31 Dec 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

ICFR Transformation is redesigning the enterprise ICFR operating model by standardizing SOX processes, reviewing controls included in reporing, clarifying control ownership, and modernizing tooling for evidence, testing, and issue management. This matters because it reduces manual effort, improves audit readiness, and creates a scalable, transparent compliance framework aligned with broader modernization priorities.

Progress is in line with early-phase expectations, with governance confirmed and key scoping and tooling activities underway.

Overall status is Green, driven by early milestones tracking to plan.

## Path to Green

With status Green, the primary focus is mitigating the risk of limited stakeholder availability by booking key workshops and approvals against audit and reporting calendars and using established governance forums to secure timely decisions.

## Milestones

-   Present the current and proposed ICFR tooling landscape for Track A by 15 May 2026, and complete receipt of all Track C business process control rationalization inputs by 15 May 2026.
    
-   Complete the Track D self-assessment pilot program launch by 18 May 2026.
    
-   Walk through the updated ITGC standard controls proposal with PwC for Track C by 22 May 2026.
    
-   Present the proposed 2026 ICFR scope to the Audit Committee for Track B by 12 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete ICFR Transformation implementation and transition to steady-state ICFR governance by 31 Mar 2027.

risks.title: Tool duplication and fragmented adoption across ICFR tooling ecosystem
risks.description: Multiple tools (Protecht, ADO, SharePoint, legacy repositories, DoubleCheck) currently support overlapping ICFR activities without a clear target-state architecture, risking continued duplication and fragmented adoption even after the transformation.
risks.impact_description: If tool duplication persists, control data may remain fragmented, evidence and testing results may be inconsistent, reporting may lack integrity, and users may experience confusion over system-of-record responsibilities, undermining efficiency, governance, and audit readiness.
risks.mitigation: Define explicit system-of-record roles for each tool, design an integration architecture, select and implement a clear future-state tooling model (Protecht-led or complementary integrated), and develop a repository retirement and migration plan to consolidate control lifecycle data.

risks.title: Change fatigue among control owners participating in ICFR transformation
risks.description: Control owners are already subject to multiple initiatives and may experience change fatigue as new ICFR processes, controls, tooling, and certifications are introduced.
risks.impact_description: If change fatigue grows, control owners may disengage, reduce quality of execution, or revert to legacy practices, leading to inconsistent control performance, incomplete evidence, and failure to sustain the new operating model over time.
risks.mitigation: Simplify control patterns where possible, introduce automation and continuous monitoring to reduce manual burden, provide clear guidance and reusable templates, and sequence changes to avoid overloading control owners during critical periods.

risks.title: PwC may refuse to use internal ICFR tools for audit interactions
risks.description: The external auditor (PwC) has previously been hesitant to use internal tools, and may continue to resist adopting Protecht or related platforms for evidence requests and status updates.
risks.impact_description: If PwC does not use internal tools, audit requests may remain email-based and ad hoc, leading to poor visibility, repeated evidence capture, unclear ownership, and additional administrative effort, and may limit the value of the new ICFR workflow and reporting capabilities.
risks.mitigation: Design and implement a controlled Excel-based exchange model for PwC status updates that integrates into internal workflows, maintain disciplined internal request intake and tracking, and agree on a structured interaction model with PwC early in the program.

risks.title: Over-scoping of ICFR due to conservative posture
risks.description: The organization may continue to define an overly broad ICFR scope, including excessive controls and application coverage, due to conservative risk and audit postures, despite transformation efforts to rationalize.
risks.impact_description: If over-scoping persists, the control universe may remain larger than necessary, driving unnecessary compliance cost and complexity, extending testing and remediation cycles, and making the framework harder to sustain and defend.
risks.mitigation: Apply materiality-led scoping criteria, document risk-based rationale for inclusion/exclusion decisions, align scoping logic with external auditor expectations, and obtain CDA approval for scope changes to avoid conservative drift.

risks.title: Non-integrated access systems and third-party portals may weaken access governance
risks.description: Some systems are not integrated with SailPoint and rely on manual processes or third-party portals, creating potential gaps in provisioning, certification, and deprovisioning controls within the ICFR scope.
risks.impact_description: If non-integrated access systems remain unmanaged, there may be inconsistent or delayed deprovisioning, incomplete access reviews, and increased risk of unauthorized access that could impact ICFR control effectiveness and audit outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Define and implement compensating access controls, establish exception governance for non-integrated systems, design measurable deprovisioning controls, and incorporate these systems into the Access Governance Modernization workstream.

risks.title: Inconsistent evidence quality across ICFR controls
risks.description: Evidence supporting ICFR controls may vary in quality, completeness, and standardization, which can undermine audit readiness and increase rework during testing and external reviews.
risks.impact_description: If evidence quality remains inconsistent, auditors may challenge control effectiveness, additional testing and rework may be required, and compliance cycle time may increase, undermining one of the core objectives of the transformation.

risk_owner.name: Quality Reviewer role / Control Design Authority

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Quality Reviewer role / Track G Lead (Shannon)

risks.mitigation: Define standard evidence patterns and requirements, embed evidence standards into workflow and templates, establish a quality review function to validate sufficiency, and provide reusable job aids and training to control owners.

risks.title: Program sprawl and excessive stakeholder model may dilute focus and slow decisions
risks.description: The ICFR transformation program may expand its scope or stakeholder base excessively, resulting in complex governance, slow decision-making, and blurred accountability.
risks.impact_description: If the program becomes overly broad with too many stakeholders, decision cycles may lengthen, priorities may become unclear, and delivery of key workstreams could be delayed or under-resourced, impacting achievement of year-1 outcomes and overall objectives.
risks.mitigation: Maintain a lean core team and a small, decision-capable Control Design Authority; define clear roles and decision rights; use structured decision forums; and manage scope through formal change control to avoid uncontrolled expansion.

risks.title: Limited stakeholder availability may delay ICFR design and implementation
risks.description: Key finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders may not have sufficient time to participate in workshops, reviews, and approvals, which could slow or stall the design, validation, and implementation of the modernized ICFR operating model.
risks.impact_description: If stakeholder availability is limited, critical design decisions may be delayed, future-state processes may not reflect operational reality, implementation timelines could slip, and the project may miss ICFR reporting and audit timelines, reducing the effectiveness and credibility of the transformation.
risks.mitigation: Plan and schedule workshops well in advance, secure Sponsor and leadership support to prioritize stakeholder time, use focused, time-boxed sessions, provide asynchronous review options, and track attendance and decisions through a formal governance cadence to keep momentum even when some stakeholders are unavailable.

risks.title: Competing business priorities may reduce participation from control owners and functional leads
risks.description: Control owners and functional leaders may prioritize other initiatives or operational demands over participation in the ICFR transformation activities, reducing timely engagement in design, testing, and adoption.
risks.impact_description: If key control owners and functional leaders do not engage, the project may deliver designs that lack buy-in, suffer from delays in approvals and adoption, and face implementation issues that compromise the effectiveness and sustainability of the new ICFR framework.
risks.mitigation: Escalate prioritization needs through the Sponsor and business leadership, clearly communicate project value and regulatory importance, align project milestones with business calendars, and incorporate ICFR tasks into performance objectives for key leaders and control owners.

risks.title: Inconsistent existing documentation may increase effort required for assessment and standardization
risks.description: Current SOX and ICFR documentation is inconsistent in quality, format, and completeness, which may increase the complexity and effort needed to perform current-state assessment, gap analysis, and standardization.
risks.impact_description: If documentation inconsistency is higher than anticipated, timelines for assessment and rationalization may extend, resource requirements may increase, and some controls or processes may be misinterpreted, leading to potential gaps in the future-state framework and additional rework.
risks.mitigation: Define clear documentation standards upfront, prioritize critical processes and high-risk areas for early review, allocate dedicated resources for documentation clean-up, and use templates and guidance to drive consistency during remediation of existing materials.

risks.title: Change resistance may slow adoption of new ICFR processes, templates, and tools
risks.description: Control owners, process teams, and other stakeholders may resist changes to established ICFR processes, documentation standards, and tooling, slowing adoption of the future-state operating model.
risks.impact_description: If change resistance is significant, the project may achieve only partial adoption, leading to inconsistent execution, mixed evidence quality, and limited realization of efficiency and governance benefits, as well as potential audit challenges.
risks.mitigation: Implement structured change management and communication plans, deliver role-based training and office hours, highlight quick wins, involve stakeholders in design decisions through governance forums, and use leadership sponsorship to reinforce expectations and accountability.

risks.title: Technology dependencies or approval delays may impact implementation timing for system enablement
risks.description: If supporting technology changes, integrations, or new tools require extended architecture, security, or procurement approvals, implementation of system-enabled ICFR capabilities may be delayed.
risks.impact_description: Delays in technology decisions or approvals could push back deployment of tooling for control repository, workflow, evidence management, and reporting, resulting in prolonged reliance on fragmented legacy tools and limiting the ability to achieve the desired automation and transparency within the project timeline.
risks.mitigation: Engage enterprise architecture, security, and procurement teams early; define and agree tooling decision criteria; prepare required documentation in advance; and schedule governance checkpoints to obtain timely approvals for Protecht/ADO and related integrations.

assumptions.title: Required stakeholders will be available for ICFR transformation activities
assumptions.description: Finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders will be available to support workshops, reviews, and approvals required for the ICFR transformation program.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The program relies on cross-functional expertise and decision-making; without active stakeholder participation, design and implementation cannot proceed effectively.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Stakeholder availability is typically constrained, but given Sponsor backing and the regulatory importance of ICFR, it is reasonable to assume that critical participants will prioritize involvement once schedules and expectations are clearly communicated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If key stakeholders are repeatedly unavailable, secure delegate representation, adjust schedules, escalate to leadership for prioritization, or narrow scope to areas with engaged ownership while planning a later wave for others.
assumptions.validation_method: Track actual attendance and participation in early workshops and governance meetings; escalate gaps through Sponsor and leadership if patterns of non-participation emerge.

assumptions.title: Scope decisions and design principles will be confirmed in a timely manner
assumptions.description: Key scope decisions and design principles for the ICFR operating model will be confirmed quickly enough to maintain project momentum.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The program is structured around phases and workstreams that depend on clear, agreed scope and design principles to proceed without rework.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The creation of a Control Design Authority and explicit governance expectations for Sponsor approval are intended to streamline decision-making, making it reasonable to assume that scope and design principles will be confirmed within agreed timelines.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If decisions are delayed, escalate to the Sponsor and CDA, time-box discussions, adopt provisional decisions for pilots, or de-scope contentious elements to avoid blocking the entire program.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor timing of key governance decisions versus planned milestones; review decision log for aging items and resolution timelines.

assumptions.title: Existing SOX documentation and process information will be accessible for review
assumptions.description: Existing SOX documentation, testing artifacts, and process information will be available and accessible to the project team for assessment and rationalization.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current-state assessment and gap analysis depend on access to existing control documentation and testing records across tools and repositories.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current ICFR and SOX operations rely on these documents, indicating that they exist and are used; the main risk is access permissions and completeness, but a high level of availability is expected.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If documentation is missing or inaccessible, engage system owners to restore or grant access, prioritize recreation for high-risk areas, and adjust timelines to allow for targeted documentation reconstruction.
assumptions.validation_method: Attempt access to key repositories and sample documents early; confirm permissions and completeness with document owners and audit teams.

assumptions.title: Funding and resourcing for approved scope will be made available
assumptions.description: Budget and human resources needed to execute the approved ICFR transformation scope will be provided by the organization.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project has been chartered as a strategic initiative, implying alignment to funding and resourcing plans.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Regulatory and governance importance of ICFR modernization increases the likelihood of funding approval, but competing enterprise priorities could still impact allocations, so confidence is moderate rather than absolute.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If full funding is not secured, prioritize highest risk and value workstreams, phase implementation over longer timelines, or seek additional funding through governance channels.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm allocated budget and headcount against the approved charter; review funding approvals and staffing assignments during mobilization.

assumptions.title: Sponsor and business leadership will actively support adoption and decision-making
assumptions.description: The Sponsor and business leadership will provide active support for adoption of new processes and tools and will participate in timely decision-making throughout the project.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Effective transformation requires visible leadership support to drive adoption, resolve conflicts, and prioritize ICFR work among competing initiatives.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Formal Sponsor approval and alignment with broader modernization and governance priorities indicate strong leadership interest, making ongoing support reasonably likely.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If leadership engagement declines, escalate through governance forums, highlight regulatory and risk implications, and adjust communications to better align with leadership needs and priorities.
assumptions.validation_method: Observe Sponsor and leadership participation in steering meetings, approvals, and communications; track escalations and their resolution times.

assumptions.title: Control universe can be reduced from ~751 to approximately 600 controls
assumptions.description: It is feasible to rationalize the current control universe of approximately 751 controls to a more focused set of around 600 controls without compromising ICFR effectiveness.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Preliminary analysis indicates over-scoping and overly granular or duplicative controls, suggesting rationalization opportunities.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Experience in similar programs often reveals rationalization opportunities; however, constraints from auditors or regulatory interpretations may limit the extent of reduction, so confidence is moderate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the control universe cannot be reduced as much as planned, focus on simplifying execution, automating key controls, and improving evidence quality to reduce operational burden without significant reduction in control count.
assumptions.validation_method: Perform detailed control rationalization analysis (Track C), including mapping to risks and processes, and review proposed reductions with CDA and external auditors.

validation_owner.name: Track C Leads (Veronica G for business processes, Mark Brady for ITGC)

assumptions.title: Application scope can be reduced through materiality-led scoping
assumptions.description: The in-scope application population for ICFR can be reduced by applying materiality and risk-based scoping criteria.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current discussions and observations suggest that application scope may extend beyond what is necessary for material financial reporting risks.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Preliminary discussions indicate that some applications are conservatively included; however, external auditor alignment is required to confirm reductions, leading to moderate confidence.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If application scope cannot be materially reduced, focus on standardizing and automating controls across the existing application set and implement more efficient testing and evidence processes to offset the complexity.
assumptions.validation_method: Conduct a formal ICFR scoping and risk assessment (Track B) based on financial statement line items, materiality thresholds, and system dependencies, and validate with external auditors.

assumptions.title: Selected controls can be shifted from per-application to domain/platform or process-level design
assumptions.description: It will be possible to redesign selected controls from a per-application or per-product basis to domain, platform, or process-level controls.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current-state controls show app-centric design that may not be necessary when risks can be managed at higher levels, reducing duplication.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The nature of many ITGCs and process controls lends itself to higher-level design, but technical and organizational constraints, as well as auditor expectations, will influence feasibility, hence moderate confidence.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If shifting controls proves infeasible in some areas, maintain necessary application-level controls while focusing on standardization and automation to limit incremental overhead.
assumptions.validation_method: Identify candidate controls during Track C rationalization, design higher-level controls, and review with CDA, process owners, and auditors to confirm acceptability.

validation_owner.name: Track C Leads (Veronica G and Mark Brady)

objectives.description: Program PMO: Govern delivery across all seven ICFR transformation tracks, including milestones, RAID (risks, actions, issues, decisions), and consolidated reporting under Steering Committee oversight.

Track A – Platform & Tooling: Define the target-state ICFR tooling architecture and govern all platform decisions, including the Protecht vs. ADO model, the auditor request workflow, and the 360° reporting layer.

Track B – ICFR Scoping & Risk Assessment: Refresh the enterprise ICFR compliance scope using materiality, business process analysis, and system dependency mapping, and align the resulting scope posture with PwC.

Track C – Control Rationalization: Reduce and rationalize the ICFR control universe from ~751 controls to a defensible, risk-based set and shift from per-application to domain and platform-level control design patterns.

Track D – Ownership & Certification: Define clear accountability for every ICFR control—from Design Authority through to Certifier—and implement a formalized quarterly certification cycle in Protecht.

Track E – Access Governance: Strengthen access governance across SailPoint-integrated and non-integrated systems, including defined exception handling for third-party portals and a measurable governance cadence.

Track F – Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM): Build a prioritized CCM capability by identifying practical, data-supported automation use cases and evaluating the right platform to scale monitoring beyond manual testing.

Track G – Change Management & Adoption: Ensure ICFR transformation changes in process and tooling are effectively adopted and sustained through targeted communications, role-based training, and adoption measurement.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The HIPAA Compliance Program is delivering a centralized, formal compliance framework for Thomson Reuters products and services that handle protected health information, including PHI inventories, updated policies, and HIPAA-aligned controls. This matters because it reduces regulatory, contractual, and reputational risk while enabling sustainable support for HIPAA-related customer commitments.

Of 9 defined milestones, 1 is complete, 6 are in progress, and 2 are planned, all currently showing zero schedule variance against their target dates. Near-term focus is on completing CoCounsel, SIU Professional Services, CLEAR, and Contract Express assessments.

Overall status is Green, driven by key product assessments and remediation workstreams tracking to their current schedules with no reported timing slippage.

## Path to Green

To keep the program Green, the team is using the SteerCo and centralized Risk and Privacy governance to manage resource-capacity risks and to enforce product-level remediation timelines for SIU Professional Services and Legal Tracker through 31 Dec 2026.

## Milestones

-   Complete HighQ HIPAA remediation, SIU Professional Services “most gaps remediated,” and CLEAR HIPAA assessment for CLEAR, CLEAR Batch, and CLEAR Investigate by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete the CoCounsel FedRamp and v.2 Commercial HIPAA assessment by 29 May 2026.
    
-   Complete SIU Professional Services HIPAA remediation for all gaps and deliver Legal Tracker HIPAA remediation for the year-end deadline by 31 Dec 2026, and update HIPAA breach notification requirements in legal notification playbooks by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete deep-dive data handling assessments for additional Professional Services groups between 06 Jul 2026 and 30 Sep 2026, and close the overall HIPAA Compliance Program by 31 Dec 2027.

risks.title: Inadequate or outdated HIPAA policies, BAAs, training, and breach notification processes

risks.impact_description: If outdated or incomplete policies, contract templates, training, or breach notification procedures remain in use, employees and customers may receive inconsistent or incorrect guidance. This could lead to misaligned BAAs, inadequate training coverage, or mishandled breach/disclosure events, resulting in compliance gaps or adverse regulatory findings.

raised_by.name: HIPAA Compliance Program Scope document and April 23, 2026 Status Report

risks.title: Competing priorities may limit product and operational teams’ capacity for HIPAA assessment and remediation
risks.description: Product and operational teams may have limited bandwidth due to competing priorities, which could constrain their ability to participate in HIPAA assessments, scope validation, and remediation work.
risks.impact_description: If teams cannot allocate sufficient time and resources to HIPAA activities, assessments and remediation may be delayed or incomplete. mitigation_plan_owner.name: Program Manager for HIPAA Compliance Program

risks.title: Variability in product architectures and data flows may prevent a single uniform HIPAA solution
risks.description: Products and services differ in architectures, data flows, and contractual commitments, which may make it difficult to implement a single standardized HIPAA compliance solution across all in-scope areas.
risks.impact_description: If a one-size-fits-all approach is pursued but proves infeasible, some products may end up with misaligned or ineffective controls. This variability could lead to uneven compliance levels, increased complexity in monitoring and audits, and potential gaps where specific product risks are not adequately addressed.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: R&C and Privacy in coordination with Product/Engineering

risks.mitigation: Develop a business-aligned control framework that distinguishes between enterprise-level controls and product-specific requirements. risks.title: Phased implementation may extend beyond initial project window
risks.description: The need for phased implementation across multiple products and services means that full HIPAA compliance maturity may require stages beyond the initial project timeline (2025-07-07 to 2027-12-31).
risks.impact_description: If the program cannot achieve full maturity within the initial project window, some products may remain partially compliant, with incomplete remediation or monitoring. This could necessitate extended funding, increase program management complexity, and leave residual compliance and operational risks unaddressed for a longer period.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Program Manager for HIPAA Compliance Program

risks.mitigation: Plan and communicate a phased roadmap that clearly identifies which capabilities and products will be addressed in each stage, including post-project activities. Secure long-term sponsorship and funding for ongoing compliance work, and embed HIPAA guidance into the broader product compliance framework to support ongoing scalability.

risks.title: Unclear decisions on signing BAAs/BASAs during discovery and remediation phases

raised_by.name: HIPAA Compliance Program Scope document (Critical Decisions sections)

risks.mitigation: Use the SteerCo to define and approve a clear decision framework for BAAs/BASAs, including conditions under which they can be signed during discovery or remediation, and any time limits. Communicate this guidance to Sales, Commercial Excellence, and Customer Trust teams as part of the broader awareness campaign.
