assumptions.title: 65% of legacy SSO connections can be migrated to CIAM by end of 2026 by de-emphasizing complex OnePass customers and compensating with other products
assumptions.description: The program is proceeding under the assumption that the 65% migration target for 2026 can still be achieved even if some large/complex OnePass customers (e.g., GLF/MLF) are not fully migrated by year-end, by accelerating migrations in other products and segments such as SafeSend, OneSource, and other legal products. The idea is that these products may be able to move faster and partially compensate for delayed or incomplete OnePass migrations, potentially resulting in a mix where OnePass is not 100% complete but overall CIAM migration still reaches approximately 65%.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Harvarinder stated he still has confidence that 65% can be achieved, but not including full OnePass completion, and suggested compensating by pushing more migrations through other products (e.g., SafeSend with ~300 connections, OneSource, other products) that may be more willing to move faster based on different communication approaches.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current leadership sentiment acknowledges that the original plan likely overestimated customer response rates and did not fully account for non-responsive customers. However, there is some evidence that other products (e.g., SafeSend, OneSource) may be easier to move and a new feature is expected to unlock faster partial migrations for legal products starting in Q3. Because these levers are not yet fully validated and rely on customer behavior, confidence is moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If analysis in late May and July shows that the 65% target cannot be met even with compensating migrations:
- Prepare a revised set of OKRs/metrics for executive approval, potentially reducing the 2026 percentage, decoupling OnePass completion from the 65% metric, or shifting some scope into 2027.
- Further re-sequence segments, focusing on highest-priority customers (e.g., GLF/MLF and Co Counsel Next candidates) even if overall percentage remains lower.
- Consider additional measures to improve customer engagement (e.g., stronger end-of-life enforcement, more aggressive escalation, or alternative outreach channels) to raise migration throughput.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) A 1–2 week projection exercise across segments and products to quantify realistic 2026 migration volumes.
2) A follow-up re-evaluation in mid-July 2026 after the new "partial migration" feature is available and early adoption data is observed.
3) Comparison of actual monthly migration throughput versus the projections to confirm whether compensating migrations are materializing.
assumptions.source_file_name: Sync on CIAM Migration timeline and metrics.docx

assumptions.title: Customer outreach volume can scale to approximately 400–600 vetted migration emails per month
assumptions.description: Planning assumptions for the SSO Migration program currently presuppose that the team can ramp and sustain a significantly higher volume of vetted customer communications, reaching roughly 350–400 emails per month in the near term and 500–600 per month in subsequent months, as data processes and account ownership identification improve.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Harvarinder and Eduardo noted that March outreach volume was around 100 emails, April around 200+, and that in the last week alone they sent approximately 80–90 emails. They discussed a trajectory where May might reach ~400 emails, June ~500, and subsequent months 500–600, assuming vetting and data processes are streamlined.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The team is already trending upward from ~100 to 200+ emails per month and has recently sent ~80–90 emails in a single week, indicating that a few hundred emails per month are feasible. However, vetting bottlenecks (e.g., identifying correct CSM/Account Specialist contacts across multiple systems) and limited data access still constrain growth, so sustained 500–600 emails per month is plausible but not yet proven.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If outreach volume cannot reach or sustain 400–600 vetted emails per month:
- Prioritize outreach to highest-impact segments and customers (e.g., GLF/MLF, Co Counsel Next prospects, upcoming migration waves) rather than broad coverage.
- Seek additional data analysis and operations support to increase vetting throughput (e.g., temporary staffing, automation, better dashboards).
- Explore alternative outreach and escalation mechanisms (e.g., leveraging sales/CSM campaigns, webinars, or account reviews) that do not rely solely on direct emails.
- Re-calculate migration throughput and adjust 2026 targets accordingly, escalating to leadership if capacity remains a hard constraint.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor monthly counts of vetted initial and follow-up outreach emails sent and compare them against the 400–600 per month target; correlate outreach volume with available vetted customer lists and vetting throughput to determine whether capacity and processes can sustain the planned scale.
assumptions.source_file_name: Sync on CIAM Migration timeline and metrics.docx

assumptions.title: Co Counsel Next enablement can proceed without requiring CIAM migration as a strict prerequisite for existing Co Counsel Legal customers
assumptions.description: The CIAM/SSO migration and Co Counsel Next product enablement plans are being discussed under the assumption that existing Co Counsel Legal customers can begin using Co Counsel Next without first being migrated to CIAM. The rationale is that these customers already have access and can be given a feature flag to enable Co Counsel Next, avoiding additional friction and delays from making CIAM migration a prerequisite.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Harvarinder explained that existing Co Counsel Legal customers already have access and that Co Counsel Next is effectively a new feature/skin enabled via a feature flag. Requiring CIAM migration as a prerequisite for these customers may introduce significant data clean-up and friction, potentially slowing time to market. There is active discussion with leadership (e.g., Marc) about whether CIAM should remain a prerequisite for these customers.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The current design indicates that Co Counsel Next can be enabled as a feature within the existing product, and leadership believes that many customers already have access with their current registration keys. However, there are concerns about customer friction, data clean-up, and perception of past access issues. Until more evidence is gathered, confidence remains moderate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If it is determined that CIAM migration must be a prerequisite for Co Counsel Next for existing Co Counsel Legal customers:
- Re-sequence the CIAM migration plan to prioritize co-counsel-related customers ahead of other segments.
- Coordinate carefully with Co Counsel Next go-to-market plans to minimize delays and communicate clearly with affected customers.
- Provide additional resources for data clean-up and migration support for these customers to shorten the prerequisite migration phase.
- Reassess CIAM migration capacity and timelines to ensure that prioritizing these customers does not critically undermine overall migration targets.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing product and architecture review between CIAM leadership and Co Counsel Next product leadership (including Marc and Hassan) to determine whether enabling Co Counsel Next without CIAM introduces unacceptable risk or experience issues; evaluation of early customer experiences and support incidents for customers enabled on Co Counsel Next without prior CIAM migration.

issues.title: Low Customer Response Rate to SSO Migration Outreach
issues.description:
Customer response to the SSO migration outreach remains significantly below the level required to support the planned migration from the legacy IDP to TR Account (CIAM). The project team is sending migration communications in waves to customers across approximately 5,500 SSO connections, requesting their engagement and action to migrate.

To date, response rates remain below 30%. Most recently, in last week's outreach wave, 96 customer emails were sent and only 13 responses were received, representing a response rate of approximately 13.5%.
issues.impact_assessment: If the response rate does not improve, the project may not be able to migrate 65% of SSO connections by Dec 30, 2026. This could result in schedule slippage, increased operational risk, and a need for stronger escalation or alternative migration enforcement mechanisms.
issues.resolution:
To address the low customer response rate, the project team is implementing several actions to increase customer engagement and create a stronger escalation path:

Update customer communication templates:
Revise the migration email template to include a clear statement regarding the planned end-of-life support for the legacy IDPs, reinforcing the urgency for customers to migrate to TR Account (CIAM).

Increase data validation capacity:
Add additional resources to support customer data validation activities, enabling the team to identify and tag more customers as ready for migration outreach.

Strengthen escalation process:
Modify the migration follow-up process so that if no customer response is received within 15 days of the initial email, the issue will be escalated to the relevant Account Specialist or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for direct customer follow-up.

These actions are expected to improve customer response rates, increase the number of customers actively engaged in the migration process, and reduce the risk of delays to the overall SSO migration timeline.

issues.title: Difficulty Identifying Account Specialist / CSM Ownership for Customer Accounts
issues.description:
The project team is facing significant challenges identifying the appropriate Account Specialist (ASM) or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for each customer account requiring SSO migration follow-up and escalation.

The required account ownership information is spread across multiple systems and is not aggregated or centralized. Many of these systems support only specific customer segments, such as Corporates, Legal, and Tax, or sometimes only a single product area, such as Legal Tracker. As a result, the team is unable to easily determine the correct ASM or CSM contact for each account.

This has created a highly manual and time-consuming process, requiring the team to review accounts one by one and coordinate with multiple teams and data analysis resources to locate the correct account owner.
issues.impact_assessment:
The lack of centralized ASM/CSM ownership data is slowing down the escalation process for non-responsive customers and may delay customer engagement, migration scheduling, and overall execution of the SSO migration from the legacy IDP to TR Account (CIAM).

It also increases the operational burden on the project team and supporting teams, creating inefficiencies and risk of inconsistent or delayed follow-up.
issues.resolution:
To address this issue, the project team recommends the following actions:

Engage data owners and business segment teams:
Partner with representatives from Corporates, Legal, Tax, and product-specific teams to identify the authoritative sources for ASM/CSM ownership data.

Create a consolidated account ownership tracker:
Build a centralized working file or dashboard that aggregates ASM/CSM information from available systems and maps each customer account to the appropriate owner.

Assign data analysis support:
Secure dedicated support from data analysis experts to help extract, reconcile, and validate account ownership data across the different systems.

Define a repeatable lookup process:
Establish a standard process for identifying ASM/CSM ownership for each account, including clear escalation paths when ownership is missing, outdated, or conflicting.

Prioritize high-risk / non-responsive customers:
Focus initial ownership mapping efforts on customers who have not responded to migration communications or who are part of upcoming migration waves.

Identify long-term data governance needs:
Escalate the lack of centralized account ownership data as a broader operational gap and recommend a long-term solution for maintaining a single, reliable source of account ownership information.

decisions.title: Conduct two-stage reevaluation of 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion
decisions.description: The team will conduct a two-stage reevaluation of the 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion goal. First, a 1–2 week exercise (by late May 2026) will produce realistic projections based on current response data, segment-by-segment analysis, and reprioritization of products (including potential compensation from Safesend, OneSource and other products if large/complex OnePass customers lag). latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Enterprise Identity and Entitlement is delivering a shared identity and fine-grained entitlement model for CoCounsel Next, including ethical wall enforcement, CIAM‑native identity, and FGA-based authorization, while preserving existing commercial infrastructure in Phase 1. This enables safer, faster customer onboarding and consistent cross-product access needed for TR’s AI-driven product strategy.

To date, 1 of 4 defined milestones is complete, with the current-state assessment delivered on plan by 08 May 2026. Post-login requirements are still in progress 5 Jun 2026

Overall status is AMBER, driven by unresolved architectural decisions and incomplete requirements that block reliable estimation and commitment for the 28 Aug 2026 GA milestone.

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to close the overdue architectural-decision risk (target closure 22 May 2026) and GA-planning risk (target closure 05 Jun 2026) by securing owners, driving decisions on CIAM/FGA/admin-tool design, and completing the full requirements set including pre-login and agentic AI flows. In parallel, the team must complete the updated architecture diagram and enterprise data model by their target closure dates of 05 Jun 2026 so engineering can estimate and sequence work for pilots and GA with confidence.

## Milestones

-   Complete current state assessment process for CoCounsel Next by 08 May 2026.
    
-   Finish gathering post-login requirements for CoCounsel Next by 2026-06-05.
    
-   Enable CoCounsel Next pilots for the defined customer cohort by 31 Jul 2026.
    
-   Enable CoCounsel Next General Availability for all US customers by 28 Aug 2026.
    
-   Complete Enterprise Identity and Entitlement Phase 1 and close the project by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: GA planning blocked: August timeline at risk, crawl scope undefined, requirements incomplete
risks.description: General availability planning for August is blocked because engineering cannot estimate or commit without (1) a clearly defined October crawl scope and (2) complete tiered requirements that cover pre-login flows, commercial touchpoints, and agentic AI. These inputs are missing, leaving uncertainty in scope and effort.
risks.impact_description: If crawl scope and full requirements remain undefined, engineering will be unable to provide reliable estimates or commitments. This may delay the August GA date, cause scope gaps, and increase the likelihood of rework or missed functionality, particularly in pre-login, commercial, and agentic AI areas.
risks.mitigation: Product team to provide clear requirements .Patrick Wagstrom produces a complete requirements document, including pre-login, commercial touchpoints, and agentic AI,

risks.title: Ethical walls — agentic AI poses breach risk if permissions not enforced correctly
risks.description: Agentic AI can traverse large volumes of content and generate derived artefacts that may unintentionally combine restricted sources. Ethical walls must be enforced based on the content accessed during generation, not just on the appearance of the output. Derived content must inherit permissions from its sources, and admin privileges must not grant agents broader content access.
risks.impact_description: If ethical wall enforcement is not correctly designed and implemented, agents may access or combine restricted content, potentially breaching client confidentiality and legal or regulatory constraints. This could cause serious compliance incidents, reputational damage, and require costly remediation or rollback of AI capabilities.
risks.mitigation: Design an ethical wall enforcement model covering: file-level vs workspace-level inheritance, integration with DMS/intake tools such as iManage and Intapp Walls, and clear scoping of agent identity and permissions so that derived content inherits source permissions and admin privileges do not expand agent content access.

risks.title: Multiple blocking architectural decisions unresolved (identity, admin tool, FGA, CIAM)
risks.description: Four interdependent architectural decisions remain unresolved and are blocking the start of build: (1) where the admin tool will be hosted, (2) how CIAM enforcement will operate, (3) which user identity (Prism GUID vs EUID) will be used by Auth0 FGA, and (4) how the FGA store will be structured. Until these are decided, downstream design and implementation cannot progress.
risks.impact_description: If these architectural decisions are not resolved quickly, the engineering team cannot start build work. This will delay delivery of the GA scope, compress testing timelines, and may force rushed or suboptimal architecture choices that increase technical debt and rework later.
risks.mitigation: Escalate to secure agreement and assignment of the correct owners for each architectural block/module (admin tool placement, CIAM enforcement model, FGA identity, and FGA store structure) and drive decisions to unblock build.

milestones.name: Post-login Requirements for CoCo Next gathered

risks.title: Admin portal is the largest GA body of work — no owner, no backlog, no funding
risks.description: The admin entitlement portal has been identified as the largest single body of work required for GA, but it currently has no confirmed owning team, no committed backlog, and no allocated funding. Building this as a net-new capability for the August release is not feasible without an immediate decision on ownership and resourcing.
risks.impact_description: If an owning team, backlog, and funding are not established promptly, the admin portal will not be delivered in time for GA. This will leave entitlements administration incomplete, impact operational readiness, and may delay GA or require manual workarounds that are risky and hard to scale.
risks.mitigation: Escalate through a core group session in the week commencing 28 April to decide admin tool placement and assign an owning team. Anthony Rokis must make the decision. No build will start until ownership is confirmed, ensuring accountability and resourcing.

assumptions.title: SAP WRP = source of truth for entitlement/billing. Auth0 FGA = runtime authorization layer only
assumptions.description: For GA, SAP WRP remains the system of record for entitlements and billing. Auth0 FGA is used only as a runtime authorization layer via a dual-write model, where admin actions update both SAP and FGA in parallel. Auth0 FGA is not intended to replace SAP as the master system.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Existing SAP WRP processes and data structures already support entitlements and billing, and replacing them before GA would be too risky and complex.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The project relies on established SAP WRP capabilities for entitlements and billing, with Auth0 FGA introduced only as a runtime evaluation engine. This lowers implementation risk by avoiding wholesale replacement of SAP before GA while enabling fine-grained authorization via a dual-write pattern.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If SAP WRP cannot be the source of truth or dual-write proves unworkable, define an alternative master (e.g., a dedicated entitlement store) and adjust integration patterns, accepting schedule or scope changes as needed.
assumptions.validation_method: Communicate and confirm this constraint with all affected teams and validate the dual-write implementation approach with the SAP/WRP team.

assumptions.title: Phase 1 only in scope for GA — minimum change, existing infrastructure preserved
assumptions.description: For GA, only Phase 1 is in scope: enabling CoCounsel Next, obfuscating registration keys, and implementing EUID-linked FGA. Subsequent phases (2A, 2B, and 3), which include billing evolution and full registration key retirement, are explicitly deferred beyond GA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Limiting GA to Phase 1 reduces risk and keeps changes to a manageable level, allowing delivery on the August timeline while preserving existing infrastructure.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The GA plan is structured around a phased delivery where Phase 1 provides the minimum necessary capability. Leadership has already aligned on this approach, making it a realistic and enforceable constraint if communicated effectively.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If pressure mounts to include Phase 2/3 items, de-scope or defer non-essential work, renegotiate timelines, or secure additional resources to avoid undermining GA quality.
assumptions.validation_method: Communicate the Phase 1 scope boundary to all workstreams and monitor plans and backlogs to ensure Phase 2/3 items are not added to GA.

assumptions.title: CoCounsel owns FGA. Commercial/platform teams own system integrations
assumptions.description: The CoCounsel product team is assumed to own the fine-grained authorization (FGA) layer itself, while commercial and platform teams (SAP, TFMS, Prism, Order Capture) own their respective system integrations with FGA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Clear ownership boundaries reduce overlap, confusion, and duplicated authorization logic across teams.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Assigning FGA ownership to the product that directly uses it (CoCounsel) and delegating integration responsibilities to system owners is a standard pattern that fits existing organizational structures, making the assumption realistic.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ownership disputes arise or responsibilities are unclear, escalate to program leadership to clarify ownership and update documentation and backlogs accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Document ownership boundaries and validate them with all involved teams to ensure shared understanding.

assumptions.title: CIAM-native is the target. Prism GUID = interim FGA identity until CIAM migration completes
assumptions.description: The long-term target is CIAM-native identity using EUID for FGA. Until the OnePass-to-CIAM migration completes (by end of 2026), Prism GUID will be used as the interim identifier for FGA. The current beta OnePass login is a temporary solution.
assumptions.rationale_basis: CIAM is the strategic identity platform, but migration is in progress, requiring an interim identity approach for FGA.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The assumption balances strategic direction (CIAM/EUID) with current technical realities (Prism GUID and OnePass), allowing FGA to be implemented now while remaining compatible with the future identity model.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If CIAM migration is delayed or Prism GUID proves unsuitable, extend the interim model, introduce additional mapping layers, or adjust timelines for CIAM-native rollout.
assumptions.validation_method: Design FGA with a clear migration path to EUID and confirm the Prism GUID interim model with Vassil and identity architecture teams.

assumptions.title: TFMS = user-to-customer master. Fine-grained access control is product-side, not commercial
assumptions.description: CIAM is assumed to be the identity master (EUID). TFMS is assumed to be the master for user-to-customer entitlement/assignment for access-based products. Content sets, folders, and workspaces are assumed to be handled by product-side logic after login, not by commercial systems.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Separating identity, commercial entitlements, and product-level content control clarifies responsibilities and reduces complexity in integration design.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Assigning TFMS to manage user-to-customer entitlements while leaving fine-grained content control to products leverages existing system strengths and aligns with known responsibilities, making this a reasonable and efficient assumption.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If TFMS cannot reliably act as the user-to-customer master, identify an alternative system or data store and adjust provisioning flows and data models accordingly, accepting potential schedule impact.
assumptions.validation_method: Document this split clearly in data flow and sequence diagrams and validate it with Dheeraj and relevant architecture stakeholders.

issues.title: Architecture diagram outdated for entitlements program
issues.description: The current architecture reference is an outdated informal diagram by Rick Dauk that does not reflect Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, or the proposed admin tool. All design discussions rely on this inaccurate baseline.
issues.impact_assessment: Using an inaccurate architecture baseline for discussions risks misaligned design decisions, incorrect integration assumptions, and rework across Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, and the admin tool. Integration and implementation planning is compromised until an authoritative diagram exists.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Architecture sessions and downstream design decisions for entitlements, including integrations between CIAM, SAP, WRP, and the admin portal.
issues.resolution: Produce an updated authoritative architecture diagram that incorporates Auth0 FGA, CIAM, SAP WRP dual-write, and the proposed admin tool, and present it at the next architecture session.

issues.title: Enterprise data model for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs unresolved
issues.description: The relationships between organization ID, subscription ID, and user ID across CIAM, Prism, SAP, and TFMS are not documented, and ownership of the future enterprise subscription store is unclear. This gap blocks final architecture and engineering estimation.
issues.impact_assessment: Without a defined data model and ownership for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs, the final architecture cannot be completed and engineering cannot provide reliable estimates, risking delays and misaligned implementations.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Final architecture decisions, engineering estimation, CIAM, Prism, SAP, TFMS, and enterprise subscription store design.
issues.resolution: Have CIAM and Enterprise Data teams define and document the data model for organization, tenant, subscription, and user IDs across CIAM, Prism, SAP, and TFMS, and clarify ownership of the enterprise subscription store by coordinating with enterprise data architects.

## Executive Summary

Enterprise AI is delivering shared AI platforms and solutions, including the LLM Orchestrator, to help product teams adopt AI at scale with consistent security, performance, and governance while reducing time-to-market and operational cost. The program underpins Thomson Reuters’ enterprise AI strategy by standardizing access to LLMs, observability, and legal-domain models across clouds and geographies.

To date, three foundational milestones are complete (Agentic AI training on 10 Dec 2025, Web Grounding Tool onboarding on 09 Mar 2026, and Braintrust observability onboarding on 28 Apr 2026), and the Overall Project Completion tracker reports 30% of project targets achieved in 2026. LLM Orchestrator adoption has reached 88% token consumption versus the 2026 target of 90%, with 22 product teams onboarded and Thomson Model v0.3 Large live in two Reuters services.

Overall status is Green, driven by strong progress on LLM Orchestrator adoption that is within 2 percentage points of the 90% 2026 enterprise consumption target.

## Path to Green

The top risk is FedRAMP certification delay due to access approvals, which is being mitigated through rigorous follow-up and escalation with approving teams to meet the current mitigation due date of 28 May 2026 and avoid impact to the 30 Jul 2026 FedRAMP deployment milestone.

## Milestones

- Complete risk mitigation activities for FedRAMP access approvals by 28 May 2026.  
- Deploy and certify the LLM Orchestrator in the AWS GovCloud production environment for FedRAMP workloads by 30 Jul 2026.  
- Operationalize the Themis Legal LLM inferencing platform under Platform Engineering ownership by 16 Dec 2026.  
- Achieve 90% enterprise LLM token consumption via the LLM Orchestrator and complete LLM Orchestrator onboarding and scale-up activities by 23 Dec 2026.  
- Complete Overall Project Completion objectives and close the Enterprise AI program by 30 Dec 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Scope**: Optimize TR Estate is driving measurable cloud cost efficiency across Thomson Reuters by eliminating waste, accelerating ARM64 migration, and optimizing Datadog spend. The initiative targets $3.5M in in-year savings for 2026, with a mandate to deliver financial material outcomes that directly reduce CIO infrastructure costs and improve cloud ROI.

**Finance-Defined CIO Savings Target — AMBER** $579K of the $3.5M 2026 CIO savings target realized to date, with $1.1M identified as potential savings, leaving a ~$2.4M gap. Status is AMBER driven by the shortfall between the current pipeline and the Finance-defined target. A full historical view of what has been done, gaps, and what is achievable is being prepared, with a leadership narrative and decision options (formal re-baselining, offsetting via product engineering over-delivery, or accepting the variance) due ahead of May 28. LLM savings tracking discussions are ongoing, with a proposal to consolidate all AI/LLM savings on the CIO tracker alongside the AI/LLM budget.

-   Systemic Waste Elimination – Daily run activities ongoing with AWARE process (orphan and email engagements) running under this milestone. ~$200K+ savings expected this quarter.
    
-   ARM64 Adoption: Monthly reporting established and stable. Key metric — percentage of workloads on ARM — reported at month-end. Graviton items moving to individual CIO trackers for visibility. Database-space Graviton (legacy environments) tracked as a separate initiative from app codebase conversion.
    

**R1 — Risk:** Current identified opportunities fall below the $3.5M savings target. **Mitigation**: Working with FinOps and Finance to evaluate current challenge LE and prioritizing Platform Engineering red lever opportunity for increased in year savings; driving deep dives with CIO teams to discuss and prioritize their forecast projects. Reviewing potential to accelerate the AWS Nat Gateway Red Lever opportunity timeline to capture savings in 2026 (Annual in year savings $1.25M)

**Path to Green**

Evaluations Prioritized as follows: (a) accelerating closure of all open savings opportunities with firm dates and named owners; (b) scheduling deep dives with CIO application teams to evaluate current cloud spend prioritizing high forecast projections; c) prioritizing AWS Nat Gateway to Check Point Cloud Guard to determine risks and business trade offs. 

 **Next Steps**

-   Finance Defined Savings Target for CIO: Prioritize discussions within CIO to evaluate current cloud spend to define business value and potential trade offs
    
-   Data Cost Efficiencies status assessment and ADO closure — May 30
    
-   Datadog Workshop Reporting: Add monthly Datadog reporting showing completions in ADO — May onwards
    
-   ARM64 adoption: Publish ARM64 / Graviton workload percentage — end of May
    
-   Resolve LLM savings tracking approach; confirm all AI/LLM savings captured on CIO tracker – Ongoing

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Time Base Integration is migrating all Time Base workloads from on‑premises and BU-owned cloud into TR-owned cloud accounts so the business can continue operating after the physical office closure and within TR’s standard platforms. The end state is a fully TR-governed cloud footprint for Time Base applications, data, and supporting tools, including CI/CD and work management.

To date, 6 of 18 defined milestones are complete, including Phase 1 migration from on‑premises to Time Base AWS and onboarding the BU AWS account into the TR AWS Organization, while Jira to Azure DevOps and DevOps repository migrations are also finished. Current work focuses on finalising non‑prod architecture, CI/CD pipeline planning and implementation, and setting up the TR Google Cloud account, all of which are tracking to planned May and June 2026 dates.

Overall status is Green, driven by on-schedule completion of Phase 1 migration and BU AWS account onboarding, with remaining non‑prod and CI/CD activities progressing against the 2026 plan.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is on the open resource availability risk at Time Base by closely tracking actions and slippage in weekly status calls and sequencing migration tasks to limit critical-path dependencies on a single SME.

## Milestones

- Complete Non‑Prod Environment Foundation and TR Google Cloud account setup for calendar by 31 May 2026.  
- Finish DevOps pipeline discovery and planning and DevOps Pipelines Migration and Standardization planning by 15 Jun 2026.  
- Start TR Cloud non‑prod environment build on 01 Jul 2026.  
- Initiate PROD preparation and TR PROD infrastructure build by 01 Sep 2026.  
- Execute production cutover and complete BU account closure, ending the program, by 31 Dec 2026.

issues.description:
Time Base has significant resource constraints, with one individual managing all tasks from the Time Base side, including coordination, alignment, and execution of migration activities.

Having a single individual managing all tasks from the Time Base side increases the risk of delays, bottlenecks, and burnout, and reduces the resilience of the project.
Project tasks may be deprioritized in favour of BAU commitments.
Risk of delays in milestones and deliverables due to limited bandwidth.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Scope:** Migrate all 60 legacy servers supporting the UFile Online Application in Montreal Data Center, as they will soon be out of vendor support.

**Change in Migration Strategy: AMS Cloud --- Justification:** On April 8, 2026, Colo Exit Management and TAP Leadership confirmed a revised migration strategy for the UFile Online Application, currently in the Montreal Data Center. The application will now migrate to AMS Cloud instead of Azure, supporting service continuity and modernization.

 **Key Reasons for strategy shift: (1)** Thomson Reuters Platform Engineering team's AMS migration expertise enables an immediate start. (2) AMS Cloud simplifies the transition, avoiding the need for rapid adaptation to new cloud-native tools by business and operations teams.

1.  **Discovery Phase (ETA: May 13):** Remaining task involves CSA organizing and documenting firewall information from Ramon. This includes aligning data with specific services in network segments and ensuring IP address lists are properly mapped.
    
2.  **Migration Architecture & Planning (ETA: May 31):** CSA has completed the first draft of the architecture diagram and plans to review it with the project team during the weekly call. Focus areas includes the architecture diagram (network topology, IAM roles, IIS permissions, database migrations, and connected environments) necessary for PCI DSS compliance review
    

 **Important Project Dependencies/ Blockers:**

-   **Infrastructure Build Timeline:** The start date for Implementation Build Work (June 2) will be delayed due to the AMS blocker (support for the 2022 pattern). Data Services team is actively investigating this issue.
    
-   **Architecture Design Milestone**: The deadline (May 20) for the Architecture Design planning milestone has passed. CSA’s are currently focused on critical requirements, including the architecture diagram (network topology, IAM roles, IIS permissions, database migrations, and connected environments) necessary for Rob’s PCI DSS compliance review
    

3.  **Metrics:** 100% of the Application migration to AMS Cloud will be fully completed by September 30, 2026. Subsequently, all decommissioning and shutdown activities will be completed by December 30, 2026.
    
4.  **Current RAG Status: Amber:** Montreal RAG currently Amber due to a number of unknown outcomes, which could impact site being closed by end 2026:
    
    -   Waiting for delivery date for MS SQL 2022 pattern for AMS builds.  Delivery team are currently reviewing priorities and will come back with available date.
        
    -   Application team resources are not familiar with cloud builds/operations, so working with team to assisgn ownership to key tasks and providing guidance from PE SMEs.
        
    -   No confirmed plan to complete migration/decoms caused by change in strategy from Azure to AMS cloud. 
        

## Path to Green

Project teams are actively engaging in multiple follow-up iteration calls to define key milestones and ensure the appropriate individuals and teams are identified and assigned clear roles and responsibilities. This alignment is being carried out in accordance with the updated AMS migration strategy. Additionally, the discussions aim to proactively identify and address early-stage challenges and risks to ensure smooth progress toward project goals.

risks.title: Environmental ambiguity between non-production and production in file management space
risks.description: There is ambiguity between non-production and production environments in the file management space, including shared file systems and mixed-use environments, which makes it unclear how to manage, migrate, and control files across environments.
risks.impact_description: If this ambiguity persists, file migration activities may be misconfigured or mis-scoped, production data might be exposed in non-production contexts, or critical files could be missed during migration. This may cause service disruptions, compliance issues, or require rework and could delay cutover and acceptance for AMS migration.
risks.mitigation: Clarify and document the environment classification and usage for all file shares, especially where production and non-production systems share infrastructure. Define clear responsibilities for file migration across dev, non-prod, and prod, including how real-time replication will be managed for production migrations, and track this ambiguity as a formal RAID item until resolved.

risks.title: Lack of clarity in ownership for infrastructure and application setup tasks
risks.description: There is confusion about who is responsible for tasks such as server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connection setup, TLS certificates, and network configuration in the AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If ownership for these tasks remains unclear, critical activities may be delayed or missed, leading to misconfigured infrastructure, security weaknesses, failed connectivity, and delays in testing and go-live. This can significantly impact the migration schedule and stability of the application post-cutover.
risks.mitigation: Refine and communicate the RACI matrix specifically for server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connectivity, TLS certificates, and network configuration. Ensure each task has a clearly assigned owner and that dependencies are documented in runbooks and migration plans.

risks.title: Ambiguity in roles and responsibilities for AMS migration (RACI)
risks.description: There is or was ambiguity in roles and responsibilities among team members during the AMS migration from the Montreal data center, which can cause overlapping efforts, missed tasks, and unclear accountability across the migration workstreams.
risks.impact_description: If role and responsibility ambiguity reoccurs, tasks may be duplicated or left incomplete, decision-making could be delayed, accountability for critical actions may be unclear, and confusion and inefficiencies could increase overall project risk, potentially impacting the migration timeline and service continuity.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a RACI workshop to clearly define and document roles and responsibilities for all migration tasks and communicate them to the stakeholders.

risks.title: Change in migration strategy from Azure to AMS may impact project completion timeline
risks.description: The decision to change the migration strategy from Azure to AMS for UFile Online introduces uncertainty and may impact the overall Montreal DC Exit project completion timeline (targeted around September 2026).
risks.impact_description: The change in strategy could cause setbacks in project timelines and deliverables, delays in task execution due to unclear ownership, increased risk of errors and inefficiencies during the migration, and miscommunication among stakeholders regarding responsibilities, ultimately threatening the September 2026 completion target.
risks.mitigation: A RACI review session will be held to realign roles and responsibilities in accordance with the updated AMS migration strategy. Subsequently, dedicated sessions will be conducted to establish milestones and timelines for each phase, as well as to identify and address early-stage challenges and risks.

risks.title: Resource constraints in service management and lack of DevOps/cloud expertise
risks.description: The service management team is already heavily loaded with other initiatives such as Hyper-V migration, and product engineering lacks DevOps and cloud engineering expertise required for AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If resource constraints and skill gaps are not addressed, key migration tasks may be delayed, executed with errors, or deprioritized. This increases the likelihood of schedule slippage, quality issues, and operational instability post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional hands-on resources with relevant DevOps and cloud skills to support the migration. Rebalance workload across service management and product engineering, and clearly prioritize AMS-related work to ensure critical tasks receive adequate attention.

risks.title: PCI DSS compliance risk for AMS production environment
risks.description: Meeting PCI DSS and other compliance requirements for a hardened, secure, documented, and certified production environment may be challenging without dedicated resources and specialized expertise.
risks.impact_description: Failure to achieve PCI DSS-compliant production infrastructure could result in non-compliance with regulatory and corporate standards, potential audit findings, restrictions on processing payment-related or sensitive data, and delays in go-live or the need to re-architect environments post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Engage the ISRM team early and integrate security and compliance activities throughout the migration. Ensure dedicated security resources review architecture, configurations, and documentation, and that a formal compliance assessment is completed before production cutover.

risks.title: Ownership gap for application configuration in new AMS environment
risks.description: While infrastructure and data migration tasks have assigned owners in platform engineering and service management, there is no clear owner for configuring and securing the application in the new AMS environment. Product engineering and service management teams lack expertise in application configuration in cloud-native infrastructure.
risks.impact_description: Without a clear owner for application configuration, critical tasks such as configuring application settings, securing endpoints, and aligning configurations with compliance requirements may be delayed or overlooked. This can jeopardize the migration timeline, create security and compliance gaps, and delay production readiness.
risks.mitigation:
Current challenge at this stage is finalizing setup documentation and validation. The business unit requires a sandbox environment to proceed with rebuild and re-engineering activities. 
•	Next Action: Gordon/Monica is currently working to define the initial build requirements for the sandbox and to identify the relevant Platform Engineering team to assist BU with Application installation.

dependencies.title: Upgrading production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version is a mandatory prerequisite for migrating to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment to ensure compatibility and mitigate risks.
dependencies.description: The migration to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment is critically dependent on upgrading the current production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version (SQL Server 2017 or later). Microsoft does not support SQL Server 2012 on Windows Server 2022, making these upgrades a mandatory preparatory step to ensure compatibility and avoid risks during the migration process. Production systems, including SQL 5, SQL 6, SQL 1, and SQL 2, must be upgraded prior to the migration, as well as the remaining pre-production reporting server.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: A delay in the AMS migration scheduled for September 2026 will impact the overall project timeline, resulting in a subsequent delay of the final major milestone—the Dilapidation and Data Center Shutdown activities planned for Q4 2026.
dependencies.mitigation:
Mitigation Plan: Separate Upgrade Phase: Perform SQL Server upgrades as a distinct preparatory phase before the cloud migration to minimize risks and ensure compatibility with Windows Server 2022.
Documented Timeline: Create a detailed schedule and timeline for SQL Server upgrades, allocating sufficient time for planning, execution, and validation of the upgraded systems.
Risk Mitigation: Include contingency plans in the migration documentation to address potential issues during the upgrade and migration process.
Alignment on Timing: Collaborate across teams to align the timing and processes for upgrades and migration, ensuring a smooth transition to the cloud environment.
Ownership Assignment: Designate responsible team members to oversee the upgrade process, document the migration plan, and ensure accountability for meeting deadlines and addressing concerns.
Validation and Testing: Thoroughly test upgraded SQL Server instances in the pre-production environment to ensure stability and performance before implementing changes in production systems.

entities.name: FedRAMP - CIAM Product Onboarding
entities.okrs:
Objective 1: Enable FedRAMP compliant customer access through a scalable CIAM foundation
Key Results
•	KR1: Deploy and operate a federation only Azure B2C CIAM solution approved for use within the FedRAMP authorization boundary. 
•	KR2: Establish standardized CIAM onboarding patterns and runbooks to support continued FedRAMP product adoption beyond the initial priority set. 
Objective 2: Complete CIAM onboarding for all priority FedRAMP products by June 30, 2026
Key Results
•	KR3: Onboard 100% of identified priority products in Non Prod to the FedRAMP CIAM solution. 
•	KR4: Onboard 100% of identified priority products in Prod by June 30, 2026, with no CIAM driven delays to authorization or customer readiness.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – CIAM Product Onboarding is delivering a FedRAMP‑compliant, federation‑only Azure B2C identity foundation and onboarding priority products in Non‑Prod and Prod so government and regulated customers can access Thomson Reuters products securely. This enables FedRAMP product readiness and creates a reusable CIAM pattern for future products.

As of 15 May 2026, 10 of 11 priority products are onboarded in Non‑Prod (91%) and 9 of 11 in Prod (82%), with overall onboarding 86% complete against targets of 11 of 11 in Non‑Prod by 30 May 2026 and full Prod onboarding by 30 Jun 2026. Milestones for Prod onboarding and project closure remain on their original dates with no reported schedule variance.

Overall status is Green, driven by Non‑Prod and Prod onboarding tracking to the 30 Jun 2026 completion date while executing the Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept.

## Path to Green

The primary focus is mitigating the Azure B2C outage recovery risk by completing the resiliency proof of concept and validating Microsoft’s resiliency guidance, alongside closing the CLEAR reg key validator dependency, all targeted for completion by the end of May 2026.

## Milestones

- Complete the Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept and achieve 11 of 11 priority products onboarded in the Non‑Prod environment by 30 May 2026.  
- Validate CLEAR reg key validator connectivity from CIAM lower environments and resolve any issues by 31 May 2026.  
- Complete Prod onboarding for all 11 priority products and overall CIAM FedRAMP product onboarding delivery by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Formally close the FedRAMP – CIAM Product Onboarding project by 30 Jun 2026.

risks.title: Business reaction risk to revised customer-ready timeline
risks.description: The business may react negatively to the revised customer-ready timeline for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If business stakeholders react poorly to the revised customer-ready timeline, it could create pressure to compress scope or timelines, drive unplanned work, or erode confidence in the FedRAMP CIAM program.
risks.mitigation: Communicate clearly that migrations are expected to start right after 3PAO audit approval (targeted for end of January), and share the team’s ETA of February 24, 2026 with Westlaw/Practical Law and other stakeholders, ensuring concerns are addressed proactively. Per the RAID log entry dated 2025-11-20, the team met with the Westlaw/Practical Law team on 2025-11-18, communicated the 2026-02-24 ETA, and received no negative reaction; stakeholders indicated that selling FedRAMP for those products would likely start around Q3.

risks.title: Risk of not completing onboarding by February 24
risks.description: There are significant risks to meeting the customer onboarding timeline (February 24) due to unforeseen engineering challenges, resource allocation issues, and the need for updated estimates.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding is not completed by February 24, customer onboarding will be delayed, potentially impacting commercial commitments, audit readiness, and the broader FedRAMP rollout schedule.
risks.mitigation: Review and refine scope and estimates, then mitigate by potentially reducing scope for the customer-ready timeline and ensuring the risk is visible at the program level. Communicate the mitigation plan and updated dates to stakeholders and plug the risk into the appropriate program-level tracker. The RAID log documents follow-up actions including Harvarinder finalizing a mitigation plan involving scope reduction and Alyssa ensuring the risk was tracked at the program level; the risk has since been closed with implementation of the agreed mitigation.

risks.title: LTS database migration risk
risks.description: LTS database migration work may not complete on time, impacting users and CIAM FedRAMP readiness.
risks.impact_description: If the LTS database migration does not complete successfully and on time (for both Non-Prod and Prod), related CIAM integrations and dependent services may be unavailable or unstable, delaying onboarding, increasing operational risk, and potentially impacting audit readiness.
risks.mitigation: Complete LTS database migration for Non-Prod and Prod, track progress and blockers via the dev team group chat, and provide regular updates. According to the RAID log, Non-Prod migration completed first, remaining blockers for Prod were resolved, and the overall LTS database migration was completed by 2026-02-26.

risks.title: Risk of not being customer ready by January 31 due to story sizing and outstanding requirements
risks.description: Based on the sizing of stories and some outstanding requirements, it is very likely that the program will not be customer ready by January 31 for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If customer-ready status is not achieved by January 31, customer onboarding timelines will slip, potentially impacting commitments made to stakeholders and compressing time available for testing, audit preparation, and operational readiness.
risks.mitigation: Refine user stories, solidify estimates, and communicate revised dates (moving the customer-ready target to February 28) to stakeholders so expectations and downstream plans can be adjusted. Per the RAID log, refinement of stories was completed and the new ETA of 2025-02-28 was communicated on 2025-10-06.

risks.title: Impact from onboarding new FTE resources replacing contractors
risks.description: Moving from contractors to FTEs may impact CIAM FedRAMP delivery as new resources are onboarded.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding of new FTE resources is slower than expected or they require extended ramp-up time, velocity on CIAM FedRAMP engineering work could drop, impacting delivery timelines and quality.
risks.mitigation: Onboard new resources onto the Kappa/Iota teams, actively monitor the impact, and adjust assignments as needed. Per the RAID log, the risk level was reduced from Medium to Low, hiring and releasing were in progress, and one additional resource hire was being monitored as of early January; ongoing monitoring ultimately supported closure of the risk.

risks.title: Non-prod Plexus cluster readiness may miss September 15 deadline
risks.description: If the non-prod Plexus cluster is not fully operational by September 15, the program is likely to miss the January 31 customer-ready milestone for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: Missing the September 15 readiness date for the non-prod Plexus cluster would delay downstream SRE and product onboarding work, putting the January 31 customer-ready milestone at risk and potentially delaying overall FedRAMP CIAM onboarding timelines.
risks.mitigation: Fix the connectivity issue and get the non-prod Plexus cluster fully functional, working with Plexus, Tech M, and Landing Zone teams to debug API endpoint access from commercial Zscaler to use1. This work was executed without stopping SRE progress, and the non-prod cluster was completed on September 22.

risks.title: Permit to Operate (PtO) may not be obtained before key resource vacation
risks.description: If the Permit to Operate is not obtained before Chris goes on vacation, the CIAM FedRAMP timeline may be impacted.
risks.impact_description: Failure to obtain PtO before a key engineering resource’s vacation could delay environment readiness and associated onboarding tasks, potentially impacting critical milestones for FedRAMP CIAM delivery.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the CIAM FedRAMP architecture, ensure the low environment is functional, and obtain ISRM approval in time to secure the Permit to Operate (PtO) before the vacation period. According to the RAID log, the PtO for Production was completed by the 2025-11-07 due date, eliminating the risk prior to the vacation window.

risks.title: Westlaw / Practical Law reg key validator certificate and connectivity issue
risks.description: After fixing a firewall product issue, requests from CIAM to Westlaw and Practical Law began failing because their reg key validator domains were not added to TLS certificates, creating a blocking dependency on those teams to update their certificates and resolve SSL errors.
risks.impact_description: If Westlaw and Practical Law do not update their certificates and resolve reg key validator connectivity issues, CIAM FedRAMP integrations that rely on these validators will continue to experience SSL failures, blocking testing and production use, and delaying onboarding timelines for Westlaw, Practical Law, and related CLEAR flows.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with Westlaw, Practical Law, and CLEAR teams to update certificates with required reg key validator domains and resolve connectivity issues, track progress via the FedRAMP Weekly CIAM Connect chat, and test across QED and Prod. Per the RAID log updates, the Westlaw and Practical Law certificate issues were resolved in Production first (with QED following), CLEAR deployments were coordinated, and by mid-April Chris confirmed that the WL/PL reg key validator issue was complete, allowing the risk to be closed.

risks.title: SAP / Audit account usage for internal testing
risks.description: Uncertainty about whether the same SAP account used for auditors can be repurposed for internal testing, and who can assist with this process, may delay test execution.
risks.impact_description: If the SAP audit account cannot be reused for internal testing, or if the decision and process are delayed, testing activities that depend on this account could be blocked or slowed, impacting schedule for validating CIAM FedRAMP scenarios that rely on SAP access.
risks.mitigation: Check with broader program management whether the audit account can be repurposed for internal testing and identify the appropriate contact(s) to assist with approvals and configuration. Adjust testing plans depending on the outcome.

risks.title: CLEAR reg key validator connectivity and availability
risks.description: CLEAR reg key validator endpoints are required for CIAM FedRAMP lower environment work, but connectivity and behavior are still being validated, with issues on CIAM’s side and dependencies on CLEAR deployments.
risks.impact_description: If CLEAR’s reg key validator endpoints are not fully functional and validated in lower and production environments, CIAM cannot reliably call these endpoints, blocking or delaying CLEAR-related onboarding flows and impacting the ability to meet CIAM FedRAMP onboarding timelines involving CLEAR.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with CLEAR to confirm reg key validator availability in QA and Prod, test and resolve connectivity issues from CIAM, and address concerns raised by CLEAR (e.g., via Doug). Track progress with regular follow-ups, especially around February–April (including confirming Prod deployment and subsequent testing).

risks.title: Outage Recovery / Disaster Recovery strategy for Azure B2C single point of failure
risks.description: Current FedRAMP CIAM architecture has a single point of failure in Azure B2C, with no proven fallback during major Azure or AWS outages. Outage on October 29 highlighted limitations, and resolution is dependent on Microsoft guidance and an internal resiliency proof-of-concept.
risks.impact_description: If a major Azure or AWS outage occurs before a robust outage recovery / DR strategy is implemented for Azure B2C, CIAM services for FedRAMP products could become unavailable, causing authentication failures for government and regulated customers, jeopardizing SLAs, damaging stakeholder confidence, and potentially impacting FedRAMP compliance posture.

risk_owner.name: Christopher Yip, Mohith Sai Krishna Katakam, and Tom Murphy

risks.mitigation: Work with Microsoft to obtain clear resiliency guidance and root cause information for past outages; evaluate Azure Front Door and related components as potential single points of failure; pursue an exception request (e.g., application gateway with B2C) where appropriate; and execute an internal resiliency proof-of-concept focused on outage recovery and DR. Per the 1-May and 15-May status updates, the primary mitigation path is to (1) validate Microsoft’s Azure B2C resiliency and outage recovery guidance by 2026-05-15, with Devarshi following up to confirm whether related work can be expedited and added to the sprint starting 2026-05-20 (noting that if it cannot be added, overall status may move to Amber), and (2) complete the internal Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept by 2026-05-30 so that the FedRAMP CIAM architecture no longer relies on an unmitigated single point of failure.

assumptions.title: No incremental commercial funding; costs managed within approved EPC allocation
assumptions.description: The CIAM FedRAMP Product Onboarding project assumes that required funding will be covered by TR Technology EPC funding for FY 2026, and that no incremental commercial funding will be needed, with all costs managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter specifies that funding comes from TR Technology EPC funding (FY 2026) and explicitly states that no incremental commercial funding is assumed, with costs to be managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current planning indicates that the EPC allocation covers all known project components (engineering, compliance, infrastructure, onboarding, audit, remediation). There are no stated requirements for commercial funding at this time, and scope is being managed within the approved budget envelope.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If EPC funding proves insufficient, raise an escalation through governance to either: (1) request incremental funding, or (2) reduce or phase scope (e.g., defer lower-priority product integrations or non-critical enhancements) to stay within the approved budget.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing comparison of actual and forecast project costs against the approved EPC budget, with finance and program reviews to confirm sufficiency of the allocation.

assumptions.title: Onboarding tracking will focus on product onboarding, not customer onboarding
assumptions.description: The project assumes that tracking and reporting for CIAM FedRAMP onboarding will focus on product onboarding only (Non-Prod and Prod), not customer onboarding, unless explicitly requested for initial customers.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter states that Harv and Alyssa agreed to track product onboarding only (not customer onboarding) unless explicitly requested for initial customers, and that Harv will align with Liat to ensure stakeholder consensus.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The agreement between program management leads and key product stakeholders is documented in the Charter, and current scope and milestones are framed around product onboarding completion. No conflicting requirements for customer onboarding tracking have been documented yet.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If stakeholders request broader tracking to include customer onboarding, formalize a scope and reporting change: define additional metrics, timelines, and owners for customer onboarding, and adjust the project plan and resourcing accordingly rather than treating these items as implicit obligations.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm in governance and stakeholder meetings (including with Liat and product stakeholders) that reporting continues to be based on product onboarding, and document any exceptions where customer onboarding tracking is explicitly requested.
