latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP – CoCounsel is extending Thomson Reuters’ existing FedRAMP Moderate authorization to include CoCounsel, delivering compliant PreProd and Prod environments in East and West regions plus required controls, monitoring, and audit artifacts. This enables secure, compliant use of CoCounsel by U.S. government and other regulated customers and unlocks access to new regulated markets.

Three of five major milestones are complete, with 4/4 FedRAMP CoCounsel environments built and validated and 5/5 core platform integrations delivered, both ahead of their planned November and December 2025 dates. Current focus is on raising ServiceNow GovCloud inventory coverage from ~50% to 100% and completing 3PAO audit activities by 2026-05-30, ahead of final authorization and project closure targeted for 2026-06-30.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by ServiceNow GovCloud discovery and CMDB inventory remaining at ~50% coverage against a 100% target needed for the 30 May 2026 audit-readiness milestone.

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to complete and stabilize ServiceNow GovCloud discovery and tagging so inventory coverage reaches 100% and audit-ready evidence can be accepted by the 3PAO by 2026-05-30, using joint troubleshooting with the vendor and AWS while maintaining the manual inventory workaround until automated discovery is reliable.

## Milestones

- Project Kickoff completed with scope, governance, and plan confirmed on 31 Mar 2025.  
- Non-Prod and Prod East/West environments built and validated (4/4 environments, 100% validation) on 14 Nov 2025.  
- Plexus, Cumulus, and Cloudflare integration and DNSSEC implementation completed (5/5 required integrations) on 19 Dec 2025.  
- ServiceNow Integration and 3PAO Audit activities to be completed, including ServiceNow GovCloud inventory at 100% and audit evidence finalized, by 30 May 2026.  
- FedRAMP authorization extended to CoCounsel and all closure activities completed by 30 Jun 2026.

risks.title: ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration stability
risks.description: Ongoing issues with the ServiceNow GovCloud setup, including asset discovery challenges, vendor engagement, and asset tagging; a manual workaround is currently in place. Discovery for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts is still not functioning as expected, requiring repeated vendor cases and engineering access changes.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration issues are not resolved, automated asset discovery and tagging will remain unreliable, forcing continued manual workarounds and risking incomplete or inaccurate inventory data needed to support FedRAMP operational monitoring and audit requirements for CoCounsel. This could create audit findings, delay audit readiness closure, and jeopardize the overall authorization and project-closure timeline.
risks.mitigation: Drive FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery via workaround: maintain AWS GovCloud discovery, track vendor cases, enable access for ServiceNow engineers, run joint working sessions, and iteratively tune until assets are reliably discovered/tagged. Following the Apr 30 session, schedule a live troubleshooting call with ServiceNow (Marshall), AWS (Ervan), and internal engineering (Prudhvi Yaswanth Kolluru) to review logs, resolve sub‑account discovery gaps, and address CMDB issues in real time.

risks.title: IaC deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus infrastructure-as-code (IaC) deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, forcing manual infrastructure provisioning.
risks.impact_description: If the IaC deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel FedRAMP infrastructure will have to be provisioned manually or via ad hoc scripts, which increases risk of configuration drift, security misconfigurations, and delays in environment creation.
risks.mitigation: Define the required IaC deployer capabilities for CoCounsel, implement missing features with support from the Cumulus/DOE team, and update pipelines so infrastructure can be provisioned consistently through Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Blue / Green deployer approval delays
risks.description: Cumulus blue/green deployments can fail if the "green" approval is delayed, causing deployment failures and requiring re-runs.
risks.impact_description: If blue/green deployments fail when approvals are delayed, production and pre-production releases for CoCounsel and related services could be slowed, result in additional manual effort to re-run pipelines, and increase the chance of deployment errors or missed release windows.
risks.mitigation: Identify and fix the blue/green deployer behavior so that delayed approvals do not cause deployment failures; deliver the fix via an updated Cumulus version and validate with CoCounsel pipelines before general use.

risks.title: Difficulty troubleshooting Cumulus installations due to incomplete logging
risks.description: Logging for Cumulus installations and pipeline creations with multiple assets can be lost or is hard to locate, making it difficult to troubleshoot failed installations.
risks.impact_description: If installation and pipeline logs remain hard to access or incomplete, teams may not be able to diagnose failed Cumulus deployments quickly, causing extended outage or delay in bringing CoCounsel pipelines online and increasing support overhead.
risks.mitigation: Work with the CICD team to improve log availability: adjust logging so installation and pipeline creation events are captured reliably, and provide solution guidance (including using single-asset installs where appropriate) so consumers can access logs needed for troubleshooting.

risks.title: Cumulus installation on Prod CI/CD account 386694349529
risks.description: Cumulus was not yet installed on the critical production CI/CD account (386694349529), blocking automated deployments for CoCounsel.
risks.impact_description: If Cumulus is not installed and available on the production CI/CD account, CoCounsel and related FedRAMP workloads cannot use the standard CPI/Cumulus deployment model, forcing manual deployments or ad hoc automation and increasing risk to release quality and timelines.
risks.mitigation: Plan and execute the installation of Cumulus on the Prod CI/CD account 386694349529, validate pipeline operation, and hand over to consuming teams for production use.

risks.title: Cumulus CPI inflation runs assets sequentially instead of in parallel
risks.description: The CPI inflation process runs multiple assets sequentially rather than in parallel, extending execution time by several minutes per run.
risks.impact_description: If CPI inflation continues to process assets sequentially, pipeline runs will be slower than expected, marginally increasing deployment lead time and reducing efficiency, though without directly blocking CoCounsel releases.
risks.mitigation: Review the CPI inflation design and either accept the sequential behavior as non-blocking or adjust the implementation; agree with stakeholders that no change is required if the added time is acceptable.

risks.title: Helm deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Helm deployer lacked feature parity and was not in sync with current source code changes, requiring services to be deployed manually and halting some Cumulus adoption.
risks.impact_description: If the Helm deployer does not support the required features and current source patterns, CoCounsel services that depend on Helm charts cannot be deployed through Cumulus pipelines, leading to manual deployments, higher operational risk, and slower delivery.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team work with the Cumulus/DOE team to define required Helm deployer capabilities, implement missing features, and remove blockers so Helm-based services can be deployed via Cumulus in GovCloud.

risks.title: Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda failure on null deployment status
risks.description: The Cumulus UI dashboard Lambda fails when a deployment record has a null status message, causing the dashboard to error and preventing blue/green deployment approvals via the UI.
risks.impact_description: If the dashboard Lambda continues to fail on null status values, teams cannot reliably use the Cumulus UI for blue/green deployment approvals, which may force manual workarounds and delay releases for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments.
risks.mitigation: Fix the dashboard Lambda to safely handle deployments with null status messages, release the updated Cumulus UI version, and verify that blue/green approvals work without error for GovCloud pipelines.

risks.title: Incorrect GovCloud pipeline links in Cumulus UI dashboard
risks.description: GovCloud pipeline links shown in the Cumulus UI dashboard used the wrong host, requiring users to manually navigate to the correct pipelines.
risks.impact_description: If GovCloud pipeline links remain incorrect, it is harder for teams to navigate from the dashboard to the underlying pipelines, slowing troubleshooting and increasing friction in managing CoCounsel FedRAMP deployments.
risks.mitigation: Update the Cumulus UI dashboard to generate correct GovCloud pipeline URLs and release the fix (v1.32.1) to all relevant environments.

risks.title: Cumulus multi-region support blocker
risks.description: A Cumulus defect blocked correct operation of multi-region pipelines needed for CoCounsel and related workloads.
risks.impact_description: If the Cumulus multi-region blocker is not fixed, CoCounsel may be unable to use a single Cumulus-based pattern to deploy to multiple GovCloud regions (e.g., East and West), leading to duplicated effort, inconsistent deployments, and higher operational risk.
risks.mitigation: Implement and validate a Cumulus fix for the multi-region blocker and roll it out to GovCloud environments used by CoCounsel, confirming that multi-region pipelines behave correctly.

risks.title: Cloudflare ingress blocked by Cumulus deployspec for Terraform
risks.description: The cumulus-deployspec-cloudflare (Terraform) implementation blocked creation of required public ingress (incoming calls) for CoCounsel and CARI services.
risks.impact_description: If the Cloudflare deployspec for Terraform cannot provision the necessary public ingress, CoCounsel and CARI services may not be reachable via Cloudflare in the FedRAMP environment, delaying go-live and creating security and availability risks.
risks.mitigation: Work through Engagement 454277 to debug and fix the Cloudflare Terraform deployer so it can successfully create required Cloudflare resources and public ingress; validate with CoCounsel pipelines before closing.

risks.title: EKS deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus EKS deployer lacked feature parity with source code changes, forcing manual deployment of EKS-based services and temporarily halting some Cumulus usage.
risks.impact_description: If the EKS deployer remains incomplete, CoCounsel services running on EKS in GovCloud cannot rely on Cumulus pipelines for deployment, increasing the need for manual steps and risking deployment errors or delays.
risks.mitigation: Have Chetan’s engineering team, with DOE support, implement the required EKS deployer features, remove identified blockers, and validate deployments for CoCounsel EKS workloads in GovCloud.

risks.title: Terraform deployer feature gaps in Cumulus
risks.description: The Cumulus Terraform deployer lacked feature parity with current infrastructure definitions, requiring teams to automate Terraform deployments outside Cumulus (e.g., via GitHub Actions).
risks.impact_description: If the Terraform deployer is not brought up to feature parity, CoCounsel infrastructure deployments will continue to rely on external automation, leading to fragmented deployment tooling, more complex operations, and higher risk of misconfiguration.
risks.mitigation: Extend the Cumulus Terraform deployer to support the required Terraform workflows for CoCounsel, align it with current infrastructure code, and transition from ad hoc GitHub Actions automation back into Cumulus-managed deployments where appropriate.

actions.title: Complete ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for FedRAMP CoCounsel
actions.description: Drive completion of the ServiceNow GovCloud setup and inventory integration required for FedRAMP audit readiness, coordinating with the vendor and internal engineers until the integration is fully working and evidence is available for auditors.

actions.title: Schedule joint troubleshooting call with ServiceNow vendor, AWS (Ervan), and internal ServiceNow/FedRAMP teams
actions.description: Schedule a joint troubleshooting meeting for FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery involving ServiceNow vendor engineer Marshall, AWS team representative Ervan, the internal ServiceNow core team, and project stakeholders to review discovery logs and understand why discovery is only occurring at the master account level and not at sub-account level.

assumptions.title: Most Westlake FedRAMP work is reusable for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that most of the work delivered for the Westlake FedRAMP implementation can be leveraged to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, with only some new components required.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project is described as an extension of the broader FedRAMP program that has been running for almost two years, and the charter explicitly states that most of the work delivered for Westlake is expected to be leveraged.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The broader FedRAMP program has already implemented compliant infrastructure, controls, and patterns for Westlake within the same authorization boundary. Because CoCounsel is being added to this existing boundary and environment, it is reasonable to expect that networking, security controls, monitoring, and many platform components can be reused, needing only incremental extensions or configuration changes rather than net‑new designs.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves limited, re‑baseline the implementation plan and budget to include additional engineering work, prioritize critical capabilities necessary for FedRAMP readiness, and potentially phase lower‑priority features into subsequent change packets.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture and design reviews comparing Westlake components to CoCounsel requirements; detailed gap analysis and implementation planning.

validation_owner.name: Lead solution architect for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: Allocated $1M capital budget is sufficient for FedRAMP CoCounsel build work
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the $1 million capital budget allocated by finance will be sufficient to cover platform, engineering, and science work required to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, despite the originally assumed May start no longer being feasible.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Rough estimates for FTEs and contractors are around $750K, which is well within the allocated $1M capital budget, providing apparent headroom for variation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The charter cites an initial estimate of $750K for FTEs and contractors versus a $1M allocation, creating a 25%+ buffer for unanticipated needs. While the May start date is no longer feasible, the underlying scope and complexity are not indicated to have substantially changed, so it is reasonable to assume the total capital requirement will remain within the approved envelope, at least until more detailed plans suggest otherwise.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If forecasts indicate the capital budget will be exceeded, prepare a change request and business justification for additional funds, or adjust scope and phasing to keep critical FedRAMP readiness work within the existing budget while deferring non‑essential features to a later packet.
assumptions.validation_method: Refined bottom‑up estimation and periodic re‑forecasting of engineering and contractor effort against actuals, reviewed with finance.

validation_owner.name: Project manager / finance partner for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: FedRAMP cadence and lessons learned from Packet #1 will reduce delivery and audit risk for CoCounsel
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that aligning execution sequencing with the established FedRAMP cadence and leveraging lessons learned from Packet #1 will materially reduce delivery and audit risk for the CoCounsel FedRAMP extension.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The charter explicitly states that execution sequencing aligns with the established FedRAMP cadence and leverages lessons learned from Packet #1 to reduce delivery and audit risk.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Having already executed FedRAMP work and a prior change packet, the team understands the expectations of 3PAO auditors and the FedRAMP PMO, common pitfalls, and realistic lead times. Using this lived experience to drive the CoCounsel schedule, scope sequencing, and artifact preparation should, in principle, lower the likelihood and severity of surprises, provided the regulatory context and core architecture remain similar.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If execution or audit activities show similar levels of risk or findings as earlier packets, adjust the plan by adding intermediate readiness assessments, dedicating additional compliance and security resources, and re‑sequencing or de‑scoping lower‑priority items to protect critical authorization milestones.
assumptions.validation_method: Retrospectives and planning sessions mapping Packet #1 outcomes and issues to the CoCounsel plan; early checkpoints during execution and pre‑audit readiness reviews to confirm reduced issues compared to earlier packets.

assumptions.title: ServiceNow GovCloud discovery configuration proven on one AWS GovCloud account will be reusable for all FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that once the ServiceNow cloud discovery process for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud is successfully configured and validated on one AWS GovCloud account, the same configuration and process can be cascaded to the remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts without requiring materially different patterns per account.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the April 30, 2026 "FedRAMP SNOW - Cloud Discovery - GovCloud" meeting, the team stated that they will only cascade the configuration to remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts after seeing a successful discovery scenario for one account, implying an expectation that the discovery pattern is reusable across accounts.
assumptions.validity_explanation: All FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts are being onboarded into the same ServiceNow GovCloud instance using common discovery patterns. The primary current issue is with discovery not reaching child/sub-account levels on the first account; once this routing and pattern issue is understood and resolved collaboratively with ServiceNow and AWS, the underlying mechanism should function similarly for other accounts in the same environment, making reuse reasonable but not yet proven.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves unreliable and each FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account requires unique discovery adjustments, replan the work to include per-account configuration and testing, prioritize accounts that are in scope for near-term FedRAMP audit, and consider temporary supplemental approaches (e.g., scripted exports or manual CMDB updates) for lower-priority accounts until discovery patterns are stabilized.
assumptions.validation_method: First achieve a fully successful discovery run (including child/sub-account coverage) on the initial FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account, then apply the same configuration to additional FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts and compare discovery results and logs to confirm that configuration is reusable without per-account customization.

dependencies.title: ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration for asset discovery and tagging
dependencies.description: Completion and stabilization of the ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration, including reliable asset discovery and tagging for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts, is required to provide accurate configuration and asset data for FedRAMP operational monitoring and audit of CoCounsel.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow vendor engineering support and internal ServiceNow platform engineers
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP CoCounsel audit readiness and ServiceNow Integration & 3PAO Audit milestone
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the ServiceNow GovCloud inventory integration is not fully working by the audit readiness target, automated asset discovery and tagging for FedRAMP CoCounsel environments will remain unreliable, forcing continued manual workarounds and risking incomplete or inaccurate inventory data for 3PAO and FedRAMP PMO audit reviews.
dependencies.mitigation: Maintain a manual inventory workaround while coordinating with ServiceNow vendor engineers via support cases and working sessions; grant required table access to engineers; iterate on configuration based on test results until GovCloud asset discovery and tagging are stable.

dependencies.title: Production monitoring verification dependent on CoCounsel production deployment
dependencies.description: Verification of production monitoring for CoCounsel in Prod East and Prod West is dependent on the CoCounsel team deploying services into the FedRAMP production environments so that monitoring, alerts, and dashboards can be exercised and evidence collected for continuous monitoring.
dependencies.dependent_on: CoCounsel production deployments in AWS GovCloud Prod East and Prod West
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP CoCounsel continuous monitoring evidence and Audit Readiness milestone
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If CoCounsel production deployments or monitoring verification are delayed, the project may lack sufficient production monitoring evidence for FedRAMP continuous monitoring, potentially delaying final authorization and project closure.
dependencies.mitigation: Coordinate deployment and monitoring verification windows between the CoCounsel engineering team and SRE/Service Management; if necessary, use targeted test deployments and synthetic traffic in production to generate monitoring events and evidence ahead of full customer rollout.

decisions.title: Use GitHub Actions as temporary CI/CD solution for Cloudflare deployments until Cumulus is ready
decisions.description: Adopt GitHub Actions, authenticated to AWS via OpenID Connect or access/secret keys, as a temporary CI/CD mechanism for Cloudflare-related infrastructure (including updating Cloudflare API tokens and deploying Cloudflare resources) while Cumulus deployer features are being completed and stabilized for GovCloud.
decisions.rationale: To keep CoCounsel FedRAMP delivery on track and avoid blocking Cloudflare work on unresolved Cumulus deployer and CPI issues, the team needed a short-term CI/CD approach that could be implemented quickly and independently of Cumulus releases.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Pause Cloudflare deployments until Cumulus deployers were fully feature-complete and stable; 2) Build an alternative CI/CD solution using GitHub Actions with temporary Cloudflare API token configuration; 3) Attempt manual Cloudflare configuration without automation.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Cumulus Issues: CoCo & CARI (GovCloud deployer feature gaps) and Cloudflare: Temp Solution API token updates and GitHub-to-AWS authentication tasks.

entities.okrs: PLE-12 – Achieve measurable cloud cost savings while enabling strategic innovation (CIO).

latest_report.content:
## **Executive Summary**

**Scope:** Cloud Modernization Office enhances Cloud Scorecard and Cloud Advise tools surfacing modernization opportunities, cost savings, and reliability improvements across Azure workloads. Initiative enables faster data-driven cloud investment decisions and reduces manual analysis for product, technology, and finance teams.

**Current Status - GREEN** because all active milestones track to original delivery dates with zero schedule variance. Azure Platform Scorecard delivered 31 Mar 2026 (25% complete), with Cloud Advise and Datadog enhancements confirming 30 Jun 2026 delivery.

**Key outcomes delivered:**  
• Azure Platform Scorecard completed - Delivered 31 Mar 2026 and integrated into Cloud Scorecard; enables platform-level assessment; first of four milestones achieved.  
• Cloud Advise VM-to-containers progressing - Azure VM migration recommendations in build phase; targeting 30 Jun 2026 delivery.  
• DB-to-PaaS recommendations advancing - Azure DB-on-VM to PaaS analysis in development; scheduled for 30 Jun 2026.  
• Datadog Scorecard enhancement underway - Integration design confirmed; build phase proceeding to schedule.

**Active RAID items:**  
• R1 — Risk: Datadog resource capacity gap requiring interim leadership. Mitigation: Implement resource capacity plan by 12 Jun 2026; confirm interim responsibilities; ensure FinOps work continuity.

## **Path to Green**

Status remains GREEN with all June milestones on track. Primary focus centers on Datadog resource mitigation, securing interim leadership by 12 Jun 2026 to prevent delays in Scorecard enhancement and related FinOps deliverables.

## **Next Steps**

• Implement Datadog mitigation - Confirm interim leadership; establish responsibilities; ensure continuity — by 12 Jun.  
• Complete VM-to-containers recommendations - Finalize build; execute testing; prepare deployment — by 30 Jun.  
• Deliver DB-to-PaaS recommendations - Complete development; integrate with Cloud Advise — by 30 Jun.  
• Deploy Datadog Scorecard enhancement - Finish integration; validate metrics; release to production — by 30 Jun.  
• Transition to steady-state - Complete remaining enhancements; establish operational model — by 29 Dec.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

LatAm Top of Funnel Migration will move the LATAM sales team onto a unified, enterprise-aligned Salesforce platform that uses Lightning and AI to improve sales efficiency, data integrity, leadership visibility, and customer engagement across the full sales lifecycle. This replaces fragmented tools with a single front-office view for LATAM sellers and leaders.

On progress, program governance, steering committee membership, and cadence are fully established (100%), and migration phasing options are 70% confirmed against a 100% target for the "Scope, Migration Option & Governance Confirmed" milestone now forecast to complete by 14 Jun 2026 instead of the original 07 Jun 2026 plan. All downstream milestones (Architecture and HLD, Data Readiness, Build, Migration, UAT, and Go-Live) remain in Not Started status with dates unchanged, so schedule risk is currently concentrated in completing the initial scope and option decisions.

Overall status is Green, driven by early completion of program governance and near-finalization of migration scope that de-risks subsequent design and build activities despite a small delay on the first milestone.

## Path to Green

The top risk is D&A capacity constraints for ECM data ingestion, and mitigation focuses on securing prioritized ECM and ECX capacity and sequencing data profiling so that the "Data Readiness & Prerequisites Complete" milestone by 25 Sep 2026 remains achievable.

## Milestones

- Complete "Scope, Migration Option & Governance Confirmed" with 100% migration option phasing approved by 2026-06-14 (currently 70% confirmed against a 100% target).  
- Complete "Architecture & HLD Approved (Top-of-Funnel)" by 2026-07-05.  
- Complete "Data Readiness & Prerequisites Complete" by 25 Sep 2026.  
- Achieve "LATAM Business Go-Live" on GSI for in-scope functionality by 14 Oct 2026.  
- Complete overall program closure and transition to BAU operations by 30 Nov 2026.

risks.title: Cost / Budget - Dual Licensing Exposure
risks.description: If quoting, renewals, or service remain in S2E while sales moves to GSI, users may require dual licenses. LATAM leadership has indicated no appetite for additional licensing cost.
risks.impact_description: Potential budget impact due to having ~150+ dual licenses.
risks.mitigation: Working with central sourcing team to transfer S2E to GSI licenses through SELA.

risks.title: Technology / Systems - Account & Data Model Misalignment (S2E vs GSI / ECM)
risks.description: LATAM S2E account hierarchy differs from GSI/ECM (gold account vs SSD/location model). Incorrect mapping may lead to duplicate accounts, orphaned records, and inconsistent reporting.
risks.impact_description: Poor data integrity, reduced user confidence, increased remediation effort post go‑live, long‑term technical debt.
risks.mitigation: Confirm target account hierarchy for LATAM; validate ECM segmentation and SSD usage; agree migration mapping rules before HLD sign‑off.

risks.title: Operations / Business Process - Service & Back‑Office Dependency on S2E
risks.description: Service, renewals, and back‑office processes remain dependent on S2E. Moving sales/opportunities to GSI without service alignment introduces duplicate records and swivel‑chair processes.
risks.impact_description: Operational inefficiency, degraded seller and service experience, continued dependency on legacy systems.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly confirm service future‑state (remain in S2E vs phased move); document interim operating model and risks for leadership decision.

risks.title: Technology / Systems - High Data Duplication & Salesforce Storage Risk
risks.description: LATAM data volumes are large. Partial migration options may significantly increase duplicate accounts/contacts in Salesforce, which is already close to storage limits.
risks.impact_description: Increased Salesforce storage cost, performance degradation, data governance issues.
risks.mitigation: Quantify duplication under each migration option; confirm storage headroom; include storage impacts in option comparison deck.

assumptions.description: Assumes prerequisites (territory alignment, ECM hierarchy, translations, limited data scope) can be completed in parallel and on time.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Validation Needed: Architecture commitment to HLD timing; prerequisite readiness confirmation.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Risk if Invalid: Delivery likely shifts to Q4 or later.

assumptions.validity_explanation: Validation Needed: Inventory of reusable vs net‑new custom fields.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Risk if Invalid: Increased cost and extended change timeline.

issues.title: D&A capacity constraints
issues.description:
Severe ECM tech capacity constraints as:
1.	there are a few high-priority projects that need to be fully resourced – Customer Data program, CPSP etc.
2.	there are multiple programs that drive resource requirements without appropriate funding and planned outside of normal cycles.
issues.impact_assessment:
Migrating the customers/contacts is critical for this project's success. 
Sales, marketing and service teams depend on this data to be migrated and sync'ed to GSI. 
They will not be able to process any sales activity in GSI until we get this data correctly.
Without ECM and ECX ingestion, we cannot easily (if at all) identify matching GSI accounts and contacts, with the following impacts:
- duplicates will be created in GSI
- accounts and contacts that would otherwise be matched will have to be included in profiling and data clean-up activities
issues.resolution: TBD

## Executive Summary

Legal Tracker Migration is moving all remaining Legal Tracker data and capabilities from legacy Salesforce instances to enterprise platforms, standardizing processes across regions and enabling full retirement of legacy technology. This will reduce technology risk, simplify support, and provide a more consistent experience for legal and commercial teams globally.

Architecture, HLD, and integration design are 80% complete against a 100% target by 29 May 2026, providing the baseline for build and data migration. Key downstream milestones remain aligned to plan, with build and data migration scheduled to complete by 15 Jul 2026, UAT by 10 Jul 2026, and business go-live on 14 Aug 2026.

Overall status is Green, driven by architecture and integration design progressing to 80% completeness and tracking to the 29 May 2026 approval milestone with no schedule variance.

## Path to Green

The top mitigation focus is on the data archive and decommission dependency, with decommissioning gated until the EDL data archival is completed, signed off, and the 30 Jun 2026 mitigation due date is met.

## Milestones

- Complete “Architecture, HLD & Integration Design Approved” by 29 May 2026.  
- Complete “UAT Completed & Business Sign-Off” by 10 Jul 2026.  
- Complete “Build, Configuration & Data Migration Complete” by 15 Jul 2026.  
- Achieve “Legal Tracker Business Go-Live” across in-scope regions by 14 Aug 2026.  
- Conclude the Legal Tracker Migration program and retire remaining legacy scope by 28 Aug 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The project team has successfully completed the server relocation and Hyper-V migration for both the Development and Production environments from Markham to the MSP Data Center, covering Phases 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.

**Project Current Progress: Phase 8: 4x Domain Controller Build and MSP Hyper-V Migration Planning**

The project request RITM0147257 was recently approved by the Solution Design team. The IaaS provisioning request (RITM0155633) was submitted yesterday, and the Delivery Provision team is currently processing it.. ETA May 29th

**Next Steps:** CSA has contacted ISRM regarding the domain controllers.

1.  Once the assigned IP addresses are received, Gordon will include them in the request for ISRM approval.
    
2.  After ISRM approves the IRR, Gordon will raise the necessary firewall rule.
    
3.  Once the firewall rule is implemented, the domain controllers can be activated.
    

**Path to Green**

Green – Despite having 5x dependencies, multiple sub-project teams are actively working with strict adherence to timelines. Any issues or risks encountered are promptly highlighted to the leadership team, ensuring continuous progress without major delays.

**A. Scope:**

1.  5x Physical Solaris Legacy/Critical Servers
    
2.  60x Virtual Machines (includes 10 Database servers)
    
3.  68x CIFS Shares Migrations
    

## Path to Green

The top risk is timely completion of dependent migrations (DT Max, HighQ Azure, CIFS shares, and remaining Hyper-V scope) required for Markham dilapidation, mitigated by dedicated dependency tracking and batch-wise CIFS owner identification ahead of the 30 Sep 2026 dependency dates.

## Milestones

-   Complete Phase 8 Domain Controller build and associated DMZ server readiness in MSP by 15 Jun 2026, bringing server migration progress to 60% of the Markham-to-MSP1 scope.
    
-   Complete Phase 9 DMZ server migration to MSP by 15 Jun 2026, achieving 100% of DMZ server moves from Markham to MSP1.
    
-   Close out remaining Hyper-V migration dependency activities supporting the Markham exit by 31 May 2026.
    
-   Complete CIFS share, DT Max, and HighQ Azure migrations that underpin Markham shutdown dependencies by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Complete Markham dilapidation and full colo site closure by 31 Dec 2026.

Any delays in these dependencies could significantly impact the project timeline, operational costs, resource availability, and compliance/security posture. issues.title: Production Access Issues for Remote Team of 50+ Canadian/Montreal Users to Canadian Drives (Issue identified: 12 May)
issues.description: Issue Summary: Andy, Heather, Orly highlighted the root is a recent change in the configuration or membership of the " 2x Z connectors in Markham" pool, which is now preventing Montreal/ Canadian users from accessing storage in Markham.
issues.impact_assessment: If the root cause has been identified, it is critical that we expedite the resolution as soon as possible. Currently, over 50 employees in Montreal are unable to work, and tasks are continuing to accumulate. Additionally, this issue is impacting colleagues in Toronto, further escalating the urgency.
issues.resolution:
Mukkaram from the TRNOC-Security team for reactivating the Markham Z connectors. I also appreciate the efforts of Aman, Palak, and Shubham for their thorough investigation and support in resolving the issue.
 
Issue resolution Summary: Mukkaram explained that the connectivity issues stem from changes in Zscaler connector routing after resources were migrated from the Markham Data Center to the MSP Data Center. Markham-specific Z connectors, previously optimized for accessing Markham resources, are now blocked when trying to access MSP resources due to MSP's stricter inbound restrictions. Elevated users using global connectors are unaffected.
 
To resolve the folder share access issues, Mukkaram suggests allowing MSP connectors to access Markham resources by updating the Markham firewall. This approach is simpler and avoids lengthy approval processes compared to enabling Markham connectors to access MSP resources. He recommends gathering a list of inaccessible resources to implement this solution effectively.

Due to latency issues introduced by Zscaler, users are experiencing significant delays in database performance. Reports that previously took only a few minutes to generate are now requiring up to four hours. This slowdown is causing disruption to daily operations, reducing productivity, and potentially delaying critical decision-making processes that depend on timely access to these reports.

Zscaler Configuration:

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Scope:** Enable Virtual Office and NetFirm to manually fail over between Azure East US 2 and Central US with minimal downtime. Build cost-effective DR in Central US across Compute, Database, and Storage, establish manual failover procedures, and validate via two non-production and one production joint failover test.

**Current Status — GREEN** All key areas are progressing well:  The teams have confirmed **Wednesday, July 8, 2026** as the date for the first joint non-prod DR test (Virtual Office + NetFirm). June 24 was ruled out due to a scheduled NetFirm release that week and hotfix conflict risk.

-   **DevOps:** Complete — All preparation items are complete, and the team is ready to support the upcoming DR test.
    
-   **DBA:** In Progress — DBA resolved a single-subnet cluster configuration failure and has redeployed to a multi-subnet setup; internal failover testing is expected to complete by May 29.
    
-   **Architecture:** Complete — sign-off received; ISRM security recommendations are being actively worked — some complete, others pending ISRM clarification on scope
    
-   Manual Sync Components: Azure Key Vault and DNS records require manual procedures (not covered by auto-sync); currently underway
    
-   **NetFirm Storage Ownership:** It was confirmed that DevOps (Brad's team) owns NetFirm storage. 
    
-   Two open risks require resolution before DR sign-off can be confirmed
    

 **R3 — Outstanding ISRM Recommendations:** Some addressed, others pending clarification on whether they are hard prerequisites for DR test sign-off or can be deferred as longer-term improvements or handled outside the DR scope. _Mitigation: 28 May meeting with ISRM to confirm pre-req vs. deferred split._

**R4 — Qualys Severity 4 & 5 Vulnerabilities:** Severity 4 & 5 findings across NetFirm servers (some dating to 2025) risk DR sign-off if not resolved or formally excepted prior to the test. _Mitigation: 28 May meeting with ISRM to determine which items are hard prerequisites for DR sign-off. DevOps to confirm ownership and classify each finding as fix, exception, or accepted risk, and remediate accordingly._

 **Next Steps**

-   ISRM/DevOps alignment meeting: confirm DR sign-off prerequisites and Qualys remediation plan – May 28
    
-    DBA internal failover testing complete; NetFirm storage DR lead confirmed with Brad – May 26 
    
-   Joint Netfirm & VO coordinated planning calls begin from June 3-July 6: DR runbook review, readiness validation, resolve interdependencies, formal sign-offs.
    
-   First Joint Non-Prod DR Test, Virtual Office + NetFirm – July 6

decisions.description:

A new "Net Amount for Rev Rec" column has been proposed to reflect properly allocated values for revenue recognition.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Certinia CS Implementation Wave 1 will deliver a unified Customer Success platform in Salesforce for Legal Professionals, TAAP, Corporates and related segments, standardising post-sales execution and success processes. This matters because it improves visibility into customer health and risk while enabling scalable, data-driven success outcomes across all segments.

Planning is tracking 11 days late versus the 16 May 2026 baseline, with completion now forecast for 27 May 2026. Downstream milestones remain ahead of the original plan, with Data Migration and UAT forecast to finish 2 and 7 days early (26 May and 09 Jun 2026) and Phase 1 completion pulled forward 47 days from 15 Aug to 29 Jun 2026, subject to resolution of design and data risks.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by delayed Phase 1 scope and requirements finalisation which is compressing the window for build, UAT and training ahead of the late June go-live target.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing the requirements and design gap by completing the scheduled TR–Certinia working sessions to finalise Phase 1 scope by 27 May 2026 and time-boxing all open design decisions to May with SteerCo escalation where needed. Build will be gated on confirmed requirements, integration readiness and early data profiling plus mock migrations, reducing rework risk and protecting the 29 Jun 2026 Phase 1 completion date.

## Milestones

- Complete the Wave 1 Planning milestone, including baselined integrated programme plan and variance closure, by 27 May 2026.  
- Complete Sandbox Data Migration for Phase 1 by 26 May 2026.  
- Complete Phase 1 UAT across all segments with sign-off by 09 Jun 2026.  
- Achieve Phase 1 Wave 1 completion with Certinia CS as the primary Customer Success platform live for all segments by 2026-06-29.  
- Close out the overall Certinia CS Implementation Wave 1 programme and transition to steady-state operations by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Open design decisions delay build
risks.description: Multiple open design decisions (including TAAP Success Plan level, health scoring model, risk data model, Gong integration scope, renewal strategy, Eloqua integration scope) may not be resolved by the planned dates, delaying the start of Certinia Phase 1 build or causing rework once build has begun.
risks.impact_description: If key design decisions (D-001 to D-006 and related items) are not resolved before build, Certinia configuration will either be delayed or proceed on unstable requirements. This could push the integrated build schedule, compress UAT and training windows, and ultimately delay the 2026-06-22 Phase 1 go-live or degrade solution quality due to rushed changes.
risks.mitigation: Time-box all open design decisions to May 2026, with decision workshops per workstream. Track each decision (D-001 to D-006) in the Decision Log, escalate unresolved items to SteerCo, and use the Executive Milestone 'Confirm Scope and Obtain Approval from Segments' (C1.2.2.7) as a hard gate before build starts.

risks.title: Data quality issues impact migration and UAT
risks.description: Subscription, hierarchy, and territory data across segments may have quality issues that could delay data migration and cause UAT failures in the Certinia CS platform.
risks.impact_description: Poor data quality (e.g., incorrect subscriptions, incomplete hierarchies, misaligned territories) will require remediation during migration, extend data mapping and cleansing timelines, and could lead to failed mock migrations. If not addressed early, this will cause defects in UAT, reduce confidence in the solution, and may delay go-live while data is corrected.
risks.mitigation: Perform early data profiling on key sources (EDL/Snowflake and other systems), define data quality acceptance criteria with segment leads, and execute multiple mock data migrations (C1.4.1.6–C1.4.1.8) before production migration. Track data issues and remediation tasks, with weekly data migration touchpoints (C1.2.2.16) to monitor progress.

## Executive Summary

Customer Success – Gainsight decommission will migrate capabilities from Gainsight to GSI and Snowflake, provide a unified relationship view in Salesforce, and fully retire Gainsight to support a scalable customer engagement model. This matters because it consolidates customer data and workflows, improving customer health monitoring and reducing tooling complexity.

Data migration from Gainsight to Snowflake was completed on 28 Feb 2026 against a planned date of 31 Mar 2026, delivering this foundational dependency about one month early. The remaining Gainsight Migration to GSI workstream is in progress toward its planned completion on 30 Jun 2026, with active mitigation for high-volume (25k) record load constraints in Salesforce via a one-time GSI load and Power BI query while scalable options are evaluated.

Overall status is Green, driven by early completion of the GS to Snowflake migration that de-risks downstream GSI and Salesforce integration work.

## Milestones

- Complete Gainsight Migration to GSI, including delivery of the unified relationship view in Salesforce and core technology updates, by 30 Jun 2026.
- Confirm handling approach for 25k record loads into GSI and Salesforce, including any required tooling or model changes, by 30 Jun 2026.
- Confirm full decommissioning readiness for Gainsight, including validation of data in Snowflake and Salesforce-based views, by 30 Nov 2026.
- Fully decommission Gainsight and close the Customer Success – Gainsight decommission program by 31 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Handling of 25K record loads may be constrained by Salesforce limitations and current one-time load approach
risks.description: There is a risk that the approach to handle 25K record loads, given Salesforce limitations and the decision to manage this as a one-time load in GSI via a Power BI dashboard query, may not scale or may be insufficient if larger or recurring loads are needed in the future.
risks.impact_description: If Salesforce limitations prevent efficient handling of high-volume record loads and the one-time load approach in GSI proves inadequate, the team may be unable to load or refresh large datasets reliably. This could result in incomplete or outdated relationship-level data, degraded reporting and customer health monitoring, increased manual workarounds, and potential disruption to Customer Success operations and analytics.
risks.mitigation: Continue discussions on how to handle 25K record loads within Salesforce limitations and future tool assessments. In the near term, manage the requirement as a one-time load in GSI using a Power BI dashboard query while evaluating longer-term options such as optimizing Salesforce data model and limits, introducing additional integration or ETL tooling, or adjusting load frequency and batch sizes.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

This project is delivering a comprehensive evaluation of alternatives to Broadcom’s CA mainframe tool suite, culminating in a go/no-go recommendation and high-level migration roadmap that protects against projected multi-fold renewal cost increases. The outcome will guide selection of an alternative (currently IBM as the preferred vendor) that balances 5–7 year total cost, migration risk, and long-term flexibility while maintaining mainframe stability.

To date, 10 of 14 defined milestones are complete, including vendor proposal intake, comparative evaluation, and a working-team decision to select IBM’s ~US$12.5M 7-year fixed-fee proposal over BMC’s ~US$16M+ 5-year option. Three milestones are in progress (executive presentation, executive approval, and procurement trigger), with completion targeted ahead of the 30 Jun 2026 project end date to meet the KPI of an approved recommendation and roadmap by that same date.

Overall status is Green, driven by the completion of vendor selection and evaluation activities with remaining work focused on securing formal executive approval and closing documentation on the planned timeline.

## Path to Green

The primary mitigation focus is on the open risk of production disruption during any future migration by ensuring the high-level roadmap and IBM statement of work mandate phased cutovers, robust parallel testing, and clearly contracted heavy-assist responsibilities before implementation proceeds.

## Milestones

- Complete the executive presentation of the Broadcom CA replacement recommendation and high-level migration roadmap by 31 May 2026.  
- Obtain formal executive go/no-go approval and endorsement of the migration roadmap, meeting the KPI deadline of 2026-06-30.  
- Trigger the procurement process for any follow-on implementation project, including a signed statement of work with the selected vendor, by 29 May 2026.  
- Review and finalize all evaluation project documentation, including financial analysis, risk register, and decision records, by 15 Jun 2026.  
- Close the evaluation project and complete formal project closure activities, aligned to the overall program end date, by 30 Jun 2026.

risks.title: Broadcom CA products not fully replaced before contract renewal date
risks.description: There is a risk that not all Broadcom CA products currently in use will be fully replaced before the Broadcom contract renewal date, even if an alternative solution is selected.
risks.impact_description: If all Broadcom CA products are not replaced before the renewal date, the organization may be forced to (a) renew Broadcom CA licenses longer than intended, (b) pay for overlapping tools during the transition period, or (c) accept reduced functionality or temporary workarounds. This would negatively impact budget, project timelines, and potentially service quality for business-critical mainframe operations.
risks.mitigation: Develop a phased migration roadmap that explicitly sequences Broadcom CA product replacements against renewal milestones, identify which products must be replaced before renewal to avoid extended overlap, and incorporate contingency plans (e.g., short-term renewals or bridge contracts) into negotiation strategy with Broadcom and alternative vendors.

risks.title: Extended reliance on vendor SMEs for Broadcom CA migration
risks.description: There is a risk that the project will require vendor Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) for an extended period to complete migrations from Broadcom CA products to any selected alternative solution.
risks.impact_description: If extended vendor SME involvement is required without secured funding and availability, migration timelines could slip, internal teams may lack the expertise to complete cutovers, and the organization could face prolonged dual-running of Broadcom CA and replacement tools. This would increase project costs, extend risk exposure around the Broadcom renewals, and potentially delay decommissioning of Broadcom CA products.
risks.mitigation: Secure extra funding and commercial terms to engage vendor SMEs for the anticipated duration of migration activities and incorporate these resource needs into the business case and procurement plan so that SME timelines align with the migration roadmap.

risks.title: Production disruption to customer-facing products during migration from Broadcom CA to IBM
risks.description: Loraine highlighted that the migration will "interrupt the production of products that we sell to customers". Moving from Broadcom CA tools to IBM equivalents (including schedulers, automation, storage management, and Content Manager OnDemand) on an already stable mainframe environment introduces a risk of outages, performance degradation, or operational errors affecting production workloads that generate customer-facing products.
risks.impact_description: If migration activities (e.g., scheduler cutovers, automation rule changes, storage/HSM transitions, CA View to CMOD migrations) destabilize the environment, TR could experience failed or delayed batch jobs, missed deliveries, or degraded performance in systems that produce customer-facing products. This would harm customer satisfaction, could breach SLAs, and may require emergency rollback or dual-running of tools, increasing operational overhead and costs.
risks.mitigation: Design and execute a phased migration with robust testing, including parallel runs for scheduler and automation changes, clear back-out plans, and carefully planned implementation windows that minimize customer impact. Leverage IBM's heavy assist to ensure experienced SMEs lead critical cutovers, and require detailed completion and acceptance criteria in the SOW. Coordinate with business stakeholders to identify critical production periods and avoid high-risk changes during those windows.

risks.title: Replacement vendor coverage gaps for Broadcom CA product capabilities
risks.description: There is a risk that no single alternative vendor will be able to cover all existing Broadcom CA product capabilities. This could result in functional gaps, the need for multiple vendors to cover the current Broadcom CA footprint, or acceptance of reduced functionality compared to the status quo.
risks.impact_description: If no single replacement vendor can cover all Broadcom CA product capabilities, the project may be forced to adopt a multi-vendor toolset or accept functionality gaps. This could increase integration complexity, operational overhead, and total cost of ownership, and may reduce system stability or supportability compared to the current Broadcom CA environment.
risks.mitigation: Identify which vendor is the best option for each specific Broadcom CA product and design a multi-vendor strategy where necessary, ensuring that critical capabilities are covered and integration implications are understood before making a final recommendation.

risks.title: Not selecting any vendor due to high cost
risks.description: There is a risk that the project may conclude without selecting an alternative vendor. Initial proposals received from prospective vendors indicate that replacement solutions carry a higher total cost than the organization's current Broadcom licensing expenditure, which may result in a decision to retain the existing Broadcom agreement. Recent discussion highlighted that if TR walks away from Broadcom VMware business and does not proceed with an alternative vendor, Broadcom may respond with aggressive pricing on mainframe renewals, potentially driving costs to several times current levels.
risks.impact_description: If no alternative vendor is selected to replace the Broadcom CA tools, the organization may need to continue under the existing Broadcom agreement. In that scenario, Broadcom could significantly increase mainframe tooling prices at renewal, particularly if TR ends the VMware relationship. Rajesh noted that the price could be "maybe four times" current levels, far exceeding earlier assumptions of up to a 150% increase. This would substantially increase annual licensing costs, undermine the project's cost-avoidance objective, and create long-term budget pressure.
risks.mitigation: Continue negotiating with alternative vendors (notably IBM) to secure a commercially viable fixed-fee and licensing proposal, while also engaging Broadcom to seek early visibility and commitments on renewal pricing. Factor potential Broadcom retaliation into financial scenarios presented to executives, so that the cost of doing nothing is clearly understood. Use the IBM proposal and its cost profile to strengthen TR's negotiating position with Broadcom and to support a timely go/no-go decision.

risks.title: Increased mainframe MLC consumption and/or performance constraints from new IBM tooling
risks.description: Replacing Broadcom CA tooling with IBM products may change workload characteristics on the Z hardware (Z15/ZOS), potentially driving higher MLC consumption or pushing CPU utilization beyond current headroom. Theo noted that current usage is close to the capacity of the two machines, so additional load from new tools (e.g., HSM and other IBM components) could either increase monthly MLC costs or cause performance degradation (slower batch and online processing).
risks.impact_description: If IBM tooling materially increases CPU and MLC consumption while the environment is already near capacity, the mainframe may experience slower processing times and potential SLA breaches for business-critical workloads. Higher sustained utilization could also push MLC usage above the prepaid bucket, increasing monthly license charges to IBM. This would erode the expected cost-avoidance benefits of moving off Broadcom CA and could require unplanned capacity optimization work or hardware/contract adjustments.
risks.mitigation: Engage IBM's mainframe and MLC experts to analyze projected workload and MLC impact for the proposed tooling set before contract execution; validate assumptions using existing utilization data and IBM's sizing tools; identify optimization opportunities in current workloads as part of migration planning; and establish monitoring and thresholds to detect and address any unexpected MLC or CPU increases early during migration phases.

risks.title: Ambiguity in IBM 'heavy assist' scope and fixed-fee coverage
risks.description: The IBM proposal describes optional 'heavy assist' activities and uses vague language around what IBM will actually perform versus what is client responsibility, as well as how heavy assist hours relate to the fixed-fee engagement. The team is concerned that ambiguous wording could allow IBM to limit their responsibility or declare scope creep, leaving TR staff to perform more migration work than expected or to incur additional time-and-materials charges.
risks.impact_description: If the heavy assist scope and fixed-fee limits are not clearly defined and agreed, IBM may later argue that specific tasks (e.g., automation rules migration, storage allocations, scheduler configuration) are out of scope or exceed heavy assist hours. This could force TR's small mainframe team to absorb additional migration effort, increasing schedule risk and stretching already limited resources, or require additional unplanned spend for change orders and T&M work. The result would be extended timelines, higher costs, and potential delays in replacing Broadcom CA tools before renewal.
risks.mitigation: Clarify with IBM, prior to contract signature, exactly which products and activities are covered by heavy assist, how responsibilities are allocated in the RACI, and how any heavy assist overages are handled under the fixed-fee model. Ensure the final SOW explicitly lists covered tasks for automation, scheduling, and storage migrations, defines what constitutes scope creep, and confirms that IBM accepts delivery risk within the fixed fee. Capture these clarifications in the contract and avoid signing until the language removes the current ambiguity.

assumptions.title: IBM will be selected as the preferred replacement vendor and engaged under a fixed-fee model starting around May 1, 2026
assumptions.description: During the IBM/BMC proposal review, the team agreed to "focus then for now on IBM", noted that IBM's 7-year proposal (~US$12.5M) is materially better than BMC's 5-year proposal (~US$16M+), and discussed IBM starting May 1 with a fixed-fee engagement. Planning discussions about heavy assist scope, responsibilities in the RACI, and risk messaging to the sponsor are being framed around IBM as the preferred option.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Cost comparison (IBM ~US$12.5M over 7 years versus BMC ~US$16M+ over 5 years), richer detail in IBM's heavy assist and SOW documentation, perceived greater level of support from IBM SMEs, and the need to mitigate Broadcom renewal risk with a viable alternative vendor.
assumptions.validity_explanation: IBM currently offers the most favorable combination of price, fixed-fee risk-sharing, and detailed migration support. However, executive sponsorship, procurement approvals, and final contract negotiations are still pending, so the selection is not yet confirmed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Maintain a viable BMC option and updated Broadcom pricing scenarios so that, if IBM is not approved, the team can quickly pivot to either negotiating a reduced-scope BMC engagement or strengthening Broadcom renewal negotiations, minimizing delay to the overall decision timeline.
assumptions.validation_method: Formal executive go/no-go decision and vendor selection, supported by the recommendation presentation to executives and any subsequent procurement approvals.

assumptions.title: IBM has proven migration tools and will provide heavy assist for scheduler, automation, and storage migrations
assumptions.description: Based on the heavy assist and SOW documents, as well as team review, it is assumed that IBM has established tools (e.g., OMA, migration utilities), methodologies, and experienced SMEs to support key migrations (scheduler, automation, storage/HSM, CA View to CMOD) and will actively provide heavy assist in these areas under the fixed-fee engagement.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Theo and others observed that IBM has already provided detailed activity lists, RACIs, and workstream descriptions, and appears to have performed similar migrations before with dedicated tooling. The team expressed confidence that IBM will do the bulk of the work in critical areas, with TR contributing where appropriate.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The level of detail in IBM’s proposal and the existence of specialized tools and documented methodologies suggest prior experience and reusable assets. However, the team has not yet executed a pilot or seen the tools in use on TR’s environment, so some uncertainty remains about actual execution quality and support depth.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If due diligence reveals gaps in IBM tooling or support, adjust the migration plan to include additional internal resourcing, training, or supplementary vendor engagements, and negotiate contract terms that explicitly cover any identified gaps (e.g., additional IBM responsibilities or service levels).
assumptions.validation_method: Further technical due diligence with IBM SMEs, clarification of heavy assist scope in the finalized SOW, and potentially reference checks or pilot activities to confirm tool capabilities and support levels.

issues.title: Mainframe resources constraint
issues.description: Given that the Mainframe team currently consists of three resources, this project's scope should be expanded to include a staffing assessment and recommendations for team augmentation — whether through internal hiring or external contractor engagement — to ensure adequate capacity to support the migration activities that will fall under TR's responsibility.
issues.impact_assessment: Delay on completing the replacement of the tools that will translate on penalties from Broadcom or stopping the support for existing tools
issues.dependencies_affecting: TR staff required to support migration activities
issues.resolution: A staffing assessment may need to be initiated to identify resource gaps, followed by internal recruitment efforts and/or engagement with external contractors to obtain service quotations for Mainframe migration support.

decisions.title: Select IBM as preferred vendor over BMC for Broadcom CA replacement
decisions.description: Working-team decision to proceed with IBM as the preferred vendor for Broadcom CA mainframe tooling replacement, and to focus evaluation, heavy-assist review, and draft statement of work discussions on IBM rather than BMC. IBM's proposal is a 7-year engagement at approximately US$12.5M with a fixed-fee migration component (~US$5.2M), detailed heavy-assist activities (including scheduler, automation, storage, HSM, CA Disk to DFSMS/HSM migration, and CA View to Content Manager OnDemand), and a clearer RACI assigning IBM responsibility/accountability for most critical migration tasks.
decisions.rationale: IBM offers a lower overall cost than BMC (IBM ~US$12.5M over 7 years vs BMC ~US$16M over 5 years), a fixed-fee migration engagement that reduces delivery risk, more detailed and mature migration methodology and tooling (e.g., OMA automation conversion and scheduling database conversion tools, predefined workstreams for CA View to CMOD and CA1 to DFSMS RMM), and heavier IBM responsibility in heavy-assist/RACI for critical areas (scheduler, automation, storage). The team perceives IBM as providing more hands-on migration support, which mitigates TR resource constraints and reduces implementation risk compared to BMC.
decisions.options_considered: 1) IBM fixed-fee proposal with heavy assist and detailed SOW; 2) BMC proposal (~US$16M over 5 years, lighter on migration assistance and tools, with customers building more of their own tooling); 3) Remaining on Broadcom CA with anticipated significant price increases.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Related risks: "Not selecting any vendor due to high cost"; "Replacement vendor coverage gaps for Broadcom CA product capabilities"; "Broadcom CA products not fully replaced before contract renewal date"; "Extended reliance on vendor SMEs for Broadcom CA migration".

## Executive Summary

ExaCS TaxOne Production Build is delivering an enterprise‑grade, cloud‑native Oracle database environment on Oracle Exadata Cloud Service on AWS to host TaxOne’s most critical database workloads. This matters because it will improve scalability, performance, and operational resilience while maintaining strong security and compliance controls to support TaxOne’s long‑term modernization goals.

The single production build milestone remains on plan, with a planned end date of 15 Jun 2026 and on track as of 21 May 2026. The production infrastructure build is in progress, with completion required before the TaxOne application team can onboard databases through the normal BAU process.

Overall status is Green, driven by the production build remaining on schedule with no variance against the 15 Jun 2026 target.

## Path to Green

Team is on-track for delivery. All infrastructure is built. The week of May 25th will be focused on data movement and migration readiness. App cutover scheduled for the weekend of 30 May.

## Milestones

-   Project start and initiation completed on 26 Mar 2026.
    
-   ExaCS production infrastructure build for TaxOne completed and ready for database onboarding by 15 Jun 2026.
    
-   Project closure and transition of the ExaCS production environment to BAU operations by 15 Jun 2026.
