latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Passwordless Authentication and Ping Migration is delivering a modern, phishing-resistant authentication model using Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2 passkeys, and Entra ID, while deprecating traditional password-based flows. This strengthens enterprise security, prepares for Ping ESSO decommissioning, and improves user experience across Windows, macOS, AVD, and Microsoft 365 logins.

The program is in early execution within the planned 01 Jan 2026 to 18 Dec 2026 delivery window, with 13 milestones defined and all currently in Planned status and no recorded schedule variance. Foundational governance is in place, with 5 risks, 5 key dependencies, and 8 major assumptions documented and tracked to protect the December 2026 delivery constraint.

Overall status is Green, driven by clear 2026 schedule constraints and early risk and dependency management in place, even though delivery work has not yet started on the dated milestones.

## Path to Green

The primary RAID mitigation focus is on the high-priority “dependency delays impacting timeline and rollout” risk, with actions to maintain a detailed dependency register, integrate it into steering governance, and resequence work if vendor contracts, resource allocations, or approvals slip against the December 2026 constraint.

## Milestones

- Production rollout completed for passwordless authentication and Entra-based application migrations by 18 Dec 2026.  
- Program delivery complete, with deployment of phishing-resistant passwordless authentication, phased migration of Ping-integrated applications to Entra ID, and establishment of the enterprise reference authentication architecture by 18 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Hybrid Entra ID and on-prem trust misconfigurations
risks.description: There is a risk that misconfigurations in the hybrid trust relationship between Microsoft Entra ID and on-premises Active Directory will cause authentication failures or inconsistent behavior.
risks.impact_description: If hybrid trust between Entra ID and on-prem AD is misconfigured, users may experience authentication failures, inconsistent sign-in experiences, or security policy gaps. This can disrupt business operations, increase incident volumes to support teams, delay rollout waves, and potentially introduce security exposure due to incorrect trust or synchronization settings.
risks.mitigation: Define and implement hardened reference configurations for hybrid trust; perform configuration reviews and peer validation; leverage non-production environments for extensive testing before production changes; create rollback plans; monitor authentication logs and health signals during and after changes to quickly detect and fix misconfigurations.

risks.title: Enrolment and policy enforcement challenges if systems are offline
risks.description: There is a risk that device enrolment into passwordless authentication (e.g., WHfB, FIDO2/passkeys) and enforcement of related policies will be difficult or fail when systems are offline or have intermittent connectivity.
risks.impact_description: If offline or intermittently connected systems cannot be properly enrolled or have policies enforced, affected users may be unable to authenticate using passwordless methods, leading to increased support calls, degraded user experience, and potential reliance on weaker, legacy authentication paths. This could slow adoption, require additional remediation work, and undermine the project’s security and experience goals.
risks.mitigation: Design enrolment and policy workflows that account for offline scenarios; leverage staged enrolment windows where users are required to connect via VPN or on-premise networks; provide fallback enrolment options and clear user communications; monitor enrolment success metrics to identify and remediate offline-related issues early.

risks.title: Legacy or unpatched laptops lacking TPM support
risks.description: There is a risk that legacy or unpatched laptops without Trusted Platform Module (TPM) capability, or with incompatible firmware/OS levels, will not support Windows Hello for Business and other passwordless mechanisms.
risks.impact_description: If a significant portion of laptops lack TPM support or required patch levels, affected users may be unable to use passwordless authentication. This would necessitate maintaining legacy password-based flows for longer, increase complexity in support and policy management, and limit risk reduction benefits. It may also drive unplanned hardware refresh or remediation costs and could jeopardize meeting the December 2026 delivery and benefit realization timeline.
risks.mitigation: Conduct early inventory and health assessment of endpoints to identify TPM capability and patch levels; coordinate with hardware and endpoint management teams to plan remediation or replacement; define minimum device standards for passwordless participation; prioritize refresh for high-risk user groups; provide temporary exceptions with defined timelines for non-compliant devices.

risks.title: Dependency delays impacting timeline and rollout
risks.description: There is a risk that delays in key dependencies—such as vendor contracts, resource allocation, business approvals, workshops, or governance sign-offs—will impact the overall timeline and rollout of the passwordless authentication and Ping migration program.
risks.impact_description: If critical dependencies are delayed, the program may miss key milestones, including pilot exit, production rollout, and Ping ESSO decommissioning readiness. This could prevent delivery by December 2026, delay realization of security and operational benefits, increase costs due to extended dual-platform operations, and require re-planning or scope adjustments.
risks.mitigation: Maintain and regularly review a detailed dependency register; assign owners to each dependency; integrate dependency status into governance reporting; escalate delays through program steering committees; resequence work where possible to reduce critical path impact; develop contingency plans such as interim solutions or adjusted rollout waves if key dependencies slip.

risks.title: Vendor-managed laptop misconfigurations causing authentication failures
risks.description: There is a risk that laptops managed by external vendors or third parties will be misconfigured (e.g., group policy, device management, security baselines), leading to passwordless authentication failures or inconsistent behavior.
risks.impact_description: If vendor-managed laptops are misconfigured, impacted users may be unable to enroll in or use passwordless authentication, leading to authentication failures, increased incidents, and degraded user experience. This can slow adoption for specific populations, require additional coordination effort with vendors, and potentially necessitate exceptions or delays in rollout for those groups.
risks.mitigation: Engage vendors early to align on configuration requirements for WHfB, FIDO2, and platform SSO; provide clear configuration guides and test scripts; include vendor-managed devices in POC and pilot testing; establish validation checklists and sign-off for vendor-managed configurations prior to wider rollout; define escalation paths for rapid remediation of misconfigurations.

assumptions.title: Microsoft Entra ID E5 P2 licenses are approved, funded, and rolled out as planned
assumptions.description: The project assumes that Microsoft Entra ID E5 P2 licenses will be fully approved, funded, and deployed to the required user populations according to the planned schedule.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Passwordless authentication and advanced identity capabilities for this program depend on Entra ID E5 P2 features being available to target users.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current strategic plans call for consolidation into Microsoft Entra ID, making license acquisition a planned investment. However, funding and rollout are still subject to approval processes and execution by procurement and operations.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If licenses are delayed or reduced, adjust rollout waves to prioritize licensed users, seek temporary license reallocations, rebaseline the schedule, or evaluate alternative technical approaches that use currently available licensing.
assumptions.validation_method: Review licensing agreements, purchase orders, and deployment plans with licensing and IT operations teams; confirm license assignment to target user groups.

assumptions.title: Stakeholders actively participate in workshops and design reviews
assumptions.description: The program assumes that key business, security, and technical stakeholders will actively participate in workshops and design review sessions.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Effective solution design and adoption depend on stakeholder input and alignment on requirements, use cases, and change impacts.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Stakeholders are accountable for identity and security outcomes and are expected to support strategic initiatives; however, competing priorities and bandwidth constraints could reduce their participation.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Escalate lack of participation through governance channels; schedule additional targeted sessions; provide asynchronous review options; adjust timelines or scope for areas where stakeholder input is missing.
assumptions.validation_method: Track attendance and participation for planned workshops and design sessions; confirm sign-offs for key design artifacts.

assumptions.title: Vendor support from Microsoft, Ping, and implementation partners will be available
assumptions.description: The program assumes that Microsoft, Ping, and implementation partners will provide timely technical and project support throughout design, POC, migration, and rollout.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project relies on vendor expertise for complex identity integrations, troubleshooting, and best practice guidance.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The organization typically maintains support contracts with strategic vendors, but responsiveness and availability of specialized resources can vary with demand and contract scope.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Escalate through vendor management; secure additional support packages if needed; build internal expertise to reduce reliance on external support; adjust timelines for complex integration tasks.
assumptions.validation_method: Review and confirm support contracts, SLAs, and engagement plans with vendor management; validate assigned technical contacts and escalation paths.

assumptions.title: Target applications are compatible with the new authentication model
assumptions.description: The project assumes that target applications designated for migration from Ping to Microsoft Entra ID will be compatible with modern, passwordless-capable authentication protocols and configurations.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The migration and passwordless rollout plan depends on being able to integrate target applications with Entra ID using supported standards and configurations.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Existing Ping integrations indicate some level of standards support, but differences between Ping and Entra ID implementations and passwordless requirements may reveal compatibility gaps.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Reprioritize migration waves based on technical readiness; plan remediation or modernization projects for incompatible applications; define exceptions where legacy authentication must remain temporarily.
assumptions.validation_method: Perform application discovery and technical assessments; review protocol support and integration guides; conduct integration tests in non-production for each application or application group.

assumptions.title: Technical decisions and outcomes are documented by assigned architects
assumptions.description: The project assumes that assigned architects will systematically document technical decisions, designs, and outcomes throughout the program.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Sustainable operations, future enhancements, and consistent implementation depend on clear documentation of architecture and design decisions.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Architects have assigned responsibilities but may face time pressure from parallel initiatives, which can deprioritize documentation work without clear governance.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Enforce documentation as a gate for approvals and go-live decisions; allocate specific time and ownership for documentation tasks; provide templates and review cycles to make documentation more efficient.
assumptions.validation_method: Review architecture repositories and project documentation checkpoints; confirm completion of agreed design documents and decision logs.

assumptions.title: Mandatory training will be delivered via Workday
assumptions.description: The program assumes that mandatory user training related to passwordless authentication and new login processes will be delivered through Workday.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project plan includes broad training and communication, and Workday is the established platform for delivering mandatory training to employees.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Workday is the standard enterprise training platform, making it a logical choice for this program, though coordination with learning teams is still required.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Workday cannot be used or is delayed, leverage alternative channels such as internal learning portals, webinars, documentation, and targeted communications; track completion via other tools until Workday delivery is possible.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm training plan and course setup with the learning and development team; verify that Workday courses are created, assigned, and monitored for completion.

assumptions.title: Ping contract remains active until Q3 2027 with interim solutions as required
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the Ping contract will remain active until Q3 2027 and that interim solutions can be used as needed during the migration period.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The phased migration of applications from Ping to Entra ID relies on continued availability of Ping services to avoid forced, high-risk cutovers.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Contract details provide an expected end date beyond the program timeline, but contracts can be renegotiated, terminated, or altered based on business decisions.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If contract continuity is at risk, prioritize migration of critical applications earlier, negotiate short-term extensions, and develop contingency access solutions; re-baseline the migration plan to reduce reliance on Ping before contract end.
assumptions.validation_method: Review contractual terms and renewal dates with vendor management and legal; monitor any changes to contract status; confirm that timelines align with the migration roadmap.

dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Lack of timely sign-offs will block pilot exit, production rollout, and Ping ESSO decommissioning readiness, risking failure to meet the December 2026 delivery constraint.
dependencies.mitigation: Engage compliance and governance stakeholders early, share design and POC outcomes promptly, and track sign-off status through program governance.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

TAAP Print Accelerate is delivering a modernized, SAP-based sales and ordering experience for Thomson Reuters Print products across digital and B2B channels, enabling Unison sunset and improved revenue and customer satisfaction. The program reuses US Legal Print architecture and processes so Tax Print, ProView, and QuickFinder can operate on a harmonized lead-to-cash model.

All early-phase discovery, architecture, and design milestones through 31 May 2026 are baselined to complete within their original windows, with recorded schedule variance of zero days on these items and downstream build, test, and cutover dates remaining unchanged through the planned September 2026 go-live and hypercare period. Critical build-stage activities such as SAP WRP configuration, data migration execution, integration testing, and UAT are sequenced from 01 June 2026 to 22 August 2026 to support a 05 September 2026 cutover and 30 September 2026 stabilization.

Overall status is Amber, driven by unresolved EPM and data-pipeline dependencies that must be closed before build and test can proceed with confidence.

## Path to Green

The path to Green centers on closing those dependencies by 31 May 2026 by updating and socializing EPM timelines, securing approval to run QA EPM jobs multiple times, formally engaging the EDL and ETL teams on their required development and support effort, and progressing SAP and DMSS changes to introduce the TAAP product identifier and scale pricing support into EPM and downstream systems.

## Milestones

- Complete Discovery and Architecture Review, Conga Print Order Flow Separation, PreSales and QuickFinder PreOrder Solution Design, Third-Party Print Order Solution Design, and Renewal Opportunities Design by 29 May 2026.  
- Finish Historical Data Migration Scoping and Additional Customer Fields Analysis by 31 May 2026.  
- Complete Proview Entitlement Migration Architecture Direction and CUAS-to-SSP Migration Planning and SAP WRP Configuration and Build by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Finish Data Migration Execution (KS to GSI) by 15 Jul 2026 and complete Integration Testing across Conga, SAP WRP, PRISM/SSP, and Proview by 31 Jul 2026.  
- Complete User Acceptance Testing by 22 Aug 2026, execute Go-Live and Cutover between 01 Sep 2026 and 05 Sep 2026, and finish Post Go-Live Stabilization and Hypercare by 30 Sep 2026.

risks.title: Tax Print SAP-West orders require new bank account and GL routing
risks.description: Tax Print orders created in SAP for the West sales organization must be routed to a new bank account and general ledger in order to separate Tax Print financials from Legal under the same legal entity (company code 0010) and West sales org. This requires new bank account and GL configuration and ensuring that payments from all channels (Digital, sales reps, service reps, phone, etc.) are diverted into the new bank account. There is also a dependency on Stripe and other payment flows to support this routing.
risks.impact_description: If a new bank account and GL for Tax Print under the West sales org are not set up and payments are not correctly routed, Tax Print and U.S. Legal financials will remain commingled under the same company code and sales org. This could cause inaccurate financial separation for Tax vs Legal, complications in accounting and reporting, potential compliance issues, and may block or delay the planned migration of Unison TAAP Print orders into SAP-West. In addition, payments from digital, sales, service, and phone channels may continue to flow to the wrong bank account, requiring rework and manual corrections.
risks.mitigation: Follow the strategy to move Unison TAAP Print into the SAP West sales org with a decision to formally establish a new bank account and GL for Tax under the same West sales org. Configure the new bank account and GL in SAP as business configuration and ensure that payment routing for all channels, including Stripe-based payments, is updated so payments are diverted to the new Tax Print bank account.

milestones.name: Additional Customer Fields Analysis (200+ fields, KS to GSI, business impact & GSI Tech limitations)

actions.title: Validate Salesforce performance and automation options for QuickFinder promo code management
actions.description: Validate that Salesforce (order capture) can handle the volume and complexity of maintaining approximately 700 QuickFinder promotions updated three times per year, and investigate automation options (such as bulk upload scripts) for promo creation and updates, in support of Option 1 for promotion discount handling.

actions.title: Determine number of associations requiring royalty tracking for promo codes
actions.description: Identify and confirm the exact number of associations that require royalty tracking so the team can determine how many association-specific promo codes are needed for QuickFinder products and whether some codes can be consolidated.

actions.title: Walk through updated EPM timelines for TAAP Print sample products with stakeholders
actions.description: Review and walk stakeholders through the updated schedule for sample Tax Print, Proview, and QuickFinder product availability in EPM-T (EMX-QA), QA cutover readiness, and data cutover support, replacing the outdated dates currently listed in the dependency log.

actions.title: Obtain permission to run QA EPM jobs multiple times for sample data loads
actions.description: Seek and obtain stakeholder permission to run QA EPM jobs multiple times in April and May to pull data from BW, process it, and pass it to downstream applications (including EDL/EDW and GSI) for sample QA data across each product category, to support GSI and Digital build activities.

actions.title: Update SAP stories based on EPM intake 159006 for TAAP product identifier and scale pricing
actions.description: Review EPM intake 159006 ("EPM support of scale pricing for ZPRC and ZPRM and ZSSH") and update related SAP user stories to include the required TAAP product identifier and scale pricing logic so EPM can distinguish TAAP vs Legal products under the West sales organization.

actions.title: Schedule and conduct workshops with business to evaluate RIA Multi Quantity pricing model
actions.description: Organize and run workshop sessions with business stakeholders to review RIA Multi Quantity pricing files, understand how the existing Unison rate card logic works, and determine whether it is worthwhile to bring the RIA tiered pricing model (with potentially hundreds of promo codes) into SAP.

actions.title: Work with BillTrust on TAAP Print and U.S. Legal invoice layout changes
actions.description: Coordinate directly with BillTrust, the third-party vendor, to design and implement invoice layout changes for TAAP Print and U.S. Legal, including bank account details, legacy product code display, D&B number, return policy, and customer service contact information, based on the final invoice template decisions.

actions.title: Collaborate with BillTrust on configuration of separate or unified invoice templates
actions.description: Partner with BillTrust to configure the appropriate number of invoice templates (separate or unified) for TAAP Print and U.S. Legal based on decisions about bank accounts, product code display, D&B number, return policy, and customer support contacts.

actions.title: Capture TAAP Print vs U.S. Legal invoice template changes in cutover and communication plans
actions.description: Document invoice template changes, including any separate TAAP Print and U.S. Legal templates, in the change management plan and ensure these are reflected in business cutover tasks and customer communication plans.

actions.title: Share TAAP Print program timelines with the EDL team
actions.description: Provide the EDL team with the TAAP Print program timelines so they can evaluate development effort and ongoing support requirements for using EDL as the source system for Tax Print product data flowing from EPM to Salesforce and Digital eStore.

actions.title: Engage EDL team to assess development and support effort for TAAP Print data loads
actions.description: Formally engage the EDL team so they can evaluate the required development effort and ongoing support needed to use EDL as the source system for loading Tax Print product data from EPM into Salesforce (GSI, Conga) and the Digital eStore.

actions.title: Decide on new bank account and GL configuration for Tax Print orders in SAP West sales organization
actions.description: Architects must formalize the decision on creating a new bank account and general ledger account for Tax Print under the West sales organization, ensuring payments from all channels (Digital, sales reps, service reps, phone) are routed to the new account in support of moving Unison TAAP Print into SAP West.

actions.title: Update DMSS intake 159006 business logic for EPM support of TAAP scale pricing
actions.description: Revise and update the business logic in DMSS intake 159006 so that EPM can support scale pricing for TAAP-related pricing conditions (ZPRC, ZPRM, ZSSH), including the TAAP product identifier needed to distinguish TAAP vs Legal products in the West sales organization.

actions.description: Schedule and conduct SAP definition sessions covering Products, Pricing, Customers and Contacts, Orders and Subscriptions, Billing and AR, and Revenue Recognition models during the week of December 15 for the TAAP Print Accelerate project.

assumptions.title: US Legal Print architecture components can be reused for TAAP Print
assumptions.description: The project assumes it can reuse the established US Legal Print architecture components (SAP, Informatica, AEM, Conga, SFDC, DCP) for TAAP Print with limited changes.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Key solution principles emphasize reusing the US Legal Print architecture to accelerate delivery and minimize build and test effort.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Existing architecture is known and stable, but solution scaling to additional TAAP Print volumes and possibly different integration patterns has not yet been fully tested.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Prepare to scale infrastructure, introduce additional instances or services, or selectively adopt new components where reuse is not feasible, including timeline and budget adjustments as needed.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture review sessions, capacity and performance analysis, and validation that TAAP-specific requirements can be supported by existing components.

assumptions.title: TAAP Print will adopt and align with US Legal Print lead-to-cash processes
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that TAAP Print can adopt and align with the US Legal Print lead-to-cash processes from the start of the project, so that sales, renewals, and returns journeys follow the existing US Legal Print model.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project objective explicitly states that TAAP Print should adopt and align with US Legal Print’s lead-to-cash processes, leveraging an already defined and functioning model rather than designing a new one from scratch.
assumptions.validity_explanation: US Legal Print has an established lead-to-cash process that is intended to be reused; however, US Tax Print may have business process differences that could limit full alignment. Discovery work with stakeholders is planned to capture existing US Tax Print processes and compare them to US Legal processes to identify differences.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If alignment proves infeasible, define a variant TAAP-specific lead-to-cash process, update scope and timelines, and adjust design for order capture, billing, and revenue recognition to accommodate required deviations.
assumptions.validation_method: Detailed process discovery and comparison between existing US Tax Print and US Legal Print processes, followed by design reviews and stakeholder sign-off.

assumptions.title: TAAP Print store will launch by reusing features from the US Legal Print Store
assumptions.description: The project assumes that a store for TAAP Print products can be launched primarily by adopting and aligning features from the existing US Legal Print Store instead of designing a completely new storefront.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The high-level scope states that the outcome is to launch a store for TAAP Print products by adopting and aligning features from the US Legal Print Store, implying significant reuse.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The existing store already supports print products and a modern digital journey, but TAAP Print’s product catalog, pricing, and customer behavior may introduce new requirements that are not fully covered by current features.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Plan for additional customization sprints to build TAAP-specific features, adjust scope and timelines, and possibly de-scope lower-priority enhancements to maintain critical launch dates.
assumptions.validation_method: Technical and UX gap analysis between TAAP Print business requirements and existing US Legal Print Store capabilities, including design playbacks and stakeholder reviews.

assumptions.title: TAAP Print journeys will be seamless for both digital and rep-led channels on the target tech stack
assumptions.description: The project assumes that end-to-end digital and rep-led journeys for TAAP Print products can be delivered as seamless experiences on the chosen target technology stack.
assumptions.rationale_basis: A core project objective is to deliver seamless digital and rep-led journeys for TAAP Print products, which underpins revenue growth and customer experience improvements.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The existing technology stack has proven capable for similar use cases, but TAAP Print may introduce journey or integration complexities (e.g., renewals, returns, rep-specific workflows) that have not yet been fully validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Prioritize core flows (e.g., new sales and renewals) for optimization, provide interim manual support or process guidance for edge cases, and plan iterative enhancements post-launch to close usability gaps.
assumptions.validation_method: End-to-end journey design reviews, prototyping and demos, followed by user acceptance testing with both digital users and sales reps.

assumptions.title: Master and transaction data for TAAP Print will be accurate and clean on the target tech stack
assumptions.description: The project assumes that accurate and clean master and transactional data (products, pricing, customers, subscriptions, and related attributes) can be loaded and maintained on the target tech stack.
assumptions.rationale_basis: A stated objective is to have accurate and clean master and transaction data on the target tech stack, which is essential for correct ordering, billing, and analytics.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The project plans include ETL and migration processes, which can be designed to enforce data standards; however, the legacy data quality and complexity of mappings between Unison and SAP ecosystems are not yet fully validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Plan data cleansing activities, implement data quality rules and exception handling in ETL, schedule remediation cycles before go-live, and consider phased migration if full quality cannot be achieved at once.
assumptions.validation_method: Data profiling and quality checks on source and migrated data, ETL testing, reconciliation reports, and sign-off by data and business owners.

assumptions.title: One-time migration and ongoing real-time synchronization of Tax Print data is feasible
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that a one-time data migration and ongoing real-time synchronization of Tax Print products, pricing, assets, and related attributes can be implemented reliably.
assumptions.rationale_basis: High-level scope explicitly includes a one-time migration and ongoing real-time sync of Tax Print products, pricing, assets, and attributes as part of the solution approach.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Existing platform capabilities suggest that migration and sync are technically possible, but specific volumes, latency requirements, and legacy system constraints for TAAP Print are still being analyzed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Implement scheduled batch updates instead of strict real-time sync where acceptable, reduce scope of synchronized attributes if needed, and define clear operational procedures for handling sync failures and manual corrections.
assumptions.validation_method: Integration design, PoC or pilot sync between source and target systems, followed by performance and reliability testing of the migration and synchronization jobs.

assumptions.title: ETL processes for customer, contact, product, and subscription data will support project timelines and scope
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the required ETL processes for customer, contact, product, and subscription data can be designed, built, and run within the planned scope and timelines.
assumptions.rationale_basis: ETL for core data domains is explicitly listed in the high-level scope, indicating reliance on ETL to populate and maintain the target systems.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Reusable ETL patterns and tools exist, but TAAP-specific data models and mappings may be more complex than anticipated, and dependencies on upstream data sources could affect delivery.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Prioritize ETL for critical data entities first, introduce phased coverage for less critical attributes, and adjust launch scope if necessary to align with what ETL can reliably deliver.
assumptions.validation_method: ETL design reviews, build progress tracking, system and integration testing focused on data completeness and correctness.

assumptions.title: Conga CPQ will support order capture, validation, and SAP integration for TAAP Print
assumptions.description: The project assumes that Conga CPQ can be implemented or configured to handle TAAP Print order capture and validation and integrate orders correctly into SAP.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The high-level scope explicitly calls out implementation of Conga CPQ for order capture, validation, and SAP integration, making CPQ a central component of the solution.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Conga CPQ has been proven in a similar domain (US Legal Print), but TAAP Print products, pricing rules, and subscription logic may introduce additional complexity not yet validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Define a fallback approach using simplified CPQ configurations, reduce complexity of pricing and product rules for initial launch, or temporarily handle certain complex orders through manual processes while a longer-term solution is developed.
assumptions.validation_method: Solution design sessions, configuration and integration proof-of-concept for TAAP Print scenarios, and end-to-end testing of order flows into SAP.

assumptions.title: Order-to-cash, billing, and revenue recognition processes can be defined and enabled within project scope
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that OTC (Order to Cash) processes, billing, and revenue recognition models for TAAP Print can be defined and enabled in SAP within the project’s scope and timeframe.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The scope explicitly calls for definition and enablement of OTC processes, billing, and revenue recognition, and this is critical for the Unison sunset strategy.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Existing finance processes on SAP reduce the need to design from scratch, but TAAP-specific revenue recognition models, tax handling, or contract structures may require additional work and approvals.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Implement interim processes (e.g., partial automation with manual adjustments), limit initial launch to simpler products with straightforward revenue recognition, and phase in complex models later.
assumptions.validation_method: SAP definition sessions with Finance and business stakeholders, followed by configuration validation and test transactions through the full OTC cycle.

assumptions.title: Migrations can be orchestrated end-to-end to enforce data consistency and process alignment
assumptions.description: The project assumes that migrations can be orchestrated as end-to-end events to enforce data consistency and process alignment across all platforms involved in TAAP Print.
assumptions.rationale_basis: A key solution principle states that migrations will be orchestrated end-to-end to enforce data consistency and process alignment across platforms.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While the tools exist to support coordinated migrations, dependencies on legacy systems, business blackout windows, and multiple stakeholder groups may complicate execution.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Adopt phased or domain-based migrations with clear reconciliation checkpoints, and put in place temporary bridging integrations or manual reconciliation processes until full alignment is achieved.
assumptions.validation_method: Migration planning workshops, dry-run migrations in non-production environments, and reconciliation testing across platforms.

assumptions.title: Backend services and existing US Legal Print Store assets will be reusable to accelerate delivery
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that existing backend services and assets from the US Legal Print Store can be reused to reduce build and testing effort for TAAP Print.
assumptions.rationale_basis: A solution principle explicitly states that delivery will be accelerated by reusing backend services and existing US Legal Print Store assets to minimize build and test effort.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Existing components are functionally relevant, but may require adaptation or extension for TAAP-specific data structures and workflows, which may reduce the degree of direct reuse.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Plan for incremental customization of services and assets, allocate additional development capacity for non-reusable areas, and re-prioritize lower-impact features if timelines become constrained.
assumptions.validation_method: Technical assessment of existing services and assets against TAAP requirements, followed by limited-scope reuse PoCs and integration tests.

assumptions.title: Estimated 10% productivity savings in SDLC, migrations, and QA will be achieved
assumptions.description: The project assumes that by reusing architecture, services, and assets, it will achieve an estimated 10% productivity savings across SDLC, migrations, and QA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The solution principles explicitly state an estimated 10% target productivity savings based on reuse and alignment with US Legal Print.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The 10% figure appears to be an estimate rather than a measured commitment, and reuse may expose unforeseen integration or adaptation work that erodes expected savings.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Adjust resource and budget plans based on actual velocity, de-scope non-critical enhancements if necessary, and communicate revised productivity expectations to stakeholders.
assumptions.validation_method: Track effort and velocity metrics against baseline estimates during design, build, and test phases; compare to historical data from US Legal Print projects.

assumptions.title: Effective change management will support rep-led and digital sales experience changes
assumptions.description: The project assumes that change management activities will be effective enough to support the transition to new rep-led and digital sales experiences for TAAP Print.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Effective change management is listed as an objective, indicating reliance on organizational readiness and adoption to realize the benefits of the new solution.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Governance and stakeholder roles are identified, but detailed change management planning and execution have not yet been demonstrated for this specific initiative.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Increase investment in training and communications, deploy additional coaching and floor support for reps, and iterate on the user experience based on feedback to improve adoption.
assumptions.validation_method: Stakeholder engagement tracking, training completion, feedback sessions, and early adoption metrics post-launch.

assumptions.title: SAP definition and Data & Analytics sessions will occur in the planned timeframe
assumptions.description: The project assumes that SAP Definition sessions (products, pricing, customers and contacts, orders and subscriptions, billing and AR, revenue recognition models) and Data & Analytics sessions (ECM/X, EPM, EDL) will take place in the week of December 15, enabling timely design decisions.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The next steps explicitly schedule SAP and Data & Analytics sessions for the week of December 15, implying dependencies on these sessions for definition work.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Core stakeholders are known, but scheduling conflicts or competing priorities may affect timely participation and decision-making.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Reschedule sessions promptly with clear escalation to governance forums, use smaller decision-making groups if full attendance is not possible, and document decisions asynchronously where needed to avoid blocking subsequent work.
assumptions.validation_method: Meeting scheduling and attendance tracking, plus confirmation that agreed outcomes (requirements, decisions, definitions) are documented and signed off.

assumptions.title: Governance structures will function as designed to manage RAIDs and change control
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the defined strategic, operational, tactical, and core governance levels will meet at the planned cadence and effectively manage RAIDs, change control, budget, and milestones.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The governance slide specifies multiple levels of review (strategic monthly, operational weekly, tactical daily) with explicit agendas including RAIDs and change control.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The framework is sound on paper, but its effectiveness depends on consistent participation, timely decision-making, and follow-through by all parties.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: Escalate governance gaps to executive sponsors, adjust meeting cadences or formats to improve effectiveness, and assign clear ownership for stalled decisions or unresolved RAIDs.
assumptions.validation_method: Tracking of meeting cadence, attendance, and decisions; periodic review of RAID logs and change control outcomes against governance expectations.

issues.title: QuickFinder promotion discount handling approach and system constraints
issues.description: The TAAP QuickFinder product category is being migrated from Unison to SAP and front-office systems such as Conga and Digital. QuickFinder uses numerous promotions and discounts throughout the year. The team must decide how to manage these discounts—whether to maintain discounts directly in order capture (Salesforce), tie them to promotions in SAP, or rely on manual discounting by sales representatives—while addressing administrative workload, technical feasibility, reporting needs, and association-specific royalty tracking.
issues.impact_assessment: Managing hundreds of QuickFinder promotions, each updated multiple times annually, poses a significant administrative and technical burden. If handled incorrectly, it could overload Salesforce/order capture, create data quality issues, complicate reporting, and jeopardize timely and accurate royalty payments for associations. The decision on where discounts are maintained (order capture vs SAP vs manual) directly affects system complexity, workload for the order capture and master data teams, and the reliability of promo code-to-discount mappings.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Salesforce order capture system, SAP promotions configuration, Master Data Operations team updates, association royalty tracking processes, and potential automation tooling for bulk promo updates.
issues.resolution: The team has selected Option 1 as the preferred approach: maintain promotions in SAP and keep the discount values in the order capture system (Salesforce), with promo code and discount passed into SAP. This approach minimizes SAP development work and aligns with current U.S. Legal processes. Resolution is contingent on confirming Salesforce performance and technical feasibility and on implementing automation for bulk promo creation and updates, as well as clarifying association-specific royalty tracking requirements.

dependencies.title: TAAP Print store depends on US Legal Print Store features and assets
dependencies.description: The outcome of the project is to launch a store for TAAP Print products by adopting and aligning features from the US Legal Print Store, creating a dependency on those features and assets being available and adaptable.

owner.name: Digital product leads for Print (including Marc Chalifoux and Jen Manwarren)

dependencies.dependent_on: Existing US Legal Print Store feature set, UI components, and assets
dependencies.consumer: TAAP Print digital store implementation team
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Additional design and development effort to create new features for TAAP Print, risking schedule slippage and increased costs.
dependencies.mitigation: Prioritize critical features for reuse, and plan incremental development of TAAP-specific features if direct reuse is not possible.

dependencies.title: TAAP Print sample products availability and EPM code readiness for QA
dependencies.description: Availability of sample Tax Print products (Print, Proview, QuickFinder) in EPM-T (EMX-QA), readiness of EPM code for QA cutover, and data cutover support from SAP-TRX to EMX-QA, including running EPM jobs to pull data from BW and push it to downstream systems (EDL/EDW, GSI) multiple times for QA purposes.
dependencies.dependent_on: EPM team delivery of updated QA schedules, EPM-T (EMX-QA) environment availability, BW data feeds, and approval to run QA EPM jobs multiple times.
dependencies.consumer: TAAP Print program, GSI team, Digital teams, and QA testers relying on sample data for build and testing.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays in EPM sample product availability and QA job runs would hinder GSI and Digital teams’ build and test phases, potentially delaying integration testing and overall project timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Update the outdated timeline, obtain permission to run QA EPM jobs multiple times in April and May, and coordinate closely with EPM and BW teams to ensure repeated QA data loads for each product category.

dependencies.title: TAAP product identifier in SAP for EPM and scale pricing support
dependencies.description: EPM requires a product identifier in SAP to distinguish TAAP products from Legal products since both reside under the West sales organization. This identifier is necessary to configure step/scale pricing in EPM for QF-RIA products so that pricing can flow correctly into Conga and the eStore.
dependencies.dependent_on: EPM intake 159006 ("EPM support of scale pricing for ZPRC and ZPRM and ZSSH"), SAP configuration to include the TAAP product identifier and support scale pricing, and DMSS intake business logic updates.
dependencies.consumer: EPM team (including Nick Lavely), Conga, eStore, and downstream pricing consumers for TAAP products.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a clear TAAP product identifier and scale pricing configuration, EPM cannot correctly distinguish TAAP vs Legal products, which would jeopardize accurate step pricing for QF-RIA products, leading to incorrect pricing in Conga and the eStore and potential revenue and customer satisfaction impacts.
dependencies.mitigation: Progress EPM intake 159006, update DMSS business logic, and implement SAP stories such as user story 1249911 to ensure the product identifier is available and propagated to EPM and downstream systems.

dependencies.title: RIA Multi Quantity pricing model decision and implementation for TAAP
dependencies.description: As part of TAAP requirements, the Digital team identified the RIA Multi Quantity pricing model used in the tax store, where the per-book cost decreases as order quantity increases. This pricing is currently controlled by a rate card in Unison. The future state must determine whether and how to bring this RIA tiered pricing model into SAP, potentially involving hundreds of promo codes.
dependencies.dependent_on: Workshops with business to review RIA pricing files, architecture and SAP design decisions on tiered pricing implementation, and potential configuration of promo codes in SAP and EPM.
dependencies.consumer: Digital tax store team, SAP pricing configuration team, and EPM team responsible for pricing models.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the RIA pricing model decision and implementation are delayed, the tax store may not support the desired tiered pricing at go-live, potentially impacting revenue, discount strategies, and customer expectations.
dependencies.mitigation: Hold dedicated workshop sessions with business stakeholders to understand current RIA rate card logic and evaluate whether to implement tiered pricing in SAP and EPM, balancing complexity, number of promo codes, and business value.

dependencies.title: Kits vs sets configuration decision for TAAP products in SAP
dependencies.description: Clarification of whether to create Kits or only Sets in SAP for TAAP products (Print, Proview, QuickFinder). During business grooming, it was discussed that there is no need to create Kits in SAP and that only Sets will be created for all products.
dependencies.dependent_on: Business architecture agreement and confirmation that only Sets are needed in SAP for all TAAP product types.
dependencies.consumer: SAP configuration team and product setup teams responsible for TAAP products in SAP.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Uncertainty about Kits vs Sets could delay SAP product configuration and downstream integration, risking schedule slippage for TAAP product migration.
dependencies.mitigation: Document and confirm the agreement from business grooming sessions that only Sets will be created in SAP, ensuring all teams align their configuration and testing activities accordingly.

dependencies.title: KS to GSI data migration for last 5 years of Sales history
dependencies.description: Migration and availability of sales history data (last 5 years) from KS to GSI or at least into EDL so that Print business and sales reps can view historical sales to drive revenue by targeting customers who purchased in the past but have not renewed. Future reporting and analytical use is noted but is not strictly part of TAAP Print scope.
dependencies.dependent_on: Confirmation that EDL has up-to-date sales history data and decisions on whether and how to load the last 5 years of KS sales data into EDL and/or GSI.
dependencies.consumer: Print business stakeholders, sales representatives, and reporting/analytics users needing historical sales visibility.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed:
If historical sales data is not available by the time TAAP Print goes live, sales reps may lack visibility into customers who previously purchased but did not renew, reducing opportunities for upsell/renewal and impacting revenue.
Future reporting and analytics use cases may also be constrained.
dependencies.mitigation: Verify existing sales history availability in EDL, and if present, leverage EDL instead of GSI for near-term needs; longer-term reporting and analytics can be planned outside the immediate TAAP Print scope.

dependencies.title: Use of EDL as source system for TAAP Tax Print data loads from EPM
dependencies.description: For the migration of Tax Print and ProView products from Unison to SAP, data will flow SAP → SAP-BW → EPM → EDL → Salesforce (GSI, Conga) and the Digital eStore. The Architecture team has recommended using EDL as the source system for loading Tax Print product data from EPM into downstream systems. The EDL team needs to evaluate the required development effort and ongoing support.
dependencies.dependent_on: Engagement with the EDL team to assess development and support needs, and alignment with overall TAAP Print program timelines.
dependencies.consumer: Salesforce (GSI, Conga), Digital eStore, EPM, and TAAP Print migration program.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If EDL engagement and required development are delayed, the data pipeline from EPM to Salesforce and the Digital eStore may not be ready in time, risking delays to go-live and potentially impacting sales and customer experience.
dependencies.mitigation: Share TAAP Print program timelines with the EDL team, formally engage them to assess effort and support, and plan EDL development activities in alignment with program milestones.

decisions.title: Creation of new bank account and GL for Tax Print orders in SAP West sales organization
decisions.description: The Tax Print business requires a new bank account and general ledger (GL) under company code 0010 and the West sales organization to separate Tax Print financials from Legal. Payments from all channels (Digital, sales reps, service reps, phone) for TAAP Tax Print orders created in SAP (West sales org) would be routed to this new bank account. This is a business configuration change that supports moving Unison TAAP Print into SAP West.
decisions.rationale: Separating Tax Print financials from Legal within the same legal entity is necessary for clearer financial reporting and alignment with business requirements. Routing all channel payments into a dedicated bank account ensures consistency and control over Tax Print financial flows when transitioning from Unison to SAP West.
decisions.options_considered:
Maintain a shared bank account and GL for both Tax Print and Legal vs create a dedicated Tax Print bank account and GL under the same West sales organization; implications include remit information differences on invoices and alignment with the broader Unison-to-SAP migration strategy.
There is also a dependency on Stripe for routing payments across channels.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Risk R001 (TAAP Tax Print orders routing to new bank account); dependencies on Stripe and SAP configuration for bank and GL setup.

decisions.title: Invoice template strategy for TAAP Print and U.S. Legal in SAP and BillTrust
decisions.description: Analysis compares Unison Tax invoice and the Legal invoice generated from SAP (excluding Proview). The data is largely aligned but there are layout, wording, and format differences. There is an open decision on whether to use separate invoice templates for TAAP Print and U.S. Legal, based on parameters such as bank account details, display of legacy Unison product code, D&B number inclusion, return policy differences, and customer service contact information. If separate templates are chosen, SAP-generated data files sent to BillTrust must include account identifiers to drive template selection.
decisions.rationale: Different bank accounts, potential inclusion of the legacy product code, possible need to display D&B numbers, differing return policies, and different customer support contact details between TAAP Print and U.S. Legal may require separate invoice templates. A unified template would simplify maintenance but may not accommodate all required differences. The decision must balance operational simplicity with business and compliance requirements.
decisions.options_considered:
Option 1: Unified invoice template for TAAP Print and U.S. Legal with conditional logic for differences.
Option 2: Separate invoice templates when any of the following apply: distinct bank accounts, differing legacy product code display ("Legacy Product Code" field), D&B number requirements, different return policies, or different customer service/support contact information.
If separate templates are chosen, include the account identifier in SAP-generated files to BillTrust so the correct template is used.
At minimum, separate bank accounts for the same legal entity would force separate templates.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Dependent on decisions related to bank account configuration (Decision D-01), product code display, D&B number requirement, return policy harmonization, and customer support contact alignment; integration with BillTrust invoice layout and SAP-to-BillTrust interface changes.

decisions.title: Future-state architecture for TAP Print ProView product entitlements
decisions.description: Define the future-state architecture for TAP Print ProView product entitlements currently stored in CUAS. Customers access content via the existing chain: Unison → CUAS → PRISM → OnePass → product site. The decision concerns how these entitlements will be managed and accessed after the migration from Unison, including any changes to systems or flows.
decisions.rationale: Migrating TAP Print and ProView products from Unison requires a clear future-state architecture for entitlements to ensure customers retain access to their content and that the entitlement flow remains secure and efficient. Architecture input is needed to design a sustainable, integrated model across CUAS, PRISM, OnePass, and downstream systems.
decisions.options_considered:
Continue using the current entitlement flow (Unison → CUAS → PRISM → OnePass → product site) with minimal changes vs defining a new entitlement model that aligns with the SAP-based future state and potentially reduces reliance on Unison.
Further options and approaches are to be defined with Architecture during the scheduled sessions.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to TAAP Print migration of ProView products, CUAS entitlement data, PRISM, OnePass, and customer access experience; dependent on Architecture team guidance.

decisions.title: Reuse US Legal Print architecture for TAAP Print Accelerate
decisions.description: The project will reuse the US Legal Print architecture, including SAP, Informatica, AEM, Conga, Salesforce (SFDC), and DCP, as the target architecture for TAAP Print Accelerate.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

**Scope:** AI-Powered Regression Testing is delivering an AI-assisted automated test development framework using Playwright and GitHub Copilot, piloted with three engineering teams to modernize regression testing. This matters because it reduces manual test effort, improves regression coverage and consistency, and establishes reusable patterns for broader adoption across Thomson Reuters.

Three of seven major milestones are complete, including vendor selection and tool evaluation, with the Proof of Concept in progress toward its 12 Jun 2026 target. Pilot team selection is also in progress against a 12 Jun 2026 goal, while framework integration, training development, and extended pilot deployment remain on the planned path to the 30-Sept-2026 project end date.

**Current Status (incl. RAID, as applicable):** Overall status is Green, driven by on-schedule PoC execution and completion of vendor and tooling decisions ahead of June pilot-gating milestones. Sprint Demo is completed.

**Next steps:** AIM to get access to ADO Sandbox - In progress

-   Make the enhancements after the demo.
    

## Path to Green

The top RAID mitigation for this green program is the open risk on pilot team readiness and automation maturity, which is being addressed through upfront readiness assessment, careful pilot team selection, and targeted enablement and coaching before the extended pilot start.

## Milestones

-   Complete the Proof of Concept and select product engineering teams for the PoC and pilot by 12 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete Framework Integration into the TR tools ecosystem by 17 Jul 2026.
    
-   Deliver the Training Development package enabling pilot onboarding by 27 Jul 2026.
    
-   Complete the Pilot/Enablement for early adopters by 17 Aug 2026.
    
-   Close out the AI-Powered Regression Testing program and transition to steady-state ownership by 30-Sept-2026.

risks.description: Delay in completing internal Quality Engineering (QE) hiring may impact the timing of knowledge transfer from vendors and the long‑term sustainability of QE capabilities within Thomson Reuters.
risks.impact_description: If internal QE hiring is delayed, vendor resources may complete their engagement before sufficient knowledge transfer occurs. This would leave TR without adequate in‑house expertise to operate and evolve the QE framework, slowing future delivery, increasing reliance on external vendors, and jeopardizing long‑term sustainability of the QE program.
risks.mitigation: Mitigate by starting the contract hiring process early so that internal QE staff are onboarded in time to participate in the engagement and receive knowledge transfer.

assumptions.title: Vendor enablement
assumptions.description: AIM will provide the initial QE framework setup and guidance, while Thomson Reuters teams progressively build internal capability over time.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project plan relies on AIM, as the selected vendor, to accelerate initial QE framework setup and provide structured guidance so that internal teams can focus on adoption rather than building everything from scratch.
assumptions.validity_explanation: AIM has been formally chosen as the vendor, decisions have been made to proceed with their enablement model, and their onboarding is in progress, making it reasonable to expect they will deliver initial framework setup and guidance.
assumptions.validation_method: Review AIM’s progress and deliverables in weekly status reviews to confirm that the framework is being set up and enablement guidance is being delivered as planned.

assumptions.title: Platform readiness
assumptions.description: Required infrastructure, GitHub, and cloud environments will be available and usable for QE execution once access and security dependencies are cleared.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The QE solution design assumes that existing TR infrastructure, GitHub repositories, and cloud environments can be leveraged once AIM and internal users receive necessary access (Fieldglass onboarding, TR email, VPN, SSO).
assumptions.validity_explanation: TR has existing infrastructure and is in the process of provisioning access for AIM; once onboarding and security are completed, these environments are expected to be operational for QE activities.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If platform readiness is delayed, adjust the schedule for QE execution, use interim environments where possible, escalate access or infrastructure blockers, or reprioritize activities that do not depend on the full platform.
assumptions.validation_method: Test access and connectivity to infrastructure, GitHub, and cloud environments once onboarding and security steps are completed.

assumptions.title: Org commitment
assumptions.description: Product teams will actively participate in QE pilots and adopt standardized Quality Engineering practices defined by the program.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The success of the QE program depends on product teams engaging in pilots, providing resources, and aligning to standard QE practices so that new methods and tooling can be rolled out consistently across the organization.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Product teams have been engaged in planning discussions and are being asked for explicit confirmation to participate in pilots, indicating a reasonable expectation of their commitment.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If some product teams are not committed, escalate to leadership, adjust pilot selection to focus on willing teams, refine change‑management and communication plans, or phase adoption to gradually bring in less engaged teams.
assumptions.validation_method: Obtain explicit confirmation from product teams regarding their participation in pilots and their commitment to adopt agreed QE standards.

assumptions.title: Proof of concept uses a representative application only
assumptions.description: The proof of concept (PoC) will be conducted against a representative application and is not expected to cover all system variations or edge cases.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The kickoff explicitly states that the PoC is intended to validate AI-assisted test generation using a representative application rather than exhaustively covering all systems or edge cases.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The SOW language and project description explicitly limit the PoC to representative scenarios, and the schedule allocates a finite period for PoC work, reinforcing that a single or small set of applications will be used.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If stakeholders demand broader coverage, prioritize representative flows and high-risk scenarios, negotiate additional scope or phases for extended coverage, or clearly document limitations of PoC results in the assessment and roadmap.
assumptions.validation_method: Review the PoC scope and acceptance criteria at Phase 2 (Proof of Concept Validation) to confirm that one or a small number of representative applications are being used and that stakeholders agree this is sufficient for evaluation.
assumptions.source_file_name: TR - Test Development with AI - Kickoff.pptx

assumptions.title: Framework focuses on reusable patterns, not a fully standardized enterprise solution
assumptions.description: The automation framework produced in this engagement will focus on reusable patterns, workflows, and templates rather than a fully standardized enterprise-wide solution.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The kickoff materials state that the framework is designed to establish reusable patterns and not fully standardized enterprise solutions, aligning with the pilot scope and timeline.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Project artifacts and AIM’s deliverable descriptions repeatedly refer to patterns, templates, and pilot-ready frameworks rather than enterprise-wide platform deployment, indicating shared understanding of the limited scope.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If pressure arises to treat the framework as an enterprise standard, document explicit limitations, define additional requirements for enterprise standardization, and propose follow-on work to address governance, scaling, and toolchain diversity.
assumptions.validation_method: At the Framework Integration (Phase 4) and Assessment & Roadmap (Phase 7) checkpoints, review documentation and governance plans to ensure the framework is clearly positioned as a pattern library and pilot-ready solution, not a finalized enterprise standard.
assumptions.source_file_name: TR - Test Development with AI - Kickoff.pptx

assumptions.title: Pilot metrics are directional, not final performance benchmarks
assumptions.description: Metrics collected during the pilot will be treated as directional indicators to inform future decisions, not as final enterprise performance benchmarks or SLAs.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The kickoff notes that pilot metrics are intended to be directional and to inform future decisions, acknowledging that pilot conditions and scope are limited and not fully representative of enterprise operations.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Project documentation frames metrics collection as an input to the roadmap and recommendations rather than as a formal KPI-setting exercise, suggesting shared understanding that results are indicative rather than conclusive.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If stakeholders begin to treat pilot metrics as binding benchmarks, include explicit caveats in presentations, propose additional validation phases, and collaborate with leadership to define more robust KPI baselines before committing to enterprise targets.
assumptions.validation_method: At the Assessment & Roadmap (Phase 7) milestone, review how metrics are presented and interpreted in the final report, ensuring they are clearly labeled as directional and accompanied by caveats and assumptions.
assumptions.source_file_name: TR - Test Development with AI - Kickoff.pptx

## Executive Summary

**Scope:** GTM4 Cloud Modernization is migrating GTM4 databases from AMS to AWS and moving Windows workloads to Linux containers to reduce infrastructure complexity, cut licensing and hosting costs, and improve scalability and reliability. This underpins TR’s cloud and platform engineering standards and creates a cloud-ready foundation for future growth and cross-cloud strategies.

On the AMS Implementation (UAT) side, all migrations and decommissioning are complete. Production database migration is running roughly two months late, with Wave1 and Wave2 revised from early April to 05 Jun 2026 and 29 Jun 2026, while Windows‑to‑Linux Phase 2 Export/Import Wave1 production rollout completed on 08 May 2026 and non‑prod cost-optimization is on track to complete by 29 May 2026. The Reporting Services PoC remains delayed beyond the 30 Apr 2026 plan, with the go/no‑go decision and contingency plan still pending while business engagement and acceptance criteria are finalized. This milestone RAG status is RED now.

**Current Status (incl. RAID, as applicable):** Overall status is Red, driven by unresolved Reporting Services feasibility risk and delayed PoC outcomes that jeopardize the ability to complete Windows-to-Linux Reporting migration and decommission Windows infrastructure by 31 Dec 2026.

## Path to Green

To move toward Green, the team will close out the Reporting Services PoC by 26 May 2026, secure business sign‑off on clear acceptance criteria, and finalize a documented contingency plan if Jasper Reports proves non‑viable, while in parallel enforcing the revised AMS production migration dates (05 Jun 2026 and 29 Jun 2026) and accelerating overdue UAT decommissioning. Dependency risks will be reduced by ensuring the HVR pattern for Content Main is delivered by 05 Jun 2026 and by confirming production wave capacity and cluster counts so that the end‑2026 migration schedule remains realistic.

**Next steps:**  
**1\. The Reporting Service POC is currently assessed as Red due to delays in decision-making and the absence of a confirmed execution plan.  
Mitigation Plan: A meeting is scheduled for 5/26 to confirm the decision following PoC completion. PoC is completed and the outcome is being evaluated by the Business.**

2\. DB migration: PROD Wave2 migration - 6/7, PROD Wave1 Cluster Decom - 6/5

3\. **Phase 2 - Modernization / Export and import management**

-   Production Rollout (Wave 2) - Aug release
    

**Phase 4 - Content modernization**

-   DB patterns readiness - 6/7
    

## Milestones

-   Complete AMS to AWS DB Migration of Prod servers Wave1 migration and decommissioning by 05 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver the GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services PoC and go/no‑go decision by 26 May 2026.
    
-   Deliver the HVR pattern for Content Main modernization by 05 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete AMS to AWS DB Migration of Prod servers Wave2 migration and decommissioning by 29 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete GTM4 Cloud Modernization, including AMS production DB migration Waves1–8 and all four Windows‑to‑Linux phases with associated decommissioning, by 31 Dec 2026.

Migrating these clusters requires re‑initializing database replication from scratch, which is time‑consuming and highly sensitive to maintenance windows. There is a risk that replication may not complete within the agreed downtime window. Additionally, a future GCP content migration is already planned, which may require repeating the same replication process—potentially resulting in two customer downtimes if not carefully planned.

Potential extended PROD downtime impacting customers
Increased operational and reputational risk if replication fails or overruns
Need for multiple customer downtimes (current migration + future GCP migration)
Possible schedule changes to GTM4 Phase / Wave execution
Minor cost impact (~$4.5K/month) if clusters are retained longer as‑is, but operational risk outweighs cost considerations.

Risk logged primarily as a decision risk
Business discussion scheduled to assess tolerance for downtime vs. deferring migration

risks.title: GTM4 Reporting Services Phase 3: Feasibility Risk – Jasper Reports vs Crystal Reports
risks.description: Feasibility risk for the GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services modernization (Phase 3). The modernization depends on validating that Jasper Reports can fully replicate Crystal Reports functionality, including complex reporting logic and handling large datasets. There is a risk that the Proof of Concept (PoC) may be successful only for a limited set of manually converted reports and may not scale or be acceptable for full production rollout.
risks.impact_description: If Jasper Reports cannot match Crystal Reports capabilities at scale, or if the PoC results do not translate into a viable full-production solution for ~1,800 reports, the Reporting Services modernization to Linux may be delayed or fail. This would prevent decommissioning of Windows-based reporting infrastructure, extend licensing and infrastructure costs, and delay cloud modernization benefits. It may also require rework to identify and implement an alternative reporting technology, impacting the overall GTM4 Windows to Linux migration timeline and cost savings.
risks.mitigation: Execute the Reporting Services PoC using Jasper Reports to convert a representative subset of Crystal Reports, focusing on complex logic and high-volume datasets, and validate output parity, performance, usability, and business acceptance. Based on PoC outcomes, define a detailed migration plan for the full report set. In parallel, prepare contingency options (such as alternative reporting platforms or a hybrid approach) in case Jasper cannot fully replace Crystal Reports, and clarify next steps if the PoC is unsuccessful.

objectives.description: Migrate GTM4 AMS Implementation (UAT) database servers from AMS to AWS to validate the target cloud architecture, migration approach, performance, and operational readiness while minimizing risk and ensuring stability before production migration.

Migrate GTM4 AMS production databases and associated application services from AMS to AWS in multiple waves, aligning with TR best practices and moving from IaaS to managed services with a defined data archiving strategy, while completing migration and decommissioning within the 2026 schedule.

Modernize the GTM4 application landscape by migrating all Windows-based components to Linux, improving platform stability, scalability, performance, security, cost efficiency, and long-term cloud readiness while reducing dependency on legacy Windows infrastructure.

Phase 1 – DPS Application Modernization: Migrate and modernize the DPS application from Windows to Linux to establish a proven Linux runtime baseline, validate CI/CD pipelines, and retire legacy Windows infrastructure for this core component.

Phase 2 – Import/Export Module Modernization: Transition the Import and Export modules from Windows to Linux environments running on Graviton-based processors, converting applications from .NET Framework 4.7.2 to .NET Standard/Core, containerizing them using Amazon ECS, and integrating with modern DevOps pipelines for scalable deployments.

Optimize costs for GTM4 Windows to Linux Migration Phase 2 by scaling down web instance types, moving workloads to containers, and reducing instance sizes for Export/Import non-prod environments (DEV, QA, Scale, IMPL/UAT) while shared infrastructure remains in use.

Phase 3 – Reporting Services Migration: Migrate GTM4 Reporting Services from Crystal Reports–based, Windows-only infrastructure to a Linux-based, containerized architecture to improve scalability, reduce licensing costs, and align with cloud modernization standards.

Conduct a Phase 3 Reporting Services Proof of Concept (PoC) to validate automated conversion feasibility using the Cloud Code AI agent, determine whether Jasper Reports can fully replace Crystal Reports at scale, and assess performance for high-volume reports (millions of records).

Mitigate feasibility risk in Reporting Services Phase 3 by validating that Jasper Reports can replicate Crystal Reports functionality, including complex report logic and large datasets, and that the PoC approach can scale to approximately 1,800 reports while meeting functional, performance, usability, and business expectations.

Phase 4 – Content Main Modernization: Migrate legacy Windows-based Content Main services to a Linux-compatible, containerized architecture, modernize the application stack, align with cloud and DevOps standards, and enable use of non-licensed databases such as PostgreSQL to improve scalability and cost efficiency.

Develop an HVR migration pattern (Phase 4 – HVR Pattern creation) to support migration of RDS SQL to Aurora PostgreSQL on AWS for Content Main modernization, to be delivered by the Data Services team.

Deliver all four GTM4 Windows to Linux migration phases (DPS, Import/Export, Reporting Services, Content Main) between July 2025 and December 2026, including migration from .NET Framework 4.7.2 to .NET Standard/Core, containerization on ECS running on Graviton-based hosts, and associated DevOps modernization and security/tech-debt remediation.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The program is onboarding all in-scope SOX 404 financial and business-critical applications into SailPoint IdentityIQ to enforce standardized identity and access management controls. This will automate provisioning, de-provisioning, and access reviews, reducing manual control effort and strengthening SOX 404 audit readiness across key finance platforms.

In Q2 2026 the target is to onboard 8 applications into SailPoint by 30 Jun 2026, with 1 of 8 (Oracle FCCS) already live as of 26 May 2026. Oracle FCCS was delivered three days ahead of its 29 May 2026 plan, while the remaining seven Q2 applications are in progress within their current 30 Jun 2026 planned go-live window.

Overall status is Green, driven by Q2 onboarding tracking to plan with Oracle FCCS completed early and no date slippage yet on remaining in-scope applications despite known API-related risks.

## Path to Green

The top risk mitigation focus is on resolving API dependencies for Sungard Avantgard Integrity, Alliant, and Tax Provision by executing the vendor engagement and escalation plans due by May end and securing committed API delivery timelines ahead of their respective go-live dates.

## Milestones

-   Deliver the Q2 milestone of onboarding 8 applications into SailPoint by 30 Jun 2026, with 1 of 8 already completed as of 26 May 2026.
    
-   Complete Blackline TR, EMS, Enterprise Commissions, JE Workflow Tool, Salesforce KS, Salesforce W&SS, by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Leadership direction will be taken on OneSource Tax Provision & Alliant - ETA 03 Jun 2026.
