dependencies.title: Rightsline user-management APIs and re-platform completion for Alliant SailPoint onboarding
dependencies.description: Alliant SailPoint onboarding depends on the Rightsline vendor providing suitable user-management APIs and/or completing their internal re-platforming with a unified user-management layer. Currently, Rightsline exposes only business APIs (not suitable for identity lifecycle), operates a closed, vendor-controlled platform that prevents TR or third parties from building integrations, and is in the middle of a major re-platforming with no committed timeline.
dependencies.dependent_on: Rightsline vendor delivery of user-management APIs and unified user-management platform for Alliant
dependencies.consumer: SOX 404 SailPoint application onboarding program for Alliant
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Rightsline does not deliver appropriate user-management APIs or complete the new unified platform in time, SailPoint cannot automate onboarding, provisioning, and deprovisioning for Alliant. This may delay Alliant onboarding into 2027, require duplicate integration work (current platform and again after migration), and leave SOX access controls for Alliant manual or fragmented.
dependencies.mitigation: Two main paths are under consideration: (1) Request Rightsline to build user-management APIs on the current setup and deliver by July 15, 2026, enabling SailPoint onboarding completion by end of Q3 2026 (noted as difficult due to vendor bandwidth); or (2) Defer Alliant onboarding until Rightsline completes its internal re-platforming and builds APIs on the new setup, accepting a likely 2027 timeline and planning interim manual controls.

decisions.title: Decision on Alliant SailPoint onboarding timing and integration approach
decisions.description: Determine whether to proceed with SailPoint onboarding for Alliant on the current Rightsline platform by requesting user-management APIs, or to defer onboarding until Rightsline completes its internal re-platforming and unified user-management layer with suitable APIs.
decisions.options_considered:
Option 1: Request Rightsline vendor to build user-management APIs on the current platform and deliver them by July 15, 2026, enabling SailPoint onboarding completion by end of Q3 2026, acknowledging that the vendor currently lacks bandwidth and this may require duplicate integration work after their re-platform.
Option 2: Defer onboarding of the Alliant application until Rightsline completes its internal re-platforming and builds user-management APIs on the new setup, accepting that this may push onboarding into a 2027 timeline and planning for extended interim manual controls.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Customer Trust AI Strategy is delivering a centralized Customer Trust platform that consolidates trusted content, introduces AI-assisted responses, and enables scalable self-service for Sales and internal stakeholders. This matters because it will replace inefficient ServiceNow workflows, reduce response times, and support growth in security, privacy, and compliance engagements while maintaining strong governance and accuracy.

The overall program latest-estimate completion has been extended to 30 Jun 2027 from the original 11 Dec 2025 to reflect all AI and self-service phases, with Phase 1 content, governance, and AI velocity milestones in progress toward their 01 Aug 2026 and 30 Sep 2026 targets. Three of six identified risks are now closed, including content backlog and Loopio API information gaps, while remaining active risks focus on sponsor absence, SME/BISO participation, and Loopio AI enablement.

Overall status is AMBER, driven primarily by ongoing sponsor absence and team restructuring, which are slowing decisions and execution on content governance, SME/BISO engagement, and AI feature enablement.

## Path to Green

The project path to Green focuses on completing Admin AI discovery and feedback analysis for the Loopio AI enablement go/ no go decision by 29 May 2026.

## Milestones

-   Launch (30 June 2026) and Improve (30 Sep 2026) Loopio Platform with AI enablement.
    
-   Establish and operationalize the content governance process for the Loopio knowledge base by 01 Aug 2026.
    
-   Complete Phase 1 work to establish the trusted content knowledge base and configure AI-enabled workflows to improve ticket closure velocity by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Implement the AI solution for the top 80% of products, enabling chatbot-based self-service for common Customer Trust inquiries, by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Implement the AI solution for sample proof-of-concept products and AI-based request submission capabilities within the Customer Trust Platform by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete the overall Customer Trust AI Strategy program across all phases by 30 Jun 2027.
    
    -   Phase 1-Launch and Improve Loopio Platform (30 Sept 2026)
        
    -   Phase 2- Launch Self-Service / Automated Response Generation - MVP1 (31 Dece 2026)
        
    -   Phase 3- Launch Self-Service / Automated Response Generation - Iteration 2 (30 Jun 2027)

Mitigation date: TBD as this is an on ongoing planning and knowledge transfer effort.
risks.impact_description: If the sponsor’s absence and team changes are not effectively managed, ramp-up time for new members will increase, reviews may take longer, rework may rise, and decision-making may slow. This could cause schedule slippage, dependency bottlenecks, and delays in delivering key milestones in the Customer Trust AI strategy.
risks.mitigation: Identify a clear strategy owner; document strategic decisions and assumptions; pair new leads with experienced stakeholders; prioritize deliverables to protect the critical path; add schedule buffer for the transition period; increase stakeholder touchpoints and review cadence; and appoint an interim strategy SME/point of contact for rapid alignment. assumptions.title: Centralized Customer Trust Platform will improve engagement and enable long-term AI strategy
assumptions.description: A new centralized Customer Trust Platform, replacing the current ServiceNow solution, will improve engagement and efficiency and enable the long-term AI strategy.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The current legacy ServiceNow platform no longer meets Customer Trust engagement needs, and the AI strategy requires a single, integrated front door with better configurability, reporting, automation, and role-based experiences.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The problem statement identifies clear limitations with the legacy ServiceNow platform, and the project charter articulates a long-term vision for a single integrated front door for Sales and internal stakeholders. The initial implementation of a new Loopio instance and planned AI-enabled self-service milestones are already underway, indicating organizational commitment and technical feasibility. These factors make it reasonable to assume that a centralized Customer Trust Platform will improve engagement and support the AI strategy.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the centralized platform does not deliver the expected benefits, reassess platform requirements and consider alternative solutions or architectural adjustments (e.g., additional integrations, enhanced governance, or a different core AI platform) while maintaining continuity of service using transitional tools like Loopio.
assumptions.validation_method: Validate through phased deployment of the new platform (including Loopio and the long-term AI platform), measurement of engagement and operational metrics, and qualitative feedback from Sales and internal stakeholders.
assumptions.source_file_name: RAID Log – 2026 Customer Trust - AI Strategy.xlsx

assumptions.title: Availability of Platform Engineering development resources after CT MVP1 design
assumptions.description: Platform Engineering development team resources, led by Matthew Schlosser, will be available to assist with long term platform set up after the Customer Trust MVP1 technical design is completed.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Planning for MVP1 is scheduled in Q2 2026, including technical discussions about the current state and future development needs. The assumption is that once design work is complete, Platform Engineering resources will be able to support development for later phases.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current planning activities in Q2 2026 include technical discussions between Customer Trust and Platform Engineering about existing capabilities and future needs. These discussions typically precede formal resource assignments for development work, making it reasonable to assume that Platform Engineering will engage post-design, though competing priorities could still affect timing.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Platform Engineering resources are not available as assumed, adjust the roadmap by re-sequencing scope, identifying alternative development resources, reducing initial feature scope, or extending timelines for MVP1 and subsequent phases. Escalate through governance forums to secure prioritized resourcing or to formalize revised timelines.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm resource allocation and timelines with Matthew Schlosser’s Platform Engineering team during Q2 2026 planning and through formal commitments in the project plan and PMO artifacts.
assumptions.source_file_name: RAID Log – 2026 Customer Trust - AI Strategy.xlsx

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Brazil Tax Reform is delivering compliant, stable product and service invoicing for Brazil by validating all SAP tax configurations and invoice outputs before regulatory deadlines. This matters because blocked or incorrect invoices create immediate financial exposure, customer dissatisfaction, and risk of non-compliance with Brazilian tax authorities.

UAT for product invoicing (TF01 and Writer TSL) is aligned to plan, with planned and actual completion dates both recorded as 08 May 2026 and reusable patterns defined for services. Services UAT for IBS/CBS remains in progress toward a planned compliance-ready milestone on 31 Jul 2026, while multiple critical issues (IPI, CBNF configuration, postal codes, and UAT orchestration) are being worked ahead of closure dates between 22 May 2026 and 31 May 2026.

Overall status is Red, driven primarily by critical IPI and CBNF configuration issues that are blocking product invoicing and Products UAT completion.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on securing specialized SAP Brazil tax expertise to resolve the IPI/CBNF configuration and postal code issues by their due dates, then enforcing full regression and evidence-based testing before any deployment. In parallel, a single UAT PM is being put in place with clear data-readiness and orchestration responsibilities so Services UAT can execute end-to-end and reach IBS/CBS compliance sign-off by 31 Jul 2026.

## Milestones

- Complete Products UAT (TF01 and Writer TSL scenarios validated with Go/No-Go decision) by 08 May 2026.  
- Resolve open TF01 IPI issue (ISS-01) and Postal Code issue (ISS-07) blocking invoice creation by 22 May 2026.  
- Establish full Orders and Billing UAT orchestration, including data readiness and UAT PM ownership for services, by 29 May 2026.  
- Achieve Services UAT Compliance Ready for IBS/CBS and release readiness decision for services (SERV-10) by 31 Jul 2026.  
- Transition to steady-state compliant invoicing operations and close the Brazil Tax Reform project by 15 Apr 2027.

risks.title: Communication Risk: Blocked Invoices
risks.description: The risk here is that ineffective or insufficient communication with the relevant stakeholders, particularly from the business side, could lead to a lack of awareness or understanding about the issue with blocked invoices. This could result in delayed resolution, increased customer dissatisfaction, and potential financial impacts.
risks.impact_description:
Delays in resolving the blocked invoices could disrupt cash flow and customer relations.
Miscommunication could lead to duplicated efforts or incorrect actions being taken.
The business may not be adequately prepared to handle customer inquiries or complaints related to the issue.
risks.mitigation:
Develop and implement a structured communication plan that outlines who needs to be informed, what information is required, and the frequency of updates.
Identify key stakeholders and ensure they are included in all relevant communications.

Provide consistent and timely updates to stakeholders about the status of the issue, actions being taken, and expected resolution timelines.
Use multiple channels (e.g., emails, meetings, dashboards) to ensure the message is received.

Assign a designated point of contact for all communications related to the blocked invoices. This person should be responsible for coordinating messages and responding to inquiries.

Establish a clear escalation process for when the issue cannot be resolved at the current level. Ensure stakeholders know how and when to escalate concerns.

Encourage feedback from stakeholders to ensure that communications are effective and that any additional information needs are identified promptly.

Maintain thorough documentation of all communications and actions taken regarding the blocked invoices. This will help in tracking progress and providing transparency.

milestones.name: Products UAT Completed (TF01 & Writer TSL Ready)

risks.title: Lack of End-to-End UAT Orchestration
risks.description:
There is a risk that Services UAT activities are executed in a fragmented or uncoordinated manner, without a clear orchestration function ensuring alignment across Technology, Business, and Tax teams. This could result in gaps in scenario execution, inconsistent validation of IBS/CBS compliance, delayed defect resolution, or misaligned sign-off timelines.
Without a defined end-to-end ownership for UAT execution, the program may face delays in achieving formal UAT completion, incomplete compliance validation, and increased risk of missing the regulatory deadline, ultimately impacting release readiness and exposing the organization to potential penalties or business disruption.
risks.impact_description: Potential delays in achieving UAT sign‑off, incomplete tax compliance validation (IBS/CBS), and increased risk of missing the regulatory deadline, which may lead to business disruption or penalties.
risks.mitigation: The mitigation strategy is to ensure that Silvia Sun assigns a dedicated Finance representative to support and co-lead the UAT process alongside the LKM team, providing end-to-end financial oversight. This role will help coordinate scenario validation, ensure IBS/CBS compliance is consistently applied, and drive alignment between business, tax, and technology activities during UAT execution. Having this dedicated Finance involvement will reduce fragmentation, improve execution quality, and ensure that UAT is completed in a timely and compliant manner aligned with regulatory expectations.

risks.title: Incomplete testing scope for SAP configuration change
risks.description:
Description: Testing scope is not fully defined across all scenarios; activating the checkbox without full regression may introduce unintended impacts across service invoices and related flows.
Risk level: High (potential production impact if not properly validated)
risks.impact_description: Risk of introducing defects into production due to untested scenarios, potentially affecting service invoices, billing flows, and financial reporting. Could lead to rework, delays, or production incidents.
risks.mitigation:
Define a full testing scope upfront (all scenarios, not just the failing one)
Use existing scenarios + Excel test cases to ensure coverage
Include mandatory regression testing (service invoices + related flows)
Assign clear validation ownership (Noelia / Carla / Gustavo / Marcio)
Require test evidence in ADO before approving any deployment

risks.title: Missing approval owner for configuration change
risks.description:
The correct approver for the IP tax checkbox activation (Branch 2060) is not identified, resulting in a blocked decision and inability to proceed with testing.
Risk level: High / Critical (directly blocks UAT progression)
risks.impact_description: Delays decision-making and testing start, which directly blocks UAT execution and puts the overall timeline at risk. No progress can be made on the checkbox solution until the correct approver is identified.
risks.mitigation:
Immediately identify the correct approval owner (Finance / Service Management / SAP governance)
Escalate within the same day via Teams or leadership if needed
Use parallel communication channels (Marcio + Gustavo + Ops/Finance leads) to avoid dependency on a single response
Define a clear fallback approver if no response is received within the day

issues.resolution:
I am reaching out to escalate a critical production issue impacting Company Code 2060 (TRBrasil CT – São Paulo, CNPJ 00.910.509/0001-71, NF-e Produto).
At this moment, we are unable to create product invoices (Nota Fiscal – Writer Invoice), which is already a production blocker with immediate financial impact.

We executed testing on Monday with Alexandro (Billing team). While the previous IPI issue has been resolved, a new blocking dependency has been identified:
•	The system now requires CBNF (Fiscal Benefit Code) as part of regulatory enforcement
•	The CBNF table exists in SAP but is not populated
•	Even when correct codes are known, the system rejects them as “code does not exist”
•	As a result, NF-e is rejected by SEFAZ
This confirms that the issue is no longer functional or testing-related, but rather a SAP configuration and data dependency.

We reviewed this with the Service Management team and at this point no resolution has been identified. The recommendation was to escalate, as we require specialized functional support with Brazil tax expertise to resolve this gap urgently.
We also checked with TCS (Carla), but they currently do not have available capacity to support.

Request:
We need your support to urgently secure a functional tax consultant (Brazil localization expertise) who can assist in loading and validating the CBNF configuration in SAP.
Without this, invoice generation will remain blocked, with direct financial and operational consequences.
Please let me know how you would like to proceed, or if we can align quickly on the fastest path to resolution.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

SafeSend One is integrating the SafeSend product onto Thomson Reuters’ strategic commercial and technology platforms, standardizing lead-to-cash, customer identity, and digital self-service so SafeSend can be sold, billed, and supported on scalable, compliant enterprise systems. This reduces reliance on legacy platforms while enabling future growth and stable operations.

Front Office High-Level Design is complete, with 15 of 15 applications approved on 16 Jan 2026 against a 15 Jan 2026 plan. Lead-to-cash UAT for all workstreams is scheduled from 25 May to 11 Jun 2026 ahead of the 20 Jun 2026 tech code release and the 13 Jul 2026 CS&S go-live that underpin the July SafeSend business launch and the New Sales go-live that will deliver 70% of project scope.

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by unresolved MDM integration issues that threaten the 20 Jun 2026 tech release and compress downstream UAT and go-live timelines.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on clearing the MDM integration risk by running a dedicated MDM and SafeSend working group with weekly checkpoints, locking committed delivery dates for required objects and interfaces, and implementing agreed interim data-load workarounds ahead of the 20 Jun 2026 code release. In parallel, CS&S capacity and UAT windows will be tightly coordinated across workstreams through June to reduce schedule conflicts, protect the 11 Jun 2026 UAT completion date, and maintain readiness for the 13 Jul 2026 CS&S production go-live.

## Milestones

- Complete Lead to Cash UAT for all workstreams by 11 Jun 2026.  
- Deliver the SSOne Market, Sales, Support and SSP tech code release by 20 Jun 2026.  
- Achieve SafeSend One CS&S production go-live on 13 Jul 2026.  
- Deliver New Sales go live, enabling SafeSend to be sold, billed, entitled and supported on the CPSP stack and representing 70% of project completion, by 27 Jul 2026.  
- Complete overall SafeSend One project delivery by 15 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Misaligned UAT schedules across CS&S workstreams
risks.description: Variation in User Acceptance Testing (UAT) windows across CS&S workstreams may cause scheduling conflicts if not properly aligned among key team members (Mike, Yvonne, Becky, Emily, Alex).
risks.impact_description: If UAT windows are not coordinated, key CS&S stakeholders may be double‑booked or unavailable, causing test cycles to slip, defects to be discovered late, and potentially delaying SafeSend go‑live activities that depend on CS&S readiness.
risks.mitigation:
1. Centralized UAT Window Alignment
2. Early Dependency & Conflict Identification

risks.title: Stripe delivery plan not aligned with SafeSend target delivery
risks.description: The current Stripe project plan is not aligned with the SafeSend target delivery date, with Stripe delivering at the same time SafeSend aims to deliver. This overlap is likely to evolve into an unmet dependency.
risks.impact_description: If Stripe is not ready or integrated when SafeSend needs payment processing, SafeSend could face a critical dependency gap for payments, risking launch delays or requiring unplanned workarounds and impacting customer billing and payment experiences.
risks.mitigation: SafeSend will continue to use Paymetric for payments until a migration plan to Stripe is in place and executed by the Payment Unification team.

risks.title: Semarchy migration delay potentially impacting April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT
risks.description: Semarchy migration is supposed to complete by Q1 2026. If this project stalls or ‘sits’, it could impact the April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT schedule due to required environment downtime.
risks.impact_description: If Semarchy migration does not complete as planned, required environment outages or incomplete data migration could prevent or delay lead‑to‑cash UAT in April 2026, which may push back defect resolution, integration testing, and overall SafeSend launch readiness.
risks.mitigation: MDM team has proposed running EPM and Semarchy in parallel so that necessary capabilities remain available while migration completes and required downtime is minimized or scheduled to reduce impact on UAT.

risks.title: Transition to new Help Center content and licenses for Help & Support
risks.description: New Help and Support content, including a new Help Center, is targeted for completion by end of Q1. Downstream teams must update their workstreams to point to the new Help Center before old Help Center licenses expire on 2026-07-01.
risks.impact_description: If downstream teams do not update their configurations, links, and workflows to the new Help Center before the old licenses expire, users may encounter broken links, inconsistent support experiences, or loss of access to help content, negatively impacting customers and product teams.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with downstream teams to ensure they update their workstreams and integrations to reference the new Help Center well before the 2026-07-01 license expiry for the old Help Center.

risks.title: Loss of key SafeSend marketing contacts and domain expertise
risks.description: Recent turnover of key SafeSend marketing contacts has reduced critical domain expertise, even though replacements have been identified.
risks.impact_description: Knowledge gaps among new marketing resources may lead to delays in marketing deliverables, misaligned or suboptimal marketing decisions, and quality issues in marketing assets that support the SafeSend launch and ongoing adoption.
risks.mitigation: monitored via SafeSend Marketing Workstream and Monthly Review cadence

risks.title: Flash migration delays tying up key CS&S resources and impacting SafeSend launch
risks.description: Completion of the Flash migration, which is required for CS&S, may be delayed. This could tie up key resources and cause a four‑week slip in SafeSend’s business launch and complicate UAT scheduling. If Flash is not delivered before mid‑July, its go‑live may be postponed to the following year.
risks.impact_description: If Flash migration slips past the planned timeframe, CS&S resources needed for SafeSend could remain focused on Flash, delaying SafeSend’s business launch by up to four weeks, impacting the planned July 2026 deployment and potentially deferring related benefits.
risks.mitigation: Close tracking of the Flash program to identify and address schedule risks early and coordinate resource allocation with SafeSend needs.

risks.title: Loss of key architect (Andy) for ECM/ECX high‑level design
risks.description: Loss of key resource Andy, the architect responsible for completing the High‑Level Design (HLD) for ECM/ECX. The current team lacks sufficient architectural capacity to finalize HLD deliverables within planned timelines.
risks.impact_description: If the HLD is delayed due to lack of architectural capacity, design sign‑off will slip, delaying the start of development and potentially affecting downstream integration, testing, and SafeSend’s overall delivery timeline.
risks.mitigation: Identify and onboard replacement or additional architectural capacity to complete the ECM/ECX HLD within the planned timeframe, and adjust plans or scope as needed to reflect available resources.

risks.title: Delay in onboarding Informatica resource for Sales workstream
risks.description: Onboarding of an Informatica resource for the Sales workstream was initially delayed and raised as a risk, as the project required Informatica expertise for scoping and integration activities.
risks.impact_description: If the Informatica resource were not onboarded, Sales workstream design and integration work relying on Informatica could have been delayed, impacting data integration, testing schedules, and overall SafeSend delivery for Sales.
risks.mitigation: Onboard the required Informatica resource and commence scoping work as soon as they join the project.

risks.title: Delay in finalizing product pricing impacting EPM data migration
risks.description: Product pricing for SafeSend needs to be finalized as soon as possible to support Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) data migration activities.
risks.impact_description: If product pricing is not finalized in time, EPM data migration and related configuration may be delayed, which can block downstream testing, reporting readiness, and the overall lead‑to‑cash schedule for the SafeSend launch.
risks.mitigation: Ameera is following up with Saima and Scott to drive timely product pricing decisions and ensure inputs are available for EPM data migration.

risks.title: CS&S team capacity constraints due to multiple parallel projects
risks.description: Multiple parallel projects affecting the Customer Service & Support (CS&S) area, including Doctor Tax and SurePrep, may stretch the CS&S team’s resources too thin to effectively support SafeSend work.
risks.impact_description: If CS&S resources are over-allocated, SafeSend-related analysis, design, testing, and deployment activities could be delayed or under‑resourced, leading to schedule slippage, reduced quality of customer support capabilities, and potential impact on the July 2026 launch objectives.
risks.mitigation:
1. Prioritize CS&S Support for SafeSend Critical Path
2. Capacity Planning & Resource Phasing

risks.title: MDM Integration Delays Impacting SafeSend One Timeline
risks.description: Ongoing Master Data Management (MDM) integration issues are causing delays in data synchronization required for SafeSend One. Dependencies on MDM readiness for customer, product, and entitlement data remain unresolved, creating a risk to planned milestones and downstream integrations.
risks.impact_description: Continued MDM integration issues may delay SafeSend One system integration testing and go‑live readiness due to incomplete or unreliable master data feeds. Prolonged delays could impact dependent integrations, compress downstream testing timelines, and increase the risk of schedule slippage and rework close to go‑live.
risks.mitigation:
Establish a dedicated MDM + SafeSend integration working group with weekly checkpoints
Confirm committed delivery dates for required MDM objects and interfaces
Identify and approve short‑term workarounds (e.g., interim data loads or controlled fallbacks)
Engaged PE as well for a temporary work around as file drop from SafeSend is not straight forward

dependencies.title: New chat experience implementation prior to SafeSend migration
dependencies.description: The new chat experience must be implemented before SafeSend migration for Customer Service & Support to maintain high call deflection rates and minimize disruptions during transition.
dependencies.dependent_on: New chat experience implementation project
dependencies.consumer: SafeSend CS&S migration workstream and contact center operations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the new chat experience is not live before migration, call deflection rates may decrease and customers could experience higher wait times and service disruption, impacting customer satisfaction and operational performance.

dependencies.title: CIAM customer migration completion before SafeSend business launch
dependencies.description: CIAM customer migration is scheduled for April to June 2026 and needs to be complete before the July 2026 lead-to-cash business launch for SafeSend.
dependencies.dependent_on: CIAM customer migration program
dependencies.consumer: SafeSend lead-to-cash business launch and related CIAM-integrated processes
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If CIAM customer migration is not complete by July 2026, the lead-to-cash business launch for SafeSend may not be able to proceed as planned, causing delays to go-live and impacting revenue realization and customer onboarding.
dependencies.mitigation: Alfredo Huerta to schedule a progress call on the proof of concept, which is due to complete by 2025-09-30, to ensure the CIAM migration stays aligned with the SafeSend launch timeline.

dependencies.title: Sales input for CS&S contact center design
dependencies.description: Customer Service & Support needs input from specific SafeSend sales team contacts to provide detailed requirements, including queues, agents, and call flow information for the contact center design.
dependencies.dependent_on: SafeSend sales team subject-matter experts
dependencies.consumer: CS&S contact center and telephony workstreams designing SafeSend support queues and flows
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without timely sales input, CS&S may design queues and call flows that do not accurately reflect sales processes, leading to rework and potential confusion for customers and internal teams at launch.

dependencies.title: Global case management delivery for CAP customers
dependencies.description: Delivery of global case management for CAP customers is planned for Q2 and is a separate initiative outside of SafeSend and migration programs. Its alignment with the new framework is a strategic roadmap dependency for SafeSend-related deliverables.
dependencies.dependent_on: Global case management initiative for CAP customers
dependencies.consumer: SafeSend CS&S and case management capabilities for CAP customers
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If global case management for CAP customers is delayed or does not align with the new framework, related SafeSend case handling and support roadmap items may be impacted, requiring rework or delaying delivery of integrated case management features.
dependencies.mitigation: Case management delivery is planned for May 2026; close coordination with the global case management initiative is required to maintain alignment.

dependencies.title: AI deflection design playback dependency on Service Cloud use cases
dependencies.description: Design playback for SafeSend AI deflection is dependent on completion of similar AI deflection use cases in Service Cloud, with design activities scheduled for Q1.
dependencies.dependent_on: Completion of AI deflection use cases and design work in Service Cloud
dependencies.consumer: SafeSend CS&S AI deflection design and enterprise-wide enablement planning
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the Service Cloud AI deflection use cases are not completed on time, the SafeSend AI deflection design playback may be delayed, impacting enterprise-wide enablement timelines and associated decisions.
dependencies.mitigation: @sri srinivasan to get HLD approved in DA forum from Srirram. If this is not approved by 05/15 then program will turn red.

dependencies.title: Informatica resource onboarding for Sales integration
dependencies.description: Onboarding of an Informatica resource was required for Sales integration activities; this dependency has been fulfilled.
dependencies.dependent_on: Availability and onboarding of Informatica technical resource
dependencies.consumer: Sales integration workstream relying on Informatica for data integration and scoping
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delay in onboarding the Informatica resource would have postponed scoping work and downstream integration activities in the Sales workstream.
dependencies.mitigation: Resource was successfully onboarded on 2026-03-03, allowing scoping work to start.

dependencies.title: Boomi and MDS effort for late-identified architecture dependency
dependencies.description: A late-identified architecture dependency requires approximately three sprints of Boomi work, with MDS effort initially unknown. A workaround with the Boomi team has been implemented, and Pranitha is working on MDS view creation.
dependencies.dependent_on: Boomi integration team and MDS view availability
dependencies.consumer: Sales integration workstream and related data flows that rely on Boomi and MDS
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Boomi and MDS work are not completed in time, sales data integrations may be delayed, impacting end-to-end lead-to-order and reporting capabilities for SafeSend.
dependencies.mitigation: A workaround has been implemented with the Boomi team, and MDS view creation is in progress under Pranitha's ownership.

dependencies.title: Salesforce object approval by architecture (TRO and product checkbox on account)
dependencies.description: Salesforce object changes, including TRO and a product checkbox on account, require approval by the architecture team. Partial approval has been granted, and Sagarika is working on creating the objects.
dependencies.dependent_on: Architecture team approval for Salesforce object design
dependencies.consumer: Salesforce Sales workstream implementing account-level fields for SafeSend
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without full architecture approval and resulting object creation, the sales workstream cannot fully implement required Salesforce account fields, delaying configuration and testing.
dependencies.mitigation: Partial approval has been received; Sagarika is proceeding with creating approved objects while awaiting any further guidance.

dependencies.title: Flash migration completion before SafeSend CS&S migration
dependencies.description: Completion of the Flash migration in May 2026 is required and may overlap with the SafeSend migration for Customer Service & Support (CS&S), creating a sequencing dependency.
dependencies.dependent_on: Flash migration program
dependencies.consumer: SafeSend CS&S migration workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the Flash migration is delayed or overlaps significantly with SafeSend migration, key shared resources may be overextended, causing schedule conflicts and potential delays to SafeSend migration activities.
dependencies.mitigation: Program is tracked closely and on-track for now. No major risk or issues to SafeSend.

decisions.title: Use Paymetric for SafeSend payments until Stripe is aligned
decisions.description: SafeSend will continue to use the current BAU Paymetric payment solution for its migration and launches, and will migrate to Stripe later in alignment with the broader Unification Payment program and CPSP timelines.
decisions.rationale: The Unification Payment program’s Stripe delivery timeline is not aligned with the 2026 SafeSend migration delivery dates; attempting to align SafeSend with Stripe now would create an unmet dependency and delivery risk.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Align SafeSend migration with Stripe delivery timeline under the Unification Payment program.
2) Proceed with SafeSend migration using existing BAU Paymetric and move to Stripe later with the rest of CPSP (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to CPSP Stripe risk R003 in the RAID log, where the Stripe project plan is not aligned with SafeSend target delivery dates.

decisions.title: Phase SafeSend One and Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launches
decisions.description: SafeSend One business launch will proceed ahead of Digital Sales and Self-Serve launches, with Digital capabilities following once foundational platforms and processes are in place.
decisions.rationale: Phasing launches ensures that foundational capabilities, including self-serve, are in place before Digital Sales and Self-Serve go live, reducing delivery risk and improving stability at launch.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Launch SafeSend One and Digital Sales & Self-Serve together.
2) Phase the launches so Digital Sales & Self-Serve follow after foundational lead-to-cash delivery (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Impacts Digital workstream roadmap and dependencies on lead-to-cash (L2C) foundational deliverables planned for July 2026.

decisions.title: Set TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launch target to January 2027
decisions.description: SSOne and TTC Digital phased deployment was agreed, with TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launch targeted for January 2027, with a possibility to bring it forward into Q4 2026 if Digital commitments are met by June 2026.
decisions.rationale: Separating the TTC Digital launch provides additional time to deliver and stabilize core lead-to-cash capabilities and allows Digital teams to commit to a realistic delivery schedule, while retaining flexibility to pull the date forward if feasible.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Align TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve launch with July 2026 L2C deliverables.
2) Target January 2027 for TTC Digital launch, with option to bring into Q4 2026 if commitments are met (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to Digital workstream scope, TTC digital rollout timing, and integration budget planning for 2026, as well as RAID risk regarding TTC scope, design, and schedule alignment with July 2026 deployment.

decisions.title: SafeSend One CS&S production go‑live date change (20 June → 13 July)
decisions.description: Decision to move the SafeSend One go‑live for CS&S area from 20 June to 13 July to allow additional time for testing, access readiness, and stabilization activities.
decisions.rationale: To avoid support peak season late July  and early August and to have time /buffer to mitigate any risk arise due to new changes.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

ETS Service Desk Automation is integrating ServiceNow (SNOW), Now Assist, and Amazon Connect into core Service Desk and ETS workflows to deflect contacts, automate high-volume tasks, and modernize the agent and employee support experience. The scope covers Agent Chat as a Vayusphere replacement, Now Assist–driven self-service, delegated knowledge base migration, and future IVR/Virtual Agent use cases such as password reset.

Core platform enablement is in place, with the Now Assist platform and out-of-the-box capabilities live since 17 Mar 2026. However, the “Conversational workflows configured” milestone has slipped by 29 days from its original 21 May 2026 target to a latest estimate of 19 Jun 2026 due to a ServiceNow access issue and the Zurich upgrade clone, and the delegated Service Desk knowledge base migration remains in progress toward a 30 May 2026 completion.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by the unresolved NAVA / ServiceNow issue introduced after the clone, which is blocking conversational workflow completion and HCL access to Now Assist dashboards needed for Agent Chat gap analysis. And in parallel there is negotiations with ServiceNow for License renewal which is blocking SNOW to resolve the access issue.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on resolving the NAVA / ServiceNow issue by applying and validating the proposed Now Assist plugin upgrades so assistants and data are fully restored in non-production, then completing conversational workflow configuration by the revised 19 Jun 2026 date and closing out the 30 May 2026 delegated knowledge base migration to reduce KB hygiene risk and enable accurate Now Assist responses.

## Milestones

-   Complete delegated knowledge base migration to production for the Service Desk knowledge base by 30 May 2026.
    
-   Finalize conversational workflows (greeting, fallback, completion, error handling) for the virtual agent by 19 Jun 2026.
    
-   Achieve Agent Chat platform readiness for Vayusphere replacement, by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver Phase 1 passwordless integration into Now Assist and Virtual Agent workflows, including pilot completion, by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete the ETS Service Desk Automation program by 24 Apr 2027.

risks.title: Agent chat interaction visibility model may not support desired multi-agent access
risks.description: Jakub requested investigating whether the same interaction conversation can be available to multiple agents at once, which is not the default behavior of Advanced Work Assignment (AWA). Current understanding is that supervisors/managers can join ongoing interactions, but it is unclear whether the system can be configured so different agents can pick up the same interaction, or if timing parameters (e.g., 1-minute search interval) must be adjusted instead.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow and AWA cannot be configured to support the desired level of multi-agent access to a single interaction, or if timing parameters for agent search are not tuned, agent collaboration workflows may be constrained. This could limit the ability for multiple agents to assist on complex cases, slow handoffs, and impact response times. Alternatively, aggressive parameter changes (e.g., very short search windows) without careful testing could destabilize routing behavior.
risks.mitigation: 1) Investigate ServiceNow and Advanced Work Assignment documentation and configuration options to confirm whether an interaction can be surfaced to multiple agents concurrently and under what conditions (e.g., supervisor join vs re-queueing). 2) Evaluate alternative approaches such as adjusting the default 1-minute agent search window to shorter intervals (e.g., 10–15 seconds) and enabling supervisor join capabilities for complex cases. 3) Prototype the desired behavior in DEV/QA and review with Jakub to confirm it meets operational needs. 4) If true multi-agent access is not feasible, document the chosen interaction handling model and ensure HCL is trained on expected behavior and escalation paths.

risks.title: Zurich upgrade and dev freeze may cause loss or rework of recent virtual agent and agent chat changes
risks.description: The upcoming Zurich upgrade will introduce a dev freeze period (May 8 to June 8) and a clone from production into the development environment. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay explained that to avoid losing in-flight development work (especially virtual agent conversational workflows, plugins, and configuration changes), developers must take backups of update sets before the end of Friday. Srinu confirmed that some changes are already captured in update sets, but others (such as plugin enabling or certain configuration options) are not; these will need to be documented and manually re-applied after the clone. If backups and documentation are incomplete, recent VA and Agent Chat work could be overwritten or require significant rework after the clone, impacting timelines.
risks.impact_description: If update sets are not properly exported and configuration-only changes are not documented before the Zurich upgrade clone, the clone from production could overwrite or remove recent development work on virtual agent conversational workflows, Agent Chat configuration, and related integrations. This would require developers (Srinu, Prashanth and others) to rediscover and re-implement these changes manually, consuming additional effort during an already constrained period and potentially delaying the May 15 conversational workflow target and other milestones. Incomplete backups could also cause inconsistencies between dev, QA, and future production deployments, increasing the risk of defects at go-live.
risks.mitigation:
1) Ensure all recent development work for virtual agent conversational workflows, Agent Chat, and related configurations is captured in ServiceNow update sets before the Zurich upgrade clone; Srinu and Prashanth to coordinate and export these update sets by end of day Friday.
2) For items not captured in update sets (e.g., plugin enablement, certain configuration options), document the exact steps and settings so they can be manually re-applied on the cloned dev instance.
3) After the clone, re-import and commit the saved update sets into the dev instance and re-apply documented configuration changes, verifying that all key VA and Agent Chat functionality still works.
4) Continue development and feedback changes in dev and QA during the prod change freeze, deferring only production promotions until after the upgrade window, as confirmed by Vinay.
5) Kiran to monitor progress and request status updates from Srinu and Prashanth on backup completion, highlighting any areas where rework is expected so they can be time-boxed and prioritized.
6) If significant rework is required post-clone, adjust internal timelines for non-prod testing and update the RAAID log and milestones accordingly.

risks.title: Agent chat access/role configuration for HCL testers not fully working

Causes appear related to legacy membership in HCL service desk groups and/or roles not propagating correctly from groups to users. If unresolved, HCL agents will not be able to perform hands-on testing of agent chat end-to-end.

This will delay completion of testing, slow feedback on defects and usability, and may push back agreed timelines and preview dates with the internal event team. Persistent access gaps could also cause partial rollouts where only some agents are enabled, creating inconsistent support experience.

risks.title: Agent queue management governance between TR and HCL not defined
risks.description: The process and ownership for managing agent chat queues (e.g., adding new hires to language queues like French or English) has not been defined. Currently HCL self-manages queues in their existing setup, but it is unclear whether, and to what extent, they will have control within the TR ServiceNow (Advanced Work Assignment) configuration or if TR will centrally own this. Without clear governance, queue changes for new/changed agents may be slow or inconsistent.
risks.impact_description: If governance for agent chat queue management is not defined, new HCL hires and role changes may not be added to the correct language/skill queues in a timely manner. This can result in agents not receiving interactions they should handle, degraded service levels, manual workarounds, and dependence on ad-hoc TR changes. Over time this can cause operational friction between TR and HCL and undermine the scalability of the agent chat solution.
risks.mitigation: 1) Inventory current Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) queue configurations (e.g., language-specific queues such as French and English) and document the required update operations (add/remove agent, change capacities). 2) Align with TR stakeholders (e.g., Vinay, Prastuti) on whether queue administration will remain a TR-only function or if selected HCL members will receive controlled access. 3) Define and document a standard process (e.g., request form or workflow) for HCL to request queue changes, including SLAs, roles and approvals. 4) Communicate the agreed process and responsibilities to HCL leadership and frontline supervisors, and update any onboarding materials for new agents. 5) Periodically review queue membership changes to ensure the process is being followed and remains efficient.

risks.title: Agent capacity and presence configuration may overload or mis-route chats
risks.description: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) agent presence and capacity settings are not yet properly configured. Many agents appear as "available" indefinitely (even after being inactive for long periods), and default capacities (e.g., number of parallel chats per agent) are effectively unset or inconsistent. This can cause the system to treat long-inactive agents as available capacity and over-assign chats beyond reasonable limits.
risks.impact_description: If agent presence and capacity configurations remain unoptimized, chats may be routed to agents who are actually offline or no longer on shift, leading to long customer wait times and abandoned chats. Agents who are online can be overloaded with too many concurrent chats, impacting quality and agent experience. Misrouted or stuck chats will undermine confidence in the new agent chat solution and may force manual interventions, slowing adoption and putting service KPIs at risk.
risks.mitigation: 1) Define standard capacity limits per agent (e.g., 5 concurrent chats/incidents as discussed) and configure these limits consistently across all pilot agents. 2) Investigate whether there is an out-of-the-box or script-based mechanism to automatically mark agents offline after a defined period of inactivity or after logout; if available, implement and test it. 3) Review historical presence data (e.g., agents still showing available after weeks) to validate that the new configuration works as expected. 4) Coordinate with Gandikota, Srinu to deploy configuration changes across DEV/QA and PROD environments to keep them aligned. 5) Monitor queue utilization and agent feedback during the pilot to refine capacity and presence thresholds before broader rollout.

risks.title: Inconsistent IMC (incident) sharing behavior from agent chat
risks.description: An HCL team member observed that, after closing the chat, the incident (IMC) was not automatically shared back to the user as expected, despite recorded demos showing that it should be shared automatically when the agent creates the incident. The root cause is unclear (e.g., chat closed before saving, configuration differences, or defects).
risks.impact_description: If the incident (IMC) details are not consistently and automatically shared back to users at the end of agent chat sessions, customers may not receive confirmation or reference numbers for their cases. This can lead to confusion, repeat contacts, and reduced trust in the new chat channel. Inconsistent behavior across environments or users also complicates training and makes it harder for HCL agents to follow a standard workflow.
risks.mitigation: 1) Reproduce the scenario reported by the HCL agent, validating the sequence of steps (when the incident is created, when the chat is closed). 2) Compare configuration and behavior with the recorded demo flow where automatic sharing worked correctly, to identify any discrepancies (e.g., scripting, workflow changes, environment differences). 3) Engage the reporting agent (via Nitin) to review their exact steps and confirm whether the chat may have been closed before saving the incident. 4) Fix any configuration or workflow issues and re-test across multiple agents. 5) Document the correct procedure and update training so agents understand when the IMC will be shared automatically and what to do if it is not.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-07 commitment
risks.description: The team committed to having a more natural, conversational virtual agent greeting, closing, and fallback experience ready by 2026-05-07, based on feedback from leaders (including Marc) that the current Now Assist chat lacks greetings, closing messages, validation, and ticket number sharing. During the 2026-05-05 SNOWNAWA working session, Shariq highlighted that there has been "no meaningful progress" on these conversational workflows, ownership is unclear (who raises the story, what Ashima and developers are working from), and admin access to edit templates is constrained. Although predefined templates and out-of-the-box system topics exist, they are not yet configured to meet the desired experience. If these items are not implemented and tested rapidly, the team may miss the 2026-05-07 target it has "given ourselves" for fixing the greetings and related chat behaviors.
risks.impact_description: If the conversational greeting, closing, and fallback workflows are not implemented and validated by 2026-05-07, the virtual agent experience will remain non-conversational (no personalized greeting, no clear closing, weak error/fallback handling, inconsistent ticket number communication). This will directly contradict commitments made to Marc and other stakeholders, undermine confidence in Now Assist as a polished product, and may delay further pilot or rollout activities that assume a baseline conversational experience. It also increases the likelihood of additional rework after leadership feedback, consuming scarce developer and SME time during an already compressed window.
risks.mitigation:
1) Capture a concrete story with clear description and acceptance criteria for the conversational workflow (greeting, closing, error handling, and fallback messages), as discussed by Vinay and Shariq, using the existing "virtual agent" story template format.
2) Shariq, Mayank, and Prithwiraj will meet immediately after the 2026-05-05 team meeting to define the exact greeting and fallback prompts, including personalization (e.g., "Hey, <name>, how can I help you?"), and provide these to Vinay the same day.
3) Ensure appropriate admin access is granted (e.g., to Mayank or another designated admin) to edit or duplicate the greeting templates and system topics in the sandbox environment.
4) Ashima has scheduled a focused working session for the next day with Srinivasan, Vinay, and others to prioritize and implement the greeting and fallback changes, treating this as a working session rather than relying on daily, asynchronous feedback.
5) Run internal "beta" testing by Shariq, Mayank, and Prithwiraj on the updated experience before requesting Marc and other leaders to retest, iterating quickly on any issues identified in the session.
6) Track progress against the 2026-05-07 target explicitly and escalate immediately if development or access constraints threaten that date.
7) As of the 2026-05-07 Service Desk AI automation sync, the team has progressed two of the seven documented conversational topics (initial greeting scenario and handover flow) but Mayank reported test failures in key scenarios (e.g., user enters a problem statement directly without "hi" and receives no greeting or empathy message; handover confirmation flow not yet implemented). Additional UX requirements were agreed, including an empathy-style acknowledgement that references the user’s name where technically feasible, replacing drop-down topic selection with visible options for top topics, and capturing all feedback and status in a centralized Excel tracker that Ashima will create. Daily 9 PM IST standups will be used to track completion of the remaining topics and retesting.

risks.title: Delay in KB refresh planning and execution may impact Now Assist accuracy and timelines
risks.description: The detailed review and refresh of the ~500 prioritized service desk KB articles has not yet started. During the April 29, 2026 KB planning meeting, Shariq noted he will not be able to meaningfully progress this work until after the upcoming long weekend and is targeting Tuesday to have an executable plan. Until the review starts and decisions are made on which KBs to keep, update, merge, or archive, Now Assist will continue to use the existing, potentially outdated content set.
risks.impact_description: If planning and execution of the KB refresh continues to slip, Now Assist will rely on a stale and partially inaccurate KB corpus. This can lead to incorrect or confusing answers, reduced trust from end users and ServiceDeskLeads, and potential pushback on broader rollout. Extended delay could also create misalignment with other milestones (e.g., virtual agent enhancements and IVR integration) that assume refreshed, curated KB content is available.
risks.mitigation: 1) Lock in a concrete plan by the Tuesday following the long weekend (early May 2026) for how to execute the KB refresh, including scope (top ~100 KBs first), sequencing, and owners. 2) Use Bineesh’s Excel list (886 total, 539 'keep', AI-suggested top 100) as the working baseline and assign reviewers (ServiceDeskLeads SMEs, Rashid, and knowledge manager Prastuti) to specific KB subsets. 3) Agree a time-boxed initial pass focused on the AI-suggested top 100 KBs so these can be validated and updated quickly, while planning subsequent passes for the remaining 'keep' KBs. 4) Track progress against this plan in the PMO tracker and adjust related virtual agent/Now Assist milestones if delays arise. 5) Escalate resourcing conflicts (e.g., Shariq’s costing model work) to leadership if they threaten the agreed refresh schedule.

risks.title: HCL may not commit effort or timelines for Amazon Connect – Virtual Agent integration
risks.description: Amazon Connect CTI migration from Avaya is essentially complete and is being tested, with CTI expected to show caller details in ServiceNow. However, integrating Amazon Connect with the virtual agent (e.g., for IVR-driven password reset and other flows) will require additional work from HCL. In the April 29, 2026 meeting, Shariq raised concern that HCL may view this as additional effort and could request 'a couple of weeks of effort' or otherwise delay or resist the integration, which affects the project’s IVR use cases.
risks.impact_description: If HCL does not agree to, or significantly delays, the Amazon Connect – virtual agent integration, the project will not be able to extend Now Assist/virtual agent capabilities into the IVR channel. This would limit the solution to chat and web only, leaving voice call flows (e.g., password reset, PIN unlock) largely manual, reducing potential call deflection and cost savings. It may also require re-planning of 2026 scope (e.g., deferring IVR integration beyond this year) and could weaken the business case that assumed voice automation.
risks.mitigation:
1) Schedule a focused alignment meeting with Mazhar and Saket (as discussed in the April 29, 2026 call) to clarify expectations, technical approach, and effort for Amazon Connect – virtual agent integration. 2) Prioritize a minimal viable IVR integration scope for 2026, focusing on password reset and closely related flows, to keep effort bounded and easier for HCL to accept. 3) Obtain HCL’s explicit commitment (including estimated effort and timing) and document it in the plan and RAAID log. 4) Incorporate CTI behavior (showing caller details in ServiceNow) into the gap analysis and end-to-end design so value is clear to HCL. 5) If HCL signals that integration will be significantly delayed, adjust the roadmap to reflect a chat-only virtual agent for 2026 and update stakeholders on reduced IVR benefits.
6) As of the 2026-05-07 Service Desk AI automation sync, Kiran reported that Sankar has agreed to schedule an IVR integration demo session for Wednesday (after additional internal testing) and that HCL is waiting on TR to provide a "green signal" for IVR cutover and to communicate the new IVR number to Thomson Reuters users before switching from Avaya to Amazon Connect. These steps partially de-risk alignment but the overall dependency on HCL effort and formal integration timelines remains.

risks.title: Conversational greeting and fallback workflow may miss 2026-05-15 target due to customization constraints and vendor dependency
risks.description: The team has committed to delivering a complete conversational virtual agent workflow (including greetings when users do not start with "hi", handover behavior, and other feedback items) by 2026-05-15. Current testing shows that if a user types a problem directly (e.g., "my Outlook is crashing") without greeting the VA, the system does not send any greeting before giving a solution, which is considered poor user experience. Initial review on the prior Thursday suggested that achieving the desired greeting behavior may not be possible purely with out-of-the-box configuration and might require customization. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay cautioned that custom scripting inside Now Assist / Virtual Agent is high risk for future upgrades and generally not recommended without ServiceNow guidance. The team is now dependent on multiple working sessions with the ServiceNow vendor (planned from Tuesday to Friday) to determine whether the required behavior can be achieved via configuration or safe customization. Until this is resolved, progress on several of the eight conversational workflow requirements remains blocked, increasing the risk that the agreed May 15 date will slip.
risks.impact_description: If the conversational greeting, closing, and fallback workflows cannot be implemented without high‑risk customization, or if ServiceNow vendor guidance is delayed, the team may miss the 2026-05-15 target for completing all eight conversational feedback items. This would leave the current poor experience in place (no greeting when users jump straight into a problem statement) and contradict commitments to stakeholders such as Marc. It could delay promotion of any completed conversational changes to production (since Kiran and Jakub prefer a single batch move once all eight requirements are done), push back pilot timelines, and force rework if interim customizations break during the upcoming Zurich upgrade.
risks.mitigation:
1) Avoid high‑risk custom scripting in Now Assist / Virtual Agent where possible; prioritize configuration-based changes to greetings and handover flows.
2) Use the scheduled ServiceNow vendor working sessions (targeting 4 sessions between Tuesday and Friday) to review the specific greeting requirement where users do not start with "hi" and obtain explicit guidance on safe configuration vs customization options.
3) Vinay to document any proposed customization and validate with ServiceNow during these sessions before implementation.
4) Ashima to keep the tracker of eight conversational feedback items updated, reflecting that greeting behavior (feedback #1) remains in progress and handover (feedback #4) is now working, based on tests by Srinu and Mayank.
5) Kiran to coordinate and ensure the vendor sessions are scheduled and attended by the right team members (Vinay, Ashima, Mayank, Prithvi) and to relay the UX requirements back to ServiceNow.
6) Defer promotion of conversational workflow changes to production until all eight requirements are implemented and validated, to avoid multiple disruptive deployments during the Zurich upgrade window.

risks.title: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover
risks.description: During the May 11, 2026 Service Desk AI automation sync, Jakub and Saket reported an issue with the URL used by the Amazon Connect CTI integration: it currently opens an incident record populated with user details instead of an interaction record, whereas the desired behavior is to start from an interaction record. This misconfiguration is blocking completion of CTI testing and prevents scheduling the previously agreed Amazon Connect demo session for Wednesday. Saket stated that once the correct URL is provided and CTI testing is successful, the team will need an additional 2–3 business days to confirm testing, followed by approximately 10–14 days for the telco/ISP to change the external IVR numbers and perform cutover, with old numbers running in parallel for 2–3 weeks. Until the URL issue is resolved, these downstream steps cannot begin, putting IVR cutover timelines at risk.
risks.impact_description: If the Amazon Connect CTI URL continues to open incident records instead of interaction records, CTI testing cannot be completed and the planned Amazon Connect demo session for HCL/TR stakeholders will be delayed. This, in turn, delays finalizing IVR cutover dates and communicating new numbers to Thomson Reuters users. Because the telco/ISP requires roughly 10–14 days to implement number changes and old numbers will run in parallel only for a limited period, any slip in resolving the URL issue can cascade into delays for Avaya-to-Amazon Connect cutover and subsequent integration of Amazon Connect with Now Assist / Agent Chat. This would slow realization of voice deflection benefits and could necessitate re-planning of 2026 IVR-related milestones.
risks.mitigation:
1) Identify and correct the CTI integration URL so that Amazon Connect opens an interaction record in ServiceNow instead of an incident record; Kiran and Bineesh to coordinate with the appropriate ServiceNow and telephony contacts (as referenced in the email chain including Ragesh).
2) Engage ServiceNow support (potentially via Presto or another POC) to validate that the corrected URL and configuration align with best practices for CTI interaction handling.

assumptions.validation_method: Confirm that four working sessions with ServiceNow are scheduled and held between Tuesday and Friday and that they produce concrete configuration or design decisions for each of the eight conversational feedback items, especially greeting behavior when users do not start with "hi".
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

assumptions.title: Developers will complete backup of update sets and documentation before Zurich upgrade clone
assumptions.description: It is assumed that developers (primarily Srinu and Prashanth, with any contributions from Prudhvi or Mayank) will export all relevant ServiceNow update sets and document configuration changes not captured in update sets before the Zurich upgrade clone from production to the dev environment, as discussed in the May 11, 2026 sync.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Vinay explained the need to take backups of update sets before Friday and to document configuration-only changes so they can be re-applied after the clone. Srinu confirmed on the call that he and Prashanth would "take care of those" and that they are aware some items require manual rework.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Srinu and Prashanth have prior experience managing update sets and clones, and they explicitly acknowledged ownership for backups and documentation on the call. However, time constraints and competing upgrade testing tasks introduce moderate risk that some items may be missed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If, upon verification, some update sets or configuration steps were not backed up, the team should (1) immediately catalog what was lost, (2) allocate time for Srinu and Prashanth to re-implement those changes on the cloned dev instance, and (3) tighten the process for future upgrades by standardizing a backup checklist and sign-off step.
assumptions.validation_method: Verify by the end of Friday that (1) update sets containing recent conversational workflow and Agent Chat changes have been exported and stored, and (2) a document exists listing configuration-only changes that must be manually re-applied post-clone.
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

assumptions.title: Non-production development can continue during Zurich prod change freeze without impacting timelines
assumptions.description: The team assumes that the Zurich production change freeze does not prevent ongoing development and testing in non-production environments (Dev1 and QA) for virtual agent conversational workflows and Agent Chat, and that only promotions to production are restricted until after the upgrade window.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay clarified that although there is a dev freeze period for production (May 8 to June 8), developers can continue to work on changes in Dev1 and QA, with only production deployments blocked until after the change freeze. Kiran explicitly sought confirmation that this would not stop their work, and Vinay confirmed it would not.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The assumption is grounded in standard ServiceNow upgrade procedures and explicit statements from the platform lead, but final enforcement depends on broader change management policy, which may impose additional constraints.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If non-prod development is restricted, the team should (1) adjust timelines for conversational workflow and Agent Chat changes, (2) explore using a separate sandbox or lower environment not subject to the freeze, and (3) communicate revised delivery dates and risks to stakeholders, updating the RAAID log accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm with the ServiceNow upgrade/change management team that Dev1 and QA can be used for ongoing development and testing during the Zurich prod change freeze, and monitor whether any unexpected restrictions or repeated clones impact their usability.
assumptions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

issues.title: ServiceNow license renewal and Now Assist license mapping blocking AI capabilities on new instance
issues.description: ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping between the legacy and new instances are preventing Now Assist and related AI capabilities from being enabled on the new ServiceNow instance. The license team has confirmed that licenses are still effectively tied to the legacy instance, causing the Now Assist mapping on the new instance to be disconnected. As a result, ongoing work on Agent Chat enhancements, Amazon Connect CTI URL fixes, and other Now Assist/virtual agent features is currently on hold until the renewal discussion is resolved and licenses are properly applied to the new instance.
issues.impact_assessment: The unresolved ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping issue directly blocks enabling Now Assist/AI capabilities on the new ServiceNow instance. This has halted progress on Agent Chat gap analysis, Amazon Connect CTI URL enhancements, and broader Now Assist work (including Teams integration and password reset use cases). Until the licensing issue is resolved, the team cannot fully use out-of-the-box Now Assist capabilities or proceed with certain ServiceNow working sessions, which risks delaying multiple SD Automation milestones and pushing out planned go-lives for chat and IVR capabilities.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Agent Chat gap analysis and enhancements; Amazon Connect CTI URL fix and IVR migration; Now Assist / virtual agent development and testing; planned ServiceNow working sessions on password reset via Teams integration.
issues.resolution: Work with the AD licensing team and the ServiceNow account manager to finalize the renewal and ensure Now Assist licenses are correctly mapped to the new instance. Request that the account manager expedite re-enablement of Now Assist capabilities on the new instance even while broader renewal negotiations continue, so that ongoing AI/virtual agent work can resume. Once licenses are corrected, re-enable Now Assist on the new instance and validate that AI capabilities (including virtual agent and Teams integration) function as expected.

issues.title: NAVA / ServiceNow issue
issues.description: Assistants are not showing to restore the data after clone, and resolution is now additionally constrained by ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping between the legacy and new instances, which prevent enabling Now Assist capabilities on the new instance.
issues.impact_assessment: In addition to delaying NAVA rollout, environment upgrades, and impacting core Service Desk functionality, the issue is now explicitly compounded by ServiceNow license renewal and license mapping problems. Licenses are still tied to the legacy instance, so Now Assist cannot be fully enabled on the new instance, blocking attempts to restore assistants and validate conversational workflows after the clone.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Conversational workflow implementation; Agent Chat gap analysis dashboards; Amazon Connect CTI URL enhancement; ServiceNow license renewal and mapping with AD and ServiceNow account manager.
issues.resolution: Continue validating the plugin-upgrade workaround in dev, but also coordinate with the AD licensing team and the ServiceNow account manager to resolve license mapping so Now Assist can be enabled on the new instance. Once licensing is fixed, re-test assistant restoration, conversational workflows, and related dashboards to confirm the issue is fully resolved.

issues.title: Some HCL pilot users cannot access Agent Chat widget despite being in NAVA pilot group
issues.description: A subset of HCL pilot users (e.g., Kandibanda, Rakesh and Sri Lakshmi) cannot see or use the Agent Chat widget in ServiceNow, even though they are members of the NAVA pilot group and others in the same group have working access. This is causing inconsistent testing coverage for Agent Chat.
issues.impact_assessment: The inability of certain HCL pilot agents to access the Agent Chat widget prevents them from participating in hands-on testing. This undermines full coverage of languages/queues (e.g., former HCL service desk group members) and delays validation of Agent Chat configurations prior to production readiness. It also complicates identifying whether issues are user-specific role problems or systemic configuration defects.

issues.resolution: Validate that group roles from the NAVA pilot group are correctly applied to affected users by checking sys_user_role mappings and scheduled jobs; adjust group membership (remove/re-add users) as needed. Collect a complete list of impacted users via the shared Excel tracker, then systematically fix their access so all HCL testers can use Agent Chat.

decisions.title: No customization of interaction record for Amazon Connect CTI; use out-of-the-box interaction view
decisions.description: For the Amazon Connect–ServiceNow CTI integration, the interaction record opened for agents must remain the out-of-the-box interaction view (showing user details, recent tasks/interactions, and assigned assets). TR and HCL agreed that no new fields or layout customizations will be implemented on this interaction record as part of the CTI URL change; the focus is solely on providing a URL that opens the standard interaction record instead of an incident.
decisions.rationale: ServiceNow vendor (John) recommended using out-of-the-box CTI capabilities and the Amazon Connect connector rather than building custom APIs or customized interaction forms. Keeping the interaction record standard reduces maintenance, avoids high-risk customizations, and ensures future compatibility, while still meeting HCLs requirement to see user details and related records when a call is received.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Customize the interaction record (new fields/layout changes) to meet HCLs expectations; 2) Use the out-of-the-box interaction record and only adjust the CTI URL to open it; 3) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and new flows in a future phase.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Amazon Connect (AWS) CTI integration with ServiceNow and Virtual Agent; Risk: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover; Action: Provide corrected CTI interaction URL for Amazon ConnectServiceNow integration.
decisions.source_file_name: Issue with Amazon CTI URL __ RITM0147285 & REQ0145658.docx

decisions.title: Prioritize minimal-change CTI URL fix for Amazon Connect migration and defer connector-based redesign
decisions.description: For the immediate Avaya-to-Amazon Connect migration, TR and HCL will prioritize a minimal-change solution that adjusts the existing CTI URL so it opens an interaction record (instead of an incident) using current architecture, rather than redesigning the integration around the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector. A connector-based redesign and proof of concept (POC) may be pursued later once the basic migration is stable and time/resources permit.
decisions.rationale: HCL reported that almost all technical and UAT activities for the Amazon Connect migration are complete, with only the URL landing page behavior pending. ServiceNow vendor guidance and internal review indicated that re-architecting around the Amazon Connect connector would require additional time, effort, and POC work, which the team cannot afford before go-live. A minimal-change CTI URL fix enables timely migration while keeping open the option to adopt the connector later.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and perform a POC in sandbox before go-live; 2) Adjust the existing CTI URL and parameters to open an interaction record instead of an incident, keeping the current architecture; 3) Continue with the current incident-landing behavior and accept the UX gap.

AI Reimagine Other Pillar Point Solutions is delivering AI-driven automation across ETS, ISRM, and Strategy & Operations to remove manual effort, reduce Service Desk demand, and embed always-on security controls.
