assumptions.title: Make Tax Digital (MTD) core finance solution remains a standalone, user-managed process with no direct IFS integration changes required
assumptions.description: Ravi and Manjunatha agreed that the MTD core finance / Make Tax Digital solution is effectively a standalone application used by finance users, where outputs from IFS are taken and then fed into the MTD software (likely from Excel or similar). They confirmed there is no direct, real-time integration from IFS to MTD; finance users manage the data transfer outside the migration project. Therefore, the project is assuming that no changes are needed to MTD as part of the IFS Azure migration and that MTD activities will continue to be handled by the finance team.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Ravi described MTD as "pretty much... a standalone application" where finance staff take an output from IFS and feed it into MTD software, with no direct technical connection. This aligns with existing understanding that MTD is out of scope for the migration.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Both technical (Ravi) and PM (Manjunatha) perspectives concur that MTD consumes exported IFS data rather than connecting to IFS directly. Existing scope classification also treats MTD as out-of-scope for technical migration work, reinforcing that it is operationally decoupled from the IFS hosting move.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If it is discovered that MTD has technical dependencies on the on-premise IFS setup (e.g., hard-coded paths, file shares, or formats), the project will:
- Create a small, focused change workstream to adjust IFS outputs or provide equivalent exports from the Azure-hosted IFS.
- Coordinate with finance to plan and test these changes before any tax-critical deadlines.
- Re-assess scope and timelines to accommodate the additional MTD-related work.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Confirm with the finance team responsible for MTD that they do not rely on direct technical integration from IFS and that their process will remain unchanged.
2) Review any existing documentation or diagrams for MTD to ensure no hidden system-to-system connections from IFS are present.
3) During test migration, have finance validate that the required IFS outputs for MTD can still be produced post-migration.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call-22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: IFS integrations will operate as a lift-and-shift with existing connection patterns preserved
assumptions.description: Ravi explained that the initial understanding of the project was that, because this is a lift-and-shift migration, connections and integrations would remain "as is" without re-architecting them. Although the team now recognizes they must explicitly discover and document the actual integration mechanisms, the working assumption for planning is still that the fundamental integration patterns (e.g., which systems integrate with IFS, the high-level flow through Boomi and EDL) will not change as part of the migration.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project was framed as a lift-and-shift from Nordlo to Azure, and Ravi noted that their original view was that integrations would "just come in as is" and they would not "redo the architecture". This assumption underpins the current migration planning and timelines.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current discussions focus on confirming endpoints, ports, and whitelisting for existing interfaces rather than proposing new integration mechanisms. This suggests that configuration changes on top of the current architecture should suffice, though the team acknowledges that discovery is still in progress and could surface exceptions.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If discovery or testing shows that certain integrations cannot simply be lifted and shifted:
- Elevate the affected integrations as specific design items, with architecture and security review as needed.
- Re-plan the migration to include design, build, and test work for alternative integration patterns, and adjust milestones accordingly.
- Consider phased migration where feasible, decoupling complex integrations from the main cutover, or implement temporary bridging solutions (e.g., additional middleware or reverse proxies) to protect the overall timeline.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Complete the integration discovery activities with Boomi, EDL, Pagero Online, and SFTP-based interfaces to confirm that each integration can be re-pointed to Azure without architectural redesign.
2) Validate with ISRM and networking that the planned connectivity methods (VPN, Data Guard-based DR, whitelisted IPs, etc.) are acceptable for each integration.
3) Prove the connectivity approach in the pilot/test environment, verifying that all key integrations behave as expected with only configuration-level changes.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call-22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: IFS test environment usage is low enough that migration over the 8–10 May 2026 window will cause minimal disruption
assumptions.description: During the 22 Apr 2026 planning call, Ravi, Bhanuka and Ranuka agreed that the IFS test environment is currently used primarily by a small group of developers for bridging-related work, and that most developments are already complete. UAT/SIT for bridging will mainly be conducted in CFG, and test is not heavily used for support cases or reporting. They therefore assume that moving the test environment to Muzulu Azure over the 8–10 May weekend (cloning the 1.6 TB database and switching DNS) will have minimal impact on users, especially if executed during a quiet period that includes TR’s Mental Health Day holiday on 8 May and a weekend, with any disruption limited to a small set of developers.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Bhanuka stated that developments for bridging are mostly complete and that UAT/SIT will primarily run in CFG, not test. He and Ranuka confirmed that test is mainly used by the development team and occasionally for minor reporting or support, not as a critical environment. Ravi highlighted that this makes the current period an ideal time to move test because usage is relatively low, and the transition can be scheduled over a weekend and TR holiday to further reduce impact.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The assumption is supported by direct input from the primary owners of test usage and by the project’s current plan to conduct formal testing in CFG rather than test. However, some uncertainty remains because Bhanuka is still confirming whether Mahesh and Sharmilan might need test for any new or rework developments, and ad hoc uses (e.g., quick reports) could arise. This warrants validation close to the migration date.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If validation shows that test is needed more heavily than expected during the planned migration window:
- Reschedule the test migration to a later weekend or lower-usage period acceptable to the affected teams.
- Coordinate with the impacted developers/users to adjust their work plans, including shifting certain activities to CFG if feasible.
- Provide clearer communication and a more detailed cutover plan (including exact downtime periods) so users can plan around the outage.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Bhanuka will confirm with Mahesh and Sharmilan whether any new or rework code changes are planned in test around the migration window and whether they rely on test for upcoming work.
2) Ranuka will validate whether test is used for any support cases or quick reports that cannot be paused over the migration weekend.
3) If needed, a short communication will be sent to known test users to confirm that the planned outage window is acceptable and to identify any critical conflicts.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call - 22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: Most IFS integrations use HTTPS 443 and DNS-based endpoints so whitelisting and port opening will be sufficient without application configuration changes
assumptions.description: Ravi and Manjunatha concluded, based on the integration map and discussion with Bhanuka, that almost all external systems (e.g., Oneflow, Elevation Documents, ECX/ECM via Boomi, Power BI and other HTTPS-based consumers) access IFS via HTTPS (port 443) using endpoint URLs. They assume that, for these integrations, moving IFS to Muzulu Azure will primarily require DNS updates and IP whitelisting/port opening, without needing application-side configuration changes. The plan is to verify and adjust as necessary through testing in the migrated test environment.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the 22 Apr 2026 call, Ravi stated that “almost everything is pretty much accessing IFS through HTTPS 443 on an endpoint basis.” He and Manjunatha agreed that for such integrations, whitelisting and DNS routing to the new Azure-hosted endpoints should be sufficient. The integration map Bhanuka shared further highlighted that many integrations call REST endpoints in IFS, reinforcing the endpoint-based pattern.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Preliminary analysis and historical architecture indicate that HTTPS-based, URL-driven integrations are the norm for many IFS consumers. However, some integrations (e.g., FireTran, AWS Glue, Zift) may use different mechanisms or rely on agents and database-level connections, and detailed confirmation is still pending. The team acknowledges this by planning to use the test migration as the main proving ground for connectivity assumptions.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If testing reveals that certain integrations require additional changes beyond DNS and whitelisting:
- Treat those integrations as specific design work items, involving the relevant system owners and TR networking/ISRM as needed.
- Update the network/integration diagrams and runbooks to capture the additional requirements (e.g., certificate updates, alternate ports, or configuration changes).
- Adjust CFG and production migration plans to include the extra work, and consider phased enablement or temporary workarounds to protect the overall go-live timeline.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Use the migrated test environment to exercise each known HTTPS-based integration (including Oneflow, Elevation Documents, ECX/ECM via Boomi, Power BI and other endpoint consumers) and confirm connectivity and functionality.
2) Coordinate with each integration owner identified by Bhanuka to verify whether they depend solely on DNS-based URLs or have any hard-coded IPs or additional configuration requirements.
3) Review logs and network traces during testing to identify any unexpected ports, protocols or destinations that might require extra configuration.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call - 22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: Single sign-on (SSO) for IFS will continue to function after migration because it is handled externally to TR and Muzulu networks
assumptions.description: In the 22 Apr 2026 planning call, Ravi asserted that SSO for IFS operates over HTTPS and is handled outside both the TR network and the Muzulu network, implying that moving IFS from Nordlo to Muzulu Azure should not materially affect SSO. The working assumption is that SSO will continue to function after migration without significant changes, assuming URLs and certificates are managed consistently.
assumptions.rationale_basis: When discussing potential impacts of DNS changes and test migration, Ravi stated that “SSO is essentially… handled outside of TR network and the Muzulu network. So that shouldn’t be a problem.” This reflects an architectural understanding that identity and SSO flows rely on external identity providers and standard HTTPS, not on internal networking specifics, and therefore should not require major changes when the application hosting location changes.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The statement about SSO being handled outside TR and Muzulu networks suggests a decoupled, standards-based SSO implementation. However, no detailed SSO verification has yet been performed against the Azure-hosted environment, and subtle dependencies (e.g., callback URLs, certificate bindings) could still exist. The assumption is reasonable but needs explicit verification in the test environment.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If SSO fails after migration or requires additional changes:
- Engage the TR identity/SSO team immediately to update application configuration (callback URLs, audience URIs, certificates) for the Azure-hosted IFS endpoints.
- Provide users with a temporary non-SSO access method (if feasible and approved by security) for test/UAT environments while SSO changes are implemented.
- Incorporate SSO configuration updates and validation steps into the CFG and production migration runbooks to prevent recurrence.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Review the current SSO configuration for IFS (e.g., relying party/application configuration in the identity provider) to confirm that it references logical URLs and certificates that can be preserved or updated.
2) Coordinate with the TR identity/SSO team to validate that moving IFS hosting to Azure does not violate any existing trust or network assumptions.
3) After migrating the test environment, perform end-to-end SSO login tests from representative user accounts to ensure authentication works as expected.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call - 22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: Downstream systems consuming EDL data do not require direct involvement if EDL ingestion from IFS is preserved
assumptions.description: Manjunatha and Ravi previously agreed that once IFS data is successfully pushed into EDL, the project team does not need to directly engage with downstream consumers such as HighRadius and other applications, treating EDL as the contract boundary. In the 13 May 2026 planning call, they reaffirmed that downstream systems (e.g., HighRadius, Ebob Finance, Eloqua) should continue to consume data from EDL without application-level changes, but agreed that those teams will be informed about the migration and asked to perform post-migration sanity checks on their reports and data extracts. The working assumption remains that no configuration changes are required in these downstream applications as long as EDL ingestion from IFS continues to function correctly.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In earlier discussions, Ravi confirmed that IFS data flows into EDL via FireTran and AWS Glue and that downstream systems like HighRadius are "customers" of EDL rather than direct IFS consumers. During the 13 May 2026 call, Bhanuka reiterated that HighRadius and similar systems query EDL using table-level access, and Ravi emphasized that the only reconnection required on the migration side is for FireTran and Glue; once data is in EDL, downstream consumers operate as before. Manjunatha suggested that HighRadius, Ebob Finance, and Eloqua should be included mainly for post-migration sanity checks rather than design changes.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The data platform pattern (IFS → FireTran/AWS Glue → EDL → downstream systems) is already in use, and both Ravi and Manjunatha view EDL as the integration boundary. The 13 May 2026 call clarified that HighRadius and similar systems build their queries on EDL table structures provided by the IFS/EDL team. While downstream teams will be engaged for sanity checks, there is no evidence so far of direct IFS connectivity, making it reasonable to treat their involvement as validation rather than core integration work.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If validation shows that any downstream system has direct or non-EDL dependencies on IFS:
- Add those systems and their owners to the migration integration list and include them in detailed planning and test cycles.
- Update the integration diagrams and runbooks to reflect their connectivity and required changes.
- Plan and implement necessary configuration changes or alternative integration paths (e.g., new views, APIs, or data exports) before production cutover.
- Communicate revised timelines and expectations to business stakeholders if additional work impacts the schedule.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Work with the EDL owner (Eljo Kadavy) to confirm the list of downstream systems (including HighRadius, Ebob Finance, Eloqua) and verify that they access data exclusively via EDL tables rather than directly from IFS.
2) Use the integrations kickoff meeting to inform downstream owners of the migration and agree on a minimum set of post-migration sanity checks.
3) After the IFS Test (and later CFG) migrations, request that HighRadius and other key downstream teams run their standard queries/reports to confirm data availability and correctness.
4) Update documentation and integration diagrams if any direct IFS dependencies are discovered.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call-22-Apr.docx

assumptions.title: Oracle version and patch level will remain unchanged during migration by using Oracle refreshable PDB cloning
assumptions.description: In the 18 May 2026 meeting, Pransh from the Data Factory/EDL team asked whether the Oracle version would change as part of the migration. Ravi confirmed that the migration uses Oracle's refreshable PDB clone feature and that the target database in Muzulu Azure will run the same Oracle version and patch set as the current Nordlo-hosted IFS database. The project is therefore assuming that Oracle version and patch level remain identical across source and target, avoiding database-level upgrade changes during the migration.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Ravi stated explicitly that the migration is a clone-based lift and shift, and that they "have to stick to the exact version and exact patch levels" in order to maintain compatibility with IFS and existing integrations. This underpins the decision not to perform an Oracle upgrade as part of this project.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The pilot migration has already demonstrated successful cloning of the 1.6 TB test database, and Ravi reiterated that the approach preserves the exact Oracle version and patch level. Oracle's PDB clone mechanism is a standard way to move databases without version changes, making this assumption technically sound provided the process is followed consistently.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If it is discovered that the Azure-hosted Oracle instance differs in version or patch level:
- Freeze further environment migrations and perform a focused compatibility assessment for IFS and key integrations.
- Decide, with IFS vendor support if necessary, whether to align by upgrading/downgrading the Azure instance or by upgrading the Nordlo source before cloning.
- Expand regression testing scope on the affected version to cover core ERP and integration scenarios.
- Update the migration plan and timelines to incorporate any required upgrade work and additional testing.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Confirm with Muzulu Oracle DBAs (Mahesh and team) that the target Azure Oracle instance is created using a PDB clone from the existing Nordlo database, preserving version and patch set.
2) Capture and compare Oracle version/patch information (e.g., from `v$version`) on both Nordlo and Azure instances as part of the pilot and Test migrations.
3) Include version checks in migration runbooks so that any deviation is detected before CFG and Production migrations.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS environment Migration from Nordlo to Muzulu-18-May-2026.docx

assumptions.title: Nordlo-hosted SFTP servers for finance uploads will remain available and reachable to IFS after migration
assumptions.description: The team plans a lift-and-shift of the IFS application to Muzulu Azure while keeping existing external endpoints (including Nordlo-hosted SFTP servers) "as is". In the 18 May 2026 call, Johan confirmed that monthly finance transactional uploads are written to an SFTP managed by Nordlo, from which IFS reads the data. Ravi stated that there is currently no plan to move these SFTP servers, and that IFS should continue to read from them post-migration, while Manjunatha noted that moving them later might be preferable. For current planning, the project assumes Nordlo-hosted SFTP services will remain available, accessible, and correctly connected to the Azure-hosted IFS after migration.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Ravi emphasised that the immediate focus is on migrating IFS and keeping other endpoints unchanged, to minimise scope. No business requirement has yet been raised to move the Nordlo SFTP services, and Johan indicated that continued IFS access to the existing SFTP would be acceptable as long as it works.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The existing SFTP integration is already in production and has not been flagged for change by business stakeholders. Network connectivity between Azure and Nordlo can be engineered via existing VPN and whitelisting approaches used elsewhere in the project. However, both Manjunatha and Johan acknowledged that relying long-term on Nordlo is not ideal, so this is treated as a valid but time-bounded assumption.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If Nordlo SFTP availability or connectivity cannot be assured:
- Prioritise design and implementation of an alternative SFTP or secure file transfer solution under Muzulu/TR control, with equivalent interfaces and credentials for finance upload processes.
- Plan a controlled cutover of finance uploads to the new SFTP, including coordination with finance teams and thorough testing.
- In the interim, agree short-term manual or alternate upload mechanisms if necessary to maintain finance operations.
- Update the risk register and migration plan to reflect the accelerated SFTP migration work and any associated schedule impacts.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) During Test and CFG migrations, validate end-to-end SFTP flows from Nordlo to the Azure-hosted IFS instance, including authentication and file transfer.
2) Confirm with Nordlo (via technical discussions led by Ravi) that the SFTP infrastructure is stable and will be maintained for at least the duration of the project and agreed post-go-live period.
3) Monitor SFTP availability and error rates via logs and alerts after each environment migration.
4) Reconfirm with finance stakeholders (Johan and Pagero finance team) that the current SFTP arrangement remains acceptable until/unless a migration of the SFTP itself is planned.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS environment Migration from Nordlo to Muzulu-18-May-2026.docx

assumptions.title: Production go-live plan assumes adequate resource availability despite European vacation period
assumptions.description: The current high-level plan targets mid-July 2026 (weeks 29–30) for production cutover. In the 18 May 2026 meeting, Johan cautioned that this period falls in the middle of the European vacation season, making it difficult to secure key personnel. Despite this, the working assumption for now is that sufficient resources can be made available via planning and coverage arrangements to support a mid-July go-live and hypercare.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project schedule, including SRB approval, Test and CFG migrations, and DR testing, currently aligns to a mid-July cutover. Moving the date substantially later could compress post-migration activities or affect dependent work, so the team is tentatively holding mid-July as the target while assessing resource availability.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The plan currently targets mid-July based on technical task sequencing rather than resource calendars. Feedback from Johan indicates a real risk that this period is not ideal for European teams. Until a structured resource planning exercise is completed, the assumption that coverage can be arranged is tentative and carries low confidence.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency:
If validation shows that resource coverage is inadequate for mid-July:
- Reschedule the production cutover to a more suitable window (e.g., late June or post-vacation), balancing technical readiness and business constraints.
- Alternatively, adjust the cutover scope (e.g., staged go-live, lower-risk changes) or reinforce coverage by bringing in additional or cross-trained staff.
- Communicate the revised timeline and rationale to all stakeholders, updating milestones and dependencies accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method:
1) Conduct a resource and vacation planning exercise with all key teams (integration owners, Boomi, EDL/Data Factory, finance, infrastructure/DBA, support) to identify availability during the proposed cutover window.
2) Confirm with Veena (sponsor), Bhanuka, and team leads whether minimum staffing levels can be met in mid-July, including backups.
3) Use the go/no-go readiness process to explicitly confirm that agreed resource coverage is in place; if not, revisit the cutover date.
4) Document any decisions to adjust the cutover window and update project and stakeholder communications accordingly.
assumptions.source_file_name: IFS environment Migration from Nordlo to Muzulu-18-May-2026.docx

dependencies.title: Whitelisting FireTran and AWS Glue IPs on Azure-hosted Pagero Oracle database
dependencies.description: To maintain EDL integrations after migrating IFS/Oracle from the Nordlo datacentre to Muzulu Azure Cloud, the project must whitelist specific external IP addresses on the Azure-hosted Pagero Oracle DB instance. FireTran requires inbound access on its default agent port (4343) from its public IP addresses to the HVA agent installed on the Oracle database. AWS Glue requires inbound access (Oracle native ODBC, typically port 1521) from TR-managed/AWS network IPs to the same database. Without these whitelist entries, the FireTran HVA agent and AWS Glue jobs will be unable to connect to the migrated Oracle database and load data into Snowflake, breaking Pagero-related EDL ingestion pipelines.
dependencies.dependent_on: Network/security configuration of the Azure-hosted Pagero Oracle DB instance (Muzulu/Nordlo/TR networking) to whitelist FireTran public IPs and TR/AWS Glue IP addresses on ports 4343 and 1521.
dependencies.consumer: IFS ERP Cloud migration team and EDL team for Pagero data ingestion into Snowflake
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the FireTran and AWS Glue IP ranges are not whitelisted before migration and testing, EDL ingestion pipelines for Pagero/IFS data will fail, preventing validation of data flows in lower environments and potentially delaying integration testing, UAT, and overall migration timelines.
dependencies.mitigation: Kadavy, Eljo V. will provide the FireTran and TR/AWS Glue IP ranges that need to be whitelisted; B H, Manjunatha R. and Ravi Edirisinghe will coordinate with Muzulu/Oracle DB administrators and TR networking to apply the whitelist changes in Azure. Connectivity will first be validated against a pilot or lower environment database, with TR Networking engaged if any connectivity or firewall issues arise.

dependencies.title: Integration testing support from TR teams for IFS ERP migration
dependencies.description: The IFS ERP platform integrates with multiple systems including Boomi, ECX/ECM, FireTran, and EDL. Successful and timely completion of the migration depends on the availability and engagement of various Thomson Reuters teams to support integration and testing activities, and on aligning this work into upstream and downstream teams’ backlogs without impacting their other deliverables.
dependencies.dependent_on: TR integration platforms (Boomi, ECX/ECM, FireTran, EDL) and the corresponding Thomson Reuters upstream/downstream teams
dependencies.consumer: IFS ERP Cloud migration team for Pagero on Muzulu Azure Cloud
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the required TR teams are not available when needed, integration and testing may be delayed, putting the overall IFS ERP cloud migration timeline at risk and potentially impacting cutover and go-live readiness.
dependencies.mitigation: Project team and all upstream/downstream teams must agree how integration and testing work will be scoped and scheduled into their respective backlogs so that migration activities are supported without significantly impacting other deliverables. As of the 15 April 2026 weekly planning call, Manjunatha will spend the next 1–2 weeks gathering detailed connection information from Boomi, EDL, Pagero Online and SFTP owners, after which a kickoff call will be scheduled to share the migration timeline and formally request each team’s testing support.

dependencies.title: Boomi-side IP whitelisting and connectivity/performance testing for Azure-hosted IFS ERP
dependencies.description: After migrating IFS ERP to Muzulu Azure Cloud, the Boomi services that integrate with Conga GSI and ECX/ECM MDM will continue to use the same service endpoints but will require the new Azure VM IP addresses to be whitelisted on Boomi’s side. Boomi will also run connectivity checks and load/performance tests to confirm that service performance is comparable to the current state.
dependencies.dependent_on: Boomi integration platform team to whitelist new Azure IFS VM IPs and execute agreed connectivity and performance tests.
dependencies.consumer: IFS ERP Cloud migration team and business processes relying on Boomi integrations (Conga GSI, ECX/ECM MDM)
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Boomi does not whitelist the new Azure IPs or complete connectivity/performance testing in time, Boomi-based integrations may fail or experience degraded performance after migration, delaying integration testing, raising go-live risk, and potentially impacting downstream systems dependent on Conga GSI and ECX/ECM data.
dependencies.mitigation: Ravi Edirisinghe will engage the Boomi team to confirm their requirements, provide the new Azure VM IP addresses once available, and agree a schedule for connectivity and load/performance testing aligned with the migration plan. Any additional Boomi security requirements will be captured and incorporated into the migration runbooks.
dependencies.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call-22-Apr.docx

dependencies.title: SRB approval required before proceeding with IFS Test environment migration to Azure
dependencies.description: The IFS Cloud Migration team must obtain Senior Review Board (SRB) approval for the updated DR architecture and connectivity design before proceeding with phase-one migration of the IFS Test environment to Muzulu Azure Cloud. Ravi and Manjunatha agreed that SRB approval is a key prerequisite, and plan to use an updated architecture deck and Eric's pre-review to streamline the SRB session.
dependencies.dependent_on: Senior Review Board (SRB) approval of the updated DR architecture and migration approach, following Eric's pre-review of the architecture deck.
dependencies.consumer: IFS Cloud Migration project team preparing to migrate the IFS Test environment to Azure
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If SRB approval is delayed, the planned phase-one migration of the IFS Test environment to Azure (targeted for the weekend of 8–10 May 2026) will be delayed, reducing the time available for integration testing, learning, and issue resolution before CFG and Production migrations, and potentially impacting the end-of-June cutover target.
dependencies.mitigation: Ravi Edirisinghe will update the DR/connectivity architecture deck incorporating Eric's previous feedback; B H, Manjunatha R. will schedule a pre-review call with Eric so he can align on the design ahead of the SRB. After Eric's endorsement, Manjunatha will schedule the SRB meeting for late April or early May to secure timely approval before the planned Test migration weekend.
dependencies.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call - 22-Apr.docx

decisions.title: Use site-to-site VPN between Nordlo datacentre and Muzulu Azure Cloud for migration
decisions.description: The project team will use a site-to-site VPN connection between the Nordlo datacentre (current IFS hosting) and the Muzulu Azure Cloud environment for the IFS ERP migration. An exception request has been submitted and approved to permit this setup even though a direct site-to-site VPN is not a Thomson Reuters standard. The VPN will remain in place only for the duration of the migration and will be removed after the production cutover is completed.

decision_owner.name: ISRM and business/leadership for the IFS Cloud Migration project

decisions.rationale: Due to bandwidth limitations with standard connectivity options, the networking team recommended a site-to-site VPN to ensure sufficient performance for migration activities. ISRM reviewed the proposal and, despite site-to-site VPN not being a TR standard, agreed to the exception given the temporary nature of the connection and the need to support migration performance.
decisions.options_considered: Standard TR-approved connectivity (non–site-to-site VPN) versus implementing a temporary site-to-site VPN between Nordlo DC and Muzulu Azure Cloud to address bandwidth constraints.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Relies on successful setup and operation of the temporary site-to-site VPN between Nordlo DC and Muzulu Azure Cloud; linked to migration performance and cutover risk accepted by ISRM and business/leadership.

decisions.title: Target weekend of 8–10 May 2026 for migrating IFS Test environment to Azure
decisions.description: During the 22 Apr 2026 planning call, the team agreed to aim for the weekend of 8–10 May 2026 to migrate the IFS Test environment from Nordlo to Muzulu Azure Cloud. The plan is to perform the database cloning and cutover activities over that long weekend (including 8 May, a TR Mental Health Day), update DNS entries to point to the new Azure-hosted Test environment, and have the environment available for developers and integration testing on the following Monday, with minimal disruption.
decisions.rationale: Test environment usage is currently low, and most bridging developments are expected to be completed by 30 April. Using the 8–10 May weekend (which includes a TR-wide holiday on 8 May) allows the migration team and Muzulu to perform cloning and cutover work during a quieter period, minimizing impact on developers while providing time over the weekend to resolve issues before users return.
decisions.options_considered: Performing the Test migration on 1 May (May Day public holiday in multiple regions) versus targeting the 8–10 May weekend which aligns better with TR availability and minimizes disruption; performing the migration during a standard weekday versus over a weekend.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Dependent on completion of repeated database clone tests to validate timing and reliability, and on SRB approval of the DR/migration design prior to the Test environment migration.
decisions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call - 22-Apr.docx

decisions.title: Exclude NodeLo / Nordlo from business-focused integration kickoff calls
decisions.description: For upcoming integration kickoff calls with upstream and downstream systems, NodeLo / Nordlo will not be invited to the regular business-focused sessions. Instead, NodeLo will be engaged separately by the IFS technical team to discuss whitelisting information, current SFTP and SMTP setups, and related infrastructure details, while the main calls will focus on testing, verification, and signoff with business and application stakeholders.
decisions.rationale: NodeLo’s involvement is primarily technical (whitelisting and infrastructure configuration) rather than business or functional testing. Handling NodeLo through direct technical discussions reduces complexity in recurring integration calls and allows those calls to concentrate on business-side testing and validation.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Include NodeLo / Nordlo in all upstream/downstream integration kickoff calls.
2) Exclude NodeLo from the recurring business-focused calls and handle their technical topics separately with the IFS technical team.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Related to dependency on NodeLo for SFTP and SMTP configurations and whitelisting; supports the existing dependency on integration testing support from TR and external teams.
decisions.source_file_name: IFS Cloud Migration - Weekly Planning call 13-05-26.docx

decisions.title: Include MDM team in integration validation despite Boomi handling connectivity
decisions.description: The Master Data Management (MDM) team will be explicitly included in integration kickoff and testing activities to validate that customer and product master data flows between MDM, GSI, and IFS (via Boomi) continue to function correctly after migration, even though Boomi handles the technical connectivity.
decisions.rationale: Although Boomi provides the integration platform, Boomi engineers typically do not validate business-level data correctness in MDM. The project team and Boomi do not have sufficient visibility into MDM’s internal data validation needs. Including MDM ensures that post-migration data streams are validated by the owning team and that any issues are detected early.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Rely solely on Boomi connectivity tests and IFS-side checks without involving MDM.
2) Include MDM representatives in testing to validate that their data streams and golden records remain correct after migration.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Supports the existing dependency on Boomi-side IP whitelisting and integration testing, and ensures master data quality for downstream systems.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Pricing Engine is delivering a centralized PROS-based pricing capability integrated with SAP, EPM, GSI, ECM/MDM, Conga, and Boomi so that Thomson Reuters can execute pricing decisions consistently across in-scope online products, customer segments, and channels, while retaining SAP/EPM as masters for other products. This matters because current fragmented pricing logic and data drive manual work, slower pricing changes, and higher risk around accuracy and compliance.

Release 1 and Release 2 designs are complete and signed off as of 27 Mar 2026 and 17 Apr 2026 respectively, and a manually validated end-to-end Conga–Boomi–PROS pricing flow is now working. However, Release 1 is trending behind plan: transactional data for optimization is only about 95% available (three remaining fields due by 22 May 2026), 4–6 Release 1 stories and 7–8 Release 2 stories are expected to spill into the next sprint, and critical integration design items such as Conga–Boomi field mapping and the PROS–SAP price list mechanism must be closed by 27 May 2026 to protect the 22 Jun 2026 SIT start and 13 Jul 2026 UAT start.

Overall status is Red, driven by Release 1 price optimization and data readiness delays that are compressing timelines to System Integration Testing, User Acceptance Testing, and the 14 Aug 2026 Release 1 go-live.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on unblocking Release 1 optimization and integrations by completing the remaining three transactional fields and composite customer key mapping by 22 May 2026, closing Conga–Boomi field alignment and PROS API/webhook sequencing by 27 May 2026, and loading full datasets into PROS DEV/QA so that the 22 Jun 2026 SIT start and 13 Jul 2026 dual-UAT start can proceed without further replan. In parallel, the team will lock the PROS–SAP price list exchange mechanism and analytics data granularity decisions by 27 May 2026, re-prioritize spillover stories onto the critical path, and secure Boomi performance and JWT integration approvals so performance SLAs and security patterns are agreed ahead of go-live.

## Milestones

- Begin Release 1 System Integration Testing (SIT) for pricing execution and optimization on 22 Jun 2026.  
- Start business-led Release 1 User Acceptance Testing across Small Law and Mid Law segments on 13 Jul 2026.  
- Achieve Release 1 Go Live with PROS-based pricing execution and optimization in production on 14 Aug 2026.  
- Achieve Release 2 Go Live with price management and pricing analytics capabilities in production on 14 Sep 2026.  
- Complete overall Pricing Engine program closure and transition to steady-state operations by 18 Sep 2026.

risks.title: Unclear PROS‑to‑EPM price publishing process may delay Release 2 price management readiness
risks.description: For products whose price lists are managed in EPM strategic stacks (e.g., Pagero), the end‑to‑end process for publishing PROS‑generated prices into EPM—including approvals, data structures, and automation boundaries—has not yet been fully defined. This clarity is required to support Release 2 price management capabilities.
risks.impact_description: If the PROS‑to‑EPM price publishing and governance process is not defined during Release 2 design, build activities may be delayed or require rework, resulting in extended manual price maintenance and delayed realization of centralized price management benefits.
risks.mitigation:
1. Conduct focused design sessions with the EPM strategic team to document current approval and price loading processes.
2. Define the future‑state PROS‑to‑EPM integration and approval model as part of Release 2 design.
3. Confirm which price management steps remain manual versus automated in Release 2.
4. Capture decisions in the Release 2 architecture and operating model documentation.

risks.title: Customer data source for pricing may not contain complete parent–child hierarchy
risks.description: The program is moving towards using GSI as the customer data source for pricing. However, there was uncertainty whether GSI contains the required parent–child customer relationships (e.g., global vs regional accounts) needed for pricing logic, and whether those relationships from ECM/D&B are properly propagated to GSI.
risks.impact_description: If GSI does not contain complete and correct parent–child customer hierarchy, the pricing engine may not be able to apply account‑hierarchy based pricing rules (e.g., global parent discounts rolling down to branches). This could lead to inaccurate pricing, rework to change the system of record to ECM, additional data mapping effort, and potential delays in design and implementation.
risks.mitigation: 1) Confirm with ECM and MDM architects (Sridhar, Kongot Sripriya) that parent–child relationships from ECM/D&B are pushed into GSI and where they are stored (e.g., Salesforce account parent fields, ultimate parent, domestic parent). 2) Have sales/MDM teams pull reports from GSI to verify those fields and the hierarchy quality. 3) Include the relevant hierarchy fields in the customer data mapping and spreadsheet so PROS can consume them. 4) If gaps are discovered, evaluate switching the pricing customer source to ECM and plan the additional mapping effort.

risks.title: Delay in receiving transactional order data extracts for price optimization design
risks.description: The team is unable to pull historical transactional/orders data from at least one source system and is also dependent on the MDM team to deliver a full extract of active materials and transactional variations across in-scope products. This data is required to understand how many variations exist (e.g., multiple UOM, banded vs fixed pricing) and to design how the price optimization engine and business rules will differentiate between models.
risks.impact_description: If complete transactional data extracts are not received in a timely manner, the team will be unable to: (1) design and validate the multi-UOM and pricing-method handling in the optimization engine; (2) confirm which attributes must be treated as drivers for optimization; and (3) finalize the business rule configuration for price optimization. This will delay Sprint 1 non-functional data setup, slow down price optimization design, and may force rework later if rules are based on incomplete patterns, potentially pushing out Release 1 optimization timelines.
risks.mitigation: 1) Work offline between TR Commercial Excellence (Arshad) and Deloitte (Neetika/Aditi) to resolve extraction blockers for the specific source that cannot currently provide orders data. 2) Continue coordinating with the MDM team to obtain a full, exhaustive extract of active materials and related transactional variations across in-scope products, and secure an explicit delivery timeline. 3) As soon as extracts are available, create a summary/segmentation view with Deloitte to identify key variation patterns and required optimization attributes in a joint working session. 4) If full-history extracts are delayed further, start with a representative subset of data for initial rule design, clearly marking assumptions and planning a validation pass once the complete extract is available.

risks.title: Price list structure and pricing model design may not be agreed in time for Release 2 price management
risks.description: The program still needs to align on the number of price lists, their segmentation logic (e.g., by product line, business unit, or sub-business unit), and the pricing models/formulas that will be configured in PROS. Current discussions reference SAP granularity (customer group, material ID, sales org, UOM), but there is not yet consensus on how to partition price books in PROS or how many price lists will exist. Neetika highlighted this as one of the most important design decisions for price management that needs to be closed within about a week and before the April 17 design target.
risks.impact_description: If agreement on price list structures and pricing models is delayed, the Release 2 price management design cannot be finalized by the planned April 17 date. This will impact configuration of PROS price management, slow down related design sessions and KDD closures, and may delay subsequent build activities for price management. It also increases the risk of suboptimal performance (e.g., overly large price books) or later rework if list segmentation decisions are changed after configuration has started.
risks.mitigation: 1) Use the full extract of active materials that Rajat and Arshad are arranging to quantify variation across segments and product families and inform practical price list segmentation options. 2) Leverage SAP’s current granularity (customer group, material ID, sales org, UOM, scales) as a baseline and workshop with TR Commercial Excellence (Rajat, Arshad) and Deloitte to propose 2–3 concrete price list segmentation scenarios (e.g., by product line or business unit). 3) Hold focused design workshops over the next week to review these scenarios, evaluate performance implications in PROS, and converge on the final number and structure of price lists. 4) Document the agreed model and lock it into Release 2 design decisions so later changes go through formal change control.

risks.title: Key design decisions (KDDs) for price management and analytics may not be closed by April 17
risks.description: Design sessions for Release 2 price management and pricing analytics have started, but the team is still in the familiarization phase and there are multiple key design decisions (KDDs) outstanding. Neetika stated that these KDDs are being targeted to close by April 17, and additional workshops are being scheduled up to that date. Given the volume of open questions (including price list structures, analytics requirements, and dashboard/chart constraints), there is a risk that not all KDDs will be fully resolved in time.
risks.impact_description: If the KDDs for price management and analytics are not closed by April 17, the ‘Design Completion Release 2’ milestone will effectively slip, delaying downstream build work on price management workflows and analytics dashboards in PROS. This can compress or push out development and testing timelines for Release 2, impact Sprint planning, and reduce the time available for validating analytics KPIs and user experience constraints (e.g., PROS five-charts-per-tab limitation), thereby increasing the likelihood of usability issues or scope reductions later.
risks.mitigation: 1) Maintain and execute the workshop schedule through April 17 with clear agendas focused on closing specific KDDs (price list structures, pricing models, analytics KPIs, and dashboard layouts). 2) Request that business stakeholders (Rajat, Arshad, Jenny and others) pre-populate required inputs such as formulas, KPIs, and process flows ahead of design sessions, as Aditi is already coordinating. 3) Prioritize the most critical KDDs that directly impact build (e.g., price list design, core analytics metrics) and formally defer lower-priority design details to later sprints if necessary. 4) Track KDD closure in Scrum calls twice a week, escalating unresolved items to Naresh and program leadership for timely decisions.

risks.title: Pricing engine call latency due to Boomi processing and batch design
risks.description: End‑to‑end pricing and optimization calls from Conga through Boomi to PROS may exceed acceptable response times, particularly during high‑volume transactions. This risk exists because Boomi parallel processing and batching patterns are being implemented for this use case for the first time, PROS batch size limits and throughput are still being validated, and final performance SLAs have not yet been proven under realistic load conditions. There is also uncertainty whether additional Boomi infrastructure capacity or PROS license scaling will be required to meet target response times.
risks.impact_description: If pricing and optimization calls exceed agreed SLAs, sales users may experience increased latency during quote creation and repricing, degrading user experience and potentially slowing deal execution and approvals. Failure to meet acceptable performance thresholds could force late architectural or capacity changes (e.g., infrastructure scaling, batch size adjustments, licensing increases), introducing schedule risk to Release 1 Go Live and subsequent releases.
risks.mitigation:
1. Define and formally agree acceptable performance SLAs for Conga–Boomi–PROS pricing and optimization calls with business stakeholders.
2. Finalize and review detailed Boomi design (batching approach, parallelization strategy) in middleware architecture sessions.
3. Perform early performance validation with PROS to confirm supported batch sizes and throughput limits; validate scalability assumptions.
4. Develop a capacity and cost estimate for potential Boomi infrastructure or PROS license scaling, if required.
5. Align on a phased performance strategy where initial go‑live meets minimum acceptable SLAs, with planned optimization improvements post‑launch if needed.
6. Communicate performance expectations clearly to business stakeholders ahead of Release 1 Go Live and secure agreement.

risks.title: Risk of exceeding PROS usage limits by onboarding all tenants
risks.description: Current direction was to onboard PROS for all tenants, but concerns were raised that if all tenants invoke PROS, the number of calls could quickly reach or exceed licensed or technically supported limits.
risks.impact_description: If all tenants begin calling PROS without usage controls, the program may exceed PROS transaction or license limits, resulting in throttling, failures, or unplanned license costs. This could force emergency restrictions or reconfiguration of integrations, delaying rollout and undermining business trust in the solution.
risks.mitigation: Revise onboarding strategy so that initially only the SCS tenant calls PROS. Defer enabling other tenants until actual usage is understood and performance and license impact are assessed. Inform Kumar of the revised direction and adjust tenant integration plans accordingly.

risks.title: Fragmented intake requests may disrupt Release 1 design closure and SLA alignment
risks.description: New intake requests related to Pricing Engine Release 1 (e.g., SAP, EPM, data, integrations) may be submitted without explicit linkage to the original program‑level intake, causing the work to be treated as net‑new. This can reset SLA expectations, create prioritization misalignment, and introduce confusion around scope, ownership, and delivery timelines during Release 1 design activities.
risks.impact_description: If Release 1–related intakes are not consistently linked to the parent Pricing Engine program context, delivery teams may reprioritize or delay work based on perceived “new” requests. This can result in missed SLAs, design churn, governance escalations, and delays to Release 1 design closure.
risks.mitigation:
1. Enforce linkage of all Release 1–related intakes as child requests under the Pricing Engine program intake.
2. Explicitly tag new intakes as Release 1 or Release 2 to maintain scope clarity.
3. Coordinate with Commercial Excellence and data domain owners to ensure consistent intake references and SLA alignment.
4. Transition any new Release 1 scope after design freeze through formal change control.

risks.title: Adding Mid Law testing alongside Small Law in Release 1 may strain UAT scope and timelines
risks.description: Originally, Release 1 UAT was aligned to focus on Small Law. Recent discussions with business teams indicate that Mid Law also wants to start testing in parallel with Small Law, using largely overlapping use cases but with some Mid Law–specific scenarios (including approval dashboard requirements). Yogesh confirmed that Small Law and Mid Law testing can happen in parallel, with weekly working sessions (Tuesdays and Thursdays), but enablement timing for Mid Law in production is still to be decided by the pricing/business team. Anantha noted this as a change item that needs leadership awareness and sign‑off, and there is not yet a clear, documented plan for when Mid Law will be enabled relative to Small Law.
risks.impact_description: If Mid Law testing is added to Release 1 UAT without a clear plan and resourcing, (1) the UAT scope and workload will increase, potentially overloading business testers and UAT support teams; (2) additional Mid Law–specific use cases and approval dashboard requirements may extend test design and execution time; and (3) ambiguity around production enablement timings for Mid Law versus Small Law could cause confusion, misaligned expectations with leadership, and last‑minute replanning. Collectively, this could delay UAT completion or force de‑scoping of test coverage for one or both segments.
risks.mitigation: 1) Document a clear plan and grid for Release 1 testing and enablement, explicitly listing which segments (Small Law, Mid Law) will test which scenarios and when, and how their UAT sign‑off aligns to release timelines. 2) Socialize this plan with enterprise and technical leadership to obtain explicit sign‑off on including Mid Law in parallel UAT, along with any required resource adjustments. 3) Work with UAT support to identify Mid Law–specific use cases and required accounts/products early, and make sure they are ready before test execution ramps up. 4) Clarify and communicate the intended production enablement sequence (e.g., whether Mid Law goes live with Release 2 while still using the optimization engine in Release 1) to avoid last‑minute scope changes.
risks.source_file_name: Price Engine - Internal Weekly Meeting (Core Working Group).docx

risks.title: Limits in SAP/EPM geographic granularity may constrain Release 2 pricing strategy
risks.description: The strategic pricing program has requested location‑specific list prices (e.g., state‑level pricing within a country). While PROS can model geography as a pricing dimension, it is not yet confirmed whether SAP and EPM master data and pricing models can support and operationalize this level of geographic granularity at scale. This clarification is required as part of Release 2 price management design.
risks.impact_description: If SAP and EPM cannot support the desired geographic pricing granularity, the end‑to‑end pricing stack may be unable to implement the requested location‑specific pricing strategy. This may require constraining geographic scope (e.g., region‑based pricing), introducing reference data workarounds, or adjusting business expectations for Release 2.
risks.mitigation:
1. Validate with PROS the supported geographic pricing dimensions.
2. Assess SAP and EPM master data structures and pricing models for their ability to support state‑ or location‑level pricing without excessive data growth.
3. Evaluate alternative design patterns (e.g., regional groupings, reference attributes) if state‑level pricing is not feasible.
4. Document supported geographic granularity and socialize constraints with strategic pricing stakeholders as part of Release 2 design.

risks.title: JWT-only PROS–TR integration approach may be delayed or rejected by Architecture Review Board
risks.description: The connection between the PROS environment and Thomson Reuters (TR) environment is currently designed to use a JWT token–based integration from Boomi to PROS. PROS product team confirmed that JWT is the only supported option (no OAuth or other alternatives). The proposed JWT solution is working in initial trials, but it still requires formal approval from the architectural review board (IRS/architecture forum), where the Boomi architect will present the design. Until this approval is granted, the integration pattern remains at risk of change.
risks.impact_description:
If the architectural review board does not approve the JWT-only integration pattern, or if the approval is significantly delayed, the program may need to revise the integration approach between Boomi and PROS. This could 
(1) delay completion of integration build and testing, 
(2) introduce rework in Boomi and PROS configuration, 
(3) postpone UAT and production readiness of pricing calls, and 
(4) potentially require exception or security waivers that add governance overhead and slow down deployment.
risks.mitigation:
1) Prepare and submit a thorough design package for the JWT-based Boomi–PROS integration to the Architecture Review Board (IRS forum), including security considerations, token lifecycle management, and auditability. 
2) Ensure the Boomi architect clearly presents that JWT is the only option PROS supports at this time, so alternatives are not assumed. 
3) Engage with security and architecture stakeholders ahead of the formal review to pre‑empt concerns and adjust minor design elements without changing the core JWT approach. 
4) Define a fallback plan (e.g., temporary exception approval or controlled scope of use) if the board raises concerns but cannot offer an immediate alternative, to avoid blocking critical integration timelines.

risks.title: Unresolved PROS–SAP price list mechanism and analytics data granularity may cause Release 2 sprint spillover
risks.description: In Week 18–19 status, Release 2 is in Sprint 2 with development focused on analytics setup and sample data loads. Progress is constrained by unresolved integration and design questions, specifically the mechanism for sending price lists from PROS to SAP (e.g., XML vs CSV) and alignment on analytics data granularity. These open items gate completion of Sprint 2 stories and threaten to cause sprint spillover and delay downstream work, even though development capacity itself is not the bottleneck.
risks.impact_description: If the PROS–SAP price list mechanism and analytics data granularity are not decided promptly, Sprint 2 stories for Release 2 will spill over, delaying completion of analytics setup and integration work. This will shorten the time available for subsequent development and testing cycles, increase the risk that analytics dashboards and price management capabilities are not ready by the planned Release 2 dates, and may force scope reductions or rework if late decisions conflict with earlier implementation assumptions.
risks.mitigation:
1) Hold a dedicated integration design workshop with SAP functional/technical teams, PROS architects, and Deloitte to compare XML vs CSV options for PROS–SAP price list exchange and decide on a single, supported mechanism.
2) Document the chosen interface format (including schema, transport, and error-handling approach) and update Release 2 integration user stories and technical designs accordingly.
3) In parallel, define target analytics data granularity by aligning Commercial Excellence, MDM, and EPM stakeholders on required dimensions and aggregation levels for dashboards, using current Sprint 2 sample data as a reference.
4) Treat these items as top-priority KDDs for Release 2; track them explicitly in sprint ceremonies and escalate to program leadership if decisions are not made within the current sprint so scope, sequencing, or timelines can be adjusted.

Per the Week 20 status, a proof of concept is underway to test CSV output from PROS instead of XML for better scalability, with PROS price list format decisions due around 2026-05-20 and all remaining integration design items (including the PROS–SAP mechanism) due by 2026-05-27.

risks.title: End-to-end pricing call performance SLA not yet agreed for Release 1
risks.description: The program does not yet have a confirmed performance model and SLA for pricing calls initiated from Conga and processed via Boomi to PROS. Boomi is implementing parallel processing with request splitting, but their current SLA is 2.5 seconds, and they cannot yet confirm expected processing time for the new pattern. Additional latency is expected due to multiple sequential calls (~3 × 300 ms), and it is unclear whether performance can be achieved without infrastructure or license cost increases. Business stakeholders have not yet agreed to the expected performance impact for initial releases.
risks.impact_description: Lack of clarity on Boomi and PROS performance and final SLA may result in slower-than-expected pricing calls for initial launches, affecting user experience and potentially delaying go-live if performance is unacceptable to business. Without a clear decision on either optimizing the integration pattern or investing in additional infrastructure and licenses, the architecture remains unsettled and business expectations cannot be managed. This uncertainty also complicates capacity planning (e.g., calling PROS from all tenants) and may force scope reductions such as limiting PROS onboarding to SCS initially.
risks.mitigation:
Potential resolutions under consideration include: 
(1) Boomi handling batching of pricing requests with optimized parallel processing; 
(2) PROS increasing batch size limits (from 10 to 40–50) to reduce the number of calls; and/or 
(3) upgrading Boomi infrastructure and licenses. 
Final resolution will require cost estimates, performance data, and business agreement on acceptable SLAs.
Agreement between Technology and Business on an acceptable Release 1 performance SLA, along with approval of any required infrastructure or licensing changes needed to meet that SLA.

Week 20 status confirms that manual end-to-end flow is working and integration design items (including field mapping and unique keys) are targeted for closure by 2026-05-27. However, performance SLAs remain to be validated once dynamic integration and guidance-driven calls are fully in place, so the risk remains open until those measurements and agreements are completed.
risks.source_file_name: PROS Pricing Engine Program Weekly Status Update (W20)_RevG.pptx

risks.title: Release 1 data extract delays increasing likelihood of late price optimization design and testing

risks.impact_description: If complete transactional data extracts (including derived attributes) continue to be delayed, PROS will not be able to finalize multi-UoM and pricing model design, determine key optimization drivers, or validate rules against real patterns. This will delay completion of Sprint 4 optimization stories, push out raw guidance generation, and may force hurried or suboptimal configuration based on incomplete data, increasing the risk of defects and further schedule slippage for Release 1.
risks.mitigation:
1) Escalate the data extract delays through the Pricing Engine SteerCo, explicitly linking them to the Red status for Release 1 and Sprint 4 blockers.
2) Work with MDM and source-system teams to define a committed delivery date for the full transactional extract, including derived attributes, and treat it as a hard milestone.
3) In the interim, expand the existing partial extract used by PROS so that at least a representative subset of events and attributes is available for continued design work.
4) Re-sequence Sprint 4 stories where possible so teams can focus on non-data-dependent tasks (e.g., Boomi integration plumbing) while waiting for the full extract, minimizing idle time.
5) If the full extract cannot be delivered within the current sprint, update the Release 1 plan and communicate revised optimization readiness dates to stakeholders.

According to the Week 20 status update, Release 1 transactional data is now approximately 95% available, with only three remaining fields (add-on indicator and AI/non-AI classification) due by 2026-05-22. The first raw deal guidance iteration, using around 50 attributes, is also targeted for 2026-05-22, after which remaining data validation will be performed.
