actions.description: Schedule a joint troubleshooting meeting for FedRAMP ServiceNow GovCloud discovery involving ServiceNow vendor engineer Marshall, AWS team representative Ervan, the internal ServiceNow core team, and project stakeholders to review discovery logs and understand why discovery is only occurring at the master account level and not at sub-account level.

assumptions.title: Most Westlake FedRAMP work is reusable for CoCounsel FedRAMP environments
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that most of the work delivered for the Westlake FedRAMP implementation can be leveraged to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, with only some new components required.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project is described as an extension of the broader FedRAMP program that has been running for almost two years, and the charter explicitly states that most of the work delivered for Westlake is expected to be leveraged.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The broader FedRAMP program has already implemented compliant infrastructure, controls, and patterns for Westlake within the same authorization boundary. Because CoCounsel is being added to this existing boundary and environment, it is reasonable to expect that networking, security controls, monitoring, and many platform components can be reused, needing only incremental extensions or configuration changes rather than net‑new designs.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves limited, re‑baseline the implementation plan and budget to include additional engineering work, prioritize critical capabilities necessary for FedRAMP readiness, and potentially phase lower‑priority features into subsequent change packets.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture and design reviews comparing Westlake components to CoCounsel requirements; detailed gap analysis and implementation planning.

validation_owner.name: Lead solution architect for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: Allocated $1M capital budget is sufficient for FedRAMP CoCounsel build work
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the $1 million capital budget allocated by finance will be sufficient to cover platform, engineering, and science work required to onboard CoCounsel into the FedRAMP environment, despite the originally assumed May start no longer being feasible.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Rough estimates for FTEs and contractors are around $750K, which is well within the allocated $1M capital budget, providing apparent headroom for variation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The charter cites an initial estimate of $750K for FTEs and contractors versus a $1M allocation, creating a 25%+ buffer for unanticipated needs. While the May start date is no longer feasible, the underlying scope and complexity are not indicated to have substantially changed, so it is reasonable to assume the total capital requirement will remain within the approved envelope, at least until more detailed plans suggest otherwise.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If forecasts indicate the capital budget will be exceeded, prepare a change request and business justification for additional funds, or adjust scope and phasing to keep critical FedRAMP readiness work within the existing budget while deferring non‑essential features to a later packet.
assumptions.validation_method: Refined bottom‑up estimation and periodic re‑forecasting of engineering and contractor effort against actuals, reviewed with finance.

validation_owner.name: Project manager / finance partner for FedRAMP CoCounsel

assumptions.title: FedRAMP cadence and lessons learned from Packet #1 will reduce delivery and audit risk for CoCounsel
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that aligning execution sequencing with the established FedRAMP cadence and leveraging lessons learned from Packet #1 will materially reduce delivery and audit risk for the CoCounsel FedRAMP extension.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The charter explicitly states that execution sequencing aligns with the established FedRAMP cadence and leverages lessons learned from Packet #1 to reduce delivery and audit risk.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Having already executed FedRAMP work and a prior change packet, the team understands the expectations of 3PAO auditors and the FedRAMP PMO, common pitfalls, and realistic lead times. Using this lived experience to drive the CoCounsel schedule, scope sequencing, and artifact preparation should, in principle, lower the likelihood and severity of surprises, provided the regulatory context and core architecture remain similar.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If execution or audit activities show similar levels of risk or findings as earlier packets, adjust the plan by adding intermediate readiness assessments, dedicating additional compliance and security resources, and re‑sequencing or de‑scoping lower‑priority items to protect critical authorization milestones.
assumptions.validation_method: Retrospectives and planning sessions mapping Packet #1 outcomes and issues to the CoCounsel plan; early checkpoints during execution and pre‑audit readiness reviews to confirm reduced issues compared to earlier packets.

assumptions.title: ServiceNow GovCloud discovery configuration proven on one AWS GovCloud account will be reusable for all FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that once the ServiceNow cloud discovery process for FedRAMP AWS GovCloud is successfully configured and validated on one AWS GovCloud account, the same configuration and process can be cascaded to the remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts without requiring materially different patterns per account.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the April 30, 2026 "FedRAMP SNOW - Cloud Discovery - GovCloud" meeting, the team stated that they will only cascade the configuration to remaining FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts after seeing a successful discovery scenario for one account, implying an expectation that the discovery pattern is reusable across accounts.
assumptions.validity_explanation: All FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts are being onboarded into the same ServiceNow GovCloud instance using common discovery patterns. The primary current issue is with discovery not reaching child/sub-account levels on the first account; once this routing and pattern issue is understood and resolved collaboratively with ServiceNow and AWS, the underlying mechanism should function similarly for other accounts in the same environment, making reuse reasonable but not yet proven.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If reuse proves unreliable and each FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account requires unique discovery adjustments, replan the work to include per-account configuration and testing, prioritize accounts that are in scope for near-term FedRAMP audit, and consider temporary supplemental approaches (e.g., scripted exports or manual CMDB updates) for lower-priority accounts until discovery patterns are stabilized.
assumptions.validation_method: First achieve a fully successful discovery run (including child/sub-account coverage) on the initial FedRAMP AWS GovCloud account, then apply the same configuration to additional FedRAMP AWS GovCloud accounts and compare discovery results and logs to confirm that configuration is reusable without per-account customization.

issues.title: DevOps resource constraint due to transfers to CoCounsel Next
issues.description: Five FedRAMP DevOps personnel moved from the FedRAMP CoCounsel Core efforts to Commercial CoCounsel Next as of 2026-04-15, significantly reducing capacity across CoCounsel Core and related workstreams. Additional transition of key staff (e.g., Rick Dauk) is also in progress.
issues.impact_assessment: Loss of five DevOps staff and a transitioning lead creates a severe capacity shortfall across FedRAMP CoCounsel Core, threatening the ability to meet key milestones such as CIAM integration, Disaster Recovery implementation, and production integrations. This may delay overall audit readiness and FedRAMP Significant Change timelines and impacts multiple dependent workstreams (Platform Engineering, CARI integration, Service Management, ISRM).
issues.dependencies_affecting: CoCounsel platform integrations (CIAM, CARI, Cumulus), Disaster Recovery workstreams, production deployments, and overall FedRAMP audit readiness timeline.
issues.resolution: Backfill DevOps capacity by leveraging commercial CoCounsel team members to reduce ramp-up time, and conduct intensive backlog replanning and prioritization to determine which milestones can be realistically met and to adjust timelines as needed.

entities.name: FedRAMP Authorization
entities.status: The FedRAMP Authorization program coordinates cross-functional work across Thomson Reuters technology pillars, ISRM, Product Management, Service Management, Platform Engineering, and external partners (e.g., HHS, Schellman, Fortreum) to obtain FedRAMP authorization for the TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud packages. entities.okrs: FedRAMP Authorization of Thomson Reuters Legal Research & Thomson Reuters Risk & Fraud packages - including Clear/WL/PL

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

FedRAMP Authorization is delivering initial FedRAMP authorization for Thomson Reuters Legal Research and Thomson Reuters Risk & Fraud packages, including shared security controls and continuous monitoring across AWS and Azure environments. This matters because authorization is required to maintain and expand access to U.S. federal customers while demonstrating a consistently managed security posture.

The FedRAMP authorization milestone remains set for 30 Jun 2026 and HHS has nearly completed its review with no outstanding questions.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by pending authorization from Federal Agency HSS.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on Federal Agency Authorization, closely followed by FedRAMP Authorization by 30 Jun 2026. TR team maintaining tight coordination with Federal Agency HHS - no outstanding actions for TR.

## Milestones

-   Achieve FedRAMP Authorization of TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud packages by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete mitigation of RA-5 container vulnerabilities for TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud and achieve full CM-8(3) automated unauthorized component detection coverage across AWS and Azure environments by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Maintain SC-10 privileged-user network disconnect and PL-4(1) external platform credential restrictions as active POA&M items with remediation milestones through 30 Sep 2026.

risks.title: FedRAMP authorization may be jeopardized by unresolved container vulnerabilities across TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud
risks.description: Moderate and low container vulnerabilities identified in RA-5 container scans for both Thomson Reuters Legal Research and Thomson Reuters Risk & Fraud (as submitted to Schellman on 6 November 2025) may not be reduced or managed sufficiently within FedRAMP expectations. If these vulnerabilities persist or new ones are introduced during the audit window, the sponsoring agency (HHS) or the 3PAO may consider the residual risk unacceptable, jeopardizing initial FedRAMP authorization or leading to conditions on the authorization that affect both product packages.
risks.impact_description: Failure to remediate or appropriately manage the portfolio of container vulnerabilities across both TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud could result in delays to FedRAMP authorization, imposition of significant POA&M items, or denial of authorization by HHS. This would prevent the program from achieving its core objective of FedRAMP authorization for both packages within the planned 2025-01-06 to 2026-06-30 timeline and could impact market access to U.S. federal customers.
risks.mitigation: Continue ISRM-led vulnerability management across shared container platforms for TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud, including regular RA-5 container scans, prioritised remediation, and tracking via POA&M. Maintain close coordination with Schellman and HHS to ensure vulnerability levels and remediation plans are acceptable for FedRAMP Moderate, and sustain "ongoing vigilance" to prevent introduction of new vulnerabilities during the authorization review period.

risks.title: Non-compliance with CM-8(3) automated unauthorized component detection across shared environments
risks.description: The CM-8(3) control for automated detection of unauthorized components currently does not operate consistently across all environments supporting TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud. ISRM has completed initial testing for AWS Linux environments, but Azure environments are still under testing. Until full coverage is implemented and validated, there is a risk that unauthorized software within the shared FedRAMP boundary is not detected automatically within the required five-minute timeframe.
risks.impact_description: If automated detection of unauthorized components is not fully implemented and demonstrated across all relevant AWS and Azure environments supporting both FedRAMP packages, the program may be assessed as non-compliant with CM-8(3). This can result in additional POA&M items, delays in the authorization decision, or conditions on the ATO, affecting both TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud and potentially requiring rework across multiple workstreams.
risks.mitigation: Complete and validate implementation of automated unauthorized component detection across all AWS and Azure environments within the FedRAMP boundary for TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud. Leverage the already successful AWS Linux testing as a pattern, extend to Azure, and document evidence for the 3PAO and HHS. Coordinate with platform engineering and infrastructure teams to ensure consistent tooling and monitoring across shared platforms.

risks.title: Network disconnect control (SC-10) for privileged users remains as a POA&M item across FedRAMP packages
risks.description: The SC-10 network disconnect control, requiring termination of privileged user sessions after 10 minutes of inactivity, is currently not enforced across the environments supporting TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud. The program plans to manage this gap as a POA&M item under PMO oversight, but there is a risk that prolonged non-compliance with this control could be viewed unfavourably by HHS or the 3PAO.
risks.impact_description: If SC-10 remains unimplemented for an extended period, or if evidence of progress is lacking, FedRAMP stakeholders may question the maturity of session management controls across the shared FedRAMP environment. This could result in additional scrutiny during assessment, increased POA&M burden, potential restrictions or conditions on the authorization for both TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud, and may require unplanned engineering work across multiple platforms.
risks.mitigation: Maintain SC-10 as an actively managed POA&M item with clear remediation milestones, owned by the FedRAMP Program PMO. Coordinate with shared infrastructure and platform engineering teams to design and implement automated session termination for privileged users across all FedRAMP-relevant environments, and regularly update HHS and the 3PAO on progress to demonstrate risk reduction.

risks.title: Inadequate restrictions on use of company credentials for external platforms (PL-4(1)) impacting FedRAMP compliance
risks.description: The current Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct lacks explicit restrictions on using company credentials to create accounts on external platforms, which is required under PL-4(1). This policy gap affects all staff supporting the FedRAMP environments for TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud and creates a program-level compliance risk until the policy is updated and adopted.
risks.impact_description: If PL-4(1) requirements are not met through an updated Code of Conduct and associated policy controls, the FedRAMP assessment may identify this as a deficiency affecting both TR Legal Research and TR Risk & Fraud authorizations. This could result in mandatory POA&M items, additional oversight, or conditions placed on the authorization, and would necessitate program-wide training and policy rollout under compressed timelines.
risks.mitigation: The PMO will work with HR and ISRM compliance to draft and adopt a standard policy document that adds explicit restrictions on using company credentials for external platforms, integrating this into the TR Code of Conduct. Once approved, communicate and roll out the updated policy across all teams supporting the FedRAMP program, and provide evidence of the policy and associated training to the 3PAO and HHS.

risks.title: Business reaction risk to revised customer-ready timeline
risks.description: The business may react negatively to the revised customer-ready timeline for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If business stakeholders react poorly to the revised customer-ready timeline, it could create pressure to compress scope or timelines, drive unplanned work, or erode confidence in the FedRAMP CIAM program.
risks.mitigation: Communicate clearly that migrations are expected to start right after 3PAO audit approval (targeted for end of January), and share the team’s ETA of February 24, 2026 with Westlaw/Practical Law and other stakeholders, ensuring concerns are addressed proactively. Per the RAID log entry dated 2025-11-20, the team met with the Westlaw/Practical Law team on 2025-11-18, communicated the 2026-02-24 ETA, and received no negative reaction; stakeholders indicated that selling FedRAMP for those products would likely start around Q3.

risks.title: Risk of not completing onboarding by February 24
risks.description: There are significant risks to meeting the customer onboarding timeline (February 24) due to unforeseen engineering challenges, resource allocation issues, and the need for updated estimates.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding is not completed by February 24, customer onboarding will be delayed, potentially impacting commercial commitments, audit readiness, and the broader FedRAMP rollout schedule.
risks.mitigation: Review and refine scope and estimates, then mitigate by potentially reducing scope for the customer-ready timeline and ensuring the risk is visible at the program level. Communicate the mitigation plan and updated dates to stakeholders and plug the risk into the appropriate program-level tracker. The RAID log documents follow-up actions including Harvarinder finalizing a mitigation plan involving scope reduction and Alyssa ensuring the risk was tracked at the program level; the risk has since been closed with implementation of the agreed mitigation.

risks.title: LTS database migration risk
risks.description: LTS database migration work may not complete on time, impacting users and CIAM FedRAMP readiness.
risks.impact_description: If the LTS database migration does not complete successfully and on time (for both Non-Prod and Prod), related CIAM integrations and dependent services may be unavailable or unstable, delaying onboarding, increasing operational risk, and potentially impacting audit readiness.
risks.mitigation: Complete LTS database migration for Non-Prod and Prod, track progress and blockers via the dev team group chat, and provide regular updates. According to the RAID log, Non-Prod migration completed first, remaining blockers for Prod were resolved, and the overall LTS database migration was completed by 2026-02-26.

risks.title: Risk of not being customer ready by January 31 due to story sizing and outstanding requirements
risks.description: Based on the sizing of stories and some outstanding requirements, it is very likely that the program will not be customer ready by January 31 for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: If customer-ready status is not achieved by January 31, customer onboarding timelines will slip, potentially impacting commitments made to stakeholders and compressing time available for testing, audit preparation, and operational readiness.
risks.mitigation: Refine user stories, solidify estimates, and communicate revised dates (moving the customer-ready target to February 28) to stakeholders so expectations and downstream plans can be adjusted. Per the RAID log, refinement of stories was completed and the new ETA of 2025-02-28 was communicated on 2025-10-06.

risks.title: Impact from onboarding new FTE resources replacing contractors
risks.description: Moving from contractors to FTEs may impact CIAM FedRAMP delivery as new resources are onboarded.
risks.impact_description: If onboarding of new FTE resources is slower than expected or they require extended ramp-up time, velocity on CIAM FedRAMP engineering work could drop, impacting delivery timelines and quality.
risks.mitigation: Onboard new resources onto the Kappa/Iota teams, actively monitor the impact, and adjust assignments as needed. Per the RAID log, the risk level was reduced from Medium to Low, hiring and releasing were in progress, and one additional resource hire was being monitored as of early January; ongoing monitoring ultimately supported closure of the risk.

risks.title: Non-prod Plexus cluster readiness may miss September 15 deadline
risks.description: If the non-prod Plexus cluster is not fully operational by September 15, the program is likely to miss the January 31 customer-ready milestone for FedRAMP CIAM onboarding.
risks.impact_description: Missing the September 15 readiness date for the non-prod Plexus cluster would delay downstream SRE and product onboarding work, putting the January 31 customer-ready milestone at risk and potentially delaying overall FedRAMP CIAM onboarding timelines.
risks.mitigation: Fix the connectivity issue and get the non-prod Plexus cluster fully functional, working with Plexus, Tech M, and Landing Zone teams to debug API endpoint access from commercial Zscaler to use1. This work was executed without stopping SRE progress, and the non-prod cluster was completed on September 22.

risks.title: Permit to Operate (PtO) may not be obtained before key resource vacation
risks.description: If the Permit to Operate is not obtained before Chris goes on vacation, the CIAM FedRAMP timeline may be impacted.
risks.impact_description: Failure to obtain PtO before a key engineering resource’s vacation could delay environment readiness and associated onboarding tasks, potentially impacting critical milestones for FedRAMP CIAM delivery.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the CIAM FedRAMP architecture, ensure the low environment is functional, and obtain ISRM approval in time to secure the Permit to Operate (PtO) before the vacation period. According to the RAID log, the PtO for Production was completed by the 2025-11-07 due date, eliminating the risk prior to the vacation window.

risks.title: Westlaw / Practical Law reg key validator certificate and connectivity issue
risks.description: After fixing a firewall product issue, requests from CIAM to Westlaw and Practical Law began failing because their reg key validator domains were not added to TLS certificates, creating a blocking dependency on those teams to update their certificates and resolve SSL errors.
risks.impact_description: If Westlaw and Practical Law do not update their certificates and resolve reg key validator connectivity issues, CIAM FedRAMP integrations that rely on these validators will continue to experience SSL failures, blocking testing and production use, and delaying onboarding timelines for Westlaw, Practical Law, and related CLEAR flows.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with Westlaw, Practical Law, and CLEAR teams to update certificates with required reg key validator domains and resolve connectivity issues, track progress via the FedRAMP Weekly CIAM Connect chat, and test across QED and Prod. Per the RAID log updates, the Westlaw and Practical Law certificate issues were resolved in Production first (with QED following), CLEAR deployments were coordinated, and by mid-April Chris confirmed that the WL/PL reg key validator issue was complete, allowing the risk to be closed.

risks.title: SAP / Audit account usage for internal testing
risks.description: Uncertainty about whether the same SAP account used for auditors can be repurposed for internal testing, and who can assist with this process, may delay test execution.
risks.impact_description: If the SAP audit account cannot be reused for internal testing, or if the decision and process are delayed, testing activities that depend on this account could be blocked or slowed, impacting schedule for validating CIAM FedRAMP scenarios that rely on SAP access.
risks.mitigation: Check with broader program management whether the audit account can be repurposed for internal testing and identify the appropriate contact(s) to assist with approvals and configuration. Adjust testing plans depending on the outcome.

risks.title: CLEAR reg key validator connectivity and availability
risks.description: CLEAR reg key validator endpoints are required for CIAM FedRAMP lower environment work, but connectivity and behavior are still being validated, with issues on CIAM’s side and dependencies on CLEAR deployments.
risks.impact_description: If CLEAR’s reg key validator endpoints are not fully functional and validated in lower and production environments, CIAM cannot reliably call these endpoints, blocking or delaying CLEAR-related onboarding flows and impacting the ability to meet CIAM FedRAMP onboarding timelines involving CLEAR.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with CLEAR to confirm reg key validator availability in QA and Prod, test and resolve connectivity issues from CIAM, and address concerns raised by CLEAR (e.g., via Doug). Track progress with regular follow-ups, especially around February–April (including confirming Prod deployment and subsequent testing).

risks.title: Outage Recovery / Disaster Recovery strategy for Azure B2C single point of failure
risks.description: Current FedRAMP CIAM architecture has a single point of failure in Azure B2C, with no proven fallback during major Azure or AWS outages. Outage on October 29 highlighted limitations, and resolution is dependent on Microsoft guidance and an internal resiliency proof-of-concept.
risks.impact_description: If a major Azure or AWS outage occurs before a robust outage recovery / DR strategy is implemented for Azure B2C, CIAM services for FedRAMP products could become unavailable, causing authentication failures for government and regulated customers, jeopardizing SLAs, damaging stakeholder confidence, and potentially impacting FedRAMP compliance posture.

risk_owner.name: Christopher Yip, Mohith Sai Krishna Katakam, and Tom Murphy

risks.mitigation: Work with Microsoft to obtain clear resiliency guidance and root cause information for past outages; evaluate Azure Front Door and related components as potential single points of failure; pursue an exception request (e.g., application gateway with B2C) where appropriate; and execute an internal resiliency proof-of-concept focused on outage recovery and DR. Per the 1-May and 15-May status updates, the primary mitigation path is to (1) validate Microsoft’s Azure B2C resiliency and outage recovery guidance by 2026-05-15, with Devarshi following up to confirm whether related work can be expedited and added to the sprint starting 2026-05-20 (noting that if it cannot be added, overall status may move to Amber), and (2) complete the internal Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept by 2026-05-30 so that the FedRAMP CIAM architecture no longer relies on an unmitigated single point of failure.

assumptions.title: No incremental commercial funding; costs managed within approved EPC allocation
assumptions.description: The CIAM FedRAMP Product Onboarding project assumes that required funding will be covered by TR Technology EPC funding for FY 2026, and that no incremental commercial funding will be needed, with all costs managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter specifies that funding comes from TR Technology EPC funding (FY 2026) and explicitly states that no incremental commercial funding is assumed, with costs to be managed within the approved EPC allocation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current planning indicates that the EPC allocation covers all known project components (engineering, compliance, infrastructure, onboarding, audit, remediation). There are no stated requirements for commercial funding at this time, and scope is being managed within the approved budget envelope.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If EPC funding proves insufficient, raise an escalation through governance to either: (1) request incremental funding, or (2) reduce or phase scope (e.g., defer lower-priority product integrations or non-critical enhancements) to stay within the approved budget.
assumptions.validation_method: Ongoing comparison of actual and forecast project costs against the approved EPC budget, with finance and program reviews to confirm sufficiency of the allocation.

assumptions.title: Onboarding tracking will focus on product onboarding, not customer onboarding
assumptions.description: The project assumes that tracking and reporting for CIAM FedRAMP onboarding will focus on product onboarding only (Non-Prod and Prod), not customer onboarding, unless explicitly requested for initial customers.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Charter states that Harv and Alyssa agreed to track product onboarding only (not customer onboarding) unless explicitly requested for initial customers, and that Harv will align with Liat to ensure stakeholder consensus.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The agreement between program management leads and key product stakeholders is documented in the Charter, and current scope and milestones are framed around product onboarding completion. No conflicting requirements for customer onboarding tracking have been documented yet.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If stakeholders request broader tracking to include customer onboarding, formalize a scope and reporting change: define additional metrics, timelines, and owners for customer onboarding, and adjust the project plan and resourcing accordingly rather than treating these items as implicit obligations.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm in governance and stakeholder meetings (including with Liat and product stakeholders) that reporting continues to be based on product onboarding, and document any exceptions where customer onboarding tracking is explicitly requested.

dependencies.title: Microsoft Azure B2C resiliency guidance for outage recovery
dependencies.description: The project depends on Microsoft providing guidance and support for Azure B2C resiliency and outage recovery patterns so that a robust fallback approach can be validated and implemented.
dependencies.dependent_on: Microsoft Azure B2C product and support teams
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP CIAM Product Onboarding project team
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Microsoft resiliency guidance and the associated POC are delayed beyond May, the Azure B2C outage recovery risk will remain open, the project may be unable to demonstrate adequate disaster recovery for FedRAMP, and the overall project RAG status is likely to remain Amber beyond the planned delivery dates.
dependencies.mitigation: Proceed with an Azure B2C resiliency proof of concept during the current sprint, refine the approach as Microsoft guidance becomes available, and continue tracking the associated outage recovery risk in RAID while planning additional hardening if required. As of the 15-May status, Devarshi Pandya is following up to request that Microsoft resiliency guidance be expedited and to confirm whether related work can be added to the sprint starting 20-May; if this cannot be added to the next sprint, the overall status for this area may turn Amber.

risks.description: If quoting, renewals, or service remain in S2E while sales moves to GSI, users may require dual licenses. LATAM leadership has indicated no appetite for additional licensing cost.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Pagero Integration is delivering end-to-end CIO and Product Engineering integration, including S3NS environments, compliant eSSO/MFA, legal entity migrations, and PDP certification, so Pagero can meet the French e‑invoicing and e‑reporting regulatory mandate from 01 Sep 2026. This matters because France compliance is non‑discretionary and underpins continued operations for key enterprise customers.  

Overall project completion is 70% against the 01 Sep 2026 mandate deadline, with S3NS pre‑prod 100% complete and internal testing underway. S3NS production build is 30% complete against a 12 Jun 2026 target, while eSSO/MFA build (85% vs 30 Jun), legal entity migrations for Belgium/Italy and Poland (each 80% vs 30 Jun/01 Jul), and the PDP mid‑year audit (60% vs 30 Jun) are progressing but leave limited schedule and compliance buffer.  

Overall status is Red, driven primarily by S3NS production readiness and security control gaps (SentinelOne, eSSO/MFA, WAF) lagging plan and compressing the window before early customer onboarding and the 01 Sep 2026 mandate.  

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to lock the 12 Jun 2026 S3NS production build date with a tightly sequenced phased onboarding plan, while securing ISRM‑approved risk acceptances and concrete deployment dates for SentinelOne EDR, Cloud Armor/WAF, and full Memority eSSO/MFA cutover ahead of peak customer traffic. In parallel, the program must close Linux Intune compliance remediation and confirm PDP mid‑year audit outputs early enough to adjust before final certification.  

## Milestones

- Complete S3NS production environment build and make France S3NS production available to customers by 12 Jun 2026.  
- Complete eSSO/MFA Memority production build, Belgium and Italy legal entity migrations, and the PDP mid‑year audit by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete Poland legal entity migration and business launch by 01 Jul 2026.  
- Achieve overall French mandate go‑live with S3NS supporting e‑invoicing and e‑reporting for France by 01 Sep 2026.  
- Submit final PDP certification and close out the Pagero Integration program by 19 Dec 2026.

risks.title: Linux developer laptops not fully managed in Intune may cause audit non-compliance and access restrictions
risks.description: A substantial number of Linux laptops used by Pagero engineering/product teams have dropped out of Intune or are not currently enrolled, and attempts to re-enroll them are encountering varied errors. Approximately 100 Linux devices are estimated to be non-Intune-managed, and the ETS team has treated remediation as low priority. This creates uncertainty about which devices exist within TR and whether private devices are being used, posing compliance risks for multiple audits and potential issues when conditional access is enabled for single sign-on.
risks.impact_description: If Linux laptops used by engineering and product teams remain unmanaged in Intune, TR cannot demonstrate control over in-scope devices during Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audits. This may result in audit findings or qualifications and could force restrictions on device access to customer data, impacting the Pagero Integration program’s ability to meet compliance expectations ahead of the French mandate. When conditional access is activated for SSO, non-compliant devices may be blocked, disrupting development, testing, or operations work required for S3NS and France delivery.
risks.mitigation: Ola Nilsson will continue working with the ETS team to diagnose and resolve the Intune enrollment issues affecting Linux laptops, including defining a standard process for keeping Linux devices active in Intune (e.g., required login cadence to the Intune app) and clearing current errors preventing re-enrollment. Christer will escalate within ETS leadership (beyond day-to-day contacts such as Mayank) to increase the priority of this work, highlighting the impact on Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audits and the risk that unmanaged or even private Linux devices may access customer data. The goal is to restore full visibility and compliance for all in-scope Linux devices before upcoming Q3/Q4 audit windows and before any conditional access changes that could otherwise disrupt engineering access.

risks.title: Developers unable to access managed databases in S3NS due to Zscaler or infrastructure configuration issues

The root cause is not yet known and may relate to Zscaler configuration or infrastructure setup. Access to these databases is critical for microservice deployments and troubleshooting.
risks.impact_description: If developers cannot reliably access managed databases in S3NS, product engineering teams will be unable to fully deploy, test, and debug their microservices in multi-region setups. This will slow down or block core service enablement, delay discovery and resolution of schema or data issues, and materially increase the likelihood of missing pre-prod and prod environment dates, thereby impacting customer onboarding schedules and the 2026-09-01 regulatory go-live.
risks.mitigation: Maintain close collaboration with the Zscaler team and internal infrastructure teams to diagnose and resolve the connectivity issue. Prioritize enabling secure developer access to managed databases as a critical blocker for pre-prod and prod readiness. Track this issue explicitly in the high-level delivery plan shared with the program so that its status and impacts are visible at SteerCo, and escalate if not resolved quickly.

risks.title: Linux developer laptops not compliant in Intune may cause audit failures and security exposure
risks.description: A large number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers dropped out of Intune because users did not log into the Intune app at least monthly. Re‑enrolling these devices into Intune is encountering errors and progressing very slowly, with different issues occurring on each laptop. Approximately 100 Linux laptops are currently not Intune‑managed, and there is poor visibility into the exact number because Intune is not functioning correctly for them. While day‑to‑day end‑user work is not currently impacted, this creates a compliance gap and a risk that non‑managed or even private Linux devices could be used to access customer data.
risks.impact_description: If Linux laptops remain unmanaged in Intune, the organization cannot demonstrate control over which devices exist within TR or whether they are compliant. This may cause failures or findings in Cyber Essentials, ISO, and SOC 2 audits, particularly the mid‑year (Q3) and Q4 audits. Lack of device control increases the risk that private, non‑company Linux devices are used to access customer data, potentially breaching internal security standards and regulatory obligations. Future activation of conditional access for single sign‑on may lock out developers with non‑compliant devices, causing disruption to development activities.

risks.title: Lack of Wiz support in SANS may delay required cloud security coverage for S3NS
risks.description: The Wiz security solution is currently not supported by SANS in the targeted environment. Bill communicated that there is no firm plan yet for how this will be addressed, despite a policy requirement to have this resolved by 2026. Recent discussions with Google (around 22 April) did not yield a clear delivery timeline for support. If support is significantly delayed, the project may lack the desired level of cloud security visibility and control, and compensating controls may be required.
risks.impact_description: If Wiz remains unsupported in SANS for an extended period, the S3NS platform will not have the intended Wiz-based visibility and protections. This may leave gaps in cloud security monitoring and vulnerability management, and could lead to deviations from TR security policy, which expects this to be in place by 2026. If auditors or internal security governance identify this gap, additional scrutiny or corrective actions may be imposed. Implementing compensating controls later under time pressure could consume significant time and resources and potentially delay other security and platform readiness activities.
risks.mitigation: Bill will obtain a more definitive timeline from SANS/Google regarding when Wiz will be supported and use that to decide on the strategy. If support can be delivered within 2026 (for example by Q4), the project may accept the delay with careful monitoring. If the timeline extends significantly (e.g., into 2027), Bill and the security team will design and implement compensating controls that provide a similar level of visibility and protection, balancing the effort and resources required against the expected duration until Wiz support becomes available.

risks.title: EU-based operations support resources required for Memority eSSO tool
risks.description: ISRM requires three EU-based operations support resources to support the new Memority eSSO/MFA tool used for compliance in the S3NS environment. Recruitment is in progress (one hire starting in July, two candidates in interview), but there is a risk that these resources may not be onboarded and fully productive in time to support pre-prod, prod, and French mandate go-live timelines.
risks.impact_description: If sufficient EU-based ops support resources are not in place in time, the Memority eSSO/MFA solution may not be adequately supported during critical test and go-live windows. This could lead to instability or outages in authentication for S3NS environments, increased reliance on vendor support, slower incident response, and potential non-compliance with French regulatory security expectations during the ramp-up period.
risks.mitigation: Continue recruitment and onboarding of three EU-based ops support resources (one confirmed start in July, two in interviews). Utilize vendor support as a contingency: the Memority vendor has agreed to support the product/tool until September 2026 if internal resources are delayed. Coordinate with legal and internal approvers to ensure any contractual or compliance approvals for vendor-supported operations are completed promptly.

risks.title: Knowledge transfer and onboarding of Memority eSSO ops resources constrained by Swedish vacations
risks.description: New EU-based operations support resources for the Memority eSSO/MFA solution are expected to sign contracts around mid-June 2026, but most Swedish subject matter experts (SMEs) will be out of office through June–July due to holidays. This creates a risk that knowledge transfer, training, and onboarding for these new joiners will be incomplete or delayed, leaving ISRM without sufficient, fully ramped resources to operate Memority ahead of the 1 September 2026 French mandate.
risks.impact_description: If new Memority ops resources arrive around July but cannot receive adequate knowledge transfer and training because key SMEs are on vacation, ISRM may enter the French mandate go-live window without fully capable operators for the eSSO solution. This could force over-reliance on R&D/engineering teams in Sweden (who should focus on delivering the France platform), create operational gaps in managing Memority changes and incidents, or require costly use of implementation partners to operate the solution. Inadequate operations coverage would increase the risk of authentication incidents in S3NS, jeopardize compliance with French security expectations, and add pressure to the already compressed pre-prod/prod schedule across multiple workstreams.
risks.mitigation: Before June 2026, Ranjan, in collaboration with Christer and Jonas, will identify the concrete Memority operational tasks that must be completed prior to 1 September 2026 and estimate the effort and timing required. Based on that analysis, ISRM will: (1) work with ProdEng to prepare detailed handover documentation and training materials that can be consumed asynchronously by new joiners; (2) schedule any critical live knowledge transfer sessions before key SMEs go on holiday; (3) determine which tasks can safely be handled by non-IAM resources in Sweden without overloading engineering teams focused on France delivery; and (4) assess the feasibility and cost of using the implementation partner to temporarily operate Memority if internal onboarding lags. The agreed plan B, including task allocation and escalation paths, will be documented and socialised with ISRM and the program before mid-June.

risks.title: Compliant eSSO solution introduction constrained by late-June availability and Swedish vacation period
risks.description: The compliant Memority eSSO solution is expected to be available around the end of June 2026, just before Swedish vacation starts. The infrastructure team advises not introducing this solution right before vacation to avoid requiring Pagero support during a period of limited TR staff availability. There is a risk that the compliant eSSO solution is not live in production by the time customers start processing data, requiring reliance on workarounds and careful control of what data is operated in the environment. As of the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, the plan is to keep the infrastructure layer on the existing eSSO while starting to use Memority from the application layer, running accounts in parallel to provide fall-back. This implies that S3NS may remain partially non-compliant from an MFA/eSSO perspective through mid-August 2026, extending the previously anticipated non-compliance window and requiring formal risk acceptance from ISRM leadership (including Sofia).
risks.impact_description: If the compliant Memority eSSO solution is not fully deployed and adopted before Swedish vacation and customer go-lives, the program may need to operate S3NS environments with interim authentication arrangements, potentially limiting the types of data and use cases allowed. Following the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, the agreed approach is to retain the existing eSSO for infrastructure while gradually enabling Memority at the application layer with parallel accounts, resulting in a period (likely July–mid-August 2026) where production environments are known to be partially non-compliant. This extended non-compliance period increases regulatory and audit risk during early customer onboarding, may require explicit risk acceptance from ISRM and business leadership, and could constrain how aggressively customers can ramp up production usage ahead of the 1 September 2026 French mandate.
risks.mitigation: Ranjan, in coordination with Bård, Christer and Kristine, will (1) finalise the detailed plan to run the existing eSSO for infrastructure while enabling Memority at the application layer with parallel accounts, ensuring a clear fall-back path if Memority causes instability; (2) quantify and document the exact duration and scope of the partial non-compliance period (expected to extend into mid-August 2026) and the associated restrictions on customer data and use cases; (3) obtain formal risk acceptance and sign-off from ISRM leadership (including Sofia - Legal) and relevant business owners for operating S3NS with this interim arrangement, explicitly covering the extended timeframe; and (4) schedule and execute the full Memority production cutover after Swedish vacation, with target completion by mid-August 2026, including validation that all critical paths (infrastructure access and application access) are operating under the new compliant eSSO/MFA configuration.

risks.title: Cloud Armor / WAF controls may not be implemented in S3NS production by customer go-live
risks.description: During the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, Bård highlighted that, in addition to SentinelOne and other ISRM tooling items, ISRM has also raised requirements for cloud application protection via Cloud Armor or an equivalent web application firewall (WAF) in the S3NS environment. Given the current focus on meeting the 12 June 2026 production readiness date and the constraints from Swedish vacations, there is a high likelihood that Cloud Armor/WAF controls will not be deployed in S3NS production by the time customers begin using the environment for live flows, and ISRM will seek a committed implementation date and potentially a formal risk acceptance for the gap period.
risks.impact_description: If Cloud Armor/WAF controls are not implemented in S3NS production before customers begin onboarding and sending live traffic (expected from July 2026), Pagero’s France solution will lack a key application-layer protection control that ISRM expects for internet-facing services. This increases exposure to web application attacks, may limit the kinds of services or endpoints that can be safely exposed to customers, and could create audit and compliance findings if TR cannot demonstrate that agreed cloud security patterns have been applied. The gap may force TR to either slow down customer onboarding, rely on less effective compensating controls, or formally accept an elevated security risk during a critical period leading up to the 1 September 2026 French mandate.
risks.mitigation: Bård and Christer will (1) work with the S3NS infrastructure and security engineering teams to define a concrete implementation plan and target date for Cloud Armor/WAF deployment in the Pagero S3NS environment, aligned with available engineering capacity after the 12 June 2026 production readiness milestone; (2) assess whether any interim technical mitigations (e.g., tightened network-level controls, rate limiting, or additional monitoring) can partially offset the absence of WAF up to the implementation date; and (3) engage ISRM leadership to agree whether a formal risk acceptance is required for the period between initial customer production traffic (from July 2026) and WAF go-live, documenting the agreed risk posture and ensuring it is visible at SteerCo. The target is to have Cloud Armor/WAF in place no later than the end of Q3 2026, with a refined date agreed by end of June 2026.

risks.title: Security tooling (SentinelOne / Wiz sensor) not fully operational in S3NS environments
risks.description: During S3NS pre-prod setup, SentinelOne was reported as not working properly in the environment. Additionally, Wiz-based agentless scanning remains on the Google/Wiz roadmap and is not yet available, requiring deployment of a local sensor by the Hawk team instead. There is a risk that security tooling will not be fully deployed and functioning by the time S3NS environments need to support production data processing. As of the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, SentinelOne deployment in S3NS production depends on a Kubernetes cluster upgrade that the Pagero team has scheduled for Q3 2026 to avoid jeopardising the 12 June 2026 production readiness date and to work around Swedish vacation constraints. This means there is a material likelihood that production customer traffic in July–September 2026 will run without full EDR coverage unless compensating controls or an accelerated upgrade are agreed with ISRM. Exposure would be for 3 months - Jul 1 to Sep 30.
risks.impact_description: If SentinelOne issues in S3NS pre-prod and prod are not resolved and the Wiz sensor deployment is delayed, production environments may lack required endpoint and container vulnerability visibility and configuration management controls. As clarified in the 21 May 2026 SteerCo follow-up, SentinelOne is considered a production go-live requirement by ISRM, and the necessary Kubernetes cluster upgrade is currently planned for Q3 2026. If this upgrade and the SentinelOne deployment are pushed out while customers begin onboarding (test traffic from June and live invoice flows from July), S3NS will operate without its primary EDR detection capability for several months. This increases the risk of undetected threats in the environment, may create audit and compliance findings when demonstrating that documented controls are in place, and could force difficult go/no-go decisions or retroactive risk acceptances for the Pagero France mandate.
risks.mitigation: Bill Brinkman will (1) confirm with the SentinelOne engineering team and Pagero infrastructure leads (including Bård and Kaushik) that there is no viable deployment path without upgrading the Kubernetes cluster; (2) obtain a more granular and aggressive target date for the Kubernetes upgrade and SentinelOne deployment immediately after the 12 June 2026 production readiness milestone, rather than a broad "Q3" window; and (3) work with ISRM leadership (including Morgan) and Christer to assess and, if necessary, define compensating controls for any period in which production customer traffic is flowing without full EDR coverage. This includes validating whether existing logging and monitoring can partially offset the gap, what additional controls might be practical, and whether a formal risk acceptance is required for any period between initial customer go-live (from July 2026) and SentinelOne becoming fully operational in S3NS.

risks.title: Delay in S3NS pre-prod and prod environment readiness impacting customer and regulatory timelines
risks.description: S3NS pre-production build has already slipped from 2026-05-08 to a target of 2026-05-15, which the infrastructure team considers "maybe a bit optimistic" given limited staff availability over May holidays. The production environment build, externally communicated to customers as available by 2026-05-31, is highly dependent on pre-prod and is now internally discussed as potentially moving to around 2026-06-12. Any further delay will compress or jeopardize customer implementation and impact key enterprise customers (e.g., Warner Brothers, Nestlé, Deloitte)
risks.impact_description: If the S3NS pre-prod and prod environments are not available close to the currently communicated dates (pre-prod mid-May, prod 2026-05-31), customer onboarding and testing in the new Europe 2 instance may be delayed, requiring re-communication of dates to multiple enterprise customers and creating customer dissatisfaction and escalations. A material slip (e.g., to 2026-07-01 or later) would compress the schedule to meet the 2026-09-01 French mandate go-live, increase operational risk at cutover, and could put regulatory compliance at risk for Pagero transactions in France.
risks.mitigation: Infra and Hawk teams are working intensively to complete the test and pre-prod environments, including creation of remaining S3 buckets and deployment of Postgres databases, with contractors being pushed to deliver within the week of 2026-05-07. Core services are being prioritized so some product engineering teams can begin limited parallel work even before all core services are fully up. A high-level delivery plan and milestones (derived from the technical flow-chart used by Hawk and Jira tasks across teams) will be created and shared with the program to track progress and dependencies. A decision checkpoint SteerCo is planned around 2026-05-20 to reassess whether the externally communicated 2026-05-31 production date must be officially revised and to define possible phased delivery options that maintain minimum viable capabilities for customers while mitigating schedule risk.

risks.title: Delay or inadequate feedback from external French auditors impacting PDP certification
risks.description: The PDP certification process for French regulatory compliance has started and depends on timely and critical feedback from external French auditors. Jonas is engaging with auditors and has meetings planned, but there is a risk that auditors' feedback is delayed or insufficient, which could affect completion of the mid-year audit and readiness for final PDP certification by 2026-12-19.
risks.impact_description: If external French auditors do not provide timely or adequate feedback, the mid-year PDP audit may not identify all gaps related to new French regulatory changes, delaying remediation activities. This could result in non-compliance being discovered late in 2026, jeopardizing the final PDP certification due 2026-Dec-19 and exposing the program to regulatory findings, fines, or mandated remediation under compressed timelines.
risks.mitigation: Maintain proactive engagement with external French auditors, including scheduled meetings in May 2026 to obtain early critical feedback. Use their input to initiate mitigation actions during the mid-year PDP audit window, ensuring that any identified gaps are addressed ahead of the final certification submission. Track auditor feedback and resulting remediation actions in the PDP mid-year audit plan to ensure visibility at SteerCo level.

assumptions.title: Vendor will support Memority eSSO tool operations until September 2026 if internal ops resources are delayed
assumptions.description: The program is assuming that the Memority vendor will continue to support the eSSO/MFA tool until September 2026 in case the required EU-based operational support resources are not fully onboarded by then.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Explicit statement in the SteerCo that the vendor will support the product tool until September if internal resources are delayed, to mitigate the risk of delayed recruitment.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The commitment has been communicated verbally in SteerCo, but formal contractual confirmation and operational planning with the vendor are required to ensure that appropriate support resources will be available throughout the period.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If vendor support cannot be confirmed or is withdrawn earlier than September, accelerate recruitment and onboarding of internal EU-based ops resources, consider temporary reallocation of existing ISRM staff, and adjust go-live or data processing scope to align with available support capacity.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm written agreement/contract language with the Memority vendor specifying support coverage through at least 2026-09-01, and track vendor resource allocation as part of ISRM vendor management.

assumptions.title: Compliant Memority eSSO solution will be available by 2026-06-30
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the compliant Memority eSSO solution can be delivered and ready around 30 June 2026, enabling testing and potentially production use before or shortly after Swedish vacation begins.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Ranjan has reported status as green and expressed confidence that the 30 June 2026 date will be met, with a possibility of bringing the date forward pending approvals.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current ISRM reporting flags the milestone as green and approvals as in progress, but infrastructure has expressed concern about the practicality of late-June introduction, suggesting that readiness must be confirmed early to avoid last-minute deferral.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If Memority eSSO is not ready by 2026-06-30, extend use of the approved workaround for testing, restrict data categories processed in S3NS environments, and plan a controlled post-vacation rollout coordinated with infrastructure and key customers.
assumptions.validation_method: Track progress against the eSSO build milestone and approval steps; confirm readiness through ISRM testing and sign-off before Swedish vacation period begins.

assumptions.title: Externally communicated S3NS production readiness date of 2026-05-31 can be maintained with at most a 1–2 week internal delay managed via communications and interim measures
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the currently communicated external customer date of 2026-05-31 for S3NS production readiness can either remain unchanged or absorb a small (1–2 week) delay without immediate formal re-communication, by using interim measures such as testing in existing global/Europe 1 instances and targeted communication to key enterprise customers.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the SteerCo, Gustav indicated that customers care primarily about production availability, not pre-prod, and that small slippages (e.g., to mid-June) might be managed through progress communications (delegation letters, testing in existing environments) without immediately revising the official date, while a larger slip (e.g., to 2026-07-01) would require broader re-communication.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While Product and Corporates leadership believe some flexibility exists, infrastructure has highlighted significant schedule risk, and the probability of needing to move the official date from 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-12 or later has been estimated as high (6–7 on a 1–10 scale), reducing confidence in this assumption.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If it becomes clear by the 2026-05-21 checkpoint that maintaining the 2026-05-31 date is unrealistic, formally revise the external date (e.g., to 2026-06-12 or 2026-07-01), coordinate communications to all affected customers, and align internal plans and regulatory messaging accordingly.
assumptions.validation_method: Reassess actual environment readiness and customer sentiment at the planned decision checkpoint around 2026-05-21, and validate with key enterprise customers (e.g., Warner Brothers, Nestlé, Deloitte) whether a small delay is acceptable without changing formal dates.

assumptions.title: Extension of service management process approvals to 30 June 2026 will not introduce additional operational risk
assumptions.description: Service management process approvals, originally targeted for 30 April, have been extended to 30 June at the request of Lalit to allow more time for discussions and approvals with Kristine. Christer and Lorna agreed that this schedule shift does not currently create additional risk because BAU operations continue under the existing setup and there is already a functioning process in place.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The existing service management process is already functioning, and BAU operations are continuing without issue under the current arrangements. The change is only to the formal approval date, not to day‑to‑day operations.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Christer explicitly stated that there is currently 'no extra risk' from shifting the process approval date and that this new date is more realistic. The team continues to operate under a known, tested process, meaning the extension is largely administrative. BAU has not shown any deterioration due to the delay, supporting the assumption that operations remain safe until formal approval is granted.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If issues surface before approval (e.g., incidents tied to process weaknesses), the team will prioritize completion and approval of the service management process earlier than 30 June and introduce interim work instructions or temporary controls to stabilize BAU operations. They can also escalate to governance to secure expedited approvals.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor BAU performance and incident handling between April and June; confirm with Kristine and governance stakeholders that no negative impacts or audit concerns arise from the extended approval date and that approvals are completed by 30 June.
assumptions.source_file_name: Pagero Integration - progress update ProdEng April 30 .docx

issues.title: Linux laptops not managed in Intune, creating compliance and audit risk
issues.description: A significant number of Linux laptops used by Pagero developers have dropped out of Intune because users did not regularly log into the Intune app, and attempts to re-enroll them are encountering varied errors on different devices. Approximately 100 Linux laptops are currently not Intune-managed, which prevents TR from demonstrating full control over devices accessing customer data and may cause issues with conditional access and compliance audits (Cyber Essentials, ISO, SOC 2).
issues.impact_assessment: Without Intune management for all Linux laptops, TR lacks an accurate inventory and compliance status for devices accessing internal systems and customer data. This undermines the ability to enforce conditional access policies for single sign-on and creates a major gap for Cyber Essential, ISO, and SOC 2 audits, where auditors require evidence that all in-scope devices are known and compliant. There is also a risk that private, non-TR Linux devices could be used to access customer data, breaching internal standards.
issues.dependencies_affecting: ETS (Intune and device management), Pagero engineering teams using Linux laptops, Cyber Essential audits, ISO certification, SOC 2 audits, conditional access policies for SSO.
issues.resolution: Re-enroll all Pagero Linux laptops into Intune, resolve the device-specific errors currently blocking re-enrollment, and ensure ongoing processes so developers regularly log into the Intune app to remain active. ETS will provide L3 support while developers perform first-line activities.

dependencies.title: SentinelOne EDR deployment dependency for S3NS production go-live
dependencies.description: Deployment of SentinelOne endpoint detection and response (EDR) in the S3NS Kubernetes environment is required to provide primary threat detection and satisfy ISRM production security requirements for Pagero customers using the new France environment.
dependencies.dependent_on: Kubernetes cluster upgrade in the S3NS environment and successful SentinelOne agent installation and validation by the Hawk/infra teams.
dependencies.consumer: Pagero Integration program overall, specifically S3NS pre-prod/prod operations and customers onboarding to the France instance from July 2026 onward.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If SentinelOne is not deployed before customers begin sending live production traffic (expected from July 2026 and ramping up toward the 1 September 2026 French mandate), the environment will lack its primary EDR-based threat detection, increasing security risk and potentially creating audit and policy non-compliance. ISRM may need to explicitly accept this gap or could require constraints on customer onboarding until SentinelOne is live.
dependencies.mitigation: Infra has deferred the required Kubernetes upgrade to protect the 12 June 2026 production readiness date and summer stability. ISRM (via Bill Brinkman) will (1) confirm whether any alternative deployment options exist that avoid or minimise the Kubernetes upgrade, (2) evaluate whether compensating controls can partially offset the lack of SentinelOne during any gap period, and (3) seek formal ISRM leadership approval if operating without SentinelOne for a defined period is required.

dependencies.title: Cloud Armor / WAF deployment dependency for S3NS production security controls

dependencies.consumer: Pagero Integration program security posture for S3NS production, including ISRM control compliance for external customer traffic and regulatory audits.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Cloud Armor / WAF is not deployed when the S3NS environment becomes production-ready and customers start onboarding, the program will operate with reduced application-layer protection, increasing exposure to web-based threats and creating a documented deviation from the target ISRM control set. ISRM leadership may need to accept this temporary gap and define a deadline for remediation.
dependencies.mitigation: Program leadership (Parkes, Lorna) will capture this gap and seek ISRM leadership sign-off on operating without Cloud Armor / WAF for an initial period, while the infra/ISRM teams agree and deliver a deployment plan. decisions.title: Maintain external S3NS production date of 31 May 2026 and defer formal revision
decisions.description: The SteerCo agreed to continue communicating 31 May 2026 as the S3NS production availability date to customers (including Deloitte, Warner Brothers, Nestlé), while internally planning around a potential shift to 12 June 2026 and deferring any formal revision of the external date until further evidence is available. A follow-up decision point was set for around 21 May 2026 to reassess whether the 31 May date can be maintained or must be revised (potentially to 12 June or 1 July 2026).
decisions.rationale: Changing the externally communicated date prematurely to 12 June 2026 could create unnecessary customer disruption and require broad re-communication. The team believes that within 1–2 weeks they will have better visibility into whether the current delays can be contained to a short slip or require a more substantial date change.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Immediately revise the external production date from 31 May 2026 to 12 June 2026.
2) Maintain 31 May 2026 externally while monitoring progress and internally tracking toward a potential 12 June 2026 date.
3) Move directly to a later date such as 1 July 2026 and broadly re-communicate to customers.
decisions.dependencies_linked: S3NS production environment build dependency on pre-prod completion; customer testing and cut-over from global/Europe 1 instances to Europe 2.

decisions.title: Transition CIO integration business systems items to BAU at end of May 2026

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The Commercial Processes and Systems Program is modernizing and standardizing end to end commercial capabilities, moving fragmented sales, billing, revenue, and post sale operations onto a unified strategic stack that supports new commercial models and stronger financial controls. This matters because it underpins revenue growth, improves auditability, and reduces operational risk across the commercial lifecycle. The program objective is to enable $158.7M in sales and $61.6M in revenue, with detailed tracking metrics now being baselined against this target.

The program remains at risk due to ongoing issues with revenue recognition for mixed billing frequency orders, which is consuming testing capacity and putting broader feature delivery at risk. SurePrep and CoCounsel Tax new sales are live and progressing well under ELS; SafeSend and Additive AI (TAAP) remain on track for core functionality ahead of the July Semi-Monthly launch. TREC has been moved out to the July Semi-Monthly release to allow the team to focus on non-TREC testing and stabilization. CoCounsel Legal remains at risk due to unresolved decisions around MVP scope and launch functionality.  

Link to full report: [2026-05-22 CPSP Status Report](https://trten.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/ELTC/Shared%20Documents/General/12.%20Program%20monitoring%20and%20control/12.1%20%20Weekly%20status%20report/Status%20Reports%202026/05-May/2026-05-22%20CPSP%20Status%20Report.docx?d=w4ebea87b6c0942b8be1c0258df902a28&csf=1&web=1&e=KnAofc)

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on locking CoCounsel Legal scope by 29 May 2026, securing Design Authority approval for Multi-Location Contracts, and completing the SurePrep professional services replanning so that downstream milestones and UAT capacity can be confirmed and protected.

## Milestones

-   Resolve CoCounsel Legal scope lockdown issue and confirm onboarding approach by 29 May 2026.
    
-   Resolve mixed billing frequency issues and deploy to production as a hot fix by 31 May 2026.
    
-   Complete replanning for Professional Services – SurePrep May Semi-Monthly and recommit to a new delivery timeline by 26 July 2026.
    
-   Complete onboarding of SafeSend Phase 1 and Additive AI for TAAP by 27 July 2026 with ELS to follow.

entities.okrs: PLE-3 - Infrastructure Modernization & AI Adoption; 2.2 Cloud Optimization / Modernization - Migrate legacy workloads from Colo to Cloud

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Program is currently being flagged as Amber due to 2 underlying projects being impacted:

Montreal RAG currently Amber due to a number of unknown outcomes, which could impact site being closed by end 2026:

-   Waiting for delivery date for MS SQL 2022 pattern for AMS builds.  Delivery team are currently reviewing priorities and will come back with available date.
    
-   Application team resources are not familiar with cloud builds/operations, so working with team to assisgn ownership to key tasks and providing guidance from PE SMEs.
    
-   No confirmed plan to complete migration/decoms caused by change in strategy from Azure to AMS cloud.
    

HighQ RAG currently Amber as one customer (Freshfield) have requested that Publishing functionality be kept available beyond the planned 31-July-2026 date until 30-Sep-2026, which means 2 UK sites (SG1/SG2) will have to remain open until end Nov-2026 at a cost around US$150,000.

\--

Colo Exit & Optimization will exit Thomson Reuters from owned and third‑party colo data centers, migrating workloads to cloud and MSP sites to reduce infrastructure technical debt, avoid Capex, and cut annual run costs from US$22.7M to US$15.5M by 2027. This improves resilience and agility while reducing exposure to financially stressed colo providers.

To date, none of the four core colo sites (Markham, Montreal, Sydney, LHR3) have been fully closed, and none of the 13 in‑scope HighQ third‑party sites have yet been decommissioned, with Markham and Montreal targeted for 31 Dec 2026 and HighQ sites targeted for closure by 30 Oct 2026. Several Montreal UFile discovery and architecture milestones due between 04 May 2026 and 15 May 2026 remain in progress past their target dates, indicating early schedule pressure on that workstream.

Overall status is AMBER, driven primarily by unresolved design, ownership, and compliance risks in the Montreal UFile migration to AMS, which threaten the 30 Sep 2026 migration milestone and the 31 Dec 2026 Montreal colo closure.

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to complete the overdue Montreal UFile discovery and architecture milestones, assign accountable owners for AMS infrastructure and application configuration, and lock a PCI DSS‑compliant design so that the 30 Sep 2026 migration date becomes credible. In parallel, the program will tighten dependency tracking across Markham and HighQ migrations to ensure the 2026 closure milestones (Markham, Montreal, and HighQ sites) remain achievable before committing downstream dilapidation dates for Sydney and LHR3.

## Milestones

-   Complete Montreal UFile Online discovery (application dependencies plus network, router, firewall) and define future‑state architecture, database, network, storage, and monitoring requirements by 2026-05-15.
    
-   Complete UFile Online migration to AMS and Phase 1 Montreal DC exit (architecture planning and migration) by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Complete final HighQ client migrations to Azure by 01 Aug 2026 and submit decoms for all HighQ sites by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Complete Markham dilapidation and site closure by 31 Dec 2026.
    
-   Complete overall Colo Exit & Optimization program by 31 Dec 2027.

risks.title: Globalscape TAXONE GEOrestricited SFTP site
risks.description: TAXONE uses the shared SFTP platform in LHR3, GlobalScape, for hosting of SFTP sites. The standard Colo Exit approach of least resistance (i.e. no redevelopment) is to migrate the SFTP sites to GlobalScape in an alternate location. At the time of LHR3 closure, the only alternate GlobalScape location available will be MSP, USA. One of the TaxOne customers has a contractual georestriction requirement; must be hosted in EU / UK. An alternate solution is available, migrating to AWS Transfer Family, but timeline is not committed.
risks.impact_description: Unable to shutdown Globalscape in LHR3, which could have impact on overall shutdown of LHR3.  Note, Globalscape licenses are set to expire end 2026.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: de Deus Lopes, Luis Fernando (TR Technology)

risks.mitigation: Application team are developing solution to replace Globalscape based on AWS transfer family.  Solution is expected to be available in 31-July-2026, but migration timescales are not yet confirmed.

risks.title: Environmental ambiguity between non-production and production in file management space
risks.description: There is ambiguity between non-production and production environments in the file management space, including shared file systems and mixed-use environments, which makes it unclear how to manage, migrate, and control files across environments.
risks.impact_description: If this ambiguity persists, file migration activities may be misconfigured or mis-scoped, production data might be exposed in non-production contexts, or critical files could be missed during migration. This may cause service disruptions, compliance issues, or require rework and could delay cutover and acceptance for AMS migration.
risks.mitigation: Clarify and document the environment classification and usage for all file shares, especially where production and non-production systems share infrastructure. Define clear responsibilities for file migration across dev, non-prod, and prod, including how real-time replication will be managed for production migrations, and track this ambiguity as a formal RAID item until resolved.

risks.title: Lack of clarity in ownership for infrastructure and application setup tasks
risks.description: There is confusion about who is responsible for tasks such as server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connection setup, TLS certificates, and network configuration in the AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If ownership for these tasks remains unclear, critical activities may be delayed or missed, leading to misconfigured infrastructure, security weaknesses, failed connectivity, and delays in testing and go-live. This can significantly impact the migration schedule and stability of the application post-cutover.
risks.mitigation: Refine and communicate the RACI matrix specifically for server configuration, load balancing, application setup, SQL connectivity, TLS certificates, and network configuration. Ensure each task has a clearly assigned owner and that dependencies are documented in runbooks and migration plans.
