risks.title: Ambiguity in roles and responsibilities for AMS migration (RACI)
risks.description: There is or was ambiguity in roles and responsibilities among team members during the AMS migration from the Montreal data center, which can cause overlapping efforts, missed tasks, and unclear accountability across the migration workstreams.
risks.impact_description: If role and responsibility ambiguity reoccurs, tasks may be duplicated or left incomplete, decision-making could be delayed, accountability for critical actions may be unclear, and confusion and inefficiencies could increase overall project risk, potentially impacting the migration timeline and service continuity.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a RACI workshop to clearly define and document roles and responsibilities for all migration tasks and communicate them to the stakeholders.

risks.title: Delay in Markham Data Center Exit Dilapidation Completion
risks.description: The completion of the Markham Data Center Exit Dilapidation, planned for October 2026, is highly dependent on the timely completion of several critical dependencies, including Content 4x Application, Hyper-V Migration, DT Max Environment migration, HighQ Azure Migration, and CIFS Shares planning and migration. Any delays in these dependencies could significantly impact the project timeline, operational costs, resource availability, and compliance/security posture. Despite active planning and rigorous efforts by the project team, the interconnected nature of these dependencies introduces inherent risks to achieving the target deadline.
risks.impact_description: Any delays in these dependencies could significantly impact the project timeline, operational costs, resource availability, and compliance/security posture. Despite active planning and rigorous efforts by the project team, the interconnected nature of these dependencies introduces inherent risks to achieving the target deadline.
risks.mitigation:
Project Dependencies and ETA for completion.

1.	Content 4x Application (Technology Pillar): In progress; expected completion by April 30th, 2026. [PM: Prasanna]
2.	Hyper-V Migration: In progress; expected completion by April 30th, 2026. [PM: Mark T.]
3.	DT Max Environment (40 VMs identified): V2V migration from Markham to MSP planned between July and September 2026. [PM: Prasanna]
4.	HighQ Azure Migration: In progress; expected completion by July 30th, 2026. [Leads: Joseph Kong, Purnesh]
5.	CIFS Shares (68 identified): Project team has initiated planning and submitted required RITMs. Internal planning calls will begin next week. ETA Sep 2026

risks.title: Change in migration strategy from Azure to AMS may impact project completion timeline
risks.description: The decision to change the migration strategy from Azure to AMS for UFile Online introduces uncertainty and may impact the overall Montreal DC Exit project completion timeline (targeted around September 2026).
risks.impact_description: The change in strategy could cause setbacks in project timelines and deliverables, delays in task execution due to unclear ownership, increased risk of errors and inefficiencies during the migration, and miscommunication among stakeholders regarding responsibilities, ultimately threatening the September 2026 completion target.
risks.mitigation: A RACI review session will be held to realign roles and responsibilities in accordance with the updated AMS migration strategy. Subsequently, dedicated sessions will be conducted to establish milestones and timelines for each phase, as well as to identify and address early-stage challenges and risks.

risks.title: Resource constraints in service management and lack of DevOps/cloud expertise
risks.description: The service management team is already heavily loaded with other initiatives such as Hyper-V migration, and product engineering lacks DevOps and cloud engineering expertise required for AMS migration.
risks.impact_description: If resource constraints and skill gaps are not addressed, key migration tasks may be delayed, executed with errors, or deprioritized. This increases the likelihood of schedule slippage, quality issues, and operational instability post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional hands-on resources with relevant DevOps and cloud skills to support the migration. Rebalance workload across service management and product engineering, and clearly prioritize AMS-related work to ensure critical tasks receive adequate attention.

risks.title: PCI DSS compliance risk for AMS production environment
risks.description: Meeting PCI DSS and other compliance requirements for a hardened, secure, documented, and certified production environment may be challenging without dedicated resources and specialized expertise.
risks.impact_description: Failure to achieve PCI DSS-compliant production infrastructure could result in non-compliance with regulatory and corporate standards, potential audit findings, restrictions on processing payment-related or sensitive data, and delays in go-live or the need to re-architect environments post-migration.
risks.mitigation: Engage the ISRM team early and integrate security and compliance activities throughout the migration. Ensure dedicated security resources review architecture, configurations, and documentation, and that a formal compliance assessment is completed before production cutover.

risks.title: Ownership gap for application configuration in new AMS environment
risks.description: While infrastructure and data migration tasks have assigned owners in platform engineering and service management, there is no clear owner for configuring and securing the application in the new AMS environment. Product engineering and service management teams lack expertise in application configuration in cloud-native infrastructure.
risks.impact_description: Without a clear owner for application configuration, critical tasks such as configuring application settings, securing endpoints, and aligning configurations with compliance requirements may be delayed or overlooked. This can jeopardize the migration timeline, create security and compliance gaps, and delay production readiness.
risks.mitigation:
Current challenge at this stage is finalizing setup documentation and validation. The business unit requires a sandbox environment to proceed with rebuild and re-engineering activities. 
•	Next Action: Gordon/Monica is currently working to define the initial build requirements for the sandbox and to identify the relevant Platform Engineering team to assist BU with Application installation.

Mukkaram from the TRNOC-Security team for reactivating the Markham Z connectors. I also appreciate the efforts of Aman, Palak, and Shubham for their thorough investigation and support in resolving the issue.
 
Issue resolution Summary: Mukkaram explained that the connectivity issues stem from changes in Zscaler connector routing after resources were migrated from the Markham Data Center to the MSP Data Center. Markham-specific Z connectors, previously optimized for accessing Markham resources, are now blocked when trying to access MSP resources due to MSP's stricter inbound restrictions. Elevated users using global connectors are unaffected.
 
To resolve the folder share access issues, Mukkaram suggests allowing MSP connectors to access Markham resources by updating the Markham firewall. This approach is simpler and avoids lengthy approval processes compared to enabling Markham connectors to access MSP resources. He recommends gathering a list of inaccessible resources to implement this solution effectively.

dependencies.title: Upgrading production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version is a mandatory prerequisite for migrating to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment to ensure compatibility and mitigate risks.
dependencies.description: The migration to Windows Server 2022 and the cloud environment is critically dependent on upgrading the current production SQL Server instances from version 2012 to a supported version (SQL Server 2017 or later). Microsoft does not support SQL Server 2012 on Windows Server 2022, making these upgrades a mandatory preparatory step to ensure compatibility and avoid risks during the migration process. Production systems, including SQL 5, SQL 6, SQL 1, and SQL 2, must be upgraded prior to the migration, as well as the remaining pre-production reporting server.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: A delay in the AMS migration scheduled for September 2026 will impact the overall project timeline, resulting in a subsequent delay of the final major milestone—the Dilapidation and Data Center Shutdown activities planned for Q4 2026.
dependencies.mitigation:
Mitigation Plan: Separate Upgrade Phase: Perform SQL Server upgrades as a distinct preparatory phase before the cloud migration to minimize risks and ensure compatibility with Windows Server 2022.
Documented Timeline: Create a detailed schedule and timeline for SQL Server upgrades, allocating sufficient time for planning, execution, and validation of the upgraded systems.
Risk Mitigation: Include contingency plans in the migration documentation to address potential issues during the upgrade and migration process.
Alignment on Timing: Collaborate across teams to align the timing and processes for upgrades and migration, ensuring a smooth transition to the cloud environment.
Ownership Assignment: Designate responsible team members to oversee the upgrade process, document the migration plan, and ensure accountability for meeting deadlines and addressing concerns.
Validation and Testing: Thoroughly test upgraded SQL Server instances in the pre-production environment to ensure stability and performance before implementing changes in production systems.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

Contact Center AI Enablement is integrating Agentforce capabilities into Salesforce Service Cloud to deliver AI-powered case summarization, answer generation, triage, and sentiment analysis for support operations. This program matters because it reduces manual effort for agents, improves response times, and provides richer insights that enhance the overall customer experience across phone, email, web, and chat channels.

Two of four defined AI capability milestones are complete (Case Summarization and Tech-only Answer Generation), with the remaining two (AI Case Deflection and Agentforce for Voice POC) on plan within their current schedules. The program is progressing within its 01 Jan 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 window, with no recorded risks, issues, or dependency impacts to date.

Overall status is Green, driven by on-schedule delivery of current milestones and the absence of active risks, issues, or schedule variance.

## Path to Green

We are sustaining Green status by closely monitoring the in-progress AI Case Deflection build and gating further channel expansion on stable performance and adoption of the already delivered summarization and answer-generation capabilities.

## Milestones

- Complete “AgentForce for Service - Case Summarization using LLM Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5” by 28 Feb 2026.  
- Complete “Answers generation (Based on Knowledges articles and cases closed condensed) - Tech only” by 23 Mar 2026.  
- Complete “Agentforce For Voice POC” by 30 Jun 2026.  
- Complete “AI Case Deflection” by 31 Jul 2026.  
- Complete overall Contact Center AI Enablement program by 31 Mar 2027.

milestones.name: AgentForce for Service - Case Summarization using LLM Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5
milestones.description: This enhancement focuses on enabling context-aware, tailored summarization prompts within Service Cloud Voice and Generative Chat. The solution will dynamically adapt prompts based on the type of support request and the specific product involved, allowing for more structured and relevant case summaries. This will improve the quality and consistency of case documentation, reduce manual effort for agents, and support better communication, handoffs, and overall case management efficiency.
milestones.metrics:
Reduction in Case Documentation Time
Summary Accuracy Rate
Agent Productivity (Cases per Agent)
Adoption Rate of AI Summarization

milestones.name: Answers generation (Based on Knowledges articles and cases closed condensed) - Tech only
milestones.description: Enable Service Cloud agents to use AgentForce-powered “Generate Answers” within the case interface to search and retrieve relevant knowledge articles, past cases, and help site content, and generate contextual, editable responses—improving resolution speed and consistency while capturing usage data for analytics.
milestones.metrics:
First Contact Resolution (FCR)– Increase in cases resolved in the first interaction
Average Handle Time (AHT) – Reduction in time taken to resolve cases
Answer Adoption Rate – of generated answers used/sent by agents to customers

milestones.name: AI Case Deflection
milestones.description:
Integrate (KoreAI or Agentforce) AI Assistant with ESC for email, webform, self-service portal, and in-product case requests.
AI-driven case triage and deflection using AEM knowledge articles.
Automated customer responses with summarized solutions and relevant links.
Logging and audit of AI interactions within ESC.
Reporting on AI Assistant effectiveness and deflection rates.
Integrate AI deflected case survey from Forsta
milestones.metrics:
Customer submits a webform; AI recommends a solution and deflects the case if confident.
Customer sends an email; AI responds automatically with knowledge articles or creates a case if unsure.
Manager reviews monthly AI deflection statistics and identifies areas for knowledge improvement.
Agent views AI interaction history when handling escalated cases.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The Compliance Program is delivering an integrated set of controls and capabilities across product, access, financial, and operational domains so that TR can meet government, regulatory, contractual, and audit expectations consistently. This matters because it reduces compliance risk, improves audit readiness, and enables secure, scalable growth in government and other regulated markets.

Across seven projects, five are Green, one is Amber, and one is Red, so 71% of workstreams are currently tracking to plan while the remainder are at risk or off plan. The NYNJ Port Authority onboarding is progressing toward mid to late 2026 production releases for HighQ, Contract Express, CoCounsel, and the Outlook Add-In, while the IA Remediations project is carrying a backlog of past-due audit items.

Overall status is Red, driven primarily by the IA Remediations workstream where 5 of 17 Internal Audit remediation milestones have due dates between 31 Dec 2025 and 31 Mar 2026 and remain incomplete.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on the IA Remediations workstream by re-baselining all overdue findings dated 31 Dec 2025 through 31 Mar 2026, sequencing remediation for high-risk items due in 2026 ahead of those due in 2027, and tracking closure against specific Protecht issue IDs. In parallel, the program will tightly manage NYNJ Port Authority dependencies such as HighQ antivirus selection, FedRAMP and HIPAA gap assessments, and CIAM integration so that the 2026 production dates remain achievable while IA backlog is reduced.

## Milestones

-   Complete CIAM integration and customer onboarding readiness for Port Authority products by 30 May 2026.
    
-   Make Contract Express available in production for NYNJ Port Authority onboarding by 05 Jun 2026.
    
-   Make HighQ available in production for NYNJ Port Authority onboarding and complete onboarding of 8 applications into SailPoint by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver CoCounsel FedRAMP, Privacy controls, and HIPAA remediation in production for NYNJ Port Authority onboarding by 30 Sep 2026.
    
-   Close the Compliance Program and transition to steady-state governance by 01 Apr 2027.

risks.title: Tool duplication and fragmented adoption across ICFR tooling ecosystem
risks.description: Multiple tools (Protecht, ADO, SharePoint, legacy repositories, DoubleCheck) currently support overlapping ICFR activities without a clear target-state architecture, risking continued duplication and fragmented adoption even after the transformation.
risks.impact_description: If tool duplication persists, control data may remain fragmented, evidence and testing results may be inconsistent, reporting may lack integrity, and users may experience confusion over system-of-record responsibilities, undermining efficiency, governance, and audit readiness.
risks.mitigation: Define explicit system-of-record roles for each tool, design an integration architecture, select and implement a clear future-state tooling model (Protecht-led or complementary integrated), and develop a repository retirement and migration plan to consolidate control lifecycle data.

risks.title: Change fatigue among control owners participating in ICFR transformation
risks.description: Control owners are already subject to multiple initiatives and may experience change fatigue as new ICFR processes, controls, tooling, and certifications are introduced.
risks.impact_description: If change fatigue grows, control owners may disengage, reduce quality of execution, or revert to legacy practices, leading to inconsistent control performance, incomplete evidence, and failure to sustain the new operating model over time.
risks.mitigation: Simplify control patterns where possible, introduce automation and continuous monitoring to reduce manual burden, provide clear guidance and reusable templates, and sequence changes to avoid overloading control owners during critical periods.

risks.title: PwC may refuse to use internal ICFR tools for audit interactions
risks.description: The external auditor (PwC) has previously been hesitant to use internal tools, and may continue to resist adopting Protecht or related platforms for evidence requests and status updates.
risks.impact_description: If PwC does not use internal tools, audit requests may remain email-based and ad hoc, leading to poor visibility, repeated evidence capture, unclear ownership, and additional administrative effort, and may limit the value of the new ICFR workflow and reporting capabilities.
risks.mitigation: Design and implement a controlled Excel-based exchange model for PwC status updates that integrates into internal workflows, maintain disciplined internal request intake and tracking, and agree on a structured interaction model with PwC early in the program.

risks.title: Service Management competing priorities may delay Port Authority work
risks.description: Competing priorities for Service Management work create a risk: Service Management needs prioritization away from the company‑wide migration to Azure and onto Port Authority work. If this does not happen, the Port Authority deadline may not be met.
risks.impact_description: If Service Management cannot reprioritize from the company‑wide Azure migration to Port Authority work, key service management deliverables for Port Authority may be delayed, risking missed contractual deadlines and impacting go‑live readiness.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional capacity so Service Management can continue the Azure migration while also supporting Port Authority work; Noah has approved $500K in CapEx for Service Management to bring in additional resources for the Azure migration.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - Contract Express available in Production
NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: Inadequate or outdated HIPAA policies, BAAs, training, and breach notification processes
risks.description: Policies, contract templates (BAAs/BASAs), training procedures, and breach notification playbooks are being reviewed and updated as part of the HIPAA program. Until updates are complete and rolled out, there is a risk that current materials may not reflect the desired future state or regulatory expectations.
risks.impact_description: If outdated or incomplete policies, contract templates, training, or breach notification procedures remain in use, employees and customers may receive inconsistent or incorrect guidance. This could lead to misaligned BAAs, inadequate training coverage, or mishandled breach/disclosure events, resulting in compliance gaps or adverse regulatory findings.

raised_by.name: HIPAA Compliance Program Scope document and April 23, 2026 Status Report

risks.mitigation: Continue updating the HIPAA compliance program charter, BAAs, HIPAA Privacy Notice, training procedures, and breach notification requirements. Distribute updated notices and templates (e.g., U.S. health plan HIPAA Privacy Notice issued in February 2026; updated BAAs delivered to suppliers and customers), assign and monitor training completion, and embed updated requirements into legal notification playbooks.

risks.title: Over-scoping of ICFR due to conservative posture
risks.description: The organization may continue to define an overly broad ICFR scope, including excessive controls and application coverage, due to conservative risk and audit postures, despite transformation efforts to rationalize.
risks.impact_description: If over-scoping persists, the control universe may remain larger than necessary, driving unnecessary compliance cost and complexity, extending testing and remediation cycles, and making the framework harder to sustain and defend.
risks.mitigation: Apply materiality-led scoping criteria, document risk-based rationale for inclusion/exclusion decisions, align scoping logic with external auditor expectations, and obtain CDA approval for scope changes to avoid conservative drift.

risks.title: HighQ: Pen testing may exceed QA testing dates
risks.description: The full Pen testing completion dates will fall outside of the QA testing date window. This could put timelines at risk.
risks.mitigation: To meet the timelines, the team will create a delta report from the HighQ Commercial instance and the HighQ Gov instance to run Pen testing on, which brings the pen testing date back down before the QA testing window dates.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: Non-integrated access systems and third-party portals may weaken access governance
risks.description: Some systems are not integrated with SailPoint and rely on manual processes or third-party portals, creating potential gaps in provisioning, certification, and deprovisioning controls within the ICFR scope.
risks.impact_description: If non-integrated access systems remain unmanaged, there may be inconsistent or delayed deprovisioning, incomplete access reviews, and increased risk of unauthorized access that could impact ICFR control effectiveness and audit outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Define and implement compensating access controls, establish exception governance for non-integrated systems, design measurable deprovisioning controls, and incorporate these systems into the Access Governance Modernization workstream.

risks.title: HighQ Transparent File Encryption (TFE) implementation for HIPAA within FedRAMP boundary
risks.description: TFE for HIPAA must be defined and implemented appropriately while on the FedRAMP boundary. Developments may be required and were not estimated; documentation and mitigating controls need to be evaluated.
risks.impact_description: If TFE is not properly defined and implemented for HIPAA within the FedRAMP boundary, HighQ may not meet HIPAA expectations or internal risk posture, potentially delaying compliance, increasing audit findings, or requiring unplanned remediation work.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate and document appropriate TFE implementation and mitigating controls for HIPAA on the FedRAMP boundary; plan and perform any required development work and update documentation accordingly.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: WL/PL privacy control requirements and impact not yet understood
risks.description: For WL/PL, the team needs to understand what the requirements are for the 24 privacy controls that have now been approved. This could impact timelines but direction is not yet clear and estimates are still needed.
risks.impact_description: If WL/PL teams do not gain clarity on the 24 approved privacy controls and complete estimates, privacy‑related work may be delayed, potentially impacting WL/PL compliance posture and any Port Authority dependencies on these products.
risks.mitigation: Meet with Jenna to review the 24 required privacy controls for WL/PL, clarify expectations, and then complete effort estimates to inform planning and resourcing.

risks.title: Inconsistent evidence quality across ICFR controls
risks.description: Evidence supporting ICFR controls may vary in quality, completeness, and standardization, which can undermine audit readiness and increase rework during testing and external reviews.
risks.impact_description: If evidence quality remains inconsistent, auditors may challenge control effectiveness, additional testing and rework may be required, and compliance cycle time may increase, undermining one of the core objectives of the transformation.

risk_owner.name: Quality Reviewer role / Control Design Authority

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Quality Reviewer role / Track G Lead (Shannon)

risks.mitigation: Define standard evidence patterns and requirements, embed evidence standards into workflow and templates, establish a quality review function to validate sufficiency, and provide reusable job aids and training to control owners.

risks.title: Program sprawl and excessive stakeholder model may dilute focus and slow decisions
risks.description: The ICFR transformation program may expand its scope or stakeholder base excessively, resulting in complex governance, slow decision-making, and blurred accountability.
risks.impact_description: If the program becomes overly broad with too many stakeholders, decision cycles may lengthen, priorities may become unclear, and delivery of key workstreams could be delayed or under-resourced, impacting achievement of year-1 outcomes and overall objectives.
risks.mitigation: Maintain a lean core team and a small, decision-capable Control Design Authority; define clear roles and decision rights; use structured decision forums; and manage scope through formal change control to avoid uncontrolled expansion.

risks.title: CIAM orchestration token correctness may delay CARI integration and customer onboarding
risks.description: Previously, CIAM integration and customer onboarding for Port Authority products were blocked not by architecture but by token correctness. An authentication gap in CIAM orchestration tokens required for CARI integration prevented completion of integration with the new legacy token service.
risks.impact_description: If CIAM orchestration token issues were not resolved, CARI's integration with the new legacy token service would be delayed, slowing customer onboarding for Port Authority and potentially impacting downstream timelines for product enablement and compliance validation across HighQ, CoCounsel, and other in-scope products.
risks.mitigation: Continue technical validation of CIAM orchestration tokens; work closely with CARI/RAS on cutover activities, obtain and verify correct CIAM tokens, and complete integration with the new legacy token service so that CIAM is no longer a blocker for customer onboarding.

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual-region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.
risks.impact_description: If the Ops team requires more time than planned to complete Cloudflare setup due to inexperience, the schedule for standing up CARI APIs in USE2 (Pre Prod and Prod) and completing Cloudflare work for APIs and MFEs may slip, which could delay broader CoCounsel readiness and associated Port Authority and FedRAMP activities.
risks.mitigation: Schedule knowledge transitions for the Ops team and engage the DOE team, which previously supported FedRAMP, for additional assistance if required. Use this support to accelerate learning and reduce schedule impact while Cloudflare work is completed.

risks.title: Sungard Avantgard Integrity onboarding blocked by lack of APIs for integration
risks.description: For Sungard Avantgard Integrity, the team is waiting for a delivery date for an enhanced API. FIS vendor is not engaged in a development role, hence currently there is nobody to build the necessary APIs for SialPoint integration.
risks.impact_description: If the required enhanced APIs are not delivered and funding is not approved in time, Sungard Avantgard Integrity cannot be integrated with SailPoint by the planned 2026-09-30 go-live. This will leave access request and related controls manual or fragmented, affecting SOX compliance coverage for this application.
risks.mitigation: Meeting FIS Vendor team post approval of SOW for support hours, to explore integration options for SailPoint onboarding.

milestones.name: Sungard Avantgard Integrity SailPoint onboarding go-live

risks.title: Competing priorities may limit product and operational teams’ capacity for HIPAA assessment and remediation
risks.description: Product and operational teams may have limited bandwidth due to competing priorities, which could constrain their ability to participate in HIPAA assessments, scope validation, and remediation work.
risks.impact_description: If teams cannot allocate sufficient time and resources to HIPAA activities, assessments and remediation may be delayed or incomplete. This could result in extended periods of noncompliance, missed project milestones, delayed implementation of controls, and increased risk exposure for TR and its customers.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Program Manager for HIPAA Compliance Program

risks.mitigation: Establish program governance with a SteerCo to drive accountability, prioritize HIPAA workstreams, and secure leadership support for resource allocation. Clearly communicate expectations to product and operational teams, integrate HIPAA activities into planning cycles, and track progress through program artifacts such as milestones, timelines, and RAAID logs.

risks.title: Variability in product architectures and data flows may prevent a single uniform HIPAA solution
risks.description: Products and services differ in architectures, data flows, and contractual commitments, which may make it difficult to implement a single standardized HIPAA compliance solution across all in-scope areas.
risks.impact_description: If a one-size-fits-all approach is pursued but proves infeasible, some products may end up with misaligned or ineffective controls. This variability could lead to uneven compliance levels, increased complexity in monitoring and audits, and potential gaps where specific product risks are not adequately addressed.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: R&C and Privacy in coordination with Product/Engineering

risks.mitigation: Develop a business-aligned control framework that distinguishes between enterprise-level controls and product-specific requirements. Tailor remediation plans to each product’s architecture and data flows while maintaining common control objectives, and leverage lessons learned from early assessments (e.g., HighQ, SIU, Legal Tracker) to build reusable patterns.

risks.title: Phased implementation may extend beyond initial project window
risks.description: The need for phased implementation across multiple products and services means that full HIPAA compliance maturity may require stages beyond the initial project timeline (2025-07-07 to 2027-12-31).
risks.impact_description: If the program cannot achieve full maturity within the initial project window, some products may remain partially compliant, with incomplete remediation or monitoring. This could necessitate extended funding, increase program management complexity, and leave residual compliance and operational risks unaddressed for a longer period.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Program Manager for HIPAA Compliance Program

risks.mitigation: Plan and communicate a phased roadmap that clearly identifies which capabilities and products will be addressed in each stage, including post-project activities. Secure long-term sponsorship and funding for ongoing compliance work, and embed HIPAA guidance into the broader product compliance framework to support ongoing scalability.

risks.title: Unclear decisions on signing BAAs/BASAs during discovery and remediation phases
risks.description: The program has not yet finalized decisions on whether to sign BAAs/BASAs for in-scope products during the discovery phase or before remediation is complete, and whether to unwind existing contracts for products without valid PHI use cases.
risks.impact_description: If decisions about BAAs/BASAs are not clarified, sales and legal teams may take inconsistent positions, either accepting excessive risk by signing agreements prematurely or missing revenue opportunities by declining deals. Existing contracts may also remain in place where TR cannot or should not support PHI, exposing the company to contractual and compliance risk.

raised_by.name: HIPAA Compliance Program Scope document (Critical Decisions sections)

risks.mitigation: Use the SteerCo to define and approve a clear decision framework for BAAs/BASAs, including conditions under which they can be signed during discovery or remediation, and any time limits. Determine criteria and processes for unwinding contracts where there is no valid PHI use case. Communicate this guidance to Sales, Commercial Excellence, and Customer Trust teams as part of the broader awareness campaign.

risks.title: Alliant onboarding blocked by Rightsline platform change and lack of integration options like APIs
risks.description: For Alliant, the Rightsline vendor is changing their platform for user management and has not shared a timeline. They currently lack bandwidth to work on the requested APIs needed for SailPoint. API availability is required by June 15 to meet the planned go-live of 2026-09-30.
risks.impact_description: If Rightsline does not provide the necessary APIs on time, SailPoint cannot integrate with Alliant as planned. This will delay automated provisioning, de-provisioning, and access reviews for Alliant and may compromise SOX control automation for this application.
risks.mitigation: Continue escalation to Krishna Polineni and work with Rightsline to obtain a firm timeline for the UI upgrade and API availability. Confirm API delivery by June 15, 2026 and, if delayed, explore alternative integration approaches or adjust the go-live plan with communicated interim controls.

risks.title: IAM/CoCounsel tight coupling with HighQ limits failover and failback options
risks.description: If IAM/CoCounsel remains tightly coupled with HighQ under the chosen hosting model, single‑component failover/failback will be limited, which is acknowledged as a constraint of the chosen hosting model.
risks.impact_description: Limited ability to fail over or fail back IAM/CoCounsel independently of HighQ could reduce system resilience and increase recovery times during incidents, potentially impacting availability commitments for the Port Authority environment.
risks.mitigation: Accept the architectural constraint for the Port Authority timeline and manage operational risk through monitoring and incident response; consider decoupling or additional resiliency improvements in future post‑Port Authority enhancements.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause microservice startup issues
risks.description: FIPS cryptography requirements may cause application startup issues, requiring additional joint troubleshooting; this is a current technical challenge for the microservices.
risks.impact_description: If FIPS cryptography requirements cause persistent startup issues, microservices may be unstable or unavailable in the FedRAMP/HIPAA environment, delaying deployment, increasing engineering effort, and potentially impacting Port Authority go‑live timelines.
risks.mitigation: Conduct joint troubleshooting of FIPS‑related startup issues for affected microservices, adjusting configurations or components as needed to ensure stable operation under FIPS requirements.

risks.title: HighQ and Contract Express resourcing at risk due to incomplete effort estimation
risks.description: There is a risk to approved HighQ and Contract Express resourcing because estimation of the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not complete.
risks.impact_description: If the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not accurately estimated, HighQ and Contract Express may be under‑resourced, causing schedule slippage, scope cuts, or quality issues in meeting contract requirements.
risks.mitigation: Complete detailed estimation for HighQ and Contract Express Port Authority work and request additional resources as needed following completion of estimation.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - Contract Express available in Production
NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.description: There is a risk to previously committed HighQ and Contract Express deliverables because estimation of the effort to meet the Port Authority contract is not complete, and the work required for the CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add‑in is not yet understood.
risks.impact_description: If total effort, including work for the CoCounsel Outlook Add‑in, is underestimated or not fully understood, HighQ and Contract Express may not deliver all previously committed functionality by the Port Authority dates, affecting contractual compliance and stakeholder expectations.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - Contract Express available in Production
NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: HighQ antivirus tool Sophos may not meet FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 requirements
risks.description: Sophos, an antivirus/security tool currently used by HighQ, has not been confirmed as compliant with FedRAMP requirements, specifically around FIPS 140‑2/3 encryption compliance. A similar issue previously required another internal team to abandon ClamAV and switch tools. If Sophos cannot prove compliance, HighQ may need to replace it with a different tool such as SentinelOne or Azure Defender, which could impact the engineering timeline.
risks.impact_description: If Sophos cannot demonstrate FIPS 140‑2/3 compliance and must be replaced, HighQ will face additional engineering work to select, integrate, configure, and validate a new antivirus tool, potentially delaying the Port Authority compliance schedule and introducing operational risk during the transition.
risks.mitigation: Evaluate Sophos for FIPS 140‑2/3 and FedRAMP compliance; if it cannot meet requirements, plan and execute a transition to a compliant tool such as SentinelOne or Azure Defender, including necessary engineering and testing.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: Project is not prioritized for the Service Management team.
risks.description: Competing priorities keep the work of permanent user role creation from starting.
risks.mitigation: Service Management believes they can work this in with existing resources. Project Charter will be  used to request the prioritization.

milestones.name: Prioritization and resources assigned for creation of permanent user roles within SAP Service Management

risks.title: HighQ antivirus scanning tool selection (Sophos / SentinelOne / Defender) remains unresolved
risks.description: For HighQ (and related CoCounsel integrations), identifying and validating a compliant antivirus/malware scanning tool is still in progress. Options under evaluation include Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender. License procurement has been completed, but verification of the selected solution against FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 and Port Authority requirements is ongoing, including a planned FARB discussion on the Sophos solution.
risks.impact_description: If a compliant antivirus solution is not fully verified and approved in time, HighQ and dependent CoCounsel integrations may face delays achieving FedRAMP/HIPAA and Port Authority security requirements. Late changes to the selected tool (e.g., replacing Sophos if it fails FIPS validation) would introduce additional engineering, configuration, and testing effort, potentially impacting the June 30, 2026 compliance milestones and increasing operational security risk.
risks.mitigation: Continue evaluation of Sophos, SentinelOne, and Microsoft Defender with a specific focus on FedRAMP FIPS 140‑2/3 compliance and Port Authority requirements. Use the completed license procurement to accelerate hands‑on verification in the HighQ/FedRAMP environment. Engage FARB and ISRM to review the proposed Sophos solution and confirm acceptability; if Sophos cannot meet requirements, pivot to a verified alternative (e.g., SentinelOne or Defender) with minimal delay.

milestones.name: NYNJ PA - HighQ available in Production

risks.title: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side may be delayed due to Ops team inexperience
risks.description: Cloudflare setup on the CARI commercial side is being performed by the Ops team for the first time. Because the team has not done this work before, there is a learning curve that may impact delivery timelines for the dual‑region CARI commercial environment that underpins CoCounsel services.
risks.impact_description: If the Ops team requires more time than planned to complete Cloudflare setup due to inexperience, the schedule for standing up CARI APIs in USE2 (Pre Prod and Prod) and completing Cloudflare work for APIs and MFEs may slip. This could delay broader CoCounsel readiness, dual‑region resilience, and associated Port Authority and FedRAMP activities that depend on these services.
risks.mitigation: Schedule and execute knowledge transitions for the Ops team, and reach out to the DOE team (which previously supported FedRAMP) for additional assistance as needed. Use DOE support to accelerate learning and unblock Cloudflare configuration for APIs and MFEs so that USE2 Pre Prod and Prod timelines can be met.

risks.title: RAS Dual Region team bandwidth constraints may delay dual-region delivery
risks.description: The RAS Dual Region workstream is constrained by insufficient team bandwidth due to org-level resource changes. Team members were moved to other projects (e.g., Catalyst and AIESE), and remaining staff are spread thin across multiple initiatives.
risks.impact_description: If bandwidth issues persist, migration waves (especially Waves 1–4, including core services, RAS Search, and Notifications) may be delayed beyond planned dates, pushing out completion of RAS Dual Region work. This would in turn impact dependent CoCounsel and CARI dual-region and FedRAMP activities, as well as failover testing and resilience commitments required for Port Authority and other government customers.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: RAS Dual Region leadership (Karen McInrue and Tim Masso)

risks.mitigation: Conduct resourcing adjustment discussions to obtain clearer time commitments and add capacity; prioritize high-priority repos and dependency chains first. As of late May 2026, five additional resources have been added to the project. Continue progressing Waves 1–4 (core services, RAS Content Display and Search repos, Notifications, and remaining repos) with close tracking to complete migrations by end of June 2026, and prepare for scale and failover testing thereafter.

risks.title: Lack of clarity from FedRamp-based HIPAA assessments for C-Track and Case Center
risks.description: For C-Track and Case Center, Fortreum conducted assessments within the FedRamp space, but the reports did not provide clear remediation guidance for identified HIPAA gaps.
risks.impact_description: Without clear remediation guidance, the product teams may be uncertain how to address HIPAA gaps, delaying remediation and limiting the ability to confidently issue BAAs. This could stall sales opportunities, leave compliance gaps unaddressed, and increase regulatory and contractual risk.

risk_owner.name: Product owners for C-Track and Case Center

risks.mitigation: R&C and Privacy will review the Fortreum assessment results, interpret the findings, and provide detailed remediation guidance to the C-Track and Case Center teams before BAAs are issued. Align the remediation steps with the HIPAA control framework and track them through Protecht or equivalent tooling.

risks.title: Potential gaps in SIU Professional Services remediation execution
risks.description: Although the SIU Professional Services HIPAA assessment is complete and a remediation plan has been developed, remediation is staged through the end of 2026, and not all gaps will be resolved by mid-2026.
risks.impact_description: If planned SIU remediation activities are delayed or not fully implemented, SIU services may remain partially noncompliant while being sold under BAAs, exposing TR to compliance and contractual risk. Extended timelines also increase the window during which issues could result in incidents or audit findings.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: SIU Professional Services remediation project lead

risks.mitigation: Execute against the defined remediation plan with milestones targeting completion of most gaps by the end of Q2 2026 and all gaps by the end of 2026. Monitor progress via Protecht or program dashboards, escalate delays to the SteerCo, and adjust resources as needed to meet deadlines.

risks.title: Legal Tracker remediation year-end deadlines
risks.description: The Legal Tracker HIPAA assessment is complete, and remediation planning is underway with deadlines expected by year-end.
risks.impact_description: If Legal Tracker remediation is not fully planned and implemented by the year-end deadline, Legal Tracker may continue to operate with HIPAA gaps, affecting its ability to support existing and new customers under BAAs and potentially exposing TR to compliance and contractual risk.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the remediation plan and hold regular working sessions between Privacy and product engineering teams to track implementation. Align the timeline with the year-end completion target and escalate any blockers to the SteerCo.

risk_owner.name: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-in team

mitigation_plan_owner.name: CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-in team

risks.mitigation: Plan and execute work to bring the CoCounsel Outlook Add‑in microservices into FedRAMP/NIST 800‑53 Rev 5 compliance in alignment with the HighQ environment; address this as part of upcoming work for the add‑in.

risks.description: For CoCounsel Core, the team needs to understand what the requirements are for the 24 privacy controls that have now been approved. This could impact timelines but direction is not yet clear and estimates are still needed.
risks.impact_description: If the requirements and effort for the 24 approved privacy controls for CoCounsel Core are not clarified and estimated promptly, planning and implementation may be delayed, which could cause CoCounsel to miss privacy‑related delivery dates for Port Authority.

risks.title: June 30 Port Authority compliance timeline may not be met for HighQ and Contract Express
risks.description: There is a risk that the June 30 timeline for compliance with the Port Authority contract may not be met because requirements were not finalized when planning began.
risks.impact_description: If HighQ and Contract Express do not achieve compliance with the Port Authority contract by June 30, 2026, the program could miss contractual deadlines, breach obligations, and damage stakeholder trust, potentially requiring schedule extensions, additional funding, and re‑negotiation with the Port Authority.
risks.mitigation:
1) Finalize and share Privacy Control requirements (completed Jan 14, 2026).
2) Share the initial set of Security Control requirements (completed Jan 21, 2026).
3) Have Fortreum complete the full Security Control gap assessment by Mar 15, 2026 to clarify work scope and close gaps in time for the June 30 deadline.

risks.title: DevOps bandwidth constraints may delay CoCounsel Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US compliance work

While application teams are progressing sprint plans (sprints 11–15 for both the Outlook Add-In privacy/security controls and CoCounsel HIPAA documentation and control-evidence work), they report very limited DevOps engagement.
risks.impact_description: If DevOps bandwidth remains constrained, key technical and operational tasks—such as Azure App registrations, CI/CD compliance gates, deployment of AKS/FIPS configurations, K8s pod security settings, and infrastructure changes in Azure Gov—may not be completed in sync with application sprints. This could delay E2E testing across Azure Gov and M365, postpone achieving compliant runtime environments for the Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US, and ultimately push out Q3 2026 delivery of HIPAA and privacy controls required for Port Authority.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize DevOps support for CoCounsel for MS Outlook Add-In and CoCounsel US workstreams through Q2 2026 by explicitly reserving capacity for Azure App registrations, CI/CD pipeline changes, and AKS/FIPS configuration work. Coordinate sprint planning between application teams and DevOps so that critical infrastructure tasks are scheduled early in sprints 11–15. Consider temporary reallocation of additional DevOps engineers or engaging shared services to cover the Q2 peak demand.

risks.title: Limited stakeholder availability may delay ICFR design and implementation
risks.description: Key finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders may not have sufficient time to participate in workshops, reviews, and approvals, which could slow or stall the design, validation, and implementation of the modernized ICFR operating model.
risks.impact_description: If stakeholder availability is limited, critical design decisions may be delayed, future-state processes may not reflect operational reality, implementation timelines could slip, and the project may miss ICFR reporting and audit timelines, reducing the effectiveness and credibility of the transformation.
risks.mitigation: Plan and schedule workshops well in advance, secure Sponsor and leadership support to prioritize stakeholder time, use focused, time-boxed sessions, provide asynchronous review options, and track attendance and decisions through a formal governance cadence to keep momentum even when some stakeholders are unavailable.

risks.title: Competing business priorities may reduce participation from control owners and functional leads
risks.description: Control owners and functional leaders may prioritize other initiatives or operational demands over participation in the ICFR transformation activities, reducing timely engagement in design, testing, and adoption.
risks.impact_description: If key control owners and functional leaders do not engage, the project may deliver designs that lack buy-in, suffer from delays in approvals and adoption, and face implementation issues that compromise the effectiveness and sustainability of the new ICFR framework.
risks.mitigation: Escalate prioritization needs through the Sponsor and business leadership, clearly communicate project value and regulatory importance, align project milestones with business calendars, and incorporate ICFR tasks into performance objectives for key leaders and control owners.

risks.mitigation: Continue coordination with Maria and Jenna; meetings have taken place and another meeting is planned to discuss current progress, clarify requirements, and incorporate findings into the overall understanding and planning.

risks.title: Inconsistent existing documentation may increase effort required for assessment and standardization
risks.description: Current SOX and ICFR documentation is inconsistent in quality, format, and completeness, which may increase the complexity and effort needed to perform current-state assessment, gap analysis, and standardization.
risks.impact_description: If documentation inconsistency is higher than anticipated, timelines for assessment and rationalization may extend, resource requirements may increase, and some controls or processes may be misinterpreted, leading to potential gaps in the future-state framework and additional rework.
risks.mitigation: Define clear documentation standards upfront, prioritize critical processes and high-risk areas for early review, allocate dedicated resources for documentation clean-up, and use templates and guidance to drive consistency during remediation of existing materials.

risks.title: Change resistance may slow adoption of new ICFR processes, templates, and tools
risks.description: Control owners, process teams, and other stakeholders may resist changes to established ICFR processes, documentation standards, and tooling, slowing adoption of the future-state operating model.
risks.impact_description: If change resistance is significant, the project may achieve only partial adoption, leading to inconsistent execution, mixed evidence quality, and limited realization of efficiency and governance benefits, as well as potential audit challenges.
risks.mitigation: Implement structured change management and communication plans, deliver role-based training and office hours, highlight quick wins, involve stakeholders in design decisions through governance forums, and use leadership sponsorship to reinforce expectations and accountability.

risks.title: Technology dependencies or approval delays may impact implementation timing for system enablement
risks.description: If supporting technology changes, integrations, or new tools require extended architecture, security, or procurement approvals, implementation of system-enabled ICFR capabilities may be delayed.
risks.impact_description: Delays in technology decisions or approvals could push back deployment of tooling for control repository, workflow, evidence management, and reporting, resulting in prolonged reliance on fragmented legacy tools and limiting the ability to achieve the desired automation and transparency within the project timeline.
risks.mitigation: Engage enterprise architecture, security, and procurement teams early; define and agree tooling decision criteria; prepare required documentation in advance; and schedule governance checkpoints to obtain timely approvals for Protecht/ADO and related integrations.

risks.title: Integration dependencies between CARI, RAS, and CoCounsel may delay dual-region readiness
risks.description: Dual-region setups for CARI and RAS introduce integration dependencies that require coordinated efforts between CARI, RAS, and CoCounsel once dual-region infrastructure is in place. The CARI Commercial – Dual Region and RAS Dual Region reports note that, after dual-region setup, coordinated work will be needed to implement regional stickiness and new endpoints on the CoCounsel side.
risks.impact_description: If integration dependencies are not coordinated and executed in a timely way after dual-region setup, the end-to-end dual-region capability—including regional stickiness, CoCounsel endpoint changes, and failover behavior—may not be fully operational by the target dates. This would limit resilience and could delay failover testing and Port Authority readiness that rely on a functioning dual-region architecture.

mitigation_plan_owner.name: CARI and RAS Dual Region leads, with CoCounsel platform lead

risks.mitigation: Plan and schedule joint architecture and implementation sessions between CARI, RAS, and CoCounsel teams to finalize integration patterns (including regional stickiness via Cobalt Website API and new CoCounsel endpoints). Track these integration tasks as follow-on work immediately after dual-region infrastructure setup in CARI and RAS, and ensure they are completed before scale and failover testing milestones targeted for June 30, 2026.

assumptions.title: Central Product Catalog (CPC) will be retired by Q4 2026
assumptions.description: Planning assumes that CPC will be fully sunset by Q4 2026, so the program is waiting for application retirement rather than fully onboarding CPC to SailPoint.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The application owner indicated that CPC is expected to sunset with an estimated timeline of Q4 2026, making long-term SailPoint onboarding potentially unnecessary.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The current roadmap from the CPC team targets retirement in Q4 2026. However, application retirement schedules often slip due to dependencies and business priorities, so this date is indicative rather than contractually fixed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If CPC retirement is delayed or cancelled, initiate SailPoint onboarding planning for CPC, including scoping, design, and scheduling, so that SOX access controls can be standardized without waiting for decommissioning.
assumptions.validation_method: Review CPC decommissioning plan and confirm actual retirement date with application owner and portfolio governance.

assumptions.title: Product managers and business owners will participate in scope validation and use-case review
assumptions.description: The program assumes that product managers and business owners will actively participate in validating HIPAA scope and reviewing use cases where PHI may be processed.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Accurate identification of in-scope products and PHI use cases requires detailed knowledge held by product managers and business owners, and the program is designed around their engagement.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The corporate culture and governance model generally require product and business owner involvement in compliance projects; however, competing priorities could limit their availability, so this assumption is reasonable but not guaranteed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If engagement is lower than expected, escalate to segment and functional leadership, leverage SteerCo authority to mandate participation, and consider dedicating central resources or business analysts to perform additional discovery in under-engaged areas.
assumptions.validation_method: Track participation of product managers and business owners in scope workshops, assessments, and reviews; confirm that each product with potential PHI use cases has documented input from its owner.

validation_owner.name: Program Manager for HIPAA Compliance Program

assumptions.title: Privacy Office and Risk & Compliance will continue to provide centralized guidance
assumptions.description: The project assumes that existing support functions, specifically the Privacy Office and Risk & Compliance, will continue to provide centralized guidance for HIPAA compliance activities.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The future-state HIPAA compliance framework and oversight model rely on these functions to define controls, policies, and monitoring, and they are already acting as central guidance providers.
assumptions.validity_explanation: These functions are integral to enterprise risk and privacy governance and are already leading aspects of the HIPAA program, making it highly likely they will continue to provide guidance throughout the project.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If centralized guidance capacity is reduced, appoint interim leaders or expand responsibilities of existing officers (e.g., interim HIPAA Compliance Officer) and consider external advisory support to maintain momentum.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm that Privacy Office and Risk & Compliance maintain dedicated roles for HIPAA and continue participating in SteerCo, program design, and assessments.

assumptions.title: Leadership sponsorship from the Chief Operating & Technology Officer and Chief Legal Officer will remain in place
assumptions.description: The project assumes that the Chief Operating & Technology Officer and Chief Legal Officer will continue to sponsor the HIPAA Controls Enhancement Program.

owner.name: Chief Operating & Technology Officer and Chief Legal Officer

assumptions.rationale_basis: Executive sponsorship is critical to secure funding, resources, and cross-functional participation for a multi-year HIPAA program.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While executive sponsorship is currently strong, leadership priorities can shift over a multi-year period, so continued sponsorship is likely but not guaranteed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If sponsorship weakens, seek formal endorsement from broader executive leadership (e.g., RC, O&T, Legal leadership), present risk and compliance implications, and adjust program scope to focus on highest-risk areas while attempting to regain executive support.
assumptions.validation_method: Review SteerCo membership and confirm ongoing participation and approvals from the sponsoring executives; monitor whether their directives continue to support the program.

assumptions.title: Contractual obligations imposing HIPAA-like requirements can be identified and included in scope
assumptions.description: The project assumes that contractual obligations (BAAs/BASAs or BAA-like clauses) that impose HIPAA or HIPAA-like requirements on products not directly regulated will be identifiable and can be incorporated into scope assessments.
assumptions.rationale_basis: To ensure comprehensive coverage, the program must account for contractual obligations beyond strictly regulated HIPAA products, and this requires being able to identify such obligations in contracts.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Initial contract searches have begun and data dumps are being produced, indicating feasibility; however, contract complexity and legacy agreements may make it difficult to ensure 100% coverage.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If comprehensive identification proves difficult, prioritize high-risk segments (e.g., healthcare, insurance, GLLF) and implement forward-looking controls such as standardized BAA templates and contract intake processes to better capture future obligations.
assumptions.validation_method: Complete contract searches for BAAs/BASAs and BAA-like clauses, validate findings against proposed in-scope products, and confirm with legal and commercial teams that the coverage is comprehensive.

assumptions.title: Funding and staffing will be sufficient to execute assessments and initial control enhancements
assumptions.description: The program assumes that funding and staffing levels will be adequate to complete HIPAA assessments, gap analyses, and initial control enhancement roadmaps across in-scope products and services.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The scope of assessments and remediation (including external advisory support) requires material investment and dedicated resources over multiple years.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Some funding and staffing have already been secured, but future phases and remediation costs may require additional approvals, creating some uncertainty.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If funding or staffing constraints arise, re-prioritize assessments and remediation to focus on highest-risk products and obligations, leverage external advisors selectively, and seek incremental funding with clear justification based on risk reduction and contractual requirements.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor budget approvals, actual spend, and staffing assignments against the planned assessment and remediation roadmap.

assumptions.title: Steering Committee (SteerCo) and program governance will be established and effective
assumptions.description: The program assumes that a SteerCo with representation from key functions (Commercial Excellence, GCO, O&T, Product, Finance, etc.) will be formed and will effectively drive accountability and decision-making.

owner.name: HIPAA Program Sponsor and Program Manager

assumptions.rationale_basis: The complexity and cross-functional nature of HIPAA compliance requires a governance body to prioritize work, resolve trade-offs, and oversee risk decisions.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Initial steps toward governance (identifying membership and scheduling kickoff) are underway, but effectiveness will depend on ongoing engagement and clarity of mandate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If SteerCo participation or effectiveness is weak, refine the charter, seek stronger executive sponsorship, adjust membership, or institute smaller working groups with delegated authority for operational decisions.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm SteerCo formation, membership, charter, and regular meeting cadence; evaluate whether key decisions and escalations are being handled through this forum.

assumptions.title: Scope of in-scope products can be accurately determined based on upload capability and known PHI use cases
assumptions.description: The program assumes that focusing on products with upload capabilities and known PHI-related patterns will allow accurate determination of which products and services are in-scope for HIPAA.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Upload capability is a primary driver of whether customers can input PHI, and initial surveys have identified specific patterns (interaction with clients of customers, matter/document management, billing products).
assumptions.validity_explanation: The approach is aligned with how customers typically supply PHI (through file uploads and similar mechanisms), but edge cases or indirect data flows may still exist.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If gaps emerge during audits or data handling reviews, expand the scoping methodology to include additional criteria (e.g., integrations, logs, support channels) and revisit products initially deemed out of scope.
assumptions.validation_method: Compare scope results against contract data (BAAs/BASAs), customer use cases, and findings from data handling reviews to confirm that no significant PHI-processing products are overlooked.

validation_owner.name: R&C and Privacy in partnership with Product

assumptions.title: Planned HIPAA assessments (HighQ, SIU, Legal Tracker, Contract Express, CLEAR, CoCounsel, etc.) will be completed on current timelines
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the scheduled HIPAA assessments for key products will be completed as planned (e.g., HighQ remediation by June 30, 2026; SIU gaps mostly remediated by end of Q2 2026; Legal Tracker by year-end).
assumptions.rationale_basis: Program planning and stakeholder expectations are built around these timelines for assessments and remediation.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current progress suggests timelines are achievable, but dependencies on external advisors, internal resources, and product priorities introduce uncertainty.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If assessment timelines slip, adjust remediation priorities, communicate revised timelines to stakeholders, and consider allocating additional resources or simplifying scope for initial phases.
assumptions.validation_method: Track assessment milestones, deliverable dates, and remediation plan approvals for each product against the program schedule.

assumptions.title: Required stakeholders will be available for ICFR transformation activities
assumptions.description: Finance, operations, business, compliance, IT, and audit stakeholders will be available to support workshops, reviews, and approvals required for the ICFR transformation program.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The program relies on cross-functional expertise and decision-making; without active stakeholder participation, design and implementation cannot proceed effectively.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Stakeholder availability is typically constrained, but given Sponsor backing and the regulatory importance of ICFR, it is reasonable to assume that critical participants will prioritize involvement once schedules and expectations are clearly communicated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If key stakeholders are repeatedly unavailable, secure delegate representation, adjust schedules, escalate to leadership for prioritization, or narrow scope to areas with engaged ownership while planning a later wave for others.
assumptions.validation_method: Track actual attendance and participation in early workshops and governance meetings; escalate gaps through Sponsor and leadership if patterns of non-participation emerge.

assumptions.title: Scope decisions and design principles will be confirmed in a timely manner
assumptions.description: Key scope decisions and design principles for the ICFR operating model will be confirmed quickly enough to maintain project momentum.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The program is structured around phases and workstreams that depend on clear, agreed scope and design principles to proceed without rework.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The creation of a Control Design Authority and explicit governance expectations for Sponsor approval are intended to streamline decision-making, making it reasonable to assume that scope and design principles will be confirmed within agreed timelines.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If decisions are delayed, escalate to the Sponsor and CDA, time-box discussions, adopt provisional decisions for pilots, or de-scope contentious elements to avoid blocking the entire program.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor timing of key governance decisions versus planned milestones; review decision log for aging items and resolution timelines.

assumptions.title: Existing SOX documentation and process information will be accessible for review
assumptions.description: Existing SOX documentation, testing artifacts, and process information will be available and accessible to the project team for assessment and rationalization.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current-state assessment and gap analysis depend on access to existing control documentation and testing records across tools and repositories.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Current ICFR and SOX operations rely on these documents, indicating that they exist and are used; the main risk is access permissions and completeness, but a high level of availability is expected.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If documentation is missing or inaccessible, engage system owners to restore or grant access, prioritize recreation for high-risk areas, and adjust timelines to allow for targeted documentation reconstruction.
assumptions.validation_method: Attempt access to key repositories and sample documents early; confirm permissions and completeness with document owners and audit teams.

assumptions.title: Funding and resourcing for approved scope will be made available
assumptions.description: Budget and human resources needed to execute the approved ICFR transformation scope will be provided by the organization.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The project has been chartered as a strategic initiative, implying alignment to funding and resourcing plans.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Regulatory and governance importance of ICFR modernization increases the likelihood of funding approval, but competing enterprise priorities could still impact allocations, so confidence is moderate rather than absolute.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If full funding is not secured, prioritize highest risk and value workstreams, phase implementation over longer timelines, or seek additional funding through governance channels.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm allocated budget and headcount against the approved charter; review funding approvals and staffing assignments during mobilization.

assumptions.title: Sponsor and business leadership will actively support adoption and decision-making
assumptions.description: The Sponsor and business leadership will provide active support for adoption of new processes and tools and will participate in timely decision-making throughout the project.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Effective transformation requires visible leadership support to drive adoption, resolve conflicts, and prioritize ICFR work among competing initiatives.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Formal Sponsor approval and alignment with broader modernization and governance priorities indicate strong leadership interest, making ongoing support reasonably likely.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If leadership engagement declines, escalate through governance forums, highlight regulatory and risk implications, and adjust communications to better align with leadership needs and priorities.
assumptions.validation_method: Observe Sponsor and leadership participation in steering meetings, approvals, and communications; track escalations and their resolution times.

assumptions.title: Control universe can be reduced from ~751 to approximately 600 controls
assumptions.description: It is feasible to rationalize the current control universe of approximately 751 controls to a more focused set of around 600 controls without compromising ICFR effectiveness.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Preliminary analysis indicates over-scoping and overly granular or duplicative controls, suggesting rationalization opportunities.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Experience in similar programs often reveals rationalization opportunities; however, constraints from auditors or regulatory interpretations may limit the extent of reduction, so confidence is moderate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If the control universe cannot be reduced as much as planned, focus on simplifying execution, automating key controls, and improving evidence quality to reduce operational burden without significant reduction in control count.
assumptions.validation_method: Perform detailed control rationalization analysis (Track C), including mapping to risks and processes, and review proposed reductions with CDA and external auditors.

validation_owner.name: Track C Leads (Veronica G for business processes, Mark Brady for ITGC)

assumptions.title: Application scope can be reduced through materiality-led scoping
assumptions.description: The in-scope application population for ICFR can be reduced by applying materiality and risk-based scoping criteria.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current discussions and observations suggest that application scope may extend beyond what is necessary for material financial reporting risks.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Preliminary discussions indicate that some applications are conservatively included; however, external auditor alignment is required to confirm reductions, leading to moderate confidence.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If application scope cannot be materially reduced, focus on standardizing and automating controls across the existing application set and implement more efficient testing and evidence processes to offset the complexity.
assumptions.validation_method: Conduct a formal ICFR scoping and risk assessment (Track B) based on financial statement line items, materiality thresholds, and system dependencies, and validate with external auditors.

assumptions.title: Selected controls can be shifted from per-application to domain/platform or process-level design
assumptions.description: It will be possible to redesign selected controls from a per-application or per-product basis to domain, platform, or process-level controls.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Current-state controls show app-centric design that may not be necessary when risks can be managed at higher levels, reducing duplication.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The nature of many ITGCs and process controls lends itself to higher-level design, but technical and organizational constraints, as well as auditor expectations, will influence feasibility, hence moderate confidence.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If shifting controls proves infeasible in some areas, maintain necessary application-level controls while focusing on standardization and automation to limit incremental overhead.
assumptions.validation_method: Identify candidate controls during Track C rationalization, design higher-level controls, and review with CDA, process owners, and auditors to confirm acceptability.

validation_owner.name: Track C Leads (Veronica G and Mark Brady)
