issues.title: Program-level issue: Low customer engagement and agreement on CIAM migration timelines
issues.description: Customer engagement and agreement on CIAM migration timelines remains significantly below what is required to support the CIAM Migrations program schedule. In the most recent period, the SSO Onboarding Team sent 96 customer outreach emails and received only 13 responses, and overall engagement following outreach is reported at approximately 40%. Because there is no forced-migration date for many federated (SSO) migrations, progress is heavily dependent on customers responding and agreeing to proposed timelines. At current engagement levels, the program is unlikely to achieve its migration goals within the targeted timeline.
issues.impact_assessment: Low customer engagement and limited agreement on CIAM migration timelines is constraining both federated (SSO) and local user migration throughput across products (e.g., OnePass, ONESOURCE, SafeSend). The program’s overall RAG schedule status remains Red, and key OKR metrics (0.38% of total active federated connections migrated) indicate significant underperformance relative to plan. Without a material increase in customer responses and timeline commitments, the CIAM Migrations program will not achieve its 65% 2026 migration target or complete OnePass migrations on the planned schedule, driving extended parallel operation of legacy IDPs and delaying retirement of those platforms.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Dependent on customer engagement and agreed timelines for CIAM migrations; relies on Customer Account Manager participation, SSO Onboarding Team capacity, and approval of OnePass legacy IDP end-of-life communications.
issues.resolution: Implement a multi-pronged response focused on: (1) introducing stronger OnePass legacy IDP end-of-life and end-of-support communications (currently drafted and under internal review), (2) reducing the escalation timeline for involving Customer Account Managers from 4 weeks to 2 weeks, and (3) accelerating the volume and timing of customer outreach communications, including bringing forward communications to more customers. Program leadership will also monitor the ramp of the expanded SSO Onboarding Team through May and consider re-baselining timelines if federated migration volumes do not recover the Q1 shortfall.

issues.title: Program-level issue: Limited and unreliable user metrics from some legacy IDPs complicate CIAM progress tracking
issues.description: Some legacy IDPs (e.g., Checkpoint and similar platforms) have historically provided limited or unreliable data on key metrics, including the number of users being migrated and the number of users per federated customer IDP. Obtaining this information, even upon request, may present challenges, and tracking it on an ongoing basis is likely to be complex and resource-intensive.
issues.impact_assessment: Inconsistent or unreliable user metrics from certain legacy IDPs reduce the CIAM Migrations program’s ability to accurately measure migration progress by platform, reconcile user counts against OKR targets, and plan federated migration timelines. This introduces uncertainty into executive reporting and may mask emerging delivery risks if user volumes are materially higher than currently visible. It also increases manual effort required from product and analytics teams to assemble and validate data across platforms.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Affects migration progress reporting for the SSO Migration (proj-107) and overall CIAM Migrations OKRs; dependent on legacy IDP platform teams’ ability to supply or improve user metrics.
issues.resolution: Leverage platform and product teams to obtain the best-available metrics from legacy IDPs, prioritize data improvements for high-volume platforms, and clearly document any known gaps or assumptions in program-level reporting. Where precise user counts cannot be obtained, use conservative estimates and focus on tracking the number of federated connections migrated as a proxy while planning targeted data remediation for critical systems.

issues.title: Low Customer Response Rate to SSO Migration Outreach
issues.description:
Customer response to the SSO migration outreach remains significantly below the level required to support the planned migration from the legacy IDP to TR Account (CIAM). The project team is sending migration communications in waves to customers across approximately 5,500 SSO connections, requesting their engagement and action to migrate.

To date, response rates remain below 30%. Most recently, in last week's outreach wave, 96 customer emails were sent and only 13 responses were received, representing a response rate of approximately 13.5%.
issues.impact_assessment: If the response rate does not improve, the project may not be able to migrate 65% of SSO connections by Dec 30, 2026. This could result in schedule slippage, increased operational risk, and a need for stronger escalation or alternative migration enforcement mechanisms.
issues.resolution:
To address the low customer response rate, the project team is implementing several actions to increase customer engagement and create a stronger escalation path:

Update customer communication templates:
Revise the migration email template to include a clear statement regarding the planned end-of-life support for the legacy IDPs, reinforcing the urgency for customers to migrate to TR Account (CIAM).

Increase data validation capacity:
Add additional resources to support customer data validation activities, enabling the team to identify and tag more customers as ready for migration outreach.

Strengthen escalation process:
Modify the migration follow-up process so that if no customer response is received within 15 days of the initial email, the issue will be escalated to the relevant Account Specialist or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for direct customer follow-up.

These actions are expected to improve customer response rates, increase the number of customers actively engaged in the migration process, and reduce the risk of delays to the overall SSO migration timeline.

issues.title: Difficulty Identifying Account Specialist / CSM Ownership for Customer Accounts
issues.description:
The project team is facing significant challenges identifying the appropriate Account Specialist (ASM) or Customer Success Manager (CSM) for each customer account requiring SSO migration follow-up and escalation.

The required account ownership information is spread across multiple systems and is not aggregated or centralized. Many of these systems support only specific customer segments, such as Corporates, Legal, and Tax, or sometimes only a single product area, such as Legal Tracker. As a result, the team is unable to easily determine the correct ASM or CSM contact for each account.

This has created a highly manual and time-consuming process, requiring the team to review accounts one by one and coordinate with multiple teams and data analysis resources to locate the correct account owner.
issues.impact_assessment:
The lack of centralized ASM/CSM ownership data is slowing down the escalation process for non-responsive customers and may delay customer engagement, migration scheduling, and overall execution of the SSO migration from the legacy IDP to TR Account (CIAM).

It also increases the operational burden on the project team and supporting teams, creating inefficiencies and risk of inconsistent or delayed follow-up.
issues.resolution:
To address this issue, the project team recommends the following actions:

Engage data owners and business segment teams:
Partner with representatives from Corporates, Legal, Tax, and product-specific teams to identify the authoritative sources for ASM/CSM ownership data.

Create a consolidated account ownership tracker:
Build a centralized working file or dashboard that aggregates ASM/CSM information from available systems and maps each customer account to the appropriate owner.

Assign data analysis support:
Secure dedicated support from data analysis experts to help extract, reconcile, and validate account ownership data across the different systems.

Define a repeatable lookup process:
Establish a standard process for identifying ASM/CSM ownership for each account, including clear escalation paths when ownership is missing, outdated, or conflicting.

Prioritize high-risk / non-responsive customers:
Focus initial ownership mapping efforts on customers who have not responded to migration communications or who are part of upcoming migration waves.

Identify long-term data governance needs:
Escalate the lack of centralized account ownership data as a broader operational gap and recommend a long-term solution for maintaining a single, reliable source of account ownership information.

decisions.title: Adopt multi-pronged strategy to improve CIAM migration outreach effectiveness
decisions.description: Leadership agreed that the CIAM migration program will simultaneously pursue four key strategies to improve customer engagement and migration progress: (1) send outreach emails to more customers (increasing volume), (2) follow up sooner and more frequently with non-responsive customers, (3) strengthen the language and tone of communications, including clearer legacy IDP end-of-life messaging to create urgency, and (4) re-segment and re-sequence migration priorities across products and customer segments to compensate for early slowness and adjust for low response rates.
decisions.rationale: Executive leadership has been concerned that reported metrics show poor progress and that initial plans were overly optimistic about customer response rates. A coordinated, multi-pronged approach is needed to increase engagement, accelerate migrations, and credibly demonstrate a 'path to green' while managing expectations about the 65% target and OnePass completion.
decisions.options_considered: Continue current outreach pace and messaging without change; focus solely on increasing email volume; focus solely on escalation through CSMs; defer changes until more data is available.

decisions.title: Conduct two-stage reevaluation of 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion
decisions.description: The team will conduct a two-stage reevaluation of the 65% CIAM migration target and OnePass completion goal. First, a 1–2 week exercise (by late May 2026) will produce realistic projections based on current response data, segment-by-segment analysis, and reprioritization of products (including potential compensation from Safesend, OneSource and other products if large/complex OnePass customers lag). Second, in mid-July 2026, the team will reevaluate the plan again using data from the new feature that allows customers to migrate without all products moving at once, assessing whether overall completion can reach approximately 90–95% of the original target.
decisions.rationale: Progress to date and very low response rates indicate the original plan may not be realistic, especially for large and complex OnePass customers. Leadership needs a more evidence-based assessment of whether the 65% target is achievable and what trade-offs (e.g., compensating with other products) are required, while also considering new feature capabilities that may accelerate legal product migrations later in the year.
decisions.options_considered: Maintain the 65% and full OnePass completion goals without reevaluation; immediately reduce targets based on early pessimism; delay any reconsideration until much later in 2026.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

The Mergers, Acquisitions & Divestitures (MAD) program governs technology integration and separation for acquired and divested businesses so that workloads, data, and support models move cleanly onto Thomson Reuters platforms or to buyers, protecting revenue and reducing operational and cyber risk. The program covers 11 active projects spanning cloud integration, divestiture TSAs, and security integration workstreams.

To date, 10 of 11 active projects report Green status, with one Amber project (SafeSend One) due to core platform dependencies. Key cloud integrations for SafeSend, Tic Tie Calculate, Signature Standalone, and Project Ochre Phase 2 migrations are In Progress with no reported schedule variance against their current target dates of 29 Jun 2026, 30 Jun 2026, and 30 Sep 2026.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by unresolved MDM integration dependencies in SafeSend One that threaten the 11 Jun 2026 Lead to Cash UAT and 13 Jul 2026 CS&S go-live.

## Path to Green

The path to Green is to fast-track SafeSend One MDM integration by locking the architecture, completing integration into lower environments ahead of the 11 Jun 2026 Lead to Cash UAT, and using a dedicated cross-team squad to resolve open data and Boomi/MDS dependencies. In parallel, the program will gate the 20 Jun 2026 tech release and 13 Jul 2026 CS&S go-live on explicit readiness checks across MDM, CIAM migration, and chat/Flash sequencing, escalating any capacity constraints early.

## Milestones

-   Deliver SafeSend One Lead to Cash UAT sign-off and SSOne Market/Sales/Support/SSP tech release by 11 Jun 2026 and 20 Jun 2026 respectively.
    
-   Complete SafeSend production migration and the final SafeSend Cloud Integration for non-production and production environments by 30 Jun 2026.
    
-   Complete Project Ochre Cloud Migration Phase 2 from TR AWS to NewCo cloud, including overall migration and cutover, by 29 Jun 2026.
    
-   Achieve Tic Tie Calculate and Signature Standalone final Azure production integrations by 30 Sep 2026.

risks.title: Incomplete or incorrect Noetica application access lists
risks.description: Application lists collected for Noetica users may be incomplete or inaccurate if they are captured as infrastructure inventories rather than user access requirements and job-profile-based usage.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, the project may base reimage and access configuration on incomplete or incorrect application lists, leading to missed critical tools for specific roles, repeated rework to fix access issues, and extended disruption for Noetica teams during the integration.
risks.mitigation: 1) Obtain user access requirement lists rather than generic infrastructure inventories. 2) Collect application usage by job profile (e.g., product, engineering, developer) instead of only per individual, to ensure a complete view of critical tools per role.

risks.title: Disaster recovery replication may conflict with Noetica customer contractual and data-isolation commitments
risks.description: Implementing a DR strategy that replicates private customer data across regions or into shared locations may conflict with Noeticas existing contractual commitments and data-isolation guarantees (e.g., one AWS account per customer for isolation). While the current proposal is to keep replication within each customers AWS account, there is still uncertainty about how this aligns with what has been agreed with customers and documented in contracts.
risks.impact_description: If the chosen DR replication approach violates contractual terms or perceived isolation guarantees, customers may object to the architecture, require contractual changes, or raise legal/compliance concerns. This could delay DR implementation, force costly redesigns, damage customer trust, and expose Thomson Reuters/Noetica to legal or regulatory scrutiny. Conversely, if DR is delayed or watered down to avoid these concerns, resilience gaps may persist and increase operational risk.
risks.mitigation: 1) Zachery to document the DR architecture explicitly stating that replication remains within each customers AWS account but across regions (no centralized shared account), highlighting how isolation boundaries are preserved. 2) Circulate this document to Ash and Donny, and route to Tom and Sabrina for legal/contractual and customer-facing review. 3) Tom and Sabrina to confirm whether the proposed architecture is compatible with existing contracts and customer expectations and identify any customers needing explicit communication or approval. 4) If any contractual gaps are found, adjust DR architecture or update contractual language as appropriate before implementation. 5) Ensure any customer communication clearly explains that data remains in their account, with encryption and key management controls maintained, and that replication is solely to enhance resilience.
risks.source_file_name: Noetica - Cold Standby DR Strategy Discussion – Requirement & Path Forward.docx

risks.title: Data loss during device reimage
risks.description: There is a risk of data loss during reimage activities if users store important data locally on their machines and backup status is unclear prior to reimage.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, locally stored user data (such as source code, configuration files, documents, or analysis outputs) may be permanently lost during reimage, impacting development, operations, and compliance, and potentially delaying integration work while data is recreated or recovered.
risks.mitigation: Ensure that all user data is backed up prior to reimage so that any necessary files can be restored if they are wiped during device rebuilding.

risks.title: Dependency on Noetica approval for AWS account transfer and billing integration
risks.description: AWS account transfer and billing integration into TR cannot proceed without explicit acknowledgment and approval from Noetica, since TR is not permitted to move accounts unilaterally.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs (i.e., Noetica approval is delayed or not obtained), AWS account transfer and billing integration into TR’s environment will be blocked, delaying cloud standardization, security control deployment, and cost management for the Noetica workloads.
risks.mitigation: 1) Engage the Noetica team early as part of the AWS account transfer workflow to secure timely acknowledgment and approval. 2) Treat Noetica’s acknowledgment as a formal, required step in the account transfer process, rather than an afterthought, ensuring it is planned and tracked explicitly.

risks.title: Delay in Qualys deployment to Noetica workstations due to packaging errors and unclear timeline
risks.description: Qualys deployment to Noetica workstations is experiencing packaging errors and there is no clear owner-provided timeline for resolution. Abir is working with the TR team (including Alex and Miguel) to fix the issues, but Ash is not directly working on them and cannot commit to dates. Leadership has requested at least a tentative delivery timeline, which is currently missing.
risks.impact_description: If this risk materializes, Qualys will not be deployed to Noetica workstations in line with the planned April 7 target, leaving workstations without standardized vulnerability scanning. This will delay visibility into endpoint vulnerabilities, extend the window of exposure for known and unknown issues, and reduce confidence when reporting progress on security control implementation to leadership.
risks.mitigation: 1) Tane and Kiran to join the existing Teams chat with Abir, Alex, and Miguel to obtain detailed status on the packaging errors. 2) Agree and document a tentative but realistic deployment timeline for workstation Qualys, explicitly communicated to leadership. 3) Track defect resolution and pilot deployment progress daily until Qualys agents are successfully pushed to workstations. 4) Escalate to Milind if access or technical issues are not resolved within the agreed window.

risks.title: Dependency on Vendor for Cloud and DNS Migration Timelines (BRS- New Co, the BRS team lacked sufficient bandwidth and specialized skillsets to perform this work internally)
risks.description: DNS hosting migration cannot be started before completing domain ownership transfer for bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, and cvmail.com.au.
risks.impact_description: If domain ownership transfer is delayed, DNS hosting migration to NewCo name servers will also be delayed. This could postpone DNS-related changes, including email and application routing, potentially affecting service availability and alignment with cloud migration timelines.
risks.mitigation: Ensure domain ownership transfers complete on schedule and prepare DNS migration plans, including record exports/imports and testing, so hosting migration can be executed quickly once ownership is transferred.

risks.title: Misaligned UAT schedules across CS&S workstreams
risks.description: Variation in User Acceptance Testing (UAT) windows across CS&S workstreams may cause scheduling conflicts if not properly aligned among key team members (Mike, Yvonne, Becky, Emily, Alex).
risks.impact_description: If UAT windows are not coordinated, key CS&S stakeholders may be double‑booked or unavailable, causing test cycles to slip, defects to be discovered late, and potentially delaying SafeSend go‑live activities that depend on CS&S readiness.
risks.mitigation:
1. Centralized UAT Window Alignment
2. Early Dependency & Conflict Identification

risks.title: Stripe delivery plan not aligned with SafeSend target delivery
risks.description: The current Stripe project plan is not aligned with the SafeSend target delivery date, with Stripe delivering at the same time SafeSend aims to deliver. This overlap is likely to evolve into an unmet dependency.
risks.impact_description: If Stripe is not ready or integrated when SafeSend needs payment processing, SafeSend could face a critical dependency gap for payments, risking launch delays or requiring unplanned workarounds and impacting customer billing and payment experiences.
risks.mitigation: SafeSend will continue to use Paymetric for payments until a migration plan to Stripe is in place and executed by the Payment Unification team.

risks.title: Semarchy migration delay potentially impacting April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT
risks.description: Semarchy migration is supposed to complete by Q1 2026. If this project stalls or ‘sits’, it could impact the April 2026 lead‑to‑cash UAT schedule due to required environment downtime.
risks.impact_description: If Semarchy migration does not complete as planned, required environment outages or incomplete data migration could prevent or delay lead‑to‑cash UAT in April 2026, which may push back defect resolution, integration testing, and overall SafeSend launch readiness.
risks.mitigation: MDM team has proposed running EPM and Semarchy in parallel so that necessary capabilities remain available while migration completes and required downtime is minimized or scheduled to reduce impact on UAT.

risks.title: Transition to new Help Center content and licenses for Help & Support
risks.description: New Help and Support content, including a new Help Center, is targeted for completion by end of Q1. Downstream teams must update their workstreams to point to the new Help Center before old Help Center licenses expire on 2026-07-01.
risks.impact_description: If downstream teams do not update their configurations, links, and workflows to the new Help Center before the old licenses expire, users may encounter broken links, inconsistent support experiences, or loss of access to help content, negatively impacting customers and product teams.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with downstream teams to ensure they update their workstreams and integrations to reference the new Help Center well before the 2026-07-01 license expiry for the old Help Center.

risks.title: Loss of key SafeSend marketing contacts and domain expertise
risks.description: Recent turnover of key SafeSend marketing contacts has reduced critical domain expertise, even though replacements have been identified.
risks.impact_description: Knowledge gaps among new marketing resources may lead to delays in marketing deliverables, misaligned or suboptimal marketing decisions, and quality issues in marketing assets that support the SafeSend launch and ongoing adoption.
risks.mitigation: monitored via SafeSend Marketing Workstream and Monthly Review cadence

risks.title: Flash migration delays tying up key CS&S resources and impacting SafeSend launch
risks.description: Completion of the Flash migration, which is required for CS&S, may be delayed. This could tie up key resources and cause a four‑week slip in SafeSend’s business launch and complicate UAT scheduling. If Flash is not delivered before mid‑July, its go‑live may be postponed to the following year.
risks.impact_description: If Flash migration slips past the planned timeframe, CS&S resources needed for SafeSend could remain focused on Flash, delaying SafeSend’s business launch by up to four weeks, impacting the planned July 2026 deployment and potentially deferring related benefits.
risks.mitigation: Close tracking of the Flash program to identify and address schedule risks early and coordinate resource allocation with SafeSend needs.

risks.title: Loss of key architect (Andy) for ECM/ECX high‑level design
risks.description: Loss of key resource Andy, the architect responsible for completing the High‑Level Design (HLD) for ECM/ECX. The current team lacks sufficient architectural capacity to finalize HLD deliverables within planned timelines.
risks.impact_description: If the HLD is delayed due to lack of architectural capacity, design sign‑off will slip, delaying the start of development and potentially affecting downstream integration, testing, and SafeSend’s overall delivery timeline.
risks.mitigation: Identify and onboard replacement or additional architectural capacity to complete the ECM/ECX HLD within the planned timeframe, and adjust plans or scope as needed to reflect available resources.

risks.title: Delay in onboarding Informatica resource for Sales workstream
risks.description: Onboarding of an Informatica resource for the Sales workstream was initially delayed and raised as a risk, as the project required Informatica expertise for scoping and integration activities.
risks.impact_description: If the Informatica resource were not onboarded, Sales workstream design and integration work relying on Informatica could have been delayed, impacting data integration, testing schedules, and overall SafeSend delivery for Sales.
risks.mitigation: Onboard the required Informatica resource and commence scoping work as soon as they join the project.

risks.title: Datadog training and integration may not be completed before production migration
risks.description: Datadog training is a prerequisite for setting up monitoring integrations for the new TR Azure subscriptions. Notes indicate that key tasks for Datadog IaC, RUM, and APM monitoring cannot be fully defined or executed until SafeSend and TR staff complete training and understand TR Datadog standards. If training and integration are delayed, monitoring for infrastructure and applications in the new TR Azure tenant may not be ready before or during production migration.
risks.impact_description: If Datadog training and integration are not completed before production migration, the project may go live without fully functional observability. This could lead to limited visibility into application and infrastructure health, slower incident detection, difficulty in troubleshooting migration issues, and increased risk of prolonged outages or performance degradation in production. Lack of compliance with TR monitoring standards could also trigger rework or governance escalations.
risks.mitigation: Arrange and complete Datadog training sessions for SafeSend and TR DevOps staff; use the documented TR Datadog integration procedures to configure log forwarding from Azure Log Analytics to Datadog and to enable RUM, APM, and infrastructure monitoring. Run a proof-of-concept to push application insights and metrics (including event logs) to Datadog in non-production, refine dashboards and alerts, and then apply the same configurations in production before the June 2026 production migration.

risks.title: Delay in finalizing product pricing impacting EPM data migration
risks.description: Product pricing for SafeSend needs to be finalized as soon as possible to support Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) data migration activities.
risks.impact_description: If product pricing is not finalized in time, EPM data migration and related configuration may be delayed, which can block downstream testing, reporting readiness, and the overall lead‑to‑cash schedule for the SafeSend launch.
risks.mitigation: Ameera is following up with Saima and Scott to drive timely product pricing decisions and ensure inputs are available for EPM data migration.

risks.title: TSA amendment approval and timelines realignment
risks.description: Cloud Migration Phase 2 for the Ochre divestiture (TR AWS to NewCo cloud for BRS, CV Mail, and RAMS) may extend beyond the May 31 TSA deadline if Phase 1 cloud migration or NewCo cloud/DNS readiness is delayed.
risks.impact_description: If Phase 2 cloud migration is not completed by May 31, 2026, the project may miss the TSA end-date for technology separation. This would impact the ability to fully transition BRS, CV Mail, and RAMS to NewCo infrastructure, potentially requiring an extension of the TSA, additional infrastructure and support costs for Thomson Reuters, and a delay in decommissioning TR cloud resources and revoking access for divested employees.
risks.mitigation: 1) Danny to confirm the NewCo infrastructure setup timelines and dependent timelines for Cloud Migration Phase 2. 2) Explore options to create cloud services in the new company before regular use, if cost is lower than extending the TSA. 3) Ensure CICD pipelines are created before cloud services are built; involve DevOps (Chandresh Sutthar and Vijay Reddy) to support pipeline setup and address technical challenges, and estimate pipeline creation timelines.

risks.title: Rework of Jira to ADO migration due to delta changes
risks.description: There is a risk that changes made in Jira between the initial migration window and the final cutover date will create a delta, requiring rework of the Jira-to-Azure DevOps (ADO) migration.
risks.impact_description: If Jira issues continue to be created or updated after the initial migration to ADO, the team may need to perform additional migration cycles or manual reconciliation. This could cause extra effort, duplicated work, potential data inconsistencies between Jira and ADO, and schedule slippage for completing the Jira to ADO migration.
risks.mitigation: Push the Time Base team to stop using Jira for new work items and instead log all new items directly in ADO, enabling Jira to be set to read-only and avoiding ongoing delta changes that would require rework.

risks.title: Snyk scanning process and challenges may delay SafeSend One, Signature Standalone, and TTC standalone timelines
risks.description: Unresolved Snyk scanning issues in the TTC/SafeSend codebase may prevent completion of required security scans in time, creating delays for three critical projects: SafeSend One, Signature Standalone (SIGSA), and TTC Standalone cloud integrations.
risks.impact_description: If Snyk scanning issues are not resolved, required security scanning may remain incomplete, delaying sign‑off and promotion of builds for SafeSend One, SIGSA, and TTC Standalone. This would push back completion of SIGSA and TTC non‑production cloud integrations in Q1 2026 and delay subsequent production cloud integration planning, potentially impacting SafeSend One production in Q2 and SIGSA/TTC production environments in Q3.
risks.mitigation: ISRM-Platforms-Security-Dev (Efstathios) and Sachin are actively investigating and addressing the Snyk scanning issues. If the problem persists into early the following week, the project team and management will consider approving a manual intervention process (estimated 1–2 days of effort) to bypass the automated Snyk pipeline blockers so that SIGSA 3x environments cloud integration can proceed and production cloud integration planning can start on time.

risks.title: Cutover and rollback planning for production migration may be incomplete before migration window
risks.description: The RunBook_Prod sheet shows that cutover and rollback planning tasks (including detailed cutover steps and rollback actions for application, database, storage, and domain changes) are marked as 'Not yet Started'. These activities are essential to safely execute the production migration and to revert changes if issues occur.
risks.impact_description: If cutover and rollback plans are not fully defined, reviewed, and tested before the production migration window, the team may be forced to improvise during cutover. This can lead to extended downtime, confusion during incident handling, inability to cleanly revert to the pre-migration state, potential data corruption or data loss, and reputational risk if customer-facing systems remain unavailable or unstable.
risks.mitigation: Finalize a detailed cutover plan covering all steps for storage, SQL, Cosmos DB, APIM, Key Vault, and application deployment, including timings and responsibilities. Define and document a rollback plan covering re-deploying the Q1 release via Azure DevOps, reverting Key Vault secrets, undoing storage and database changes, and reversing domain changes via GoDaddy. Conduct at least one rehearsal of critical steps in a non-production environment to validate feasibility and timing, and ensure all stakeholders understand their roles during cutover.

risks.title: Production storage and table migrations may fail or overrun due to untested migration service setup
risks.description: Production storage blob and table migrations depend on deploying a migration service and VM/AKS-based tooling (AzCopy, scripts, jobs) during April 17–27, 2026. The RunBook_Prod notes that the service for storage migration needs to be deployed and that Ravindra must update the storage migration plan with prerequisites and tasks. If these prerequisites are not ready or adequately tested, the production storage migrations may fail or take longer than the planned window.
risks.impact_description: If the migration service, VM/AKS infrastructure, and scripts for storage and table migration are not properly set up and tested, data transfers may fail, stall, or run longer than expected. This can result in incomplete or inconsistent storage content in TR Azure, requirement for multiple re-runs, extended maintenance windows, potential data loss, and unavailability of application features that rely on blob or table storage during or after migration.
risks.mitigation: Implement and validate the full storage migration toolchain (VM, AKS, AzCopy-based scripts, configuration generation, failed-job handling) in non-production environments (Dev, QA, STG), leveraging the detailed POC steps already executed there. Update the production storage migration plan with all prerequisites and tasks, including change feed configuration, SAS-based transfers, delta container handling, and cleanup procedures. Schedule sufficient buffer in the production window, and pre-run trial migrations on a sample of production containers to validate performance and error handling before the full migration.

risks.title: Key Vault secret migration and validation may delay production deployment readiness
risks.description: In the RunBook_Prod, key vault secret migration tasks (creating target Key Vault, bulk secret migration, ATUM deployment, and secret validation) are all marked as 'Not yet Started'. Dev notes from earlier environments indicate that application deployment depends on Key Vault being updated and operational. If key vault tasks slip, production deployment readiness may be delayed.
risks.impact_description: If Key Vaults are not created and populated with correct secrets before production deployment, applications may fail to start or function correctly due to missing or incorrect configuration secrets (e.g., connection strings, API keys). This could block production cutover, require emergency changes during the migration window, or lead to post-migration incidents and rollbacks.
risks.mitigation: Create the target production Key Vaults and configure access as per TR standards, then use bulk migration tools or scripts (and ATUM) to populate secrets. Validate secret correctness with EMs and application owners before the migration window by running application readiness checks in a pre-production setup. Incorporate Key Vault readiness checks into the production runbook and treat them as mandatory gates before proceeding with application deployment.

risks.title: Incomplete CI/CD migration from Azure DevOps to GitHub Actions could impact non-production DevOps migration timeline
risks.description: The DevOps Migration Phase (Non-Prod) indicates that ADO to GitHub migration is in progress with several outstanding tasks such as bulk creation of CI/CD pipelines as GitHub Actions workflows, validation of builds and artifacts, and full end-to-end dry runs. Notes highlight constraints around JFrog version updates and limitations with variable group mapping, requiring conversion of variable groups into YAML files.
risks.impact_description: If the migration of CI/CD pipelines from Azure DevOps to GitHub Actions is not completed and validated before the non-production DevOps migration deadline (Q4 2025 / availability to developers in early February 2026), developers may be forced to continue using legacy pipelines or experience disruptions in build and deployment workflows. This can slow feature delivery, complicate production migration readiness, and increase operational overhead by maintaining dual tooling.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the design and implementation of GitHub Actions workflows for all CI and CD pipelines, including addressing JFrog version alignment and converting ADO variable groups to YAML-based configuration. Run all CI pipelines to generate artifacts and validate pushes to JFrog, verify test coverage, and perform end-to-end dry runs across CI, CD, CT, and CO stages. Address any issues in mapping test cases and service connections, and ensure developers are onboarded and trained on the new workflows before the planned non-prod DevOps migration date.

risks.title: Wildcard certificate and domain management constraints may impact SSL and customer subdomain strategy
risks.description: The QA and Dev runbooks note ongoing POCs for SSL certificates via Venafi and for adapting existing domains, as well as discussion around wildcard certificates for customer-specific subdomains (thousands of potential subdomains). TR standards typically do not accept wildcard certificates, requiring exceptions or design changes. Although one historical RAID entry indicates the team decided not to proceed with wildcard certificates, the broader production SSL and domain strategy (including potential migration from GoDaddy to AWS Route 53) still requires alignment and impact analysis.
risks.impact_description: If SSL and domain strategies (including handling of customer-specific subdomains) are not fully aligned with TR standards and implemented before production, the team may face blockers in obtaining required certificates, delays in domain configuration, or security policy exceptions. This may delay production cutover, force suboptimal workarounds, or require post-migration rework of customer access patterns and portal design.
risks.mitigation: Complete the Venafi-based certificate POCs, finalize the decision to avoid wildcard certificates for customer portals, and document the new design approach for handling customer access without wildcard certs. Coordinate with TR PKI, security, and domain management teams to confirm migration plans from GoDaddy to AWS Route 53 where applicable, and ensure required certificates and DNS records are provisioned and tested in non-prod before production cutover.

risks.title: Snyk scanning process and challenges impacting SafeSend One, Signature Standalone, and TTC Standalone timelines
risks.description: Unresolved issues in the Snyk scanning process may continue to block or delay security scans for SafeSend One, Signature Standalone (SIGSA), and TTC Standalone codebases. If the scanning problems persist, the project teams may be unable to complete required security checks in time to meet non-production and production cloud integration timelines.
risks.impact_description: If the Snyk scanning issue is not resolved promptly, security scans for three critical projects (SafeSend One, Signature Standalone, and TTC Standalone) may not be completed on time. This would delay sign-offs and cloud integration activities for SIGSA 3x environments, push back the start of production cloud integration planning, and jeopardize the overall delivery timelines for these products.
risks.mitigation: ISRM-Platforms-Security-Dev (Efstathios) and Sachin are working together to resolve the Snyk scanning issue. If the issue is still not resolved into early the following week (after Feb 25), the project team and management will consider approving and proceeding with a manual intervention process to complete the required checks for SIGSA 3x environments cloud integration. This manual process is expected to take 1–2 days and would allow production cloud integration planning to begin on time.

risks.title: Resource Availability – Time Base
risks.description: Due to ongoing Business-as-Usual (BAU) tasks and a high operational workload, responses to current customer requests. There is a risk of delays in milestones and deliverables due to limited capacity.
risks.impact_description:
Project tasks might be deprioritized to accommodate BAU commitments.
There is a risk of delays in milestones and deliverables because of limited bandwidth.
Delivery timelines could be affected by dependencies on time-based resources.
risks.mitigation: Track and flag delays early in weekly status call.

risks.title: Loss of access to Noetica applications after desktop reimage
risks.description: After Thomson Reuters-managed reimage of Noetica users’ devices, users may lose access to required Noetica applications if application inventories and access paths are not fully understood before reimage.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, Noetica staff will be unable to access key applications after their devices are reimaged to TR standards, causing immediate disruption to engineering and product work, potential delays to integration activities, and loss of productivity for affected teams.
risks.mitigation: 1) Collect detailed application lists per user and understand how each application is accessed (VPN, SaaS, internal). 2) Validate all application access requirements before starting any device reimage. 3) Coordinate with the Noetica Security team to confirm access mechanisms so that configurations can be preserved or replicated on TR-managed devices.

risks.title: VPN dependency blocking application access after integration
risks.description: Some Noetica application access may depend on OpenVPN or other VPN paths that are not aligned with TR’s ZPA-based remote access, which could block access once devices are reimaged or network paths change.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, users whose application access depends on OpenVPN or specific VPN routes may lose access when moved to ZPA or TR network standards, causing outages for impacted applications and requiring urgent reconfiguration or coexistence solutions.
risks.mitigation: 1) Determine whether each application’s access path goes through OpenVPN or direct internet. 2) Allow temporary coexistence of OpenVPN and ZPA where necessary to avoid disruption during the transition.

risks.title: CS&S team capacity constraints due to multiple parallel projects
risks.description: Multiple parallel projects affecting the Customer Service & Support (CS&S) area, including Doctor Tax and SurePrep, may stretch the CS&S team’s resources too thin to effectively support SafeSend work.
risks.impact_description: If CS&S resources are over-allocated, SafeSend-related analysis, design, testing, and deployment activities could be delayed or under‑resourced, leading to schedule slippage, reduced quality of customer support capabilities, and potential impact on the July 2026 launch objectives.
risks.mitigation:
1. Prioritize CS&S Support for SafeSend Critical Path
2. Capacity Planning & Resource Phasing

risks.title: Security policy constraints on TR-managed devices blocking Noetica applications

risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, TR-managed security controls will prevent Noetica applications from functioning correctly, leading to application outages, increased support overhead, and delays while exception rules and policies are configured.
risks.mitigation: 1) Configure backend security and access policies to explicitly allow Noetica application traffic. 2) Engage Matt Pyane to support ZPA configuration and policy enablement for Noetica applications. 3) Use formal security processes to request and approve external access exceptions where required.

risks.title: MDM Integration Delays Impacting SafeSend One Timeline
risks.description: Ongoing Master Data Management (MDM) integration issues are causing delays in data synchronization required for SafeSend One. Dependencies on MDM readiness for customer, product, and entitlement data remain unresolved, creating a risk to planned milestones and downstream integrations.
risks.impact_description: Continued MDM integration issues may delay SafeSend One system integration testing and go‑live readiness due to incomplete or unreliable master data feeds. Prolonged delays could impact dependent integrations, compress downstream testing timelines, and increase the risk of schedule slippage and rework close to go‑live.

Engaged PE as well for a temporary work around as file drop from SafeSend is not straight forward

risks.title: Complexity and architectural blockers in transferring Noetica AWS accounts into TR AWS organization
risks.description: Transferring Noetica AWS accounts into the Thomson Reuters (TR) AWS organization requires decomposing AWS Control Tower and Identity Center usage at the Noetica org root, recreating OUs, and changing the account provisioning model. The Noetica team highlighted multiple technical concerns: heavy dependency on Control Tower and Identity Center, IAM role and org ID dependencies, CloudFront/WAF behavior, GPU capacity reservations, logging aggregation, and the lack of an easy rollback path if issues occur. Identity Center was called out as a major blocker because it must run at the org root, which conflicts with TR’s current FedRAMP constraints. If these complexities are underestimated or not fully mitigated, the org transfer project may cause subtle production breakages or stall indefinitely.
risks.impact_description: If the technical complexity and architectural blockers around Control Tower and Identity Center are not fully addressed, the Noetica AWS org transfer could (a) introduce subtle failures in IAM roles, org ID–dependent automation, CloudFront/WAF behavior, and GPU capacity reservations, leading to production incidents; (b) result in extended outages or degraded performance for Noetica customers due to misconfigured access or infrastructure; (c) leave the migration half-completed with no straightforward rollback, increasing operational risk and support burden; or (d) cause the entire transfer initiative to stall, delaying cost savings, security integration, and alignment with TR standards.

raised_by.name: John Willis / Donny Yung / Ash Alam (Noetica infrastructure and security leaders)

risk_owner.name: Bleninger, Zachery (TR Technology, Cloud Solutions Architect)

mitigation_plan_owner.name: Bleninger, Zachery (TR Technology, Cloud Solutions Architect)

risks.mitigation: 1) Zach Bleninger to document all outstanding technical risks and dependencies for the AWS org transfer, including Control Tower decommissioning, Identity Center constraints, IAM/org ID dependencies, CloudFront/WAF configuration, GPU capacity reservations, CI/CD impacts, quotas, and logging aggregation. 2) Schedule and conduct a deep-dive SME working session focused on these technical workstreams (Identity, Control Tower decomp, CI/CD, WAF, quotas) with TR Platform Engineering and Noetica infra/security leads. 3) Design a phased migration approach that includes non-production pilots, explicit success criteria, and a tested rollback plan before any production account transfer. 4) Evaluate alternatives or mitigations for Identity Center’s org-root requirement within TR’s FedRAMP constraints (e.g., replacement patterns, scoped access models). 5) Only commit to production cutover dates after SMEs agree that critical blockers are addressed and pilot results are acceptable.

risks.title: Board-level pressure to realise AWS cost savings may drive an overly aggressive Noetica AWS org transfer timeline
risks.description: TR leadership and the board are exerting pressure to realise AWS cost savings (~26% forecast) by moving Noetica accounts into the TR AWS organization quickly. While this transfer enables enterprise discounts and premium support, the Noetica team and product leadership emphasised the need to avoid derailing the product roadmap and to manage significant technical risks around Control Tower/Identity Center, security, and contracts. There is a risk that schedule pressure leads to an aggressive migration timeline that does not allow for adequate design, testing, and risk mitigation.
risks.impact_description: If board-level cost-savings pressure forces an accelerated AWS org transfer without sufficient technical due diligence and alignment with the Noetica roadmap, the project could (a) disrupt Noetica’s product development and customer commitments due to resource diversion to migration; (b) increase the likelihood of outages or degraded service quality caused by rushed identity, networking, or infrastructure changes; (c) damage trust between Noetica and TR technology/leadership if the migration is perceived as prioritising cost over stability; and (d) still fail to deliver expected savings if technical blockers (e.g., Identity Center, contracts) are encountered late and require rework or deferral.
risks.mitigation: 1) Use Noetica’s in-flight cost-optimisation work (already yielding ~31% MTD reduction) as an immediate lever to demonstrate savings while a careful AWS org transfer plan is developed. 2) Noetica to share a detailed cost-optimisation summary by the agreed date (end of Thursday) so leadership can see short-term savings independent of org transfer. 3) Zach Bleninger to document a balanced set of options that explicitly trade off speed, risk, and roadmap impact, including phased or partial migration scenarios. 4) Schedule a deep-dive SME session to decompose technical workstreams and produce realistic effort/timeline estimates before committing to firm dates. 5) Reconvene the full group with cost data, roadmap clarity, and a phased recommendation, and socialise this with leadership to set expectations that stability and roadmap protection are non-negotiable constraints.

risks.title: Starting pilot device reimage without full security and access alignment
risks.description: The project may begin the pilot reimage of Noetica devices before application lists, access paths, security, and ZPA configurations are fully aligned, which could reduce confidence from the Noetica Security team and cause avoidable issues.
risks.impact_description: If this risk occurs, the pilot may experience significant access and security issues, eroding Noetica Security’s confidence in the integration approach, creating rework to fix early problems, and potentially delaying broader rollout while trust is rebuilt.
risks.mitigation: 1) Delay the pilot until application lists are complete and access paths are validated. 2) Align security configuration, ZPA settings, and access controls across TR and Noetica before executing the pilot.

risks.title: Lack of implemented cold standby DR strategy for Noetica customer data
risks.description: The agreed cold standby disaster recovery (DR) strategy for Noetica—replicating customer private data from S3 buckets to a paired AWS region—may not be implemented in time (or at all), leaving Noetica workloads without a documented and tested DR option outside their current region. This is particularly relevant as Noetica integrates with other Thomson Reuters products that may have tighter SLAs and resilience expectations.
risks.impact_description: If a cold standby DR strategy is not implemented, a regional outage or data loss event in the primary AWS region could result in prolonged or total loss of access to Noetica customer data and services. This could lead to breach of SLAs, inability to support integrated TR products, reputational damage with customers who expect enterprise-grade resilience, and potential regulatory or contractual scrutiny around lack of disaster recovery capabilities.
risks.mitigation: 1) Zachery to draft a written proposal / architecture decision record describing the cold standby DR approach (S3 replication to a paired region per customer account, plus optional coverage for RDS and OpenSearch where required). 2) Circulate the proposal to the core group (including Ash, Donny, Noah) and route it to Tom and Sabrina for review and sign-off, ensuring contractual and customer expectations are addressed. 3) Donny to confirm with the product/firm library team whether full recovery is possible from S3 alone or if RDS/OpenSearch backups are also required, and feed this back into the DR design. 4) Once approved, define and agree a concrete implementation timeline (targeting H2) with Noetica engineering and security. 5) Track progress and implementation as a defined work item so the risk can be closed once DR replication is in place and validated.
