assumptions.title: Phase 1 cloud migration completes in time to enable Phase 2 and dependent work
assumptions.description: Assumption that Phase 1 cloud migration (Colo to TR AWS Cloud for BRS and CV Mail) will complete on the planned dates (e.g., BRS by 2026-03-09 and CV Mail by 2026-03-24), enabling Phase 2 cloud migration, domain transfer, DNS hosting migration, and other downstream activities.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The HL Milestones show Phase 1 migrations for BRS and CV Mail as largely complete with specific cutover dates, and dependencies such as Phase 2 cloud migration and domain/DNS activities are scheduled assuming Phase 1 will be finished by early March 2026.
assumptions.validity_explanation: As of the latest updates, BRS AWS migration tasks are all marked Complete with a final cutover date of March 9, 2026. CV Mail AWS migration, including QA/Staging and Prod execution, is also reported as Complete with revised dates accepted. These completed tasks demonstrate that the assumption that Phase 1 would be delivered in early March has largely held true, making it a valid basis for planning subsequent work.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If any remaining Phase 1 activities slip, adjust Phase 2 schedule and prioritize critical workloads for earlier migration. Consider parallelizing some preparation for Phase 2 (e.g., CICD pipeline base structure, inventory and design work) so that the impact of minor Phase 1 delays on overall TSA timelines is minimized.
assumptions.validation_method: Track completion status of Phase 1 tasks in the HL Milestones (BRS AWS and CVMail AWS lines) and confirm Go-Live dates with the cloud migration team.

assumptions.title: ADO migration will be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration
assumptions.description: Assumption that migration of data from TR ADO to BRS ADO will be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration due to financial and other dependencies.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The RAIDD log lists a dependency that ADO migration should be completed before Phase 2 cloud migration because of financial dependencies. Project planning schedules ADO migration during April–May 2026, ahead of the overall Phase 2 completion date of June 29, 2026.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The ADO migration work item is scheduled for 2026-04-01 to 2026-05-29, with ownership assigned and TechM involved from the TR side. However, there are notes that vendor contract timing and start date are still to be confirmed, meaning the assumption is reasonable but not yet fully validated.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If ADO migration cannot be completed before Phase 2, defer non‑critical ADO-related scope from Phase 2 or implement temporary read‑only access to TR ADO for the buyer until migration completes. Re-sequence Phase 2 cutovers to prioritize environments that are less dependent on historical ADO data.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm ADO migration start and completion dates against the HL Milestones and verify that required data (e.g., development ticket history) is present and usable in BRS ADO before Phase 2 cutovers.

assumptions.title: Domain transfer must complete before DNS hosting migration and O365/email migrations
assumptions.description: Assumption that ownership transfer of key domains (e.g., bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, cvmail.com.au, cvmail.net) can be completed before DNS hosting migration and before Office 365 / email migrations that depend on the new DNS setup.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Project notes describe domain ownership transfer as a prerequisite for DNS hosting migration and subsequent O365 migrations. The HL Milestones show detailed steps for domain transfers (Phase 1) followed by a separate Phase 2 DNS hosting migration, and O365 migrations are noted as dependent on domain/email setup.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Multiple domain transfer tasks are already marked Complete, including bigredsky.com.au, bigredsky.au, cvmail.au, and cvmail.net. A combined task to transfer bigredsky.com, cvmailuk.com, and cvmail.com.au is scheduled through 2026-04-10 with active follow‑up reported. Given this progress and clear sequencing, it is reasonable to assume remaining transfers will complete ahead of DNS and O365 work.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If any critical domain transfer is delayed, delay dependent DNS hosting migration and email migrations for that domain while proceeding with unaffected domains. Implement temporary mail forwarding or aliases using existing TR infrastructure during the TSA to maintain service continuity until ownership transfer is complete.
assumptions.validation_method: Track completion of each domain transfer task in the HL Milestones and confirm registrar ownership change plus internal DNS updates before proceeding to Phase 2 DNS hosting migration and O365 cutovers.

assumptions.title: Office 365, SharePoint, and OneDrive migrations will complete successfully within TSA timelines
assumptions.description: Assumption that migration of user email (M365), SharePoint, and OneDrive data to the buyer’s environment can be completed using the chosen tools and vendor within the TSA period, after domain and email setup are finished.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Planning notes describe O365 migration as typically straightforward and handled by the O365 migration team, with a defined migration tool (AvePoint Fly) and third‑party provider (Troppus). Detailed phases (pre‑migration setup, identity/object mapping, pre‑stage and delta migration, cutover, validation and cleanup) are already scheduled.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The project has an agreed migration tool (AvePoint Fly), a migration vendor (Troppus), and documented progress showing completion of early phases and substantial work on pre‑stage/delta migration. However, Phase 4 (cutover) and Phase 5 (validation/cleanup) are not yet started and are tied to broader milestone readiness, so while the approach is sound, there remains schedule and coordination risk.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If migration appears unlikely to complete by TSA end, prioritize critical user mailboxes and high‑value SharePoint/OneDrive content for early cutover, extend O365 migration windows where possible, and if necessary arrange temporary continued TR access for a subset of users or data until final validation is complete.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor execution and completion of each migration phase in the HL Milestones and obtain confirmation from Neel and the buyer’s IT that all required mailboxes and data have been successfully migrated and validated.

assumptions.title: NewCo will have cloud and DNS infrastructure ready in time for Phase 2 migration and DNS hosting cutover
assumptions.description: Assumption that the buyer (NewCo) will set up the necessary cloud environments and DNS infrastructure (including name servers and any Cloudflare/CloudFront integration) in time to support Phase 2 TR AWS to NewCo cloud migration and DNS hosting migration within planned dates.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The Phase 2 cloud migration plan and DNS hosting migration plan both rely on NewCo having its own cloud infrastructure and DNS servers ready. Notes state that DNS hosting migration cannot start until Phase 2 cloud migration infrastructure is in place and that NewCo must set up DNS servers and related records.
assumptions.validity_explanation: While project notes indicate Danny is actively engaged in planning and that NewCo is moving forward with other technical capabilities, there is also explicit feedback that Phase 2 may not meet a May 31 date due to infrastructure readiness concerns. This suggests partial progress but not yet confirmed readiness, making the assumption plausible but not secure.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If NewCo infrastructure is not ready, pursue: (1) temporary extension of TR hosting for critical workloads; (2) phased migration where components can move to any ready NewCo environments while others remain on TR; and (3) revisiting TSA scope/costs to cover extended hosting and support until NewCo is fully ready.
assumptions.validation_method: Obtain firm dates and readiness confirmation from Danny and NewCo technical leads (e.g., Vish, Parvathi) for cloud environment availability and DNS/server configuration, and verify with test deployments and DNS record changes prior to production cutover.

assumptions.title: Cold standby DR implementation for Noetica will be delivered in H2 2026
assumptions.description: Planning for the Noetica integration assumes that the cold standby disaster recovery (DR) solution (S3 multi-region replication, and any additional components such as RDS/OpenSearch where required) will be designed, approved, and implemented during the second half of 2026 (H2).
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the meeting, Zachery and Kiran referenced H2 as the targeted timeframe for DR implementation, with the expectation that design documentation, reviews, and customer/contract checks will be completed beforehand.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The H2 timeline was agreed at a high level but remains dependent on completion of design documentation, contractual review, and customer communications. Until those prerequisites are completed and resourcing is confirmed, the H2 date is a planning assumption rather than a committed schedule.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If it becomes clear that H2 implementation is not achievable, update the risk register to reflect extended exposure, adjust integration plans and SLAs accordingly, and consider an interim, lower-effort backup posture (e.g., enhanced intra-region backup and recovery procedures) while a full multi-region DR implementation is rescheduled.
assumptions.validation_method: Confirm by mid-2026 that a detailed DR implementation plan, including specific milestones and resourcing, has been baselined and approved; verify through program plans and DR work items that implementation is scheduled in H2.
assumptions.source_file_name: Noetica - Cold Standby DR Strategy Discussion – Requirement & Path Forward.docx

assumptions.title: Noetica customers will accept intra-account multi-region replication of their private data for DR
assumptions.description: It is assumed that Noetica customers, who were originally provided strong isolation guarantees through a one-AWS-account-per-customer architecture, will accept multi-region replication of their private data within their own AWS account (e.g., S3 and possibly RDS/OpenSearch replication) for disaster recovery purposes, provided isolation and encryption controls remain in place.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Donny stated that, from a technical and security perspective, intra-account multi-region replication is feasible and comparable to how other applications manage private customer data, and expressed a belief that customers would be understanding of this for backup purposes. However, he also noted the need for someone closer to customers and contracts (e.g., Tom and Sabrina) to confirm acceptability.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The proposed DR strategy keeps data within the same customer-owned AWS account and aims to preserve existing security controls, suggesting minimal change in data control and isolation. However, explicit customer and legal confirmation is still pending, so confidence remains moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If customers do not accept intra-account multi-region replication, explore alternatives such as (1) contract updates explicitly permitting DR replication, (2) customer-selectable DR options with documented trade-offs, or (3) a more limited DR posture (e.g., enhanced intra-region backups only) paired with transparent risk acknowledgement.
assumptions.validation_method: Tom and Sabrina to review the proposed DR architecture and compare it against contractual language and customer commitments; where necessary, discuss the approach with key customers and document their acceptance or required changes.
assumptions.source_file_name: Noetica - Cold Standby DR Strategy Discussion – Requirement & Path Forward.docx

assumptions.title: Noetica environments can be fully recovered from S3 (and minimal additional) backups
assumptions.description: The DR design assumes that Noeticas core customer environments can be fully reconstructed primarily from S3 backups (raw documents) and, if necessary, a minimal set of additional data sources (e.g., RDS snapshots and OpenSearch snapshots), without requiring complex or bespoke recovery flows beyond those backups.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the discussion, Donny indicated that customer data is split across S3 (raw documents), OpenSearch (processed/chunked data), and RDS (linking and metadata), and that he believes OpenSearch content can be recreated from S3 and RDS. He committed to validate with the team that handles the firm library functionality to confirm the exact recovery requirements.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The current architecture already separates raw and derived data and uses managed services with snapshot capabilities, making it reasonable to expect that an appropriate combination of S3 and managed-service snapshots can support full recovery. However, detailed confirmation of dependencies and data flows is still outstanding.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If it turns out that additional data sources or services must be replicated or backed up to achieve full recovery, expand the DR scope to include those elements (e.g., multi-region RDS snapshots, OpenSearch snapshot replication to S3), and update timelines and cost estimates accordingly. If the required scope becomes too complex for initial implementation, prioritize a minimal viable DR scope with clearly documented limitations and a follow-on enhancement plan.
assumptions.validation_method: Donny to consult the product/firm library team to confirm whether complete reconstruction is possible from S3 alone or if RDS/OpenSearch data must also be replicated or backed up across regions; document the confirmed data recovery model in the DR architecture proposal.
assumptions.source_file_name: Noetica - Cold Standby DR Strategy Discussion – Requirement & Path Forward.docx

assumptions.title: Snyk scanning issues will be resolved or manually bypassed in time to avoid delays to SIGSA and TTC non‑prod and production cloud integrations
assumptions.description: Project planning assumes that the current Snyk scanning issues in the SafeSend/TTC codebase will either be fully resolved by the ISRM-Platforms-Security-Dev team or, if not, that a manual intervention process will be approved and executed (within 1–2 days) so that SIGSA and TTC non‑production cloud integrations can complete in Q1 2026 and production cloud integration planning can start on schedule.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Non‑production cloud integration for SIGSA and TTC must complete in Q1 2026 to keep SafeSend One production in Q2 and SIGSA/TTC production in Q3 on track. Automated Snyk scanning is a prerequisite for promotion, so the team planned on either timely resolution of the Snyk issue or an approved manual workaround.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The risk log shows that the Snyk scanning risk was managed with direct involvement from the ISRM security team and a clearly defined contingency of manual intervention. The risk entry is marked as resolved by 2026-02-26, indicating that either the automated scanning was restored or an acceptable workaround was implemented in time, confirming the assumption held true for planning purposes.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If automated Snyk scanning cannot be restored promptly, proceed with the agreed manual intervention process (1–2 days) to perform required security checks and unblock deployments, while coordinating with ISRM and project leadership to document approvals and ensure compliance.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitor progress of ISRM-Platforms-Security-Dev work on the Snyk issue and confirm either successful restoration of automated scans or completion of the manual intervention process; verify that SIGSA and TTC non‑production integrations complete by Q1 2026 and that production planning starts as scheduled.

assumptions.title: Noetica cloud migration to Thomson Reuters landing zone will occur in 2028 and is out of near-term scope
assumptions.description: Planning for the Noetica integration assumes that any large-scale cloud migration or landing zone change (e.g., moving core Noetica workloads from their current AWS architecture into a standardized Thomson Reuters landing zone) will not occur until 2028. Current work in the Technology CIO workstream is therefore focused on nearer-term items such as network integration, minimum viable controls (MVCs), disaster recovery design, and AWS account transfer/billing alignment, without attempting a full cloud migration in the current planning horizon.

owner.name: Bleninger, Zachery (TR Technology, Cloud Solutions Architect)

assumptions.rationale_basis: During the April 30, 2026 weekly sync, Milind asked whether there was any planned cloud migration that would be demanded alongside network integration. Zachery responded that cloud migration is planned for 2028, and the group treated this as sufficiently distant that it does not need to be actively planned now. This establishes 2028 as the informal target for any major cloud migration activity.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The statement about a 2028 cloud migration target was made in a live integration governance forum without objection and was treated as a long-term horizon by multiple participants. However, it has not been formally captured in a signed roadmap or governance decision, and TR strategic priorities could change, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If plans change and cloud migration for Noetica is required earlier than 2028, update the integration scope, create dedicated migration risks, and establish a separate migration workstream with its own funding, resources, and milestones instead of folding migration into existing DR/network/account-transfer efforts. Re-baseline timelines and capacity to avoid overcommitting current teams.
assumptions.validation_method: Review TR and Legal portfolio cloud roadmaps and integration plans annually (or upon major strategic changes) to confirm that 2028 remains the target for Noetica cloud migration. Validate with Zachery, Milind, and Kiran that no earlier migration initiatives have been approved that would affect Noetica.
assumptions.source_file_name: Noetica Integration Technology CIO  Workstream Mtgs -- Weekly Sync.docx

assumptions.title: Pre-created AWS account model will be a viable replacement for Control Tower-driven per-customer account creation for Noetica
assumptions.description: It is assumed that, after moving Noetica accounts into the TR AWS organization and removing Control Tower at the org level, Noetica will still be able to operate effectively by using a model where TR pre-creates batches of AWS accounts in Noetica OUs, and Noetica's automation and deployment pipelines are adapted to consume these pre-existing accounts for new customers instead of creating accounts via Control Tower on demand.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the April 30, 2026 meeting, Zachery proposed that, because Control Tower cannot be retained at the TR org level without FedRAMP/access complications, TR would "inflate batches" of AWS accounts in the Noetica OUs based on expected customer demand (e.g., 5–10 accounts for upcoming customers). Ash noted that current pipelines assume Control Tower-driven account creation and that they would need to assess changes to automation. This proposal forms a working assumption that adapting to pre-created accounts is feasible.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Conceptually, using pre-created accounts is a common pattern in large organizations, and TR has existing mechanisms to do so. However, Noetica's current automation, SCP layout, and on-call access patterns are built around Control Tower and may require non-trivial refactoring. Since these changes have not yet been designed or tested, confidence is only moderate.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If testing or design review shows that pre-created accounts are not a viable operational model, explore alternatives such as: (1) constrained use of Control Tower within the TR org under FedRAMP-compliant access controls, (2) a hybrid model where some Control Tower features are replaced by custom automation built by TR and Noetica, or (3) deferring the account transfer until a more robust solution is identified. In parallel, work with AWS account teams to revisit contractual options (e.g., extending TR discounts/support to Noetica's existing org) if technical constraints make account transfer too risky.
assumptions.validation_method: Document the proposed pre-created account model in Zachery's AWS org/account transfer proposal and have Noetica's engineering and automation teams review it. Prototype or dry-run the updated automation pipeline against a small set of pre-created accounts to confirm that customer onboarding and deployment can be performed without Control Tower. Capture results and go/no-go decision in the integration design review.

validation_owner.name: Bleninger, Zachery (TR Technology, Cloud Solutions Architect)

assumptions.source_file_name: Noetica Integration Technology CIO  Workstream Mtgs -- Weekly Sync.docx

assumptions.title: Short-term Noetica-led AWS cost optimisation can substantially reduce spend and ease timing pressure on AWS org transfer
assumptions.description: Planning for the Noetica AWS org transfer assumes that Noetica’s own cost-optimisation efforts (e.g., rightsizing OpenSearch and other infrastructure, tuning usage, and exploring savings plans) can deliver substantial near-term AWS savings (on the order of ~30%) so that TR can demonstrate meaningful cost reduction without immediately completing the complex org transfer into the TR AWS organization.
assumptions.rationale_basis: In the meeting, Donny Yung reported that Noetica has already achieved approximately 31% month-to-date AWS cost reduction through rightsizing (OpenSearch and other components) and expects further savings from additional tuning and potential savings plans. He advocated maximising these optimisations first while longer-term architecture and migration paths are defined, in order to avoid derailing the product roadmap and to reduce pressure to rush the org transfer.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Concrete MTD savings provide strong early evidence that optimisation is effective, but it is not yet proven that these levels can be sustained or further improved without impacting performance or roadmap priorities. Market conditions, workload growth, or unforeseen technical limits could reduce the achievable savings, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If optimisation does not continue to deliver meaningful or sustainable savings, increase focus on alternative cost levers such as (a) carefully scoped, phased AWS org transfer steps that target high-value accounts first, (b) renegotiating discounts or support arrangements that do not require full org transfer, or (c) deprioritising lower-value features or projects to free up capacity for migration work. In parallel, escalate a revised, risk-aware migration plan to leadership to align expectations on achievable timing and risk profile.
assumptions.validation_method: 1) Noetica to produce and share a detailed AWS cost-optimisation summary (baseline vs current, initiatives, and forecast) by the agreed near-term date. 2) Track monthly AWS spend trends for Noetica accounts over the next 1–2 quarters to confirm that optimisation is delivering and maintaining targeted savings. 3) Use this data in leadership communications and migration planning to confirm that short-term savings are sufficient to support a more deliberate transfer timeline.

assumptions.title: Shifting Noetica customer renewals to standard TR contracts from June 1 will reduce some current contractual constraints on AWS architecture and integration options
assumptions.description: The integration planning assumes that, starting June 1, Noetica customer renewals moving onto standard TR contracts will reduce certain existing contractual constraints (e.g., strict single-tenant commitments and bespoke terms), thereby providing greater flexibility for future AWS org, security, and DR architecture decisions compared to legacy Noetica contracts.
assumptions.rationale_basis: During the discussion on security and contract impacts (single-tenant customer contracts, Cognito pools, logging aggregation, security tooling), Sharon Smelter clarified that from June 1, Noetica customer renewals will move to standard TR contracts. This was positioned as a factor that may ease some of the contractual constraints currently influencing technical options for integration and DR.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The expectation is grounded in how TR typically standardizes contracts to support shared platforms, but actual customer renewals and negotiations may still result in exceptions or special terms, especially for large or sensitive customers. Until several renewals have been completed and analysed, the extent of constraint reduction is uncertain.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If standard TR contracts do not significantly reduce constraints, integration planning should (a) explicitly catalogue which contractual terms remain limiting for AWS org transfer and DR design, (b) prioritise technical patterns that comply with the strictest remaining requirements, and (c) consider targeted contract amendments or customer-specific DR options where needed. Additionally, adjust timelines and scope for AWS org transfer and DR implementation to reflect the added complexity of operating under heterogeneous contractual obligations.
assumptions.validation_method: 1) Legal and commercial teams to review the standard TR contract language being applied to Noetica renewals and compare it to current Noetica customer commitments relevant to AWS tenancy, region, and data handling. 2) As renewals occur after June 1, track any customer objections or carve-outs that preserve existing constraints. 3) Confirm with Sabrina and TR legal/commercial leads whether the new contracts materially widen the range of technically permissible integration/DR patterns.

issues.title: Priority issues during Azure Databricks migration

issues.impact_assessment: The Databricks migration issues risked delaying data processing capabilities and the broader cloud integration timelines for SafeSend and dependent projects. Both DNS and subnet delegation problems directly blocked Databricks deployment.

issues.resolution: Raised support requests REQ0069376 and REQ0070250 to create the required Private DNS Zone and enable subnet delegation for Azure Databricks with VNet injection, resolving the blocking conditions.

issues.description: The return date for 10 users’ laptops needed to be extended from January 31 to February 28, requiring updates to divestiture files and reconfiguration of SailPoint IAM jobs and device compliance. One user, Lewis Betterton, experienced access problems during account reactivation, including issues with TR email, Salesforce, Genesys, and device compliance.
issues.impact_assessment: Laptop returns for 10 divesting users could not occur by the original date of 2026-01-31, which would have led to premature revocation of access while devices were still needed. IAM automation via SailPoint required updated end dates to prevent unintended access removal. Additionally, user 'Lewis Betterton' experienced critical access interruptions (TR mail inbox, database access, Zscaler, Salesforce, Genesys cloud) and device non-compliance errors during account reactivation, impacting his ability to perform support activities.

issues.title: DKIM Issue Impacting Salesforce Email Forwarding

owner.name: Eric Vogan, Greg Burch, Ryan Hardtke, Udit Kumar

issues.impact_assessment: Incorrect or unverified DKIM keys in Salesforce risked email delivery failures and improper authentication of emails used to generate Salesforce cases. This could disrupt customer support workflows relying on email-to-case functionality during the divestiture transition.
issues.dependencies_affecting: Salesforce case creation and email forwarding configurations, including dependencies on DNS and email security settings.
issues.resolution: Verify and activate correct DKIM keys in Salesforce and complete end‑to‑end testing of email forwarding to ensure emails are successfully delivered and create cases as expected.

issues.title: Resource Availability – Time Base
issues.description:
Time Base has significant resource constraints, with one individual managing all tasks from the Time Base side, including coordination, alignment, and execution of migration activities.
Due to competing Business-as-Usual (BAU) activities and high operational workload, responses to customer requests and actions may be delayed.
issues.impact_assessment:
Having a single individual managing all tasks from the Time Base side increases the risk of delays, bottlenecks, and burnout, and reduces the resilience of the project.
Project tasks may be deprioritized in favour of BAU commitments.
Risk of delays in milestones and deliverables due to limited bandwidth.
issues.resolution: Track and flag delays early in weekly status calls.

dependencies.consumer: TR Platform Engineering and product teams implementing CoCounsel–Noetica integrations

dependencies.title: Flash migration completion before SafeSend CS&S migration

dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If the Flash migration is delayed or overlaps significantly with SafeSend migration, key shared resources may be overextended, causing schedule conflicts and potential delays to SafeSend migration activities.
dependencies.mitigation: Program is tracked closely and on-track for now. No major risk or issues to SafeSend.

dependencies.title: Resolution of AWS Identity Center and FedRAMP constraints to enable Noetica AWS org transfer
dependencies.description: The proposed transfer of Noetica AWS accounts into the Thomson Reuters AWS organization depends on resolving architectural and compliance constraints related to AWS Identity Center and FedRAMP. Identity Center currently must run at the AWS org root, which conflicts with TRs existing FedRAMP-boundary policies and makes a straightforward reuse of Noeticas current Control Tower/Identity Center setup infeasible. Without a resolved pattern for Identity and Control Tower decommissioning, the org transfer remains high risk and difficult to roll back.

owner.name: Bleninger, Zachery (TR Technology, Cloud Solutions Architect)

dependencies.dependent_on: Definition and approval of an AWS Identity Center and Control Tower decommissioning pattern that complies with TR FedRAMP boundary policies while supporting Noetica account and access management needs
dependencies.consumer: Thomson Reuters Cloud Solutions Architecture and Noetica technology integration workstream
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Identity Center and Control Tower constraints are not resolved, Noetica AWS accounts cannot be safely transferred into the TR AWS organization without high risk of subtle breakages (IAM role/org ID dependencies, CloudFront/WAF behaviour, GPU capacity reservations, logging and security tooling integrations) and limited rollback options. This would delay realization of ~26% AWS cost savings and postpone alignment with TR security and audit controls.
dependencies.mitigation: Conduct a focused SME design exercise (including TR Platform Engineering, Security, and Noetica infrastructure/security leads) to evaluate alternative identity and account-governance patterns that do not require Identity Center at the TR org root, such as pre-created accounts with updated CI/CD pipelines, alternative SSO/role-assumption flows, or staged/partial migrations. Validate proposed patterns against FedRAMP requirements and document a recommended approach for leadership review before executing any org transfer steps.

decisions.title: Decision for Laptop issuance for Noetica
decisions.description: Determine if laptop should be issued by Noetica Vendor or TR Vendor
decisions.rationale: The discussion will evaluate laptop issuance options (Noetica‑issued vs TR‑issued) to ensure the selected approach meets contractor onboarding needs while aligning with TR security, risk, and compliance requirements. This includes validating ISRM expectations, confirming whether TPRM assessments are required, and ensuring appropriate data protection and endpoint controls are in place before access is granted.

decisions.title: Use Paymetric for SafeSend payments until Stripe is aligned
decisions.description: SafeSend will continue to use the current BAU Paymetric payment solution for its migration and launches, and will migrate to Stripe later in alignment with the broader Unification Payment program and CPSP timelines.
decisions.rationale: The Unification Payment program’s Stripe delivery timeline is not aligned with the 2026 SafeSend migration delivery dates; attempting to align SafeSend with Stripe now would create an unmet dependency and delivery risk.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Align SafeSend migration with Stripe delivery timeline under the Unification Payment program.
2) Proceed with SafeSend migration using existing BAU Paymetric and move to Stripe later with the rest of CPSP (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to CPSP Stripe risk R003 in the RAID log, where the Stripe project plan is not aligned with SafeSend target delivery dates.

decisions.title: Phase SafeSend One and Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launches
decisions.description: SafeSend One business launch will proceed ahead of Digital Sales and Self-Serve launches, with Digital capabilities following once foundational platforms and processes are in place.
decisions.rationale: Phasing launches ensures that foundational capabilities, including self-serve, are in place before Digital Sales and Self-Serve go live, reducing delivery risk and improving stability at launch.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Launch SafeSend One and Digital Sales & Self-Serve together.
2) Phase the launches so Digital Sales & Self-Serve follow after foundational lead-to-cash delivery (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Impacts Digital workstream roadmap and dependencies on lead-to-cash (L2C) foundational deliverables planned for July 2026.

decisions.title: Set TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launch target to January 2027
decisions.description: SSOne and TTC Digital phased deployment was agreed, with TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve business launch targeted for January 2027, with a possibility to bring it forward into Q4 2026 if Digital commitments are met by June 2026.
decisions.rationale: Separating the TTC Digital launch provides additional time to deliver and stabilize core lead-to-cash capabilities and allows Digital teams to commit to a realistic delivery schedule, while retaining flexibility to pull the date forward if feasible.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Align TTC Digital Sales & Self-Serve launch with July 2026 L2C deliverables.
2) Target January 2027 for TTC Digital launch, with option to bring into Q4 2026 if commitments are met (selected).
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to Digital workstream scope, TTC digital rollout timing, and integration budget planning for 2026, as well as RAID risk regarding TTC scope, design, and schedule alignment with July 2026 deployment.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

AI Reimagine (CIO) is delivering AI-enabled transformation across CIO to reduce operating costs, automate service and engineering workflows, and shift teams from manual execution to exception-driven operations. The program aggregates AIOps, AI coding agents, service desk automation, and AI service management agents to create a measurable productivity and stability uplift across the technology estate.

Two of six constituent projects are Green while four remain Amber, so most value is still in build-and-adopt phases rather than steady-state. Key delivery milestones are slipping, including the Service Management AIOps proof of value moving from 31 Mar 2026 to 29 May 2026 (59-day variance) and ETS conversational workflow configuration moving from 21 May 2026 to 19 Jun 2026 (29-day variance).

Overall status is Amber, driven primarily by delayed AIOps and service desk automation milestones that are on the program’s critical path to unlocking 2026 efficiency and stability benefits.

## Path to Green

The path to Green focuses on closing the overdue AIOps proof of value and MVP early-adopter onboarding by 31 May 2026, recovering the slipped conversational workflow milestone for ETS, and locking validated 2026 value-realization roadmaps for Service Management, Commercial Engineering, and ETS so that Amber workstreams have a clear, sequenced route to their committed benefits.

## Milestones

- Complete the SM AIOps/Event Management Proof of Value for Legal Tracker by 29 May 2026.
- Deliver the MVP early-adopter onboarding for ONESOURCE GTM and CIAM by 31 May 2026.
- Configure ETS conversational virtual agent workflows (greeting, fallback, completion, error handling) by 19 Jun 2026.
- Achieve Service Management, Platform Engineering, and Commercial Engineering benefits unlock across AI agents and AIOps workstreams by 31 Dec 2026.
- Complete the overall AI Reimagine (CIO) program and transition to steady-state by 30 Dec 2027.

risks.title: Unresolved ServiceNow CI–service association behaviour may block cutover from Datadog incidents
risks.description: During the May 12, 2026 AIOps Product Onboarding regional sync, the team observed that ServiceNow is not associating services with the correct CIs for large applications such as Legal Tracker. Internal analysis suggests that a configurable limit of approximately 1,000 CIs per service causes additional CIs to be handled via dynamic CI groups, which in turn prevents correct service association and grouping. ServiceNow’s consultant (Doug) indicated there are “traverse rules” that might address this but needs to consult CMDB experts. Until a clear recommendation and fix are in place, the Legal Tracker product team considers this a showstopper for disabling Datadog-direct incident creation.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow continues to mis-associate or partially associate CIs to services due to the current service–CI association behaviour, AIOps cannot reliably determine which service is impacted by an event or alert for large applications. For Legal Tracker, this would mean that incidents created by AIOps could lack correct service context or rely on dynamic CI groups, undermining routing, impact analysis, and leadership reporting. As a result, Legal Tracker stakeholders will not agree to cut over from Datadog-direct incident creation, delaying the POV completion, delaying onboarding of subsequent products, and prolonging reliance on legacy workflows.
risks.mitigation: ServiceNow’s consultant Doug will escalate the CI/service association issue to their CMDB experts to review the current configuration, including the apparent 1,000-CI-per-service association limit and available traverse rules. Together with the TR CMDB team, they will: (1) determine whether the association limit can be safely tuned without degrading ServiceNow performance; (2) design appropriate traverse rules or alternative modelling (e.g., hierarchical services) to support large applications like Legal Tracker; and (3) validate the chosen approach in a lower environment before promoting changes to production. In parallel, Jot will log this as a formal blocker in status reporting, and Talia will escalate via email and stakeholder channels (including Eric and John) to ensure it receives high priority attention from ServiceNow and the CMDB team. Cutover from Datadog-direct incidents for Legal Tracker will be deferred until a recommended and tested fix is in place.
risks.source_file_name: AIOps Product Onboarding Reg Sync 12 May 26.docx

risks.title: Incorrect priority and severity mapping from Datadog to ServiceNow incidents
risks.description: Priority and severity values from Datadog monitors are not yet consistently or correctly mapped into ServiceNow alert and incident fields. Severity has sometimes been populated from unexpected payload fields, custom test fields exist, and the mapping between Datadog alert_priority/alert_type and ServiceNow severity, impact, urgency, and priority is still being designed. If this is not resolved before enabling automated incident creation, incidents may be mis‑prioritized.
risks.impact_description: Mis‑prioritized incidents (e.g., P1 issues created as P3, or minor warnings created as P1) will distort SLAs, paging, and escalation. Major Incident processes could be flooded with false majors or miss real ones. This will reduce trust in the AIOps solution, force manual reprioritization, and may cause teams to resist adopting event‑driven incident creation.
risks.mitigation: Define and document a definitive mapping: use Datadog monitor priority (P1–P5) as the authoritative input, add custom impact and urgency fields on the alert record, map monitor priority into those fields via event rules, and customize the incident-creation subflow to derive incident priority solely from those values. Validate mapping with test payloads and a parallel run comparing new incidents to historical ones before turning off legacy Datadog incident creation.

risks.title: Lack of monitoring governance and standardized thresholds across products
risks.description: There is no centralized event management practice or monitoring governance. Platform Engineering publishes Datadog policies on SharePoint but does not audit or enforce them. Thresholds and configurations vary by product; 80% of monitors are synthetics with product‑specific thresholds, and 75% of GCC events come from one product (HighQ). Many teams do not understand event threshold concepts (informational/warning/critical).
risks.impact_description: Without standardized thresholds, tagging, and governance, noisy or misconfigured monitors will continue to flood Event Management and produce inconsistent event classification across products. AIOps capabilities (filtering, correlation, prioritization) may be overwhelmed or misused, leading to limited noise reduction, poor comparability between services, and difficulty onboarding new teams into the AIOps model.
risks.mitigation: Define and implement a monitoring governance model: standardize thresholds where feasible (infrastructure monitors), define enterprise guidelines for synthetic thresholds, establish tagging standards (including Asset Insight ID, service tags, and TR_‑prefixed custom tags), and create an auditing mechanism to flag non‑compliant monitors. Use Legal Tracker as a pilot to refine policies before scaling to other Tier 1 products such as HighQ.

risks.title: Departure of key AIOps architect (Chris Rutherford) may impact continuity and governance
risks.description: During the 30-Apr-2026 regular sync, Jot and the team thanked Chris Rutherford and noted that he would not be on the project from the following day. Chris has been the primary architect and leadership liaison for the ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management design, including incident priority behaviour, governance model, onboarding approach, and alignment with the Datadog hygiene programme. His departure creates a risk that architectural context, design rationale, and decision history may be lost or diluted, slowing future rule changes, onboarding of new products, and governance maturation.
risks.impact_description: Without Chris’s ongoing involvement, the team may struggle to maintain a consistent architectural vision and governance approach for AIOps. Questions about incident priority tuning, standard rule sets, and onboarding patterns could take longer to resolve; decisions may be revisited without full context; and onboarding of additional products “aggressively” (as planned) may slow or diverge from the intended cookie-cutter model. This could delay achieving scale benefits, increase rework on rules and standards, and reduce leadership confidence that AIOps is being guided by a clear owner.
risks.mitigation:
1) Ensure a structured handover of architectural and governance responsibilities from Chris to designated internal owners (e.g., Paul as programme lead, Prastuti and Vinay on the platform side, and Jot for project coordination).
2) Treat Doug’s in-progress training videos and configuration documentation as critical artefacts and complete them on the agreed timeline, capturing rule designs, priority behaviour, and onboarding patterns in a single reference.
3) Explicitly assign a new technical architecture lead for AIOps/Event Management within TR and communicate this to all stakeholders and vendors.
4) Review open design decisions and risks that had Chris as owner or key contributor, and confirm updated ownership and next steps so that work does not stall when onboarding new products “aggressively.”

risks.title: High concentration of noise from HighQ overshadowing other Tier 1 services
risks.description: 75% of GCC monthly events come from a single product (HighQ) out of ~50 Tier 1 products. If this concentration of noise is not addressed, it will continue to dominate GCC workload and may mask important events from other services, even after Event Management is enabled.
risks.impact_description: HighQ’s excessive alert volume may consume much of GCC and AIOps analysis capacity, leaving less focus on other services and skewing correlation and reporting. Important issues in other Tier 1 products could be delayed or overlooked, undermining fairness and effectiveness of the event management rollout.
risks.mitigation: Treat HighQ as a specific remediation target in the monitoring governance program: review and rationalize its monitors, apply stricter thresholds and suppression for noisy synthetics, and consider product‑specific filtering and correlation rules. Use HighQ data as a pilot to demonstrate volume reduction and incorporate lessons into broader standards before onboarding all Tier 1 products.

risks.title: Datadog and ServiceNow event volume and storage constraints
risks.description: There are concerns about the volume of events if all Datadog accounts send events into ServiceNow. While Datadog does not charge egress fees, ServiceNow storage is finite (e.g., ~4TB per instance), and high event volume could consume storage and impact performance if retention and filtering strategies are not defined.
risks.impact_description: If too many raw events are ingested without filtering and reasonable retention policies, ServiceNow databases may grow rapidly, potentially degrading performance or forcing unplanned data purges. Budget discussions with ServiceNow may be triggered, and the team might need to rework the architecture (e.g., move some correlation back to Datadog).
risks.mitigation: Engage the ServiceNow account team to confirm event storage limits, recommended retention periods, and cost implications. Implement lifecycle rules to purge older events while retaining alerts and incidents for reporting. Decide on a scoped ingestion strategy (starting with Legal Tracker and a subset of monitors), and only expand the number of sources and products once event filtering and correlation are proven to reduce noise.

risks.title: Agent chat PROD Functionality Failing
risks.description: Core Agent Chat functionality failing in PROD Check Ticket & Support Status” works in DEV/QA but not in PROD
risks.mitigation: PROD not aligned with DEV/QA configuration/code. Align PROD with DEV/QA configuration

risks.title: Teams without Event Management access losing visibility during cutover
risks.description: Not all operational teams (e.g., Major Incident team) currently have access to the Event Management module and dashboards. If the legacy Datadog–driven incident creation is disabled before those teams have alternative visibility, they may not see or manage critical events during and after cutover.
risks.impact_description: Major Incident and other central teams could lose timely visibility into critical alerts and incidents, delaying triage, page-outs, and communications. This would directly increase MTTA/MTTR and could cause missed SLAs for high-priority services like Legal Tracker.
risks.mitigation: Run legacy and new integrations in parallel for at least 24 hours while verifying parity, and only decommission the legacy path once all necessary operational teams have appropriate access to Event Management or alternate views. As part of cutover planning, review and adjust role assignments so Major Incident and other key groups can see grouped alerts, incidents, and AIOps dashboards. Following the 12 May 2026 regular sync, extend this to ensure GCC managers and operators (e.g., Rajendran’s team supporting Legal Tracker) are explicitly granted Event Management access before they are expected to monitor alerts, so that Legal Tracker and GCC can align their support model around the event-first view.

risks.title: CI binding from events/alerts to CMDB CIs may not work reliably
risks.description: Despite existing CIs in the CMDB with matching names, ServiceNow’s out‑of‑the‑box CI identification and binding logic is often failing to associate incoming Datadog events/alerts with the correct CI records.
risks.impact_description: If CI binding continues to fail, alerts and incidents generated by Event Management will not be accurately tied to infrastructure or application CIs. This will reduce the value of correlation, service impact analysis, and reporting, and could cause confusion during incident triage (wrong CI, or no CI attached). It may also block some auto‑remediation flows that depend on CI context and erode stakeholder confidence in the AIOps solution.
risks.mitigation: Doug and the ServiceNow team will analyze why out‑of‑the‑box CI identification is not working despite seemingly matching CI names and host attributes. They will review event payload mappings, identification rules, and any missing attributes (e.g., host vs. FQDN vs. CI name). Legal Tracker and GCC will provide additional event samples (including synthetic tests) to validate host/CI mappings. Where needed, adjust event rules or identification logic, and document any required payload standards back to Datadog (e.g., always sending host rather than FQDN).

risks.title: Legal Tracker monitor priorities and severities may not align with TR standards needed for AIOps
risks.description: Legal Tracker’s Datadog monitors currently have impact, urgency, and priority configured in Terraform, but those settings may not align with the TR incident priority matrix or with what AIOps expects to calculate severity/priority in ServiceNow.
risks.impact_description: If Legal Tracker monitors are not using severity/priority consistently with TR standards, the incidents created by AIOps may have inappropriate impact/urgency, leading to mis‑prioritized work (e.g., too many high‑priority incidents or true P1s classified lower). This could reduce trust in the new solution and require rework after go‑live.
risks.mitigation: Andrea and the Legal Tracker team will review all monitors in Terraform to ensure severity and priority reflect actual business impact and urgency, aligning with TR’s incident priority matrix. They will work with Luis and GCC to confirm how these values map into ServiceNow AIOps, and adjust monitor configurations where needed. This review will be incorporated into the onboarding checklist for Legal Tracker before final incident‑creation cutover.

risks.title: Agent chat interaction visibility model may not support desired multi-agent access
risks.description: Jakub requested investigating whether the same interaction conversation can be available to multiple agents at once, which is not the default behavior of Advanced Work Assignment (AWA). Current understanding is that supervisors/managers can join ongoing interactions, but it is unclear whether the system can be configured so different agents can pick up the same interaction, or if timing parameters (e.g., 1-minute search interval) must be adjusted instead.
risks.impact_description: If ServiceNow and AWA cannot be configured to support the desired level of multi-agent access to a single interaction, or if timing parameters for agent search are not tuned, agent collaboration workflows may be constrained. This could limit the ability for multiple agents to assist on complex cases, slow handoffs, and impact response times. Alternatively, aggressive parameter changes (e.g., very short search windows) without careful testing could destabilize routing behavior.
risks.mitigation: 1) Investigate ServiceNow and Advanced Work Assignment documentation and configuration options to confirm whether an interaction can be surfaced to multiple agents concurrently and under what conditions (e.g., supervisor join vs re-queueing). 2) Evaluate alternative approaches such as adjusting the default 1-minute agent search window to shorter intervals (e.g., 10–15 seconds) and enabling supervisor join capabilities for complex cases. 3) Prototype the desired behavior in DEV/QA and review with Jakub to confirm it meets operational needs. 4) If true multi-agent access is not feasible, document the chosen interaction handling model and ensure HCL is trained on expected behavior and escalation paths.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: [CE3] SAP Coding Assistant - Productivity/Benefits realization
risks.impact_description: If the native SAP Coding Assistant remains unavailable for on‑prem deployment and teams must rely on GitHub Copilot, overall SAP development productivity gains may be lower than planned. This could result in missed Q1 adoption and usage targets, reduced benefits realisation, and potential gaps against the finance-backed quarterly savings plan for the CE AI Coding Agents Efficiency project.
risks.mitigation: Adopt GitHub Copilot for SAP development with strong governance for both vendor and FTE teams to drive deeper usage. Implement an enablement plan to provide access to the majority of target users (aiming for 95–98% coverage) and configure an AI usage dashboard for tracking usage percentages and benefits. Revise Q1 targets as needed while agreeing critical actions with the VP to improve the baseline adoption and ensure alignment with the finance-backed quarterly savings plan.

risks.title: Correct Road Map
risks.description: ServiceDesk case does not have a firm roadmap in place on how VC outcomes will be achieved in 2027 regarding HCL Insource/Renegotiation. Commit to 2026/2027 service desk delivery roadmap, backwards-planned from December 2027 and from the HCL-renegotiation date
risks.mitigation:
Establish a Backward‑Planned Service Desk Roadmap (2026–2027)

Define clear 2027 VC outcomes for Service Desk (e.g., cost, quality, productivity, automation, sourcing mix).
Backward‑plan a multi‑year Service Desk delivery roadmap starting from:

December 2027 VC outcomes, and
HCL renegotiation decision date as a hard commercial milestone.


Decompose the roadmap into quarterly milestones for:

Automation & deflection (e.g., Virtual Agent, Now Assist, self‑service)
Operating model evolution (insource vs vendor-delivered)
Capability build (process maturity, tooling, workforce readiness)
Define explicit decision gates aligned to the HCL contract timeline:

Gate 1: Proof points on automation/deflection and productivity gains
Gate 2: Comparative insource vs vendor cost/service scenarios
Gate 3: Final sourcing recommendation (renegotiate vs insource vs hybrid)


Each gate must have:

Entry/exit criteria
Data requirements (metrics, benchmarks, pilot outcomes)
Accountable owners

risks.title: Benefit Mechanism
risks.description: Comm Eng benefits assumptions are tied to a contract model change (T&M → SOW + AI clauses) - outside the program’s direct control and may face attribution challenges
risks.mitigation: Ongoing engagement with Pillar VP and Finance to ensure savings attribution to AI are fair and accurate

risks.title: Production go-live before Event Management configuration and plugins are stable
risks.description: Event rules, respond rules, CI binding logic, and some plugins/scheduled jobs in upper environments are still under active revision. Doug has had to rebuild event rules from scratch due to conflicting behaviors, and some plugins in cloned environments require repair. There is pressure to meet the April 1, 2026 go‑live date for AIOps Event Management.
risks.impact_description: If incident creation and event processing are enabled in production before rules, mappings, and plugins are stable, the platform may create duplicate or missing incidents, fail to bind CIs, or mis‑route alerts. This could disrupt operations, undermine confidence in the new solution, and require emergency fixes in production.
risks.mitigation: Delay full go‑live of automated incident creation until: (1) event rules and respond rules are cleaned up and only approved rules are migrated; (2) required plugins and scheduled jobs are repaired in upper environments; (3) Datadog webhook payloads are standardized; and (4) a 24‑hour (or longer) dual‑run period validates behavior. Implement a change freeze so only Doug modifies AIOps event and alert rules until configuration is finalized, and prepare a clear checklist and ownership map for production enablement.

risks.title: Event forwarding between ServiceNow production and lower environments will function for test data
risks.description: The team is planning to use ServiceNow’s event forwarding from the production instance to dev and QA so that lower environments receive representative Datadog event traffic for testing rules and correlation without needing separate Datadog integrations for each environment.
risks.impact_description: If event forwarding between the production and lower environments does not function reliably, dev and QA will not receive representative production event traffic. This will limit the team’s ability to safely test new event rules, correlation logic, and responder rules using real-world data, increasing the risk that problematic configurations are promoted directly to production or that rule tuning is delayed.
risks.mitigation: Enable the event forwarding configuration in production, trigger Datadog events into the SNOW prod instance after webhook cutover, and confirm that corresponding events appear in dev (and subsequently QA) according to the expected schedule. If forwarding proves unreliable, fall back to (1) pointing Datadog test webhooks directly to dev/QA for specific monitors, or (2) manually injecting sample events into lower environments for rule testing. Coordinate with Doug to adjust or repair event management plugins if out-of-box forwarding behaviour is defective.

risks.title: Delivery Quality
risks.description: Until all platforms have consistent adoption reporting, delivery quality and efficiency tracking remains partially mixed and directional rather than definitive.
risks.mitigation: Getting all platforms on the AI adoption dashboard to enable automated tracking and measurement rather than manual tracking

risks.title: Zurich upgrade and dev freeze may cause loss or rework of recent virtual agent and agent chat changes
risks.description: The upcoming Zurich upgrade will introduce a dev freeze period (May 8 to June 8) and a clone from production into the development environment. During the May 11, 2026 sync, Vinay explained that to avoid losing in-flight development work (especially virtual agent conversational workflows, plugins, and configuration changes), developers must take backups of update sets before the end of Friday. Srinu confirmed that some changes are already captured in update sets, but others (such as plugin enabling or certain configuration options) are not; these will need to be documented and manually re-applied after the clone. If backups and documentation are incomplete, recent VA and Agent Chat work could be overwritten or require significant rework after the clone, impacting timelines.
risks.impact_description: If update sets are not properly exported and configuration-only changes are not documented before the Zurich upgrade clone, the clone from production could overwrite or remove recent development work on virtual agent conversational workflows, Agent Chat configuration, and related integrations. This would require developers (Srinu, Prashanth and others) to rediscover and re-implement these changes manually, consuming additional effort during an already constrained period and potentially delaying the May 15 conversational workflow target and other milestones. Incomplete backups could also cause inconsistencies between dev, QA, and future production deployments, increasing the risk of defects at go-live.
risks.mitigation:
1) Ensure all recent development work for virtual agent conversational workflows, Agent Chat, and related configurations is captured in ServiceNow update sets before the Zurich upgrade clone; Srinu and Prashanth to coordinate and export these update sets by end of day Friday.
2) For items not captured in update sets (e.g., plugin enablement, certain configuration options), document the exact steps and settings so they can be manually re-applied on the cloned dev instance.
3) After the clone, re-import and commit the saved update sets into the dev instance and re-apply documented configuration changes, verifying that all key VA and Agent Chat functionality still works.
4) Continue development and feedback changes in dev and QA during the prod change freeze, deferring only production promotions until after the upgrade window, as confirmed by Vinay.
5) Kiran to monitor progress and request status updates from Srinu and Prashanth on backup completion, highlighting any areas where rework is expected so they can be time-boxed and prioritized.
6) If significant rework is required post-clone, adjust internal timelines for non-prod testing and update the RAAID log and milestones accordingly.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF  Sync (1).docx

risks.title: Agent chat access/role configuration for HCL testers not fully working
risks.description: Some HCL users (e.g., Kandibanda Rakesh, Sri Lakshmi and others) cannot see or use the agent chat widget despite being added to the "Nava pilot users" / HCL groups with required roles. Causes appear related to legacy membership in HCL service desk groups and/or roles not propagating correctly from groups to users. If unresolved, HCL agents will not be able to perform hands-on testing of agent chat end-to-end.
risks.impact_description: If agent chat access and role issues for HCL testers are not fully resolved, HCL will be unable to explore agent chat hands-on "without any issues" as required. This will delay completion of testing, slow feedback on defects and usability, and may push back agreed timelines and preview dates with the internal event team. Persistent access gaps could also cause partial rollouts where only some agents are enabled, creating inconsistent support experience.
risks.mitigation: 1) Validate that all HCL pilot users (including but not limited to Kandibanda Rakesh and Sri Lakshmi) are correctly added to the "Nava pilot users" / HCL pilot groups. 2) Verify in the backend sys_user_has_role (or equivalent) table that roles (interaction, agent workspace, AWA agent) have been fully allocated from groups to each user; re-run or re-trigger scheduled jobs if needed. 3) For users with legacy membership in HCL service desk groups, test removing and re-adding them to the pilot group to force role alignment, as suggested by Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth. 4) Maintain and review the Excel list of who has access vs who still has issues (to be updated by HCL within ~1 hour) and work through all remaining names. 5) Provide support during UK/ISU hours via Gandikota, Srinu and L, Kiran Kumar to quickly resolve any new access problems reported by testers.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: Agent queue management governance between TR and HCL not defined
risks.description: The process and ownership for managing agent chat queues (e.g., adding new hires to language queues like French or English) has not been defined. Currently HCL self-manages queues in their existing setup, but it is unclear whether, and to what extent, they will have control within the TR ServiceNow (Advanced Work Assignment) configuration or if TR will centrally own this. Without clear governance, queue changes for new/changed agents may be slow or inconsistent.
risks.impact_description: If governance for agent chat queue management is not defined, new HCL hires and role changes may not be added to the correct language/skill queues in a timely manner. This can result in agents not receiving interactions they should handle, degraded service levels, manual workarounds, and dependence on ad-hoc TR changes. Over time this can cause operational friction between TR and HCL and undermine the scalability of the agent chat solution.
risks.mitigation: 1) Inventory current Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) queue configurations (e.g., language-specific queues such as French and English) and document the required update operations (add/remove agent, change capacities). 2) Align with TR stakeholders (e.g., Vinay, Prastuti) on whether queue administration will remain a TR-only function or if selected HCL members will receive controlled access. 3) Define and document a standard process (e.g., request form or workflow) for HCL to request queue changes, including SLAs, roles and approvals. 4) Communicate the agreed process and responsibilities to HCL leadership and frontline supervisors, and update any onboarding materials for new agents. 5) Periodically review queue membership changes to ensure the process is being followed and remains efficient.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: Agent capacity and presence configuration may overload or mis-route chats
risks.description: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) agent presence and capacity settings are not yet properly configured. Many agents appear as "available" indefinitely (even after being inactive for long periods), and default capacities (e.g., number of parallel chats per agent) are effectively unset or inconsistent. This can cause the system to treat long-inactive agents as available capacity and over-assign chats beyond reasonable limits.
risks.impact_description: If agent presence and capacity configurations remain unoptimized, chats may be routed to agents who are actually offline or no longer on shift, leading to long customer wait times and abandoned chats. Agents who are online can be overloaded with too many concurrent chats, impacting quality and agent experience. Misrouted or stuck chats will undermine confidence in the new agent chat solution and may force manual interventions, slowing adoption and putting service KPIs at risk.
risks.mitigation: 1) Define standard capacity limits per agent (e.g., 5 concurrent chats/incidents as discussed) and configure these limits consistently across all pilot agents. 2) Investigate whether there is an out-of-the-box or script-based mechanism to automatically mark agents offline after a defined period of inactivity or after logout; if available, implement and test it. 3) Review historical presence data (e.g., agents still showing available after weeks) to validate that the new configuration works as expected. 4) Coordinate with Gandikota, Srinu to deploy configuration changes across DEV/QA and PROD environments to keep them aligned. 5) Monitor queue utilization and agent feedback during the pilot to refine capacity and presence thresholds before broader rollout.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: Delayed monitor and tag standardization for GTM4 and SIAM may slip AIOps onboarding timelines
risks.description: GTM4 and SIAM subject-matter experts have expressed concerns that they may not be able to complete required Datadog monitor/tag standardization work (FinOpsDatadogAlerts updates, Asset Insight ID, primary support group, TR API name tags) by the targeted dates (end of this week / May 18). Luis has begun making some standardization changes, but key inputs such as synthetic monitor design and TR API name still depend on product teams. Without those updates, the AIOps webhook cannot be enabled because payloads would lack required fields, preventing correct grouping, routing, and service identification for these products.
risks.impact_description: If GTM4 and SIAM cannot complete the required Datadog monitor and tagging updates on time, the team will be unable to safely point their monitors at the AIOps webhook. This will delay onboarding for these early adopter products, push out the MVP / early adopter milestone, and limit the evidence base beyond Legal Tracker for demonstrating AIOps value. It may also create a staggered, uncoordinated rollout and erode stakeholder confidence if timelines repeatedly slip due to insufficient preparatory work on the product side.
risks.mitigation: Continue working closely with GTM4 and SIAM SMEs over the remaining working sessions (through May 18) to (1) explicitly list the required tag and monitor changes (Asset Insight ID, primary support group, TR API name, environment type) for each FinOpsDatadogAlerts monitor; (2) apply as many standardization changes centrally as possible where Luis can safely do so; (3) obtain product-team decisions on synthetic monitor design and TR API names during the current working sessions rather than deferring; and (4) only enable the webhook for each product once the minimum payload/tagging standard is verified. If a team cannot complete changes by May 18, re-plan their onboarding date explicitly rather than proceeding with incomplete data.

risks.title: Inconsistent IMC (incident) sharing behavior from agent chat
risks.description: An HCL team member observed that, after closing the chat, the incident (IMC) was not automatically shared back to the user as expected, despite recorded demos showing that it should be shared automatically when the agent creates the incident. The root cause is unclear (e.g., chat closed before saving, configuration differences, or defects).
risks.impact_description: If the incident (IMC) details are not consistently and automatically shared back to users at the end of agent chat sessions, customers may not receive confirmation or reference numbers for their cases. This can lead to confusion, repeat contacts, and reduced trust in the new chat channel. Inconsistent behavior across environments or users also complicates training and makes it harder for HCL agents to follow a standard workflow.
risks.mitigation: 1) Reproduce the scenario reported by the HCL agent, validating the sequence of steps (when the incident is created, when the chat is closed). 2) Compare configuration and behavior with the recorded demo flow where automatic sharing worked correctly, to identify any discrepancies (e.g., scripting, workflow changes, environment differences). 3) Engage the reporting agent (via Nitin) to review their exact steps and confirm whether the chat may have been closed before saving the incident. 4) Fix any configuration or workflow issues and re-test across multiple agents. 5) Document the correct procedure and update training so agents understand when the IMC will be shared automatically and what to do if it is not.
risks.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

risks.title: Missing Service Associations in AIOps-generated incidents may delay Datadog cutover
risks.description: Legal Tracker incidents created via AIOps in ServiceNow are missing service associations (impacted service mappings) or have them populated incorrectly. As of 12-May, this is called out as an LT blocker and work-in-progress item owned by Doug, with the project explicitly stating that Datadog direct incident creation cannot be cut off until the service association issue is resolved.
risks.impact_description: If impacted services continue to be missing from or incorrectly populated in AIOps-generated incidents, the team will be unable to safely disable Datadog’s direct incident creation for Legal Tracker. This will prolong the dual-run period, maintain duplicate/parallel incidents, and delay full realization of AIOps benefits such as reduced incident volume and improved routing. It may also erode stakeholder confidence if incidents lack correct service context, complicating impact assessment and communications during incidents.
risks.mitigation: Continue treating the missing service association as a critical blocker for Legal Tracker cutover. Doug and Yash to (1) analyze current CI and service-mapping logic used by Event Management and incident creation flows; (2) update mapping rules so that service associations are derived correctly from Datadog payload fields (e.g., Asset Insight ID, service tags) and CI bindings; (3) validate behaviour on recent Legal Tracker incidents to confirm services populate as expected; and (4) only after consistent service association is confirmed, plan and execute the cutover step to disable Datadog-driven incident creation for Legal Tracker. Document the final mapping approach as part of the central configuration standards so it can be reused for future products.

risks.title: Knowledge base hygiene & scope creep
risks.description: Large volumes of legacy KB articles and unclear ownership, risking VA accuracy and MVP focus.
risks.impact_description: Large volumes of legacy KB articles and unclear ownership, risking VA accuracy and MVP focus. In the April 29, 2026 KB planning call, the team reconfirmed that ~886 KBs exist, with ~539 currently marked 'keep', but many of these (e.g., Citrix/WebEx-related) are likely outdated. AI-based selection is driven by full content, not just file names, so even after identifying a top 100 KB set, unreviewed KBs may still be surfaced. If this clean‑up and refresh is not completed, Now Assist may continue to return incorrect or conflicting KBs, undermining user trust and delaying broader rollout.
risks.mitigation: Review all ~886 KBs and assign KB owners, retire or archive out‑of‑scope or outdated articles (e.g., legacy Citrix/WebEx content), and curate a high‑quality subset (initially ~100 KBs) for Now Assist. Coordinate with ServiceDeskLeads SMEs (e.g., Rashid), knowledge manager (Prastuti), and IT Ops to categorize ~500 service desk–relevant KBs into: (1) self‑help (end‑user facing), (2) service desk internal only, and (3) remove/archive. Use Bineesh’s Excel working copy (with AI‑identified top 100 candidates) as the baseline, but perform human review to confirm which KBs to keep, merge, update, or delete. Ensure that obsolete KBs are removed from the Now Assist index so they are no longer considered by the AI.
