dependencies.title: Service Management
dependencies.description: How / where CCE lines up in the onboarding plan to AIOps / Event Mgmt

dependencies.title: FedRAMP governance approval and AIOps plugin enablement before ServiceNow clone
dependencies.description: AIOps integration for FedRAMP environments depends on completing FedRAMP governance documentation and enabling the required ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management plugins before the scheduled ServiceNow clone over the weekend so that configurations are cascaded to lower environments.
dependencies.dependent_on: FedRAMP governance/compliance review and ServiceNow AIOps plugin configuration managed by ROE, TIM and Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth
dependencies.consumer: AIOps/Event Management implementation in FedRAMP-scoped ServiceNow environments
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If FedRAMP governance documentation is not completed and required AIOps plugins are not enabled before the clone, lower environments may not have the necessary configurations to support AIOps testing and validation in FedRAMP scope, potentially delaying compliance approval and rollout for those environments.
dependencies.mitigation: If the clone occurs before governance documentation or plugin enablement is complete, perform a follow-up configuration pass on lower environments post-clone, and coordinate a subsequent clone or targeted migration to propagate AIOps plugins and settings once FedRAMP approval is obtained.

dependencies.title: Enable AIOps/Event Management in FedRAMP ServiceNow instance
dependencies.description: AIOps/Event Management rollout for FedRAMP-hosted applications (including HighQ and other FedRAMP services) depends on enabling and configuring the same AIOps/Event Management modules and integrations in the FedRAMP ServiceNow environment as in the enterprise instance, while complying with FedRAMP-specific approval and compliance requirements.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow FedRAMP instance configuration, FedRAMP compliance approvals, and guidance from Vinay Kumar and FedRAMP representatives
dependencies.consumer: FedRAMP-hosted applications requiring AIOps/Event Management (e.g., HighQ and other FedRAMP services)
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If AIOps/Event Management is not enabled in the FedRAMP ServiceNow instance in a timely manner, FedRAMP applications will continue to generate unmanaged alert noise, delaying noise reduction and correlation benefits and creating divergence between enterprise and FedRAMP operational models.
dependencies.mitigation: Perform an assessment of current enterprise AIOps configuration, mirror only necessary modules into FedRAMP, ensure AI training data sharing is disabled per FedRAMP requirements, and involve a FedRAMP project/compliance representative early to validate the approach and approvals before enabling features.

dependencies.title: Resolution of CI/service association behaviour by CMDB resource and ServiceNow consultant
dependencies.description: Legal Tracker AIOps alert management and incident routing depend on a CMDB resource (identified by John) and ServiceNow consultant Doug completing analysis and configuration changes to fix CI–service association behaviour so that impacted services populate correctly in AIOps-generated incidents.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow CMDB expert resource identified by John and Doug’s configuration changes to CI/service association logic
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow AIOps/Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker and future onboarded products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If CI/service association behaviour is not corrected in a timely manner, impacted services will remain missing from AIOps-generated incidents, making alert categorization and routing difficult and preventing cutover from legacy Datadog-direct incident creation. This will delay full realization of AIOps benefits and may erode stakeholder confidence.
dependencies.mitigation: Talia Loch to schedule a follow-up session next week with the identified CMDB resource and Doug to review design options and agree next steps. In the interim, continue using the temporary approach of passing service and priority from Datadog while closely monitoring incident behaviour, and keep Legal Tracker stakeholders informed that cutover is dependent on this dependency being resolved.

dependencies.title: ServiceNow vendor configuration of event rules, responder rules, and mappings
dependencies.description: The project relies on the ServiceNow vendor (Doug and team) to define and adjust event rules, alert correlation, CI binding logic, and incident mapping logic in the dev instance and to prepare these for promotion to production.
dependencies.dependent_on: ServiceNow professional services team
dependencies.consumer: TR AIOps / Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker and future products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If vendor rule and mapping work is delayed, the team cannot fully validate CI binding, incident creation behaviour, or implement advanced correlation and responder rules, potentially delaying go-live.
dependencies.mitigation: Use a minimal set of out-of-the-box rules plus three TR-specific rules for initial go-live; capture vendor changes in update sets for later refinement; maintain existing Datadog→ServiceNow incident integration as fallback.

dependencies.title: Establish monitoring governance practice and ownership for Legal Tracker event management
dependencies.description: Formal monitoring governance must be in place so Datadog and Azure Alerts remain the detection layer under a controlled, standardized configuration model. This includes standardized thresholds for infrastructure monitors (~20%), auditing and enforcement of classification standards, and clearly defined ownership of monitor configuration governance for Legal Tracker (and later other products) before and during AIOps rollout.

owner.name: Service Management / GCC monitoring governance lead (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

dependencies.dependent_on: Monitoring governance practice and owner (GCC / Platform Engineering) being defined and operational
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Event Management implementation for Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a formal monitoring governance practice and owner, Legal Tracker monitors may continue to use inconsistent thresholds and classifications, leading to noisy or misclassified events entering ServiceNow. This will reduce the effectiveness of filtering, prioritization, and correlation, and could undermine confidence in the AIOps solution.
dependencies.mitigation: Proceed with Legal Tracker using interim governance based on existing Datadog hygiene standards while accelerating definition of a formal governance model. Use Legal Tracker as the pilot to refine governance artifacts (policies, review process, exception handling) and then institutionalize them via GCC and Platform Engineering.

dependencies.title: Select and implement integration mechanism for consolidating monitoring sources into ServiceNow
dependencies.description: To redirect events from Datadog and Azure Alerts into the ServiceNow event table, an integration mechanism must be selected and implemented (e.g., Lambda-based integration vs Service Graph Connector). Monitor inventory and integration design must support consolidation of Datadog, Azure Alerts, and cloud-native monitors into a single event ingestion path for Legal Tracker.
dependencies.dependent_on: Chosen integration mechanism (e.g., AWS Lambda integration, Service Graph Connector) and completed monitor inventory for Legal Tracker
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Event Management ingestion for Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If an integration mechanism is not selected and implemented in time, Legal Tracker events from Datadog, Azure Alerts, and other cloud-native monitors cannot be redirected into the ServiceNow event table. This will block the architectural shift from direct-to-incident to event-first processing and delay all downstream capabilities (filtering, correlation, prioritization).
dependencies.mitigation: Use the simplest viable integration (e.g., existing Datadog webhook plus incremental Azure integration) as an MVP while evaluating Service Graph Connector or Lambda for longer-term standardization. Maintain the legacy Datadog→incident path as fallback until consolidated ingestion is proven.

dependencies.title: Define event taxonomy for informational, warning, and exception events
dependencies.description: An event taxonomy must be defined for Legal Tracker monitors to distinguish informational, warning, and exception events. This taxonomy is the basis for filtering, classification rules, and event prioritization in ServiceNow Event Management and will guide which events generate incidents versus being suppressed or treated as informational.

owner.name: Incident Management and AIOps design leads (e.g., Heymann, Damian; Rutherford, Chris)

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreement on Legal Tracker event taxonomy (informational vs warning vs exception) and documentation of how it maps to ServiceNow severity and incident policies
dependencies.consumer: Event filtering and prioritization configuration for Legal Tracker in ServiceNow
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without a defined event taxonomy, filtering and prioritization rules cannot be consistently implemented. This will result in inconsistent suppression of informational events, potential creation of non-actionable incidents, and difficulty standardizing behaviour across monitors and products.
dependencies.mitigation: Draft an initial, directional taxonomy for Legal Tracker based on current incident practices and iterate during early AIOps usage. Use lessons learned to refine and formalize the taxonomy before broader rollout.

dependencies.title: Define incident creation policy for AIOps events
dependencies.description: An explicit incident creation policy must be defined for Legal Tracker to decide when correlated events should generate incidents versus remaining as events or being handled through auto-remediation. This governs whether every actionable event creates an incident or whether some remediation can occur under event records only.

owner.name: AD Al-Ghourabi (TR Technology) with input from Service Management leadership

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreement on incident creation criteria (e.g., only exceptions create incidents; some remediations handled at event level) and configuration of corresponding rules in ServiceNow
dependencies.consumer: ServiceNow Incident Management behaviour for AIOps-generated events in Legal Tracker
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If incident creation policy remains undefined, AIOps may either create too many incidents (replicating the 1:1 pattern) or too few (risking missed incidents). This uncertainty will delay tuning of incident rules and hinder safe cutover from the legacy Datadog incident path.
dependencies.mitigation: Define a provisional incident creation policy for Legal Tracker (e.g., incidents only for exception-level events and primary correlated groups) and validate during a controlled observation period, adjusting policy before applying it as a standard for other products.

dependencies.title: Define notification tiers for after-hours paging vs next-business-day alerts
dependencies.description: Notification tiering rules must be defined to determine what event or incident severities trigger after-hours pages versus next-business-day notifications for Legal Tracker. This is needed to reduce notification noise and align on-call behaviour with the new alert-centric AIOps model.

owner.name: Service Management / Incident Management leadership (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

dependencies.dependent_on: Agreed set of notification tiers mapping event/incident severity to after-hours paging vs next-business-day notification, and corresponding configuration in ServiceNow on-call and notification modules
dependencies.consumer: On-call paging and notification behaviour for Legal Tracker and future AIOps-onboarded products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Without defined notification tiers, teams may continue to receive excessive after-hours pages for non-critical events or insufficient notifications for true exceptions. This undermines one of the key benefits of AIOps (notification reduction) and may cause resistance from on-call engineers.
dependencies.mitigation: Adopt an interim rule (e.g., only P1/P2 incidents from primary correlated alerts generate after-hours pages) based on current practice, then refine notification tiers once incident creation and prioritization behaviour is stable.

dependencies.title: Improve KB and runbook quality to enable phased automation and AI-assisted resolutions
dependencies.description: KB articles and runbooks must be improved for Legal Tracker so that incidents arriving with enriched context from correlated events can leverage reliable remediation content. This is a prerequisite for introducing automated remediation and AI-recommended resolutions in later phases of Event Management.

owner.name: Knowledge management and AIOps remediation lead (e.g., Doug – ServiceNow consultant – in partnership with GCC)

dependencies.dependent_on: Consolidated, high-quality KB articles and runbooks for top Legal Tracker incident scenarios, integrated with ServiceNow knowledge and Flow Designer
dependencies.consumer: Later-phase AIOps capabilities (automated remediation, Now Assist / LEAP suggestions) for Legal Tracker and other products
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If KB and runbook quality is not improved, later-phase AIOps capabilities such as AI-suggested resolutions and automated remediation workflows will be ineffective or inaccurate. This will limit MTTR improvements and delay realization of higher-stage value from the AIOps program.
dependencies.mitigation: Delay automation-focused capabilities for Legal Tracker until core ingestion, correlation, and incident behaviour are stable, while running a parallel workstream to uplift KB/runbook content for the most frequent incident types.

decisions.title: Use out-of-the-box ServiceNow AIOps incident priority calculation instead of custom impact/urgency event fields
decisions.description: The team will not persist custom impact and urgency fields on ServiceNow event records to mirror Datadog values. Instead, Datadog monitors will be configured with appropriate severity and priority, and ServiceNow will use its out‑of‑the‑box logic (including severity and alert type) to calculate incident impact and urgency.
decisions.rationale: Custom impact/urgency fields add complexity and diverge from the out‑of‑the‑box product design. Using ServiceNow’s standard AIOps logic simplifies maintenance and ensures consistency as the solution scales across products, even though it requires additional work to train teams on correct use of severity and priority in Datadog.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Introduce custom impact/urgency fields on events populated directly from Datadog and map them to incidents.
2) Stay out-of-the-box by configuring severity/priority in Datadog and relying on ServiceNow’s AIOps engine to derive impact/urgency for incidents.
3) Hybrid approach using both custom fields and AIOps calculations.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow CI binding and incident creation behaviour; Datadog monitor configuration standards; removal of custom event fields added by Yash.

decisions.title: Legal Tracker AIOps to proceed using minimal rule set (out-of-the-box plus three TR rules)
decisions.description: For Legal Tracker go‑live, the team will rely primarily on out‑of‑the‑box ServiceNow event rules with a small set of three Thomson Reuters–specific rules, rather than waiting to design a comprehensive custom rule library.
decisions.rationale: Using a minimal rule set allows the team to start realizing AIOps value sooner and avoids over‑engineering for the first product. Additional rules can be added iteratively once real event data and behaviours are better understood.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Design extensive custom event and correlation rules for Legal Tracker before go‑live.
2) Use out-of-the-box rules only.
3) Use out-of-the-box rules plus a small number of TR-specific rules for initial go-live.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow vendor rule configuration; Datadog payload contents; cutover planning for incidents.

decisions.title: Event forwarding from ServiceNow production to dev/QA is not a go-live blocker
decisions.description: The team agreed that ServiceNow event forwarding from production to lower environments (dev and QA) is helpful for testing but is not required for the initial Legal Tracker go‑live.
decisions.rationale: Forwarding allows consistent test data across environments, but its absence does not prevent AIOps from functioning in production. Delaying go‑live until forwarding is perfect would unnecessarily slow delivery.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Make event forwarding a prerequisite for go-live.
2) Treat forwarding as a post-go-live improvement while focusing on production connectivity and incident behaviour.
decisions.dependencies_linked: ServiceNow event forwarding configuration managed by Yash; Datadog webhook pointing to production.

decisions.title: Pilot parallel incident run in QA before enabling AIOps incidents in production
decisions.description: Before AIOps begins creating incidents in production for Legal Tracker, the team plans a time‑boxed parallel run in a QA environment where AIOps incidents can be compared to existing Datadog‑driven incidents, to assess completeness and volume reduction.
decisions.rationale: A QA parallel run allows the team to validate that AIOps does not miss important incidents and provides incident volume reduction, without risking production operations or confusing support teams with duplicates.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Immediately enable AIOps incident creation in production and disable Datadog incidents.
2) Run AIOps alerts only in production and compare manually.
3) Run AIOps incidents in QA for a short period while keeping production unchanged, then decide on production enablement.
decisions.dependencies_linked: QA environment setup; ability to mirror event data into QA; cutover plan for disabling Datadog incidents per product.

decisions.title: Use single NAVA pilot group for Agent Chat access and avoid creating additional groups
decisions.description: HCL pilot agents for Agent Chat will use the existing NAVA pilot users group for access. No additional groups will be created or granted access unless absolutely required, to keep access management simple and centralized.
decisions.rationale: Centralizing Agent Chat access through a single NAVA pilot group simplifies administration, reduces configuration complexity, and minimizes inconsistencies in role assignments. It also avoids proliferation of redundant groups that could cause access discrepancies.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Create separate groups for different HCL cohorts; 2) Reuse existing HCL service desk groups; 3) Use a single NAVA pilot group for all pilot users.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Agent Chat access configuration for HCL testers; NAVA pilot user group role assignments.
decisions.source_file_name: Service Desk AI automation WF Daily Sync.docx

decisions.title: Track Agent Chat issues and access problems in a shared Excel for continuous updates
decisions.description: All Agent Chat issues and access-related problems will be tracked in a shared Excel file, kept open for HCL testers to add new items continuously. TR (including Srinu and Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth) will use this tracker to prioritize and resolve items across UK and ISU hours.
decisions.rationale: Using a shared Excel tracker allows real-time capture of issues from multiple HCL testers without waiting for batch updates, enabling better prioritization and coordination between TR and HCL teams across time zones.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Collect issues via periodic emails; 2) Have HCL compile and send issues in batches; 3) Maintain a shared Excel tracker for continuous entry and prioritization.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Resolution of Agent Chat access issues; coordination between HCL testers and TR support (Srinu, Kolluru, Prudhvi Yaswanth).

decisions.title: Define support process for UK and ISU hours via Gandikota, Srinu and escalation through L, Kiran Kumar
decisions.description: During UK and ISU hours, Gandikota, Srinu will be the primary support contact for Agent Chat issues. HCL testers can also reach out to L, Kiran Kumar, who will route issues to Srinu or Male, Prashanth as appropriate.
decisions.rationale: Assigning a clear support owner for UK and ISU hours ensures prompt resolution of Agent Chat issues encountered by HCL testers and clarifies escalation paths across time zones.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Ad-hoc support via whoever is available; 2) Dedicated UK/ISU support via Gandikota, Srinu with escalation through L, Kiran Kumar; 3) Route all issues only through daily sync meetings.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Timely resolution of HCL Agent Chat issues; effectiveness of the shared Excel issue tracker.

decisions.title: Define notification tiers for after-hours vs next-business-day alerts
decisions.description: The team must decide what severity levels and event types trigger after-hours paging versus next-business-day notification for Legal Tracker, based on correlated incidents and event severity.

decision_owner.name: Service Management / Incident Management leadership (e.g., Heymann, Damian)

decisions.rationale: Tiered notifications reduce alert fatigue by ensuring that teams are only paged for true service-impacting exceptions while less severe events are handled during business hours.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Only P1 (and possibly P2) incidents generated from primary correlated alerts trigger after-hours pages; others become next-business-day notifications.
2) Include some high-severity warnings in after-hours paging for specific services.
3) Maintain current incident-based paging behaviour initially and gradually introduce alert-driven paging tiers.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Incident creation policy, on-call configuration on the ServiceNow alert/incident tables, and Legal Tracker on-call agreements.

decisions.title: Timebox QA observation period for new AIOps product onboardings
decisions.description: For new products being onboarded to AIOps/Event Management (such as ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM), the QA observation period for running their monitors and alerts through ServiceNow will be timeboxed to no more than three to four weeks, with a target of one to two weeks, to avoid prolonged onboarding and encourage iterative movement towards production.
decisions.rationale: AD emphasized the need to avoid letting QA observation drag on, preferring short, iterative cycles so that teams can move to production quickly while still gaining sufficient insight into alert grouping and rule behaviour.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Run QA observation for an open-ended period until all issues are resolved.
2) Timebox QA observation to a maximum of three to four weeks with a target of one to two weeks before deciding on production onboarding.
3) Skip QA observation and onboard directly to production using enterprise rules.
decisions.dependencies_linked: AIOps onboarding plans for ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM; Legal Tracker lessons learned; QA data ingestion for GTM4 and SIAM.

decisions.title: Proceed with onboarding ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel with caution
decisions.description: The team will initiate AIOps/Event Management onboarding for both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel, while closely monitoring the workload and alert volumes from GTM4 and leveraging QA observation to understand and manage the expected high volume of findings.
decisions.rationale: Both GTM4 and SIAM generate significant alert volume and their teams are ready to engage. Despite concerns about the effort required for GTM4, the group agreed that starting with both, with a cautious and timeboxed QA approach, provides maximum learning and impact.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Onboard only ONESOURCE GTM4 first, then onboard SIAM later.
2) Onboard only SIAM first.
3) Onboard both ONESOURCE GTM4 and SIAM in parallel, with a timeboxed QA observation period and readiness assessments.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Readiness assessments for GTM4 and SIAM monitors; Datadog webhooks and QA event flow; Legal Tracker feedback influencing configuration adjustments.

decisions.title: Prioritize AIOps capabilities in sequence: ingestion → correlation & prioritization → notification → root cause & resolutions
decisions.description: For Legal Tracker, capability rollout will follow a defined order: (1) Alert ingestion (event-first processing) as the foundation; (2) Intelligent correlation as the highest-value capability; (3) Event prioritization and notification reduction; and (4) later-phase root cause identification and AI-suggested resolutions once correlation and data volume are sufficient.
decisions.rationale: Sequencing capabilities ensures a stable foundation before introducing advanced features. Ingestion and correlation deliver the highest immediate value by breaking the 1:1 event-to-incident pattern, while notification reduction and advanced root cause/AI resolutions depend on stable correlation, prioritization, and sufficient historical data.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Implement all capabilities at once (ingestion, correlation, prioritization, notification, root cause, AI resolutions).
2) Focus only on ingestion and correlation for MVP and defer all other capabilities.
3) Implement capabilities in the chosen sequence: ingestion → correlation & prioritization → notification → root cause & resolutions.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Ingestion readiness (integration mechanism), correlation tuning, event taxonomy definition, KB/runbook quality, and sufficient historical incident data.

decisions.title: Adopt deterministic Datadog monitor priority as MVP incident priority for Legal Tracker
decisions.description: For the Legal Tracker MVP, ServiceNow’s out-of-the-box incident priority calculation has been disabled and Datadog monitor priority is passed deterministically through to the incident priority. This patch aligns incident priority with existing Legal Tracker practices while the team gains experience with AIOps and prepares to tune non-deterministic priority behaviour in lower environments.
decisions.rationale: Legal Tracker and GCC are accustomed to deterministic incident priority based directly on Datadog monitors. Early trials of AIOps-native, non-deterministic priority were perceived as too aggressive (e.g., raising priority after only two alerts). To avoid blocking the production MVP and to meet previously communicated timelines, the team agreed to a temporary deterministic configuration as an MVP, while planning a ‘laboratory’ effort in dev/QA to tune native AIOps scoring before reintroducing it.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Keep ServiceNow out-of-the-box non-deterministic incident priority (based on CI importance, blast radius, and alert state).
2) Temporarily disable AIOps-native priority and deterministically map Datadog monitor priority directly to incident priority for Legal Tracker.
3) Delay Legal Tracker MVP until non-deterministic behaviour is fully tuned and accepted by the product team.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Linked to risk 'Reliance on temporary customizations for incident priority and CI binding instead of AIOps-native behaviour' and dependency 'ServiceNow vendor configuration of event rules, responder rules, and mappings'; also interacts with future tuning sessions in dev/QA for non-deterministic priority.

decisions.title: Use incident data from new ServiceNow instance (January 2026 onward) without backfilling legacy instance data for initial AIOps onboarding prioritization
decisions.description: For the first round of AIOps onboarding prioritization, the team will rely on incident data extracted from the new ServiceNow instance (approximately January 2026 onward) combined with existing alert data, and will not pursue extracting or merging historical incident data from the legacy ServiceNow instance at this stage.
decisions.rationale: Paul Berry judged that five months of incident data from the new ServiceNow instance is sufficient to reveal patterns and identify candidate applications for the top 40 AIOps migration list. Fetching and merging legacy incident data would consume additional effort without materially improving the directional signals needed for round-one prioritization. Any anomalies (e.g., applications with high recent incidents but lower historical alert ranking) will themselves be useful signals to investigate rather than reasons to delay decisions.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Extract and merge legacy ServiceNow incident data with new-instance data to create a full-year, like-for-like incident view.
2) Limit analysis to incident data from the new ServiceNow instance (January 2026 onward) and compare with existing alert data for prioritization.
3) Restrict both alert and incident datasets to a common time window starting January 2026, requiring additional re-extraction but still avoiding legacy system queries.
decisions.dependencies_linked: AIOps product prioritization spreadsheet; action for Rodriguez, Luis Jorge to add incident data column from new ServiceNow instance.
decisions.source_file_name: AIOps Product Onboarding Reg Sync 30 Apr.docx

decisions.title: Define ingestion scope for Legal Tracker monitors entering ServiceNow
decisions.description: The team needs to decide whether all Legal Tracker monitors will send events into the ServiceNow event table from the outset, or whether AIOps will start with a defined subset of monitors and expand in later phases.

decision_owner.name: TR AIOps leadership (e.g., Rutherford, Chris; AD Al-Ghourabi)

decisions.rationale: Ingestion scope affects both risk and value. Including all monitors maximizes observability and correlation opportunities but may introduce noise and configuration risk; starting with a subset reduces initial complexity but may limit early value and require additional rollout planning.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Route all Legal Tracker monitors into ServiceNow from day one.
2) Start with a defined subset of monitors (e.g., infrastructure and critical synthetics) and expand in Phase 2.
3) Pilot with only specific regions or monitor types before full ingestion.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Event ingestion dependencies (integration mechanism, monitor inventory) and filtering/correlation configuration for Legal Tracker.

decisions.title: Define Legal Tracker event taxonomy for informational, warning, and exception events
decisions.description: The project must agree on what constitutes informational, warning, and exception events for Legal Tracker monitors. This taxonomy will drive filtering, suppression, and classification rules in ServiceNow Event Management.

decision_owner.name: Incident Management and AIOps design leads (e.g., Heymann, Damian; Rutherford, Chris)

decisions.rationale: A clear event taxonomy is necessary to consistently suppress non-actionable events, classify exceptions that should create incidents, and align monitor configurations with business impact expectations.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Adopt a simple three-level taxonomy (informational, warning, exception) aligned with current incident severity definitions.
2) Use a more granular taxonomy (e.g., multiple warning levels) for synthetics versus infrastructure.
3) Defer to existing Datadog priority levels and map them directly to ServiceNow severities with minimal new taxonomy definition.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Event prioritization configuration, monitor classification standards, and Datadog hygiene programme alignment.

decisions.title: Set incident creation policy for AIOps-correlated events
decisions.description: A decision is required on whether every actionable event should create an incident or whether some remediation can occur at the event level without incident records, based on correlation and classification outcomes.

decision_owner.name: AD Al-Ghourabi (TR Technology) with Service Management leadership

decisions.rationale: Incident creation policy determines the balance between visibility and noise. Creating incidents for all actionable events maintains legacy visibility but risks retaining the 1:1 event-to-incident pattern; restricting incidents to true exceptions reduces noise but requires strong confidence in correlation and remediation processes.
decisions.options_considered:
1) Every actionable event creates an incident.
2) Only exception-level events (as defined by the event taxonomy) create incidents; informational and warning events remain as events.
3) Some remediations are executed and recorded at the event level only, with incidents created only if remediation fails or service impact is detected.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Correlation rule tuning, event taxonomy definition, and incident management SLAs for Legal Tracker.

decisions.title: No customization of interaction record for Amazon Connect CTI; use out-of-the-box interaction view
decisions.description: For the Amazon Connect–ServiceNow CTI integration, the interaction record opened for agents must remain the out-of-the-box interaction view (showing user details, recent tasks/interactions, and assigned assets). TR and HCL agreed that no new fields or layout customizations will be implemented on this interaction record as part of the CTI URL change; the focus is solely on providing a URL that opens the standard interaction record instead of an incident.
decisions.rationale: ServiceNow vendor (John) recommended using out-of-the-box CTI capabilities and the Amazon Connect connector rather than building custom APIs or customized interaction forms. Keeping the interaction record standard reduces maintenance, avoids high-risk customizations, and ensures future compatibility, while still meeting HCLs requirement to see user details and related records when a call is received.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Customize the interaction record (new fields/layout changes) to meet HCLs expectations; 2) Use the out-of-the-box interaction record and only adjust the CTI URL to open it; 3) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and new flows in a future phase.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Amazon Connect (AWS) CTI integration with ServiceNow and Virtual Agent; Risk: Amazon Connect CTI URL misconfiguration may delay IVR demo and cutover; Action: Provide corrected CTI interaction URL for Amazon ConnectServiceNow integration.
decisions.source_file_name: Issue with Amazon CTI URL __ RITM0147285 & REQ0145658.docx

decisions.title: Prioritize minimal-change CTI URL fix for Amazon Connect migration and defer connector-based redesign
decisions.description: For the immediate Avaya-to-Amazon Connect migration, TR and HCL will prioritize a minimal-change solution that adjusts the existing CTI URL so it opens an interaction record (instead of an incident) using current architecture, rather than redesigning the integration around the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector. A connector-based redesign and proof of concept (POC) may be pursued later once the basic migration is stable and time/resources permit.
decisions.rationale: HCL reported that almost all technical and UAT activities for the Amazon Connect migration are complete, with only the URL landing page behavior pending. ServiceNow vendor guidance and internal review indicated that re-architecting around the Amazon Connect connector would require additional time, effort, and POC work, which the team cannot afford before go-live. A minimal-change CTI URL fix enables timely migration while keeping open the option to adopt the connector later.
decisions.options_considered: 1) Redesign the integration using the ServiceNow Amazon Connect connector and perform a POC in sandbox before go-live; 2) Adjust the existing CTI URL and parameters to open an interaction record instead of an incident, keeping the current architecture; 3) Continue with the current incident-landing behavior and accept the UX gap.

latest_report.content:
**under review**

## Executive Summary

Cloud Optimization is driving standardized FinOps practices, application modernization to AWS, and governance via the Cloud SteerCo so that CT&O reduces average cloud waste by 7%, improves cloud value transparency, and meets the 2026 cloud spend goal. The program combines modernization workstreams (e.g. Cobalt, GTM4, GST), FinOps transformation, and a Cloud Modernization Office to align technology, finance, and sustainability outcomes.

Against 2026 targets, Win-to-Linux modernizations are 20% in progress with recent Onvio Discovery completion; remaining 5% pipeline identified to drive toward the 25% year-end goal. Graviton adoption remains at 55% versus an 80% target and has declined 1 point since March. Cloud forecasting accuracy is at 2.2% variance against a 1% target and 9 of 15 tech organizations are within the 7% cloud waste threshold, up by 2 organizations since March but still short of full coverage.

Overall status is AMBER, driven by a $2.4M gap between the CIO’s $3.5M FY26 cloud savings target and the current Optimize TR Estate pipeline of approximately $1.1M (with ~$568K realized). Offsetting this risk, Cloud Cost Optimization delivered $1.6M in May savings, moving Product Engineering to 109% and the program overall to 91% of the FY26 target.

## Path to Green

Close the CIO savings gap by expanding the FinOps opportunity pipeline—including Ongoing alliance with FinOps and CIO Finance to evaluate current challenge LE—while aligning on cloud spend targets with awareness to Cloud SteerCo, to include prioritizing Platform Engineering red lever opportunity for increased in year savings & scheduling deep dives with CIO application teams to evaluate current cloud spend prioritizing high forecast projections (June 26)

Remove key Modernization production blockers and de-risk delivery by:

-   Finalizing GST SQL contention and batch stability validation and securing leadership-approved cutover (May 22)
    
-   Confirmation from GTM4 regarding Reporting Services decision, and committing to a content modernization plan (May 26)
    
-   Cobalt's Website timeline impacted 2026 savings - driving (a) confirming Website POC viability and locking delivery scope/capacity (date tbd, working with product team to redefine); (b) securing development commitments and migration plans for five Elastic Search instances (May 29); (c) finalizing phased S3 Document Store approach with updated savings profile by May 22.
    

## Milestones

-   Deliver GST Modernization Phase 1B (Batch Services) and Phase 2A (FSx) by June 19 to stabilize AWS-based GST workloads and realize cost and reliability benefits.
    
-   Deploy the AI-powered FinOps Assistant (TRUCCR Bot) and complete Q2 EPC Business Case Tracker – Modernization reporting by June 30 to enhance self-service FinOps insights and ensure EPC reporting compliance.
    
-   Finalize the Onvio Modernization project plan based on Discovery inputs from Product stakeholders and the PLE Architect (by 3 June)
    
-   Complete Datadog cost efficiency initiatives no later than May 30 to advance Datadog as a cost optimization platform and increase identified savings opportunities.

risks.title: GTM4 Content PROD Cluster Migration
risks.description:
The GTM4 Content PROD environment includes three critical content clusters with high customer dependency. Migrating these clusters requires re‑initializing database replication from scratch, which is time‑consuming and highly sensitive to maintenance windows. There is a risk that replication may not complete within the agreed downtime window. Similar challenges were experienced during the earlier on‑prem to cloud migration, where replication delays caused operational issues.
Additionally, a future GCP content migration is already planned, which may require repeating the same replication process—potentially resulting in two customer downtimes if not carefully planned.
Risk Impact:
Potential extended PROD downtime impacting customers
Increased operational and reputational risk if replication fails or overruns
Need for multiple customer downtimes (current migration + future GCP migration)
Possible schedule changes to GTM4 Phase / Wave execution
Minor cost impact (~$4.5K/month) if clusters are retained longer as‑is, but operational risk outweighs cost considerations.
Risk Probability:
Medium – based on past replication challenges and dependency complexity, pending business decision. 
Current Status / Decision Pending:
Risk logged primarily as a decision risk
Business discussion scheduled to assess tolerance for downtime vs. deferring migration
Final approach may change based on Business Unit agreement
Mitigation / Next Steps:
Review and align with the Business Unit on acceptable downtime and migration approach
Explore deferring migration of these clusters to align with future GCP migration, avoiding double downtime
Document final business decision in ADO and update RAID accordingly (close or re‑categorize risk)

risks.title: GST Phase 1B - SQL contention affecting all Batch Services
risks.description: A SQL contention issue is impacting batch processing and customer-facing workloads in GST Phase 1B. The contention must be resolved and validated via regression and scale testing before production cutover; otherwise, production stability and customer experience could be compromised, and the production cutover date may slip from mid‑May to late May.
risks.impact_description: If the SQL contention issue is not fully resolved and validated before production cutover, batch processing performance and stability will be degraded, potentially impacting all GST batch services and customers. This could force a delay of the production cutover (from May 16 into late May), extend the timeline for realizing cloud cost savings (estimated at $9K per month), and increase the likelihood of post‑cutover incidents and customer disruptions.
risks.mitigation: Complete the SQL contention fix and then run comprehensive regression and scale testing. Finalize and agree a detailed testing and cutover plan (targeted to be set in the April 14 meeting). Only proceed to production once: (1) the fix is implemented, (2) regression and scale tests pass with no critical defects, (3) the cutover plan is confirmed with stakeholders, and (4) leadership approves the production release. Use short schedule flexibility (shifting cutover from May 16 to late May if needed) to prioritize stability and protect customer experience.

risks.title: GST Phase 1B - GST Batch Transfer Issue not resolved
risks.description: During GST Phase 1B migration from the AMS environment to native AWS, a critical defect was discovered: the GST batch transfer operation (moving tax return data and locators between internal systems or client sub-accounts) consistently fails in both AMS-to-AWS flows and in AWS (FSx-backed) environments. A potential fix is under development and testing, but until it is fully validated this remains a high-impact risk.
risks.impact_description: If the GST batch transfer issue is not fully resolved and validated before go-live, a core tax data transfer process will fail in production. This could cause widespread production system failures, incorrect or incomplete data transfers between systems and client sub-accounts, and serious customer impact during critical tax processing periods. The Phase 1B go-live would likely need to be delayed, undermining the modernization schedule and delaying realization of cloud cost savings.
risks.mitigation: Complete the GST batch transfer fix and validate it in lower environments, followed by full regression testing to ensure no critical defects remain. Once testing passes, finalize a cutover plan with stakeholder alignment and obtain leadership approval prior to production release. Maintain the decision to delay the Phase 1B go-live until after tax season if necessary, prioritizing customer stability and avoiding changes to critical systems during peak tax usage.

If sufficient clusters cannot be migrated in each wave, the current plan to complete production migration in 2026 may not be achievable.
risks.impact_description: If the team cannot include enough production clusters in each migration wave, the GTM4 production database migration from AMS to AWS will extend beyond 2026. This would delay full decommissioning of AMS infrastructure, prolong dual-running costs, limit realization of cloud cost savings and performance benefits, and could create ongoing operational complexity managing two environments for longer than planned.
risks.mitigation: Finalize the number of production clusters per migration wave based on available capacity, adjust wave sizing and schedule to ensure all clusters can be migrated within 2026, and secure any additional resources needed to deliver the planned throughput. If required, re-baseline the migration plan with realistic wave sizes and timelines while maintaining risk controls for production stability.

risks.description: Feasibility risk for the GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services modernization (Phase 3). The modernization depends on validating that Jasper Reports can fully replicate Crystal Reports functionality, including complex reporting logic and handling large datasets. There is a risk that the Proof of Concept (PoC) may be successful only for a limited set of manually converted reports and may not scale or be acceptable for full production rollout.
risks.impact_description: If Jasper Reports cannot match Crystal Reports capabilities at scale, or if the PoC results do not translate into a viable full-production solution for ~1,800 reports, the Reporting Services modernization to Linux may be delayed or fail. It may also require rework to identify and implement an alternative reporting technology, impacting the overall GTM4 Windows to Linux migration timeline and cost savings.
risks.mitigation: Execute the Reporting Services PoC using Jasper Reports to convert a representative subset of Crystal Reports, focusing on complex logic and high-volume datasets, and validate output parity, performance, usability, and business acceptance. Based on PoC outcomes, define a detailed migration plan for the full report set. In parallel, prepare contingency options (such as alternative reporting platforms or a hybrid approach) in case Jasper cannot fully replace Crystal Reports, and clarify next steps if the PoC is unsuccessful.

If adequate scale testing is not completed by April 30, the go-live and associated savings for .NET Modernization Phase 1 (Doc) will be delayed to around May 27, resulting in an estimated loss of approximately $150,000 in planned 2026 savings and a schedule slip against the EPC modernization plan.

4/28 Update - Another scale test is planned for 4/30.  We need 2-3 good tests in QED before we can hotfix into Prod.  Earliest this could happen is May 12 but the release is two days later so this will need to be discussed.
risks.mitigation: Coordinate with stakeholders (including discussing the situation with Jesse Haroldson) to agree on a realistic testing and go-live schedule, adjust the savings date if necessary, and ensure sufficient time and resources are allocated to complete scale testing before the revised target date.

risks.title: Datadog Resource Capacity & Reduced Ability to Identify Savings
risks.description: There is a risk that limited Datadog engineering capacity, including lack of a dedicated lead and competing operational workload, will reduce the team’s ability to proactively identify waste and savings opportunities through Datadog tooling and analysis.
risks.impact_description: If Datadog engineering capacity remains constrained, proactive waste identification and cloud savings discovery using Datadog will slow down. This may reduce visibility into optimisation opportunities, delay or diminish cost savings captured for the CIO organisation, and contribute to missing overall cloud savings targets tied to TRUCCR and related FinOps objectives.
risks.mitigation: Maintain visibility of this risk via RAID item 477891 and explicitly frame it as a capacity-driven risk. Review the risk monthly and keep it open for potential escalation or backfill justification if capacity constraints persist, so that leadership can consider additional staffing or re-prioritisation to restore Datadog’s savings-identification capability.

issues.title: Delayed GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services production migration and decommissioning
issues.description: The GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services production migration will only be partially completed in the May 2026 release, with remaining report pages targeted for completion in the August 2026 release. As a result, the associated Windows servers cannot be decommissioned until August 2026, and only partial (approximately 30–40%) of the originally planned Q2 cost savings will be realized in the interim.
issues.impact_assessment: The phased completion of Reporting Services migration delays full server decommissioning from Q2 2026 to around August 2026. This extends the period of dual‑stack (Windows and Linux) operations and reduces near‑term cost savings to approximately 30–40% of what was planned for Q2, impacting the GTM4 Windows to Linux modernization financial objectives.
issues.dependencies_affecting: GTM4 Windows to Linux Migration Phase 3 – Reporting Services Migration and Decom, including server decommissioning and associated cost optimization goals.
issues.resolution: Complete the remaining Reporting Services pages in the August 2026 release to enable full migration to Linux, after which the legacy Windows servers can be decommissioned and the full cost savings realized. Find out the impacted savings and close the risk and issue.

milestones.name: GTM4 Windows to Linux Migration Phase 2 - Export and import management Production Wave2 Rollout

issues.title: SQL contention issue affecting GST batch services
issues.description: A SQL contention issue is impacting GST batch processing and customers, creating a primary risk to production stability and requiring resolution before production cutover.
issues.impact_assessment: SQL contention is currently affecting GST batch services and customer-facing processing. The issue must be resolved and validated via regression and scale testing before production cutover. Failure to resolve the contention prior to cutover may require shifting the production cutover date from May 16 to later in May, which would delay realization of cloud savings by approximately $9,000 per month and increase the risk of post-cutover stability issues.
issues.dependencies_affecting: GST Phase 1B production cutover schedule and associated cost savings; overall GST modernization milestone completion dates.
issues.resolution: Implement a SQL contention fix, then execute regression and scale testing to validate stability. Finalize a detailed testing and cutover plan, confirm stakeholder alignment, and obtain leadership approval prior to production release.

issues.title: GST batch transfer defect during Phase 1B migration
issues.description: During GST Phase 1B migration from AMS to native AWS, the GST batch transfer operation that moves tax return data (locators) between internal systems or client sub-accounts has been failing consistently in AMS-to-AWS and AWS (FSx-backed) environments in testing.
issues.impact_assessment: The GST batch transfer defect affects a core tax data transfer process. If left unresolved, it could cause serious production system failures and data transfer errors when the migration goes live. To protect customer stability, leadership has already delayed the Phase 1B go-live until after tax season. The issue directly impacts the ability to complete GST Phase 1B migration and realize associated benefits on the original timeline.
issues.dependencies_affecting: GST Phase 1B batch migration timeline; AMS-to-AWS and AWS FSx-backed data flows; production go-live scheduling relative to tax season.
issues.resolution: Develop and deploy a fix for the GST batch transfer process, test the fix in lower environments, conduct regression testing to ensure no critical defects remain, confirm the cutover plan with stakeholders, and obtain leadership approval before proceeding to production.

dependencies.title: Reporting Services modernization dependency on Jasper Reports feasibility
dependencies.description: The success of GTM4 Windows to Linux Reporting Services modernization depends on validating that Jasper Reports can fully replicate Crystal Reports functionality, including complex reporting logic, large datasets, and high‑volume workloads. The Proof of Concept converts a subset of Crystal Reports to a Linux‑compatible solution using Jasper Reports and validates output parity, performance, and usability at scale.
dependencies.dependent_on: Jasper Reports’ ability to functionally and performance‑wise replace Crystal Reports for ~1,800 existing reports and future reporting needs, validated via the Reporting Services PoC.
dependencies.consumer: GTM4 Windows to Linux Migration Phase 3 – Reporting Services Migration and Decom
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If Jasper Reports cannot be validated as a full replacement, or if the PoC does not scale beyond a limited set of manually converted reports, overall Reporting Services modernization timelines may slip, jeopardizing the ability to complete Windows to Linux migration and associated decommissioning within planned dates.
dependencies.mitigation: Develop and agree a contingency plan if the PoC is unsuccessful, including alternative reporting technologies or approaches, revised timelines, and criteria for business acceptance before proceeding to full production rollout.

dependencies.title: Content Main modernization dependency on HVR pattern delivery
dependencies.description: Modernization of GTM4 Content Main services to a Linux‑compatible, containerized architecture depends on the Data Services team delivering an HVR pattern to migrate RDS SQL to Aurora PostgreSQL on AWS. This pattern is required to align with cloud and DevOps standards and to enable use of non‑licensed databases such as PostgreSQL for improved scalability and cost efficiency.
dependencies.dependent_on: Delivery of a reusable HVR pattern by the Data Services team for migrating RDS SQL databases to Aurora PostgreSQL on AWS.
dependencies.consumer: GTM4 Windows to Linux Migration Phase 4 – Modernization of Content Main and associated database modernization workstreams.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays in delivering the HVR pattern will postpone Content Main modernization timelines, delay adoption of Aurora PostgreSQL, and defer expected stability, performance, and cost efficiency benefits, potentially impacting the broader GTM4 cloud transformation schedule.
dependencies.mitigation: Use interim approaches such as maintaining existing RDS SQL deployments, prioritizing pattern development for critical Content Main components, or planning phased adoption of Aurora PostgreSQL once the pattern is available.

dependencies.title: Production migration schedule dependency on cluster capacity per wave
dependencies.description: The GTM4 AMS to AWS DB production migration schedule depends on finalizing how many production clusters can be included in each migration wave. The current plan assumes migrating five clusters per wave, but this capacity has not yet been confirmed.
dependencies.dependent_on: Agreement on and provisioning of sufficient capacity (resources and operational readiness) to migrate up to five production clusters per wave.
dependencies.consumer: GTM4 AMS to AWS DB Migration of Prod servers, including all planned migration and decommission waves scheduled through 2026.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: If sufficient capacity to migrate five clusters per wave is not available or agreed, the existing migration schedule will extend beyond 2026, impacting program completion dates and potentially increasing operating costs for legacy environments.
dependencies.mitigation: Review capacity constraints, adjust the number of clusters per wave as needed, update the migration plan and schedule accordingly, and secure additional resources or staggered waves to achieve completion within acceptable timeframes.

dependencies.title: Cost Management team dependent on TRUCCR team for completing Cloud Advise: Azure VM to Plexus Recommendations and CloudAdvise: Azure DB on VM to PaaS Databases Recommendations milestones.
dependencies.description:
CloudAdvise: Azure VM to Plexus Recommendations - analyze non‑database workloads on Azure VMs and estimate savings from waste/rightsizing, containerization density, Windows → Linux re-platforming, and ARM64 adoption
 
CloudAdvise: Azure DB on VM to PaaS Databases Recommendations - detect SQL Server databases running on Azure VMs and evaluate migration to Azure PaaS equivalents (e.g., Azure SQL Managed Instance/Azure SQL Databases), with projected savings

dependencies.mitigation: Cost Managment team to continue partnering with TRUCCR team until end of May so milestones stay on track for completion.

decisions.title: Website Module Delivery Date Re-planned to Sept 30 from July 1
decisions.description: On 4/7 the original target completion date was changed from July 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 due to team indicating that effort was larger than first scoped.  This re-plan date creates  a variance of -$274,119 in cost savings versus the original July 30, 2026 estimate. This continues to be the largest single contributor to the overall savings gap and reflects the larger-than-anticipated scope of work. Website POC re-evaluation is in progress to determine likelihood of supporting the September 30, 2026 date.
decisions.rationale: Effort is larger than initially scoped.
decisions.options_considered: Website POC re-evaluation is in progress to determine likelihood of supporting the September 30, 2026 date or possibly pulling date forward.

decisions.title: Delay GST Phase 1B go-live until after tax season
decisions.description: Leadership decided to delay the GST Phase 1B migration go-live until after tax season to avoid jeopardizing a critical customer-facing system during peak usage while the GST batch transfer defect is resolved and validated.
decisions.rationale: The GST batch transfer issue is a high-impact defect affecting a core tax data transfer process. Proceeding with go-live during tax season would risk serious production failures and data transfer errors. Delaying the go-live prioritizes customer stability over deadlines and allows time to develop, test, and validate the fix before deployment.
decisions.options_considered: Proceed with Phase 1B go-live during tax season with elevated risk; delay Phase 1B go-live until after tax season to allow time for defect resolution and testing.

latest_report.content:
## Executive Summary

GCP Cloud Migration Program is a CIO‑sponsored strategic initiative, jointly aligned with Product Engineering, focused on demonstrating cloud portability while modernizing TR's application landscape. GCP Program targets the migration of ~59 applications across ~18 product families from AWS to GCP over a 30‑month, wave‑based roadmap. This matters because it consolidates platforms, enables cloud portability, and sets up AI-ready foundations while maintaining service reliability for customers using the GTM, IDT, DT, and Data Hub applications.

Program Initiation and Planning completed on 10-Apr-2026 as planned, and the Foundation Architecture and Landing Zone phase is in progress toward its 22-Jun-2026 completion date under Google’s 16-week Cloud Foundations engagement. Pilot workload selection is underway for a Jun-Aug window, with Constellation confirmed as the first pilot and supporting dependencies such as DevSecOps toolchain decisions and wave planning tracking against Jun'26 target dates.

Overall status is **Green**, with Foundations and Landing Zone progressing well to plan.

## Milestones

-   Complete DevSecOps approach and CI/CD toolchain decision, enabling pilot build activities, by 22 May 2026.
    
-   Complete the Foundation Architecture and Landing Zone Ready phase, including initial IaC build and deployment, by 22 Jun 2026.
    
-   Deliver pilot workloads live on GCP, migrating two applications including Constellation, by 31 Aug 2026.
    
-   Subsequent Wave Migrations Completion.
    
-   Complete overall AWS to GCP migration and close the program by 30 Sep 2028.
