assumptions.title: Google funding and Professional Services support will be available as planned
assumptions.description: The program assumes that approximately $16M in Google funding for migration and modernization and an additional $14M in Google Professional Services support will be provided over the full 30‑month program period.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Funding commitments have been outlined as part of the CIO‑sponsored strategic initiative with Google as a key partner.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Google funding and PS support are core elements of the business case for the AWS to GCP migration and have been explicitly quantified in program documentation, but are still subject to detailed commercial agreements and ongoing governance.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If funding is reduced or delayed, reprioritize application families and customer onboarding scope, adjust wave content, and seek alternative TR funding or cost optimizations to preserve critical program outcomes.
assumptions.validation_method: Formal confirmation through executed contracts and ongoing financial governance reviews between TR, Accenture and Google.

assumptions.title: Program can complete AWS to GCP migration within the 30‑month timeline
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the pilot phase and four migration waves, covering 59 in‑scope applications and customer onboarding, can be completed within the April 2026 to October 2028 period.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The timeline has been set by the CIO‑sponsored initiative, aligned with resource forecasts and wave planning assumptions across Global Trade, Indirect Tax and Platform portfolios.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The initial high‑level plan allocates time for pilot and four waves, supported by governance and weekly RAID reviews, but the schedule depends on timely decisions, environment readiness and resource availability across all parties.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If schedule risk increases, resequence applications between waves, reduce or defer lower‑value scope, or extend the program with Executive Steering Board approval.
assumptions.validation_method: Integrated schedule reviews during Program Board sessions, with periodic re‑forecasting based on wave progress and dependency status.

assumptions.title: GCP Landing Zone validated for pilots will be suitable for broader portfolio
assumptions.description: The program assumes that the GCP Landing Zone and associated patterns validated during pilot migrations will be suitable for the majority of the 59 in‑scope applications across 18 families.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Landing Zone design is intended as a reusable, standardized foundation for all migrated workloads, with pilots used to validate key patterns.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Landing Zone designs are typically reusable, but this program spans diverse applications and regulatory requirements, so suitability must be validated through pilots and architecture governance.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If pilots reveal significant gaps, plan controlled Landing Zone enhancements and re‑baseline wave schedules to incorporate necessary changes before broad rollout.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture Board reviews of pilot migration outcomes, Landing Zone validation assessment reports, and security/compliance sign‑offs before expanding to additional waves.

assumptions.title: TR will provide required VDI access and technical enablement to Accenture on time
assumptions.description: The program assumes that Thomson Reuters will provision VDI access with required tools, software and repository connectivity for Accenture teams according to agreed dates.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Accenture relies on TR‑provided VDI environments for secure access to application code and tools across all workstreams.
assumptions.validity_explanation: TR Platform Engineering has accountability for VDI provisioning and is engaged via program governance, but provisioning timelines are still being actively managed.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If VDI provisioning slips, prioritize critical teams and applications for access, explore interim access mechanisms where compliant, and escalate delays through program governance.
assumptions.validation_method: Tracking of VDI provisioning milestones and periodic status review in Workstream Steering and Program Board meetings.

assumptions.title: A program‑wide DevSecOps approach and CI/CD tooling will be agreed before major build activities
assumptions.description: The program assumes that a standard DevSecOps approach, including selection of CI/CD tools and network connectivity between AWS and GCP, will be agreed by TR Platform Engineering, Accenture and Google before intensive pilot and wave build work begins.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Consistent DevSecOps practices are required to support secure, repeatable deployments across all applications and waves.
assumptions.validity_explanation: All parties recognize the need for a unified DevSecOps approach, but final decisions on tools and connectivity are still pending.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If alignment is delayed, define a minimal common toolset for pilots and restrict divergence, while fast‑tracking final decisions through Architecture and Transformation Boards.
assumptions.validation_method: Architecture Board and Workstream Steering review and approval of the chosen DevSecOps tools, patterns and connectivity model.

assumptions.title: Wave planning and application sequencing will be agreed and baselined early in the program
assumptions.description: The program assumes that application sequencing into the four migration waves will be discussed, agreed and baselined between TR and Accenture early in WS1 Planning & Baselining.
assumptions.rationale_basis: A clear wave plan is needed to coordinate resources, manage dependencies and align workstreams across Global Trade, Indirect Tax, Platform and customer onboarding.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Initial preparation for wave planning is underway, but the final sequence requires cross‑portfolio agreement and governance sign‑off.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If agreement cannot be reached on time, adopt a phased approval (e.g., approve first two waves while refining later ones) and limit unplanned changes through strict change control.
assumptions.validation_method: Formal approval of the wave plan at the Program Board and incorporation into the integrated program schedule.

assumptions.title: Program governance forums will operate as defined in the governance framework
assumptions.description: The program assumes that all governance forums (Integrated Delivery Pods, Workstream Steering, Program Board, Architecture Board, Transformation Board, Executive Steering Board) will meet with the prescribed cadence, membership and escalation paths.
assumptions.rationale_basis: The RAID log and instructions define a multi‑tier governance model with specific responsibilities and escalation rules.
assumptions.validity_explanation: The governance model is agreed on paper, but its effectiveness depends on consistent participation and disciplined execution by all parties.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If governance forums under‑perform, rationalize or adjust the governance structure, clarify decision rights, and escalate persistent gaps to the Executive Steering Board.
assumptions.validation_method: Monitoring adherence to the governance calendar, meeting attendance, and timely resolution of escalated items.

assumptions.title: Planned customer onboarding volumes (800 GTM IP customers) are achievable within the program
assumptions.description: The program assumes that onboarding of approximately 800 GTM IP customers to the new GCP‑based services can be achieved within the program timeframe and capacity constraints.
assumptions.rationale_basis: Customer onboarding is explicitly defined as Workstream 3 and is integral to realizing business value from the migration.
assumptions.validity_explanation: Customer onboarding targets are set at a program level, but depend on customer readiness, internal capacity, and technical stability of migrated services.
assumptions.mitigation_contingency: If onboarding lags, reprioritize high‑value customers, adjust onboarding schedules, and consider additional resources or extended timelines with Executive Steering Board approval.
assumptions.validation_method: Detailed onboarding planning, capacity analysis, and tracking of customer onboarding KPIs through Workstream Steering and Program Board reviews.

dependencies.title: DevSecOps approach and toolchain decision
dependencies.description: Program-level DevSecOps approach and decisions are required, including CI/CD tooling and networking/interconnectivity between AWS and GCP, to support migrations across waves.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Platform Engineering to define and agree the DevSecOps approach, CI/CD tooling, and cross-cloud networking model
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – migration and engineering teams executing pilot and wave migrations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays pilot application migration and impacts planned program deliverable D2, with knock-on delay risk to subsequent migration waves.
dependencies.mitigation: Engage closely with Platform Engineering to obtain direction and finalize the DevSecOps approach, including CI/CD tools and networking, as a priority.

dependencies.title: GTM MVP applications low-level sessions
dependencies.description: Low-level sessions are required to define code-level deployment approaches, testing assets (test scripts and documentation), and database and external dependencies for GTM MVP application families.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Product Engineering to run product-family-focused low-level design and deployment sessions
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – migration planning teams for GTM applications
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays creation of the migration plan for GTM applications, affecting scheduling and content of migration waves within the program.
dependencies.mitigation: Organize focused sessions by product family to cover deployment approach, testing, and dependency details.

dependencies.title: Migration wave planning and sequencing
dependencies.description: Program-level wave planning session to agree application sequencing into migration waves across the Global Trade, Indirect Tax, and Platform portfolios.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Programme Delivery to schedule and complete wave planning and to approve application sequencing
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – program migration planning and execution teams across waves
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays the overall migration plan and wave structures, impacting planned program deliverable D6 and alignment of all workstreams.
dependencies.mitigation: Agree on wave sequencing and planning with Thomson Reuters Programme Delivery leads and formalize the wave plan through program governance.

dependencies.title: Pilot application deep-dive sessions
dependencies.description: Deep-dive working sessions are required to gain detailed understanding of Constellation (the second pilot application) and its technical and functional landscape.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Product Engineering to organize and participate in deep-dive sessions for the selected pilot application(s)
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – pilot migration team requiring detailed application knowledge
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays pilot application migration activities and impacts program deliverable D2 associated with pilot migrations.
dependencies.mitigation: Organize deep-dive sessions for the finalized pilot application while the second pilot application selection is being finalized.

dependencies.title: Pilot applications scope confirmation
dependencies.description: Scope and list of pilot applications must be finalized for planning and migration to GCP under the program pilot phase.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Programme Delivery to finalize pilot applications and their scope
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – program team planning and executing pilot migrations
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays discovery and start of pilot migration activities, impacting planned program deliverable D2 and subsequent migration waves.
dependencies.mitigation: Finalize the second pilot application with Thomson Reuters to avoid delays to pilot planning and execution.

dependencies.title: Elastic workload migration dependency due to existing AWS-based Elastic credits.
dependencies.description: Elastic workloads cannot be migrated from AWS to GCP until February 2027, as current financial credits are tied to Elastic on AWS and cannot be transferred to GCP. Thomson Reuters aims to avoid dual active Elastic contracts across AWS and GCP.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – commercial and vendor management teams to manage Elastic contract timing and AWS-based credits, and to define the allowed migration window to GCP.
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – migration planning and execution teams for Wave 1 and subsequent migration waves that include Elastic-dependent components.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays Wave 1 and subsequent migration timelines for Elastic-dependent workloads and may compress later-wave schedules, impacting the program’s ability to meet the 30‑month AWS to GCP migration timeline while honoring Elastic commercial commitments.
dependencies.mitigation: Decouple Elastic-dependent components from non-Elastic workloads to allow earlier migration of non-dependent workloads; plan migration waves and go-live sequencing to explicitly account for the February 2027 earliest migration date; coordinate between Thomson Reuters, Accenture, and Elastic/commercial teams to avoid dual active contracts and confirm the exact migration window.

dependencies.title: Landing Zone readiness for pilot applications
dependencies.description: GCP Landing Zone must be made available to Accenture for validating suitability for application migration and modernization in the pilot phase.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Platform Engineering to deliver a usable GCP Landing Zone for pilot applications
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – program migration team conducting pilot application landing zone validation
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Delays the Landing Zone validation assessment report and subsequent activities, impacting planned program deliverable D2 and downstream pilot and wave planning.
dependencies.mitigation: Closely track Landing Zone readiness and escalate delays to program delivery leads.

dependencies.title: VDI provisioning and technical enablement
dependencies.description: VDI access provisioning with access to required tools, software, and repositories for program delivery teams across the GCP Migration Program.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Platform Engineering to provision fully configured VDI environments with required tools, software, and repository access
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – delivery teams across program workstreams
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: Lack of timely access to fully configured VDI environments can hinder upcoming planning and engineering activities, affecting planned milestones and delivery timelines across migration waves.
dependencies.mitigation: Request VDI access in bulk with timely follow-ups on approvals, closely track provisioning progress, and escalate delays to program delivery leads.

dependencies.title: VDI setup on the client side
dependencies.description: VDI on the client side is unstable. Sometimes it works for a few minutes then fails shortly after. This primarily affects Mac OS laptops, while Accenture’s Windows laptops are working well.
dependencies.dependent_on: Thomson Reuters – Program Manager and TR support teams to resolve client-side VDI instability (including conditional access policy changes for Mac OS laptops).
dependencies.consumer: Accenture – delivery teams across program workstreams requiring stable VDI access to tools, software, and repositories.
dependencies.impact_if_delayed: High risk to project schedule; potential multi-week delay in start of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) development and Accenture’s migration scope.
dependencies.mitigation: Follow up on TR support ticket INC1412900 and investigate conditional access policies for Mac OS; expedite remediation to restore stable client-side VDI access.

decisions.title: Definition of program scope and wave-based delivery model
decisions.description: The program will migrate approximately 65 applications across 18 product families from AWS to GCP over a 30‑month timeline, using a wave-based approach that includes application migration, platform modernization, and customer onboarding.

decision_owner.name: Thomson Reuters Corporate Tax & Trade leadership with Program Ferrari governance

decisions.rationale: A wave-based scope and timeline enable manageable risk, phased learning, and coordinated customer onboarding while fitting within funding and resource constraints.
decisions.options_considered: Big‑bang migration of all applications; limiting scope to infrastructure-only migration without modernization; extending duration beyond 30 months with smaller waves.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Customer onboarding phases dependent on GTM IP migration; GCP landing zone readiness before large-scale application migrations.

decisions.title: Adoption of a three‑party strategic partnership model
decisions.description: The AWS to GCP Migration Program will be executed as a structured three‑party partnership with clear accountability: Thomson Reuters owns business outcomes, product priorities, security standards, and final acceptance; Google Cloud provides consultancy on platform, foundations, and architecture governance; Accenture executes migration and modernization activities under defined governance.

decision_owner.name: Matt Dimich (Program Sponsor, Thomson Reuters) with Google and Accenture executive leads

decisions.rationale: A three‑party model aligns each partner to their strengths—TR owning outcomes and risk, Google providing deep GCP expertise and foundations, and Accenture providing migration factory execution—reducing risk and improving delivery velocity across multiple workstreams.
decisions.options_considered: Single vendor responsible for both foundations and migration; internal-only migration using Thomson Reuters resources; two‑party partnership without a dedicated SI migration factory.
decisions.dependencies_linked: GCP landing zone readiness before large-scale application migrations; Completion of Google Foundations prior to full migration waves; Architecture governance model to support migration decisions.

decisions.title: Adoption of migration guiding principles for the program
decisions.description: The program will be guided by principles of minimum customer interruption, reliability from day one, cloud-native automation aligned with TR standards, combined migrate-and-modernize activities, and enabling future transformation and agentic AI.
decisions.rationale: Shared guiding principles provide consistent decision criteria across projects and vendors, ensuring that short‑term migration choices support long‑term resilience, automation, and AI‑ready capabilities.
decisions.options_considered: Focusing solely on lift‑and‑shift with minimal modernization; prioritizing speed over customer impact; deferring AI and automation considerations to a future program.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Infrastructure as Code modules availability for migration factory; Completion of Google Foundations prior to full migration waves.

decisions.title: Google Foundations scope limited to infrastructure and landing zone
decisions.description: Google Cloud Professional Services will focus on infrastructure-only scope: building the target-state GCP landing zone via IaC, conducting AWS architecture audits, and providing architecture governance. Manual workload migration, data transfer, and application code refactoring are explicitly out of scope and will be handled by the SI partner.

decision_owner.name: Google Cloud TR Account Lead (Hesham Rasmy Ali) with Thomson Reuters program leadership

decisions.rationale: Keeping Google PSO focused on foundations and governance maximizes leverage of GCP expertise while avoiding overlap with SI responsibilities, clarifying accountability and funding usage.
decisions.options_considered: Including workload migration and data transfer in Google PSO scope; a narrower advisory-only role for Google without IaC delivery; combining foundations and migration under a single vendor.
decisions.dependencies_linked: AWS environment inventory and service mapping for foundation design; Infrastructure as Code modules availability for migration factory; Completion of Google Foundations prior to full migration waves.

decisions.title: Establishment of architecture governance and escalation model
decisions.description: The program will operate with a structured architecture governance and escalation model: architecture decisions are owned at the lowest appropriate level, with defined escalation paths from Architecture Council to Program Governance to Joint Steering Committee, and a fast‑track mechanism for critical, time‑bound decisions affecting delivery, risk, or customer continuity.

decision_owner.name: Thomson Reuters Enterprise Architecture leadership in conjunction with Google and Accenture program leads

decisions.rationale: Clear governance and escalation reduce decision latency, align stakeholders, and ensure consistent architecture across multiple projects and vendors while protecting customer continuity.
decisions.options_considered: Ad‑hoc decision making without formal councils; centralized decision making only at executive level; vendor-specific governance without a joint model.
decisions.dependencies_linked: Architecture governance model to support migration decisions; GCP landing zone readiness before large-scale application migrations.

decisions.title: Use of a migration factory model for wave-based delivery
decisions.description: The program will use an Accenture-led migration factory to execute wave-based AWS to GCP migrations, including planning, assessments, wave design, migration execution, testing, cutover, hypercare, and coordination of customer onboarding.

decision_owner.name: Accenture Program Delivery Lead (Tejesh Nandyala) with Thomson Reuters program leadership

decisions.rationale: A factory model supports standardized processes, economies of scale, and repeatable patterns across many applications and product families, improving predictability of delivery.
decisions.options_considered: Individual project-by-project migrations led by separate teams; in-house only migration teams; fully automated tooling-only migration approach without a structured factory.
decisions.dependencies_linked: GCP landing zone readiness before large-scale application migrations; Infrastructure as Code modules availability for migration factory; Nomination of application and data owners for migrations.

milestones.name: Overall Program Status
milestones.description:
CIO-sponsored strategic transformation aligned with Product Engineering to deliver cloud portability and modernize TR’s application estate. The program targets migration of ~59 applications across ~18 product families from AWS to GCP over a 30‑month, wave-based roadmap—enabling platform consolidation, AI-ready foundations, and sustained service reliability across GTM, IDT, DT, and Data Hub.
Milestone Status:
Program Initiation and Planning completed on 10-Apr-2026 as planned. Foundations and Landing Zone phase is in progress and on track for 22-Jun-2026 completion under Google’s 16-week engagement. Pilot selection is underway, with Constellation confirmed and key dependencies (DevSecOps toolchain, wave planning) tracking to Jun’26 milestones.
Overall Health: Green — delivery progressing to plan.
milestones.metrics:
59 in-scope applications (across 18 families) delivered via Pilot + 4 waves
Accenture requires TR to nominate 2 in‑scope applications for Pilot Migration
Confirmed first pilot - Constellation

milestones.name: Program Initiation & Planning
milestones.description:
Program kick-off completed. Google Cloud and Accenture onboarded as strategic partners and initial planning and discussions are completed. Discovery and foundation workshops are complete. Program governance and cadence are stood up (weekly tri‑party standup + working sessions), with foundational program artifacts created and program reporting integrated into CIO governance (classified as a critical program; added/being added in CIO tracker). 
Kickoff readiness, workshop planning & session structure, stakeholder alignment, and early program controls (RACI consolidation, RAID logs, Stakeholder Register, Program Plan) documents are ready. SOW is finalized. Initiation & Planning Phase is completed successfully.

milestones.name: Foundation Architecture & Landing Zone Ready
milestones.description: Program is currently in Foundation Architecture & Landing Zone Ready phase with key dependencies in-flight. Google’s 16‑week Cloud Foundations is underway, and the teams have completed the initial 3‑day foundational workshops (architecture, security posture, network topology). Program is now progressing through follow‑up Landing Zone and Networking decision sessions, closing architecture, security, tagging, and CI/CD decisions while advancing toward Infrastructure‑as‑Code (IaC) build and deployment through late June. Accenture SOW is finalized, awaiting confirmation.

milestones.name: Pilot Workload Live on GCP
milestones.description:
Pilot workload selection is underway for a Jun-Aug window, with Constellation confirmed as the first pilot and supporting dependencies such as DevSecOps toolchain decisions and wave planning tracking against Jun'26 target dates.

Overall status is Green, with Foundations and Landing Zone progressing well to plan.

Constellation has been confirmed for migration.
